n: The Enhanced Fujita Scale has 6 categories. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 14-16]
xs: The Enhanced Fujita Scale has **6** categories — option **(3)** is correct.
It runs **F0/EF0 to F5/EF5**, measuring **tornado** **wind speed and damage**.
**Saffir-Simpson** has **Category 1 to 5** — a common confusion.
xa: **Beaufort Scale** runs **0 to 12** (wind force).
Tornado winds: **105 to 322 km/h**.
**INES** has **Level 0 to Level 7**.

19.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Strong convective instability, abundant moisture and strong updrafts are atmospheric factors associated with hailstorms.
II. Western Disturbances and wind discontinuity lines are synoptic factors associated with hailstorms.
III. Plateaus and hilly regions enhance convection associated with hailstorms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
19.x: All three are correct: convective instability, moisture and updrafts are atmospheric factors, western disturbances are synoptic factors, and plateaus and hills boost convection.
19.tq: Recall the causes of hailstorms.
n: Strong convective instability is an atmospheric factor associated with hailstorms. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 39-41]
Abundant moisture is an atmospheric factor associated with hailstorms. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 39-41]
Strong updrafts are an atmospheric factor associated with hailstorms. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 39-41]
Western Disturbances are synoptic factors associated with hailstorms. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 39-41]
Wind discontinuity lines are synoptic factors associated with hailstorms. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 39-41]
Plateaus enhance convection associated with hailstorms. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 39-41]
Hilly regions enhance convection associated with hailstorms. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 39-41]
xs: All three statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **atmospheric** factors — **strong convective instability**, **abundant moisture**, **strong updrafts**.
II: **synoptic** factors — **Western Disturbances**, **wind discontinuity lines**.
III: **terrain** — **plateaus and hilly regions** **enhance convection**.
xa: **Climate change:** increasing **frequency and intensity** of extreme convective events.
Hailstorms are part of **pre-monsoon convective weather**.
Cumulonimbus towers reach **15 km** in unstable, moist air.

20.s: Weather is best defined as:
o: The state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time
The long-term distribution of vegetation over a region
The average atmospheric condition over a period of 30 years
The seasonal variation in ocean currents only
20.x: Weather refers to the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time. Climate refers to average weather over a long period.
20.tq: Distinguish the short-term weather definition from the long-term climate definition.
xs: **Weather** is the **state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time** — option **(1)**.
The **30-year average** describes **climate**, not weather.
xa: ⚠ **Weather** = one place and time; **Climate** = **30-year** average (WMO).
A **climograph** plots a station's monthly temperature (line) + rainfall (bars).
Elements: temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, precipitation, cloudiness.

20.s: The World Meteorological Organization’s standard period for describing climate normals is:
20.x: The WMO standard describes climate using average weather conditions over a period of 30 years.
20.tq: Test the standard numerical period directly.
xs: The **WMO** standard for climate is average weather over **30 years** — option **(3)**.
Climate is long-term; weather is the state at **one place and time**.
xa: IMD's SW monsoon normal (**868.6 mm**) uses the **1971-2020** base period — a 30-year normal.
A **biome** is a large natural community shaped by **climate**.
**Climograph**: temperature as a **line**, rainfall as **bars**.

20.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A climograph represents monthly temperature and rainfall of a station on one chart.
2. Temperature is generally represented by a line in a climograph.
3. Rainfall is generally represented by bars in a climograph.
4. A climograph can assist in identifying the climate type of a place.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: A climograph combines monthly temperature, shown by a line, and rainfall, shown by bars, and is used to interpret the climate type of a station.
20.tq: Combine the chart components and their use before selecting the coded answer.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
A **climograph** shows a station's **monthly temperature (line)** and **rainfall (bars)** on **one chart**.
It is used to **read the climate type** of the station.
xa: Climate = average weather over **30 years** (WMO).
**Biome**: large natural community of flora and fauna over a major habitat, shaped by climate (UPSC).
**Anthromes**: ecological units shaped by sustained human use (croplands, villages, cities).

20.s: The current IMD rainfall normal for the southwest monsoon season, based on the 1971–2020 period, is:
20.x: The IMD normal rainfall for June–September, based on the 1971–2020 base period, is 868.6 mm.
20.tq: Separate the precise normal value from nearby numerical distractors.
xs: IMD's SW monsoon (**Jun-Sep**) normal (LPA) is **868.6 mm** — option **(2)**.
It is based on the **1971-2020** period.
xa: WMO standard climate period: **30 years**.
Elements of climate: temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, **precipitation**, cloudiness.
About **40** coastal districts may warm by over **1** degC by **2040**; **AP and Tamil Nadu** to get excess SW-monsoon rain.

20.s: Which one of the following is NOT regarded as a control of climate?
20.x: Distance from a river is not a recognised control of climate. Latitude, altitude and distance from the sea influence climatic conditions.
20.tq: Find the factor that does not belong to the standard climatic controls.
xs: **Distance from a river** is **not** a control of climate — option **(3)** (APPSC GS **2025**).
**Latitude** (angle of rays, insolation), **altitude** (lapse rate) and **distance from the sea** (equable vs continental) are true controls.
xa: Other controls: **mountain barriers/relief**, **ocean currents**, **winds and pressure belts**.
**Himalayas** keep north India **3-8 deg C** warmer in winter.
**Shimla** is far cooler than **Amritsar** at a similar latitude — altitude.

20.s: The mainland of India lies approximately between which latitudes?
20.x: India’s mainland extends approximately from 8°N to 37°N. Insolation generally decreases towards the poles.
20.tq: Recall the precise geographical range rather than the broader regional location.
xs: India's mainland lies between about **8°N and 37°N** — option **(3)**.
**Latitude** controls climate through the angle of the sun's rays; areas south of the **Tropic of Cancer** are tropical.
xa: The **Tropic of Cancer** crosses **8 states** and crosses the **Mahi twice**.
AP lies between **12 deg 41' N** and **19 deg 07' N**.
Insolation **falls poleward**.

20.s: The normal rate at which temperature decreases with increase in altitude is approximately
20.x: Temperature falls at approximately 6.5°C for every 1,000 metres of ascent under the normal lapse rate.
20.tq: Use the standard numerical value associated with altitude and temperature.
xs: The normal lapse rate is about **6.5°C per 1,000 m** — option **(1)**.
That is the same as about **6.5 degC per km**.
xa: Example: **Shimla** is far cooler than **Amritsar** at a similar latitude.
Koeppen's **H** (highland) group is **cold due to altitude**.
The **tree line** marks the altitude beyond which trees cannot grow — **alpine tundra** lies above.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the climatic contrast produced by distance from the sea?
o: Distance from the sea affects rainfall but not temperature
Coastal areas have continental extremes, while interiors are equable
Coastal areas are generally equable, while interiors experience greater extremes
Both coasts and interiors have identical seasonal ranges
20.x: The sea moderates temperatures near the coast, whereas inland areas tend to experience greater temperature extremes and a continental climate.
20.tq: Identify the correctly reversed coastal–continental comparison.
xs: **Coasts are equable/maritime**, while **interiors are extreme/continental** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) reverses this; the sea moderates both seasonal and daily ranges.
xa: **A&N Islands**: equable, humid; the **monsoon arrives there first**.
⚠ Distance from a **river** is not a climate control.
Other controls: latitude, altitude, relief, ocean currents, winds and pressure belts.

20.s: Which of the following statements regarding ocean currents and climate is correct?
o: Ocean currents have no effect on coastal climates
Warm currents make tropical western coasts permanently arid
Cold currents make tropical western coasts cool and dry
Cold currents make eastern continental coasts warm and rainy
20.x: Cold currents cool and dry adjacent coasts, particularly on the western margins of tropical continents. Warm currents tend to make coasts warmer and wetter.
20.tq: Discriminate between the contrasting effects of cold and warm currents.
xs: **Cold currents** make **tropical west coasts cool and dry** (arid) — option **(3)**.
**Warm currents** make **east coasts warm and rainy**, so options (2) and (4) swap the roles.
xa: **Hot deserts** lie at **15-30 deg N and S** on **western margins** — caused by subtropical high, offshore trade winds and **cold currents**.
Examples: **Sahara, Kalahari, Namib, Atacama**, Arabian, Thar, Great Australian.
**Atacama** (northern Chile, west of the Andes) is the world's **driest** place.

20.s: The Tropic of Cancer crosses how many Indian states?
20.x: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
20.tq: Test a fixed geographical count and its associated list.
xs: The **Tropic of Cancer** crosses **8** states — option **(3)**.
They are **Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram**.
xa: It crosses the **Mahi river twice**.
Areas south of the Tropic of Cancer are **tropical**; **Aw** covers most of the Peninsula south of it.
India's mainland: **8 deg N-37 deg N**.

20.s: What would be the most significant climatic consequence for northern India if the Himalayas did not exist?
o: The southwest monsoon would reverse permanently into a north-easterly wind.
The region would receive heavier monsoon rainfall because cold air would enter freely.
Northern India would tend to become a desert because the Himalayas would no longer block cold Central Asian air or trap the monsoon.
The Tibetan Plateau would become a permanent oceanic low-pressure centre.
20.x: The Himalayas block cold Central Asian air and help trap the monsoon over the subcontinent. Without them, northern India would tend to become a desert.
20.tq: Apply the barrier and trapping functions of a major relief feature to a hypothetical situation.
xs: Without the **Himalayas**, northern India would tend to become a **desert**, as nothing would **block cold Central Asian air** or **trap the monsoon** — option **(3)**.
The Himalayas **block cold Central Asian winds** and **trap the monsoon**.
xa: They keep north India **3-8 deg C** warmer in winter than places on the same latitude.
**Relief**: windward slopes wet, leeward slopes in **rain-shadow**.
**Mawsynram** (mean **1,187 cm**) is wettest due to **funnelling + orographic lifting**.

20.s: Who proposed the empirical climatic classification scheme based on mean temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation?
20.x: Wladimir Koeppen proposed an empirical climatic classification based on mean temperature and precipitation, with climate types linked to natural vegetation.
20.tq: Use the direct name-and-contribution recall method.
xs: **Wladimir Koeppen** proposed the empirical scheme based on **temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation** — option **(4)**.
**Thornthwaite** (**1931**, revised **1948**) used **precipitation effectiveness** and **thermal efficiency**.
xa: Koeppen groups: **A** tropical humid, **B** dry, **C** warm temperate, **D** cold snow-forest, **E** polar, **H** highland.
Second letters: **f** no dry season, **m** monsoon, **w** dry winter, **s** dry summer.
AP is predominantly **Aw**.

20.s: In Koeppen’s classification, the letter ‘H’ denotes:
20.x: H denotes a highland climate in which low temperatures are controlled mainly by altitude.
20.tq: Discriminate the exact classification letter from similar-sounding alternatives.
xs: Koeppen's **H** is a **highland** climate, **cold due to altitude** — option **(1)**.
Hot desert is **BW**; **E** is polar.
xa: **E** = warmest month below **10 degC** (ET tundra, EF ice cap).
Lapse rate: ~**6.5°C per 1,000 m**.
**Alpine tundra** lies above the tree line in the **Himalayas, Andes, Alps**.

20.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in respect of the second letters used in Koeppen’s classification?
20.x: The second letter f indicates that there is no dry season. The letters m, w and s indicate monsoon, dry winter and dry summer respectively.
20.tq: Use the confusable-pair method for the letters w and s.
xs: **f — no dry season** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**m** = **monsoon**, **w** = **dry winter**, **s** = **dry summer** — so options (2)-(4) are wrong.
xa: **Amw** = west coast south of Goa; **Aw** = Peninsula; **As** = Coromandel.
**Cwg** = monsoon with **dry winter** (Ganga plain).
**Dfc** = Arunachal Pradesh.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about climatic classifications:
1. Koeppen's scheme is based on atmospheric pressure and winds rather than temperature and precipitation.
2. Thornthwaite's scheme is based on precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency (potential evapotranspiration).
3. Thornthwaite proposed his classification in 1931 and revised it in 1948.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statement 3 is correct: Thornthwaite's scheme dates from 1931 and was revised in 1948. Statement 2 is correct: it uses precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency. Statement 1 is wrong: Koeppen's empirical scheme uses mean temperature and precipitation, linked to natural vegetation. So '3 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 1 are wrong.
20.tq: Koeppen = temperature + rain + vegetation; Thornthwaite = P-effectiveness + thermal efficiency.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Koeppen's** empirical scheme is based on mean **temperature and precipitation**, linked to **natural vegetation**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Thornthwaite** used **precipitation effectiveness** + **thermal efficiency** (potential evapotranspiration).
Statement 3 is correct: Thornthwaite proposed it in **1931**, revised in **1948**.
xa: Koeppen groups: **A** tropical humid, **B** dry, **C** warm temperate, **D** cold snow-forest, **E** polar, **H** highland.
Group **A**: coldest month above **18 degC**; group **E**: warmest month below **10 degC**.
Second letters: **f** no dry season, **m** monsoon, **w** dry winter, **s** dry summer.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its climatic criterion in the classification table?
20.x: Group D has the coldest month below -3°C, not above 18°C. The criteria stated for Groups A, B and E are correct.
20.tq: Find the one reversed temperature criterion.
xs: **D — coldest month above 18°C** is wrong — option **(1)**; **D** (cold snow-forest) has its coldest month **below -3 degC**.
**Above 18 degC** for the coolest month is group **A**.
The other pairs are right: **A** — coolest month above 18; **E** — warmest below **10**; **B** — evaporation exceeds precipitation.
xa: **C** = coldest month between **-3 and 18 degC**.
**H** = highland, cold due to altitude.
India's **Dfc** region: **Arunachal Pradesh**.

20.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Code)
a. Amw
b. As
c. BWhw
d. Dfc

List-II (Area)
i. Arunachal Pradesh
ii. Extreme western Rajasthan
iii. West coast south of Goa
iv. Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu
20.x: Amw occurs on the west coast south of Goa, As on the Coromandel coast, BWhw in extreme western Rajasthan and Dfc in Arunachal Pradesh.
20.tq: Start from the sure code-area pair and eliminate the remaining combinations.
xs: Correct match: **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**Amw** — west coast south of Goa; **As** — Coromandel coast of TN.
**BWhw** — extreme western Rajasthan; **Dfc** — Arunachal Pradesh.
xa: **Aw** — most of the Peninsular plateau south of the Tropic of Cancer.
**Cwg** — Ganga plain, eastern Rajasthan, northern MP, most of NE India.
APPSC-G1 **2024** asked a similar code-area match.

20.s: The Koeppen code 'Aw' represents which climatic type and area in India?
o: Monsoon with dry summer; Coromandel coast
Tropical savanna; most of the Peninsular Plateau south of the Tropic of Cancer
20.x: Aw denotes tropical savanna and covers most of the Peninsular Plateau south of the Tropic of Cancer.
20.tq: Pair the code with both its exact climate meaning and area.
xs: **Aw** = **tropical savanna**, covering **most of the Peninsular plateau south of the Tropic of Cancer** — option **(4)**.
Hot desert of western Rajasthan is **BWhw**; dry-summer Coromandel is **As**; polar is **E**.
xa: **AP** is predominantly **Aw** (tropical wet and dry).
⚠ **As** = Coromandel; **Amw** = west coast south of Goa.
Savanna: **wet summer, dry winter**; tall grass with scattered trees.

20.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the climatic type of Andhra Pradesh under Koeppen's classification?
o: The State is predominantly classified as Aw.
The State is predominantly classified as Cwg.
The State is predominantly classified as BWhw.
The State is predominantly classified as Dfc.
20.x: Andhra Pradesh is predominantly Aw, representing a tropical wet-and-dry or tropical savanna climate.
20.tq: Apply a broad regional classification to the State rather than a local exception.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** is predominantly Koeppen **Aw** (tropical wet and dry) — option **(1)**.
**Cwg** is the Ganga plain; **BWhw** extreme western Rajasthan; **Dfc** Arunachal Pradesh.
xa: AP extent: **12 deg 41' N** to **19 deg 07' N**.
**Four climatic regions**: humid coastal, deltaic, **semi-arid Rayalaseema**, hill micro-climates (Araku, Lambasingi, Horsley Hills).
AP has **six agro-climatic zones** (older books say seven); India has **15**.

20.s:
Match List-I (Koeppen code) with List-II (Area in India):

List-I
a. Amw
b. As
c. Cwg
d. BShw

List-II
i. Ganga plain
ii. North-west India
iii. West coast south of Goa
iv. Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
20.x: As in APPSC-G1 2024: Amw is the west coast south of Goa, As the Coromandel coast (dry summer, winter rain), Cwg the Ganga plain (monsoon with dry winter) and BShw north-west India. The other codes swap Amw with As, Cwg with BShw, or Amw with Cwg.
20.tq: Amw west coast; As Coromandel; Cwg Ganga plain; BShw NW.
xs: Correct match: **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)** (as in APPSC-G1 **2024**).
**Amw** — west coast south of Goa; **As** — Coromandel coast (winter rain).
**Cwg** — Ganga plain (monsoon with dry winter); **BShw** — north-west India.
xa: **BWhw** — extreme western Rajasthan; **Dfc** — Arunachal Pradesh.
**Aw** — Peninsular plateau and **AP**.
⚠ **As** is India's parallel of the **Mediterranean type**.

20.s: Which one of the following climatic regions is characterised by dense evergreen hardwoods such as mahogany and ebony, with rain almost every day?
20.x: The equatorial region, including the Amazon, Congo and Indonesia, has dense evergreen hardwood forests and almost daily rainfall.
20.tq: Directly link the vegetation and rainfall pattern with the climatic region.
xs: The **equatorial** region has **dense evergreen hardwoods** (**mahogany, ebony**) and **rain almost daily** — option **(2)**.
**Mediterranean** has winter rain; **taiga** conifers; **savanna** tall grass.
xa: Equatorial belt (**0-10 deg**): **Amazon, Congo, Indonesia**, SE Asia.
Afternoon **convectional rain**; rain **50-260 inches**.
Very small annual range (**2-3 degC**) with rain every month = equatorial; **Pygmies** live in these forests.

20.s: The tropical monsoon region of India and South-East Asia is chiefly associated with which vegetation?
20.x: Tropical monsoon forests in India and South-East Asia include teak and sal; the trees shed their leaves during the dry season.
20.tq: Match the climatic region with its representative vegetation.
xs: Tropical monsoon forests have **teak and sal** — option **(1)**.
Trees **shed leaves in the dry season**; rainfall **700-2,000 mm**.
**Spruce and fir** belong to the **taiga**; **mosses and lichens** to the **tundra**; **oak and maple** to temperate deciduous forests.
xa: Region: **India, SE Asia, N Australia**; seasonal wind reversal, summer rain.
AP is Koeppen **Aw** (tropical wet and dry).
Temperate deciduous trees (oak, beech, maple, birch) shed leaves in **autumn**.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about the taiga (boreal) biome:
1. It occurs in both the northern and southern hemispheres.
2. It is dominated by evergreen conifers such as spruce, fir and pine.
3. It is associated with acidic podzol soils.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the taiga of northern North America and Eurasia has evergreen conifers (spruce, fir, pine) on acidic podzol soils. Statement 1 is wrong: the taiga occurs in the northern hemisphere only. So '2 only' misses statement 3, and options with statement 1 are wrong.
20.tq: Taiga = northern hemisphere only, conifers, podzol.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **taiga** occurs in the **northern hemisphere only** (northern North America, Europe, Asia).
Statement 2 is correct: it is dominated by evergreen **conifers** — **spruce, fir, pine**.
Statement 3 is correct: it has acidic **podzol** soils.
xa: **Taiga is the largest land biome**; it has the **lowest productivity** of all forests.
⚠ Taiga has a **wide** winter-summer temperature range — "narrow range" was the wrong statement (**APPSC G1 2023, 2024**).
Taiga wildlife: **moose, beavers, lynxes, wolves, wolverines**.

20.s: Which one of the following statements about the taiga biome is NOT correct?
o: It is the largest land biome.
It has the highest productivity of all forests.
It has a wide range of temperature between winter and summer.
20.x: Taiga is the largest land biome, has a wide seasonal temperature range and moderate precipitation, but it has the lowest productivity of all forests.
20.tq: Find the statement that reverses a specific comparison.
xs: "**Highest productivity of all forests**" is wrong — option **(3)**; the taiga has the **lowest productivity** of all forests.
The rest are correct: the taiga is the **largest land biome**, with **moderate precipitation** and a **wide** winter-summer temperature range.
xa: ⚠ "Narrow range" was the incorrect statement in APPSC G1 **2023, 2024**.
Taiga soils: acidic **podzol**; trees: **spruce, fir, pine**.
**Yakuts** (Siberia) live in the taiga/Arctic.

20.s:
Which of the following is characteristic of the tundra biome?
1. Permafrost
2. Mosses and lichens
3. Absence of trees
4. Dense evergreen hardwood canopy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
20.x: Tundra has permafrost, mosses and lichens, and generally no trees. A dense evergreen hardwood canopy is not a tundra feature.
20.tq: Eliminate the vegetation statement belonging to another biome.
xs: **Permafrost**, **mosses and lichens** and **no trees** mark the tundra — option **(1)** (**1, 2 and 3 only**).
A dense evergreen hardwood canopy belongs to the **equatorial rainforest**, not the tundra.
xa: Tundra lies on **Arctic coasts** of N America and Eurasia; **alpine tundra** above the tree line.
Fauna: **reindeer, arctic fox, musk-ox**.
Peoples: **Inuit** (Canada, Alaska, Greenland), **Sami** (Scandinavia).

20.s: The tree line refers to the altitude or latitude beyond which:
20.x: The tree line is the altitude or latitude beyond which trees cannot grow; alpine tundra lies above it.
20.tq: Test the exact definition of a geographical term.
xs: The **tree line / timber line** is the altitude or latitude **beyond which trees cannot grow** — option **(3)** (APPSC GS **2019**).
It is the **upper limit of tree growth** on mountains or in high latitudes.
xa: Above it lies **alpine tundra** — in the **Himalayas, Andes, Alps**.
Tundra: **permafrost**, mosses, lichens, no trees.
Koeppen **H** = highland, cold due to altitude.

20.s: Which of the following regions is associated with the China-type climate?
o: Sudan belt and East Africa only
20.x: The China-type climate is associated with central and southern China, as well as areas such as the south-eastern United States, southern Brazil and eastern Australia.
20.tq: Identify the representative area from a climate classification list.
xs: The **China type** climate covers **central and southern China** — option **(2)**.
It is a **warm humid east-margin** climate with **summer rain**; also **SE USA**, S Brazil, E Australia.
Arctic coasts are **tundra**; Sahara and Kalahari **hot desert**; Sudan belt **savanna**.
xa: ⚠ **China type** = east margin; **Mediterranean** = **30-45 deg** western margins; **hot deserts** = **15-30 deg** western margins.
Notes confirm the sub-tropical biome = **eastern China and SE USA**.
**British type** deciduous biome = **NW Europe**.

20.s: The British-type climate is characterised by which combination?
o: Westerlies, rainfall throughout the year and mild conditions
Summer drought, winter rain and evergreen shrubs
Wet summer, dry winter and tall grass
Permafrost, no trees and very low precipitation
20.x: The British type is influenced by westerlies and has rainfall throughout the year with mild conditions.
20.tq: Distinguish the British type from Mediterranean and savanna climates by rainfall seasonality.
xs: The **British type** has **westerlies**, **rain throughout the year** and **mild** conditions — option **(1)**.
Summer drought with winter rain is **Mediterranean**; wet summer/dry winter is **savanna**; permafrost is **tundra**.
xa: British type = temperate deciduous of **NW Europe**; also British Columbia, S Chile, New Zealand.
Trees **oak, beech, maple, birch** shed leaves in **autumn**.
Mid-latitude location (APPSC G2 **2025**).

20.s:
Arrange the following climatic regions from the Equator towards the polar region, in the broad order indicated by their characteristic belts:
A. Tundra
B. Equatorial
C. Temperate deciduous
D. Tropical monsoon
Select the correct answer.
20.x: Moving broadly from the Equator towards the poles, the sequence is equatorial, tropical monsoon, temperate deciduous and tundra.
20.tq: Use latitudinal progression from the Equator towards the poles.
xs: From equator to pole: **Equatorial → Tropical monsoon → Temperate deciduous → Tundra** — **B, D, C, A**, option **(1)**.
Equatorial is at **0-10 deg**; temperate deciduous is **mid-latitude**; tundra on **Arctic coasts**.
xa: Tropical monsoon covers **India, SE Asia, N Australia**.
**Taiga** lies between temperate deciduous and tundra, in the northern hemisphere only.
Hot deserts: **15-30 deg**; Mediterranean: **30-45 deg** (western margins).

20.s:
Consider the following statements about the location of climatic regions:
1. The Mediterranean climate occurs mainly between 30° and 45° N and S on the western margins of continents.
2. The China-type climate occurs on the western margins of continents.
3. Hot deserts occur mainly between 15° and 30° N and S on the western margins of continents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statement 3 is correct: hot deserts lie at 15-30° on western margins (subtropical high, offshore trades, cold currents). Statement 1 is correct: Mediterranean climate lies at 30-45° on western margins. Statement 2 is wrong: the China type is a warm humid east-margin climate. So '3 only' misses statement 1, and options with statement 2 are wrong.
20.tq: West margin: desert 15-30°, Mediterranean 30-45°; east margin: China type.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Mediterranean** climate lies at **30-45 deg N/S** on **western margins**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **China type** is a **warm humid east margin** climate.
Statement 3 is correct: **hot deserts** lie at **15-30 deg N and S** on **western margins**.
xa: Hot desert causes: **subtropical high** + offshore **trade winds** + **cold currents**.
China type areas: Central/S China, **SE USA**, S Brazil, E Australia; **summer rain**.
Mediterranean: **hot dry summers, mild wet winters** — rain from **westerly depressions**.

20.s: Which combination best explains the occurrence of hot deserts on the western margins of continents?
o: Subtropical high pressure, offshore trade winds and cold currents
Polar easterlies, glaciers and high humidity
Equatorial low pressure, onshore trade winds and warm currents
Monsoon depressions, warm currents and rising air
20.x: Subtropical high pressure suppresses rainfall, offshore trade winds reduce moisture supply, and cold currents further stabilise and dry the air.
20.tq: Match the desert location with the combined pressure, wind and current conditions.
xs: Hot deserts on western margins result from **subtropical high pressure**, **offshore trade winds** and **cold currents** — option **(1)**.
Equatorial low pressure, onshore winds and warm currents bring rain, not deserts.
xa: **Cold currents** cool and dry coasts, making tropical west coasts arid.
Hot desert: rain **under 25 cm**, high diurnal range, **xerophytes**.
Desert peoples: **Bedouin** (Arabia, Sahara), **Tuareg** (Sahara), **Bushmen (San)** (Kalahari).

20.s: A biome is best described as which one of the following?
o: A transition zone between two adjacent ecosystems
An artificial ecosystem maintained only by human beings
A small community containing only one species
A large natural community of flora and fauna over a major habitat, shaped mainly by climate
20.x: A biome is a large natural community of flora and fauna occupying a major habitat and shaped by climate. It contains many habitats.
20.tq: Distinguish the definition of a biome from community, ecosystem and ecotone.
xs: A **biome** is a **large natural community of flora and fauna** over a **major habitat**, **shaped by climate** — option **(4)**.
It **contains many habitats**, so it is not a single-species community or a transition zone; human-made units are **anthromes**.
xa: **Anthromes**: ecological units shaped by **sustained human use** (croplands, villages, cities).
**Taiga** is the **largest land biome**.
**Tree line**: beyond it trees cannot grow (APPSC GS **2019**).

20.s: Anthropogenic biomes, also called anthromes, are ecological units shaped by which of the following?
o: Sustained human use such as croplands, villages and cities
20.x: Anthropogenic biomes are ecological units shaped by sustained human use and include croplands, villages and cities.
20.tq: Apply the definition to examples of human-shaped ecological units.
xs: **Anthromes** (anthropogenic biomes) are shaped by **sustained human use** — **croplands, villages, cities** — option **(1)**.
Natural biomes, by contrast, are shaped by **climate**.
xa: A **biome** contains many habitats.
**Climograph**: monthly temperature (line) + rainfall (bars).
Climate = average weather over **30 years** (WMO).

20.s: Alpine tundra is generally found in which situation?
o: In the humid equatorial belt below 10° latitude
Above the tree line in mountains such as the Himalayas, Andes and Alps
Below the tree line in tropical lowlands
20.x: Alpine tundra occurs above the tree line in high mountain systems such as the Himalayas, Andes and Alps.
20.tq: Apply the definition of alpine tundra to altitude and location.
xs: **Alpine tundra** is found **above the tree line** in the **Himalayas, Andes and Alps** — option **(2)**.
The **tree line** is where trees cannot grow, so alpine tundra cannot be below it or in equatorial lowlands.
xa: Arctic tundra: **Arctic coasts** of N America and Eurasia; **permafrost**.
Tree line asked in APPSC GS **2019**.
Koeppen **E** (polar): warmest month below **10 degC** — **ET** tundra, **EF** ice cap.

20.s: Mediterranean climate receives most of its rainfall during winter because
o: the subtropical high-pressure belt dominates in winter
cold ocean currents produce continuous monsoon rainfall
westerly depressions and cyclonic systems affect the region in winter
the trade winds reverse and produce convection throughout winter
20.x: In winter, the seasonal shift of pressure belts allows westerly depressions to bring cyclonic rainfall to Mediterranean regions.
20.tq: Connect the seasonal pressure-belt shift with the timing of rainfall.
xs: Mediterranean winter rain comes from **westerly depressions** (**cyclonic rain**) — option **(3)**.
Reason: the **seasonal shift of pressure belts**; in **summer** the **subtropical high** brings hot, dry drought — so option (1) is reversed.
xa: Pattern: **hot dry summers, mild wet winters**.
Location: **30-45 deg N/S** on **western margins**.
India's parallel: Koeppen **As** on the **Coromandel coast**.

20.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with Mediterranean climate?
20.x: Darwin is not among the listed Mediterranean climatic locations. Mediterranean conditions occur in places such as Santiago, Cape Town and Perth.
20.tq: Find the location outside the recognised Mediterranean-climate regions.
xs: **Eastern Australia — Darwin** is not a Mediterranean pair — option **(2)**.
Mediterranean Australia is **SW and south Australia** (**Perth, Adelaide**); **E Australia** is listed under the **China type**.
The rest are correct: **Central Chile** — Santiago; **SW Australia** — Perth; **SW Cape** — Cape Town.
xa: Other Mediterranean towns: **Rome, Athens, Los Angeles, San Francisco**.
Mediterranean belt: **30-45 deg**, western margins.
China type: central/S China, **SE USA**, S Brazil, E Australia — **summer rain**.

20.s: The Mediterranean climatic region is popularly known for the cultivation of
20.x: Mediterranean regions are known as orchard lands and are associated with citrus fruits, grapes and wine production.
20.tq: Use the characteristic crop association to identify the climate.
xs: Mediterranean regions are known for **citrus fruits, grapes and wine** — option **(2)** ("**orchard lands**").
Natural vegetation: **evergreen shrubs, olives, citrus**.
xa: Climate: **hot dry summers, mild wet winters**.
Location: **30-45 deg N/S**, western margins.
⚠ **Warm dry summer, mild wet winter** description = Mediterranean.

20.s: The Steppe belt is significant because it separates:
20.x: The Eurasian Steppe belt separates Cold Asia from Dry Asia.
20.tq: Test the geographical relationship associated with a named region.
xs: The Steppe belt separates **Cold Asia from Dry Asia** — option **(3)** (APPSC G1 **2022**).
It runs from **Ukraine to Central Asia** — Russia east of the **Urals**.
xa: Steppes are **temperate** grasslands.
Fauna of temperate grasslands: **bison, prairie dogs, antelope**.
**Central Asian steppes** are cited as rangelands (UN Year **2026**).

20.s:
Consider the following pairs:
Grassland — Region
1. Prairies — USA and Canada
2. Pampas — Argentina and Uruguay
3. Veld — Australia
4. Canterbury — New Zealand
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
20.x: Pair 1 is correct: the Prairies lie in both the USA and Canada. Pair 2 is correct: the Pampas are in Argentina and Uruguay. Pair 3 is wrong: the Veld is in South Africa; the Downs are the Australian grassland. Pair 4 is correct: Canterbury is in New Zealand. So 1, 2 and 4 only (B); A leaves out the true pair 4, while C and D include the wrong pair 3.
20.tq: Veld = South Africa, Downs = Australia; swapping these two is the usual trap.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Prairies** — **USA and Canada**; **Pampas** — **Argentina, Uruguay**; **Canterbury** — **New Zealand**.
Pair 3 wrong: the **Veld** is in **South Africa**; Australia's grassland is the **Downs**.
xa: Exam angle: Prairies are in USA **and** Canada (not USA alone, not Mexico).
Tropical grasslands: **savanna** (Africa), **Llanos** (Venezuela), **Campos** (Brazil).
⚠ **Llanos** = Venezuela; **Pampas** = Argentina; **Campos** = Brazil.

20.s: Which one of the following is a tropical grassland rather than a temperate grassland?
20.x: Llanos is a tropical grassland of the Orinoco basin, whereas Pampas, Steppes and Veld are temperate grasslands.
20.tq: Separate the tropical category from the group of temperate grasslands.
xs: The **Llanos** (**Venezuela**-Colombia, **Orinoco basin**) is a **tropical** grassland — option **(3)**.
**Steppes, Veld** and **Pampas** are all **temperate** grasslands.
xa: Other tropical grasslands: **savanna** (Africa), **Campos** (Brazilian Highlands).
Temperate: **Prairies, Pampas, Steppes, Veld, Downs, Canterbury**.
Savanna climate: **wet summer, dry winter** (tropical wet-dry).

20.s:
Consider the following statements about temperate grasslands:
1. The Pampas are the temperate grasslands of Venezuela and Colombia.
2. They support animals such as bison, prairie dogs and antelope.
3. Their climate has hot summers, chilly winters and only 25-50 cm of rain.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
20.x: Statement 3 is correct: steppe-type grasslands have hot summers, chilly winters and 25-50 cm of rain. Statement 2 is correct: bison, prairie dogs and antelope live there. Statement 1 is wrong: the Pampas are in Argentina (and Uruguay); Venezuela-Colombia has the Llanos, a tropical grassland. So '3 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 1 are wrong.
20.tq: Llanos = Venezuela (tropical); Pampas = Argentina (temperate).
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **Pampas** are in **Argentina**, Uruguay; **Venezuela-Colombia** has the **Llanos** (tropical).
Statement 2 is correct: temperate grasslands support **bison, prairie dogs, antelope**.
Statement 3 is correct: **hot summers, chilly winters**, rain only **25-50 cm**.
xa: **Prairies** = **USA and Canada**; **Veld** = **South Africa**; **Downs** = **Australia**.
**Steppes** separate **Cold Asia from Dry Asia** (**APPSC G1 2022**).
⚠ **Campos** = **Brazil** (tropical); **Llanos** = Venezuela (tropical).

20.s: Which one of the following statements about savanna vegetation is correct?
o: It consists exclusively of mosses and lichens over permafrost.
It is dominated by spruce, fir and pine in acidic podzol soils.
It includes elephant grass, guinea grass, baobab and acacia, and is naturally fire-prone.
It is composed mainly of olives and citrus receiving winter rain.
20.x: Savanna vegetation includes tall grasses such as elephant and guinea grass, along with baobab and acacia; it is naturally prone to fire.
20.tq: Use the vegetation list and ecological adaptation to identify the savanna.
xs: Savanna has **elephant grass, guinea grass, baobab and acacia** and is **naturally fire-prone** — option **(3)**.
Mosses over permafrost = **tundra**; spruce/fir in podzol = **taiga**; olives and citrus = **Mediterranean**.
xa: Savanna fauna: **wildebeest, zebra, giraffe**.
Climate: **wet summer, dry winter**; tall grass with scattered trees.
**Masai** (Kenya, Tanzania) are savanna herders.

20.s: The United Nations has declared 2026 as the International Year for:
20.x: The UN declared 2026 the International Year for Rangelands and Pastoralists. Rangelands (grasslands, savannas, shrublands) cover about half of Earth's land. The other options are not the 2026 theme.
20.tq: 2026 = Rangelands and Pastoralists.
xs: The UN declared **2026** the **International Year for Rangelands and Pastoralists** — option **(2)**.
Rangelands (**grasslands, savannas, shrublands**) cover about **half** of Earth's land.
xa: Examples: **Central Asian steppes**, African savanna, **US Great Plains**.
Pastoralist peoples: **Masai** (savanna), **Kirghiz / Kazakh** (steppes).
Steppe rainfall: only **25-50 cm**.

20.s: The lowest temperature ever recorded on Earth is associated with
20.x: Vostok in Antarctica recorded the lowest known temperature, about −89.2°C. Oymyakon and Verkhoyansk are associated with the cold pole among inhabited places.
20.tq: Separate the absolute recorded extreme from the coldest inhabited locations.
xs: The lowest recorded temperature is at **Vostok, Antarctica** — **-89.2 degC** — option **(4)**.
**Oymyakon / Verkhoyansk** are the **cold pole** for **inhabited** places; **Death Valley** is the hottest; **Mawsynram** the wettest.
xa: Hottest: **Death Valley**, **56.7 deg C** (**1913**).
India lowest: **-45 deg C at Dras** (**1908**).
⚠ Hottest = Death Valley (not **Al Aziziya**); coldest = **Vostok**.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the exceptional rainfall of Mawsynram and Cherrapunji?
o: Funnelling of moist air and orographic lifting
Cold currents and subtropical high pressure
20.x: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji receive more than 1,100 cm of annual rainfall because moist air is funnelled and forced to rise over the terrain.
20.tq: Link the climatic extreme to the physical mechanism producing it.
xs: **Funnelling** of moist air and **orographic lifting** explain their rainfall — option **(3)**.
**Mawsynram and Cherrapunji** get **over 1,100 cm** a year; descending air and rain-shadow would make them dry.
xa: **Mawsynram** (Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) — mean **1,187 cm**, the wettest place.
**Relief**: windward slopes wet, leeward rain-shadow dry.
Driest in the world: **Atacama**; in India: **Ruyli, Jaisalmer** (**8.33 cm**).

20.s: The Atacama Desert is regarded as one of the driest regions of the world and is located in
o: central Australia, west of the Great Dividing Range
southern Argentina, east of the Andes
the interior of the Arabian Peninsula
northern Chile, west of the Andes
20.x: The Atacama Desert lies in northern Chile, west of the Andes, and is recognised for extreme aridity.
20.tq: Combine the climatic superlative with the correct location.
xs: The **Atacama** Desert lies in **northern Chile, west of the Andes** — option **(4)**.
It is the world's **driest** place.
xa: Hot deserts lie at **15-30 deg** on **western margins** — subtropical high, offshore trade winds, **cold currents**.
India's driest: **Ruyli, Jaisalmer** (**8.33 cm**) in the Thar.
Wettest: **Mawsynram**, mean **1,187 cm**.

20.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Ganganagar — approximately 50°C in 1935
2. Dras — approximately −45°C in 1908
3. Ruyli, Jaisalmer — about 8.33 cm annual rainfall
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
20.x: All three pairs are correct. Ganganagar represents India’s highest noted temperature, Dras its lowest noted temperature, and Ruyli its driest location in the cited records.
20.tq: Verify each numerical place–record pair before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three pairs are correct — option **(4)**.
India highest: ~**50 deg C at Ganganagar** (**1935**); lowest: **-45 deg C at Dras** (**1908**).
India driest: **Ruyli, Jaisalmer** (**8.33 cm**) a year, in the Thar.
xa: ⚠ India lowest = **Dras**, highest = **Ganganagar**.
World: hottest **Death Valley** (**56.7 deg C**); lowest **Vostok** (**-89.2 degC**).
Wettest: **Mawsynram** (mean **1,187 cm**).

20.s: The highest air temperature ever recorded on Earth, 56.7 °C (1913), is associated with:
20.x: Death Valley in California holds the record of 56.7 °C (1913); the WMO rejected Al Aziziya, Libya. Ganganagar's ~50 °C (1935) is India's highest, and the Atacama is the driest place, not the hottest.
20.tq: Hottest = Death Valley (Al Aziziya rejected).
xs: The **56.7 °C** (**1913**) record belongs to **Death Valley, California** — option **(2)**.
The **WMO rejected Al Aziziya, Libya**; **Ganganagar** (~**50**, **1935**) is India's highest; the **Atacama** is the driest place.
xa: ⚠ Hottest = Death Valley; coldest = **Vostok** (**-89.2**).
Cold pole for inhabited places: **Verkhoyansk / Oymyakon**, Siberia.

20.s: The Kirghiz and Kazakh peoples are traditionally associated with the
20.x: The Kirghiz and Kazakh peoples are associated with the grasslands and steppes of Central Asia.
20.tq: Use the natural-region association to distinguish steppe peoples from desert and tundra groups.
xs: The **Kirghiz and Kazakh** are peoples of the **Central Asian steppes** — option **(4)**.
Greenland tundra = **Inuit**; Kalahari = **Bushmen (San)**; Congo forest = **Pygmies**.
xa: Steppes separate **Cold Asia from Dry Asia** (APPSC G1 **2022**).
Steppe climate: hot summers, chilly winters, rain **25-50 cm**.
**Yakuts** live in Siberia (taiga/Arctic).

20.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
20.x: The Yakuts are associated with Siberia and the taiga or Arctic environment. The Tuareg are associated with the Sahara, while the Bedouin are associated with Arabia and the Sahara.
20.tq: Start from the complete three-part match and reject swapped environments.
xs: **Yakuts — Siberia — Taiga/Arctic** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Tuareg** belong to the **Sahara** (hot desert); **Bedouin** to **Arabia, Sahara**; **Kirghiz** to **Central Asian steppes**.
xa: **Sami (Lapps)**: Scandinavia, tundra; **Inuit**: Canada, Alaska, Greenland.
**Bushmen (San)**: Kalahari (Botswana, Namibia).
Taiga (Siberian) climate: **long severe winter, short cool summer**, very large annual range.

20.s:
Match List-I (Climatic description) with List-II (Climate type):
List-I
(a) Very small annual range (2-3°C), rain every month
(b) Hot wet summer, long dry winter
(c) Very hot, very large daily range, rain below 25 cm
(d) Long severe winter, short cool summer, very large annual range
List-II
(i) Hot desert
(ii) Taiga (Siberian)
(iii) Equatorial
(iv) Savanna / monsoon
20.x: A tiny annual range with rain every month is equatorial; a hot wet summer with a long dry winter is savanna or monsoon; extreme heat, a large daily range and under 25 cm of rain is hot desert; a long severe winter, short cool summer and very large annual range is the Siberian taiga. So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii. The other codes swap equatorial with savanna, desert with taiga, or savanna with desert.
20.tq: Small range = equator; huge annual range = Siberia; huge daily range = desert.
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Very small annual range (**2-3 degC**), rain every month = **Equatorial**; hot wet summer, long dry winter = **Savanna / monsoon**.
Very hot, large daily range, rain below **25 cm** = **Hot desert**; long severe winter, very large annual range = **Taiga (Siberian)**.
xa: **Warm dry summer, mild wet winter** = **Mediterranean**.
Equatorial: rain **almost daily** (afternoon convectional rain).
Savanna: **wet summer, dry winter**; tall grass with scattered trees.

20.s:
Match List-I (People) with List-II (Natural region):

List-I
a. Masai
b. Pygmies
c. Bushmen (San)
d. Inuit

List-II
i. Kalahari hot desert
ii. Arctic tundra
iii. Savanna of Kenya and Tanzania
iv. Equatorial forest of the Congo basin

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
20.x: The Masai are herders of the Kenya-Tanzania savanna, the Pygmies hunter-gatherers of the Congo equatorial forest, the Bushmen (San) live in the Kalahari desert, and the Inuit in the Arctic tundra. The other codes swap Masai with Pygmies, Bushmen with Inuit, or Masai with Bushmen.
20.tq: Masai-savanna; Pygmies-Congo; San-Kalahari; Inuit-tundra.
xs: Correct match: **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Masai** — savanna of **Kenya, Tanzania**; **Pygmies** — **equatorial forest** of the Congo basin.
**Bushmen (San)** — **Kalahari** hot desert; **Inuit** — **Arctic tundra**.
xa: ⚠ **Masai** = savanna; **Pygmies** = equatorial forest; **Bushmen** = Kalahari.
**Bedouin** and **Tuareg** — hot deserts; **Sami** — tundra.
**Yakuts** — Siberia (taiga/Arctic).

20.s: Magnetic minerals preserved in the sediments of Bakhira Lake are significant because they provide a record of Indian monsoon variability extending approximately:
20.x: Magnetic minerals in Bakhira Lake sediments provide an approximately 25,000-year record of Indian monsoon variability.
20.tq: Use the distinctive large-number recall technique.
xs: **Bakhira Lake** sediments give a record of Indian monsoon variability spanning about **25,000 years** — option **(3)**.
The record comes from **magnetic minerals** in the lake sediments.
xa: Bakhira Lake is in **UP**.
IMD SW monsoon normal: **868.6 mm** (**1971-2020** base).
About **40** coastal districts may warm by over **1** degC by **2040**.

20.s: Which statement correctly describes the geographical and climatic setting of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It lies between 19°07′ N and 25°41′ N and is classified as E/ET.
It lies between 8°41′ N and 15°07′ N and is classified as Amw.
It lies entirely north of 20° N and is classified as BWhw.
It lies between 12°41′ N and 19°07′ N and is classified as Aw, or tropical wet and dry climate.
20.x: Andhra Pradesh extends from 12°41′ N to 19°07′ N and is classified as Aw, representing a tropical wet and dry climate.
20.tq: Combine latitude limits with the correct Koeppen code and reject reversed ranges.
xs: AP lies between **12°41′ N and 19°07′ N** and is Koeppen **Aw** (**tropical wet and dry**) — option **(4)**.
**E/ET** is polar/tundra, **Amw** the west coast south of Goa, and **BWhw** extreme western Rajasthan.
xa: AP's four climatic regions: **humid coastal, deltaic, semi-arid Rayalaseema, hill micro-climates**.
Hill micro-climates: **Araku, Lambasingi, Horsley Hills**.
AP has **six agro-climatic zones**; India **15**.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four climatic regions identified in Andhra Pradesh?
20.x: The four regions are humid coastal, deltaic, semi-arid Rayalaseema and hill micro-climates. Ladakh is not an Andhra Pradesh climatic region.
20.tq: Find the geographically misplaced regional description.
xs: A **cold snow-forest region of Ladakh** is not one of AP's climatic regions — option **(2)**.
AP's four: **humid coastal**, **deltaic**, **semi-arid Rayalaseema**, **hill micro-climates** (Araku, Lambasingi, Horsley Hills).
"Cold snow-forest" is Koeppen group **D** (coldest month below **-3 degC**).
xa: AP extent: **12 deg 41' N** to **19 deg 07' N**.
AP is predominantly **Aw**.
**Six** agro-climatic zones in AP (older books say seven).

20.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the number of agro-climatic zones in Andhra Pradesh and India?
o: Andhra Pradesh has fifteen, while India has six.
Andhra Pradesh has four, while India has fifteen.
Andhra Pradesh has six, while India has fifteen.
Both Andhra Pradesh and India have seven.
20.x: The current figures stated are six agro-climatic zones for Andhra Pradesh and fifteen for India.
20.tq: Use the direction of comparison to avoid interchanging state and national figures.
xs: AP has **six** agro-climatic zones, while India has **fifteen (15)** — option **(3)**.
Older books say AP has **seven**; **four** is the number of AP's **climatic regions**, not agro-climatic zones.
xa: AP's six zones are listed against the **13 pre-2022 districts**.
Four climatic regions: humid coastal, deltaic, semi-arid **Rayalaseema**, hill micro-climates.
AP is Koeppen **Aw**.

20.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the global ocean climate in 2025:
1. Oceans held more than 90% of the excess heat.
2. Approximately 90% of the ocean surface experienced marine heatwaves.
3. Less than 10% of the excess heat was held by the oceans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the oceans held more than 90%, not less than 10%, of the excess heat.
20.tq: Spot the numerical reversal in the false statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 correct: oceans held **>90%** of excess heat (WMO State of the Global Climate **2025**).
Statement 2 correct: ~**90%** of the ocean surface saw **marine heatwaves** in 2025.
Statement 3 wrong: it contradicts statement 1 — oceans held more than 90%, not less than **10%**.
xa: About **40** coastal districts may warm by over **1** degC by **2040**.
**Bakhira Lake** (UP) holds a **25,000-year** monsoon record.
Cold currents make tropical west coasts arid; warm currents make east coasts warm and rainy.

20.s:
Which of the following are elements of climate rather than factors (controls) of climate?
1. Cloudiness
2. Sunshine or insolation
3. Jet streams
4. Ocean currents
5. Temperature range
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
20.x: Cloudiness, temperature range and sunshine (insolation) are elements of climate, the conditions that are measured, along with temperature, pressure, wind, humidity and precipitation. Ocean currents and jet streams (with latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, pressure and wind systems, relief and vegetation) are factors or controls that shape those elements. So 1, 2 and 5 only; the other codes include a control (2 or 4) or list only controls.
20.tq: Element = what you measure; factor = what causes it.
xs: **Cloudiness**, **sunshine/insolation** and **temperature range** are elements — option **(1)** is correct.
Elements of climate: **temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, cloudiness, precipitation, insolation, temperature range**.
**Jet streams** and **ocean currents** are **factors (controls)** of climate.
xa: Other controls: **latitude**, **altitude**, **distance from the sea**, **relief**, **vegetation**.
⚠ **Distance from a river** is **not** a control of climate (**APPSC GS 2025**).
**Climate** = average weather over **30 years** (WMO); **weather** = one place and time.

20.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Antarctica is the world’s largest desert by cold-desert classification.
Statement B: The Sahara is the world’s largest hot desert.

Which of the following is correct?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
20.x: Both are true: Antarctica is the largest desert, a cold one, and the Sahara the largest hot desert.
20.tq: Discriminate cold from hot deserts.
n: Antarctica is the world’s largest desert by cold-desert classification. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
The Sahara is the world’s largest hot desert. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Antarctica** is the **world's largest desert** by **cold-desert classification**.
The **Sahara** is the **world's largest hot desert**.
xa: **Driest place:** the **Atacama Desert**, northern Chile.
**Driest polar region:** the **McMurdo Dry Valleys**.
**Lowest recorded:** **Vostok (Antarctica), -89.2 degC**.

20.s:
Assertion (A): The McMurdo Dry Valleys of Antarctica are among the driest places on Earth.
Reason (R): The Atacama Desert is the driest non-polar desert.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
20.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the Atacama's record among non-polar deserts is separate from the extreme dryness of Antarctica's McMurdo Dry Valleys, caused by katabatic winds and mountains blocking ice.
20.tq: Keep polar and non-polar dryness records apart.
n: The Atacama Desert is the driest place on Earth. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The McMurdo Dry Valleys are the driest polar region. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A is true: the **McMurdo Dry Valleys** are the **driest polar region**.
R is true: the **Atacama Desert** is the driest place (non-polar) — a separate fact that does not explain A.
xa: Atacama lies in **northern Chile**, west of the **Andes**.
**Hottest recorded:** **Furnace Creek**, **Death Valley** (**56.7 deg C**, **1913**).
**Wettest:** **Mawsynram**, Meghalaya — mean **1,187 cm**.

20.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Congo Basin
(b) Siberia, Canada and Scandinavia
(c) Western Europe and Eastern USA
(d) Mediterranean lands

List-II
(i) Tropical Rainforest
(ii) Taiga or Boreal Forest
(iii) Temperate Deciduous Forest
(iv) Mediterranean Forest
20.x: The Congo Basin has tropical rainforest, Siberia, Canada and Scandinavia the taiga, western Europe and the eastern USA temperate deciduous forest and Mediterranean lands Mediterranean forest, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
20.tq: Recall the forest type of each region.
n: The Congo Basin is the second-largest tropical rainforest. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests are also called Taiga forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests are also called boreal forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests occur in Canada. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests occur in Scandinavia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests occur in Siberia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate deciduous forests occur in the eastern United States. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate deciduous forests occur in Western Europe. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mediterranean forests occur in Mediterranean lands. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mediterranean forests occur in the Mediterranean Basin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Congo Basin** = **tropical rainforest**; **Siberia, Canada, Scandinavia** = **taiga/boreal**.
**Western Europe, Eastern USA** = **temperate deciduous**; **Mediterranean lands** = **Mediterranean forest**.
xa: Mediterranean forests also in **California**, **Central Chile**, **SW Australia**, **Cape Province**.
**Mangroves** (tidal forests): **Sundarbans** and coastal tropics.
**Tropical deciduous** (monsoon) forests: **India, Africa, Myanmar, SE Asia**.

20.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The taiga is often described as the world's largest terrestrial biome.
II. Selva forests are characterised by broadleaf evergreen trees.
III. Mangrove forests are coastal, saline and tidal forests.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: All three are correct: the taiga or boreal forest is called the largest land biome, selvas are broadleaf evergreen rainforests and mangroves are coastal tidal forests.
20.tq: Recall the features of each forest type.
n: The highest percentage of the world’s forest area by type is represented by temperate coniferous forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Tropical rainforests are also called Selva forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Tropical rainforests have broadleaf evergreen trees. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mangrove forests are also called tidal forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mangrove forests occur in coastal, saline, tidal environments. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mangrove forests contain salt-tolerant trees. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mangrove forests occur in coastal tropical regions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
xs: All three statements **I, II and III** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
I: **taiga is the largest land biome**.
II: **Selva** (tropical rainforest) has **broadleaf evergreen trees**.
III: **mangroves** are **coastal, saline, tidal** forests.
xa: Mangroves have **salt-tolerant trees** with **pneumatophores**.
Taiga = **needle-leaved evergreen softwood** trees of **conical shape**.
Rainforests: **more than 200 cm** rainfall, **multilayered canopy**.

20.s:
Which of the following are characteristics of tropical rainforests?
1. They receive more than 200 cm of rainfall.
2. They have hot and humid conditions.
20.x: Both are correct: tropical rainforests get over 200 cm of rain a year and stay hot and humid throughout, giving an equatorial climate.
20.tq: Check each feature against the equatorial climate.
n: Tropical rainforests receive more than 200 cm of rainfall. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Tropical rainforests have hot and humid conditions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
xs: **Both 1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
Tropical rainforests get **more than 200 cm** of rainfall.
They are **equatorial**, **hot and humid**.
xa: They have **nutrient-poor soil** and **rapid decomposition**.
Found in the **Amazon Basin**, **Congo Basin**, **Indonesia**, **SE Asia**.
⚠ Other notes give rainforest rain as **50-260 inches**.

20.s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Canopy structure of tropical rainforests
(b) Plant forms found in tropical rainforests
(c) Decomposition in tropical rainforests

List-II
(i) Rapid
(ii) Climbers and epiphytes
(iii) Multilayered canopy
20.x: Rainforests have a multilayered canopy, many climbers and epiphytes, and rapid decomposition, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-i.
20.tq: Recall the features of rainforests.
n: Tropical rainforests have a multilayered canopy. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Tropical rainforests contain climbers and epiphytes. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Tropical rainforests have rapid decomposition. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-ii, c-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Rainforest canopy = **multilayered**; plant forms = **climbers and epiphytes**.
**Decomposition** is **rapid**.
xa: Soil is **nutrient-poor** despite dense growth.
Trees: **broadleaf evergreen** hardwoods (**mahogany, ebony**).
Rainforests hold **over half** of all known species.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about temperate forests:
1. Temperate deciduous forests have broadleaf trees that shed their leaves in autumn.
2. Temperate coniferous forests occur in Canada, Scandinavia, Russia and Alaska.
3. Temperate deciduous forests occur in the eastern United States, Western Europe and East Asia.
4. Temperate coniferous (taiga) forests consist of broadleaf hardwood trees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: temperate deciduous forests are broadleaf trees shedding leaves in autumn in the eastern USA, Western Europe and East Asia, and the taiga covers Canada, Scandinavia, Russia, Siberia and Alaska. Statement 4 is wrong: coniferous trees are needle-leaved evergreen softwoods of conical shape. So '1 and 3 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 4 are wrong.
20.tq: Conifer = needle-leaved, conical, softwood.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
1 and 3: **temperate deciduous** forests have **broadleaf trees** shedding leaves in **autumn** — **eastern US, Western Europe, East Asia**.
2: **temperate coniferous** forests occur in **Canada, Scandinavia, Russia, Alaska**.
4 is wrong: conifers are **needle-leaved evergreen softwood** trees of **conical shape**.
xa: Taiga also called **boreal** forest; **cold-temperate**, **long winters**.
Temperate deciduous trees: **oak, beech, maple, birch**.
Taiga soils are acidic **podzol**.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about Mediterranean forests:
I. They have hot, dry summers.
II. They have mild, wet winters.
III. They contain evergreen shrubs.
IV. They contain oaks.
V. They contain cork trees.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
II, III, IV and V only

20.s:

20.s: The Samoyed or Nenets groups traditionally inhabit which of the following regions?

The mountainous rainforest interiors of Luzon

20.s:
Consider the following statements:

n: Chukchi is grouped with Koryak in the notes. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]

Chukchi or Koryak communities inhabit tundra regions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]

20.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Afridi?

A Pashtun tribal group associated with Pakistan and South Asia
An Orang Asli community associated with Malaysia
An Indigenous Negrito group associated with the Philippines

n: Afridi are a Pashtun tribal group. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Afridi are associated with Pakistan and South Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
xs: The Afridi are **a Pashtun tribal group associated with Pakistan and South Asia** — option **(2)**.

20.s:

20.s:

20.s: Which of the following characteristics is associated with the Yakuts?

21.s:
Consider the following statements about recent global temperature records:
1. The years 2015-2025 are the eleven warmest years on record.
2. 2024 was the hottest year on record, about 1.55°C above pre-industrial.
3. 2025 was the warmest El Niño year on record.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
21.x: Statement 2 is correct: 2024 was the hottest year, about 1.55°C above pre-industrial. Statement 1 is correct: 2015-2025 are the 11 warmest years (WMO 2025). Statement 3 is wrong: 2025 (about 1.43°C) was the warmest La Niña year on record, not El Niño. So '2 only' misses statement 1, and options with statement 3 are wrong.
21.tq: 2024 hottest (1.55); 2025 warmest La Niña (1.43).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **2015-2025** are the **11 warmest years** (**WMO State of the Global Climate 2025**).
Statement 2 is correct: **2024** was the **hottest year**, about **1.55 degC** above pre-industrial.
Statement 3 is wrong: **2025** (**~1.43 degC**) was the **warmest La Nina year**, not El Niño.
xa: **India** warmed about **0.7 degC since 1900** vs **1.59 degC** for global land.
**Gangotri** retreated about **1,700 m since 1935** (**APPSC G2 2025**).
**Sea level** is up about **11 cm since 1993**.
Earth's **energy imbalance** is at a **65-year peak**.

xa: **Gangotri** glacier has retreated about **1,700 m since 1935** (APPSC G2 2025).
**2024** was the hottest year on record at about **1.55 degC** above pre-industrial.

xs: **Gangotri Glacier** has retreated about **1,700 m since 1935** — option **(3)**.

xa: **Sea level** has risen about **11 cm since 1993**.
**WMO 2025:** **Arctic** sea ice near record lows; **Antarctic** sea ice **3rd lowest**.
Earth's **energy imbalance** is at a **65-year peak**.

21.s: According to the global temperature record (as of February 2026), the year 2019 ranks as the:

2019 lies within the **11 warmest years (2015-2025)**, and being seventh it is not the coldest of that period.
xa: This fact was asked in **APPSC GS 2019**.

21.s:
With reference to evidence of global warming, consider the following statements:
1. Global sea level has risen by about 11 cm since 1993.
2. According to WMO 2025, Arctic sea ice is near record lows.
3. According to WMO 2025, Antarctic sea ice is at its highest extent on record.

21.x: Statement 1 is correct: sea level is up about 11 cm since 1993. Statement 2 is correct: WMO 2025 puts Arctic sea ice near record lows. Statement 3 is wrong: Antarctic sea ice was the 3rd lowest, not the highest. So 1 and 2 only; option A misses statement 2, and C and D include the false statement 3.
21.tq: Both poles low: Arctic near record low, Antarctic 3rd lowest.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **sea level** is up about **11 cm since 1993**.
Statement 2 is correct: **WMO 2025** puts **Arctic** sea ice **near record lows**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Antarctic** sea ice was the **3rd lowest**, not the highest.
xa: **Gangotri** has retreated about **1,700 m since 1935**.
Earth's **energy imbalance** is at a **65-year peak**.
Sea-level rise comes from **thermal expansion** plus **ice melt**; **Kiribati** and **Tuvalu** are at risk.

21.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Precession — wobble of the rotational axis
21.x: Precession refers to the wobble of Earth’s axis. Eccentricity concerns orbital shape and obliquity concerns axial tilt.
21.tq: Separate the three easily confusable components of the Milankovitch cycles.
xs: **Precession** is the **wobble** of the rotational axis — option **(3)** is correctly matched.
**Eccentricity** is the **orbit shape**, not axial tilt; **Obliquity** is the **axial tilt**, not orbit shape.
**Milankovitch cycles** drive **ice-age cycles**; volcanic ash is a separate natural cause.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Eccentricity = shape**, **Obliquity = tilt**, **Precession = wobble**.
**Volcanoes:** **SO2 + ash** act as **cooling aerosols**.
The **Little Ice Age** lasted about **1500-1850**.

21.s: The Little Ice Age is generally placed approximately between:
21.x: The Little Ice Age is placed approximately in the period 1500–1850.
21.tq: Use the historical range as the discriminator among overlapping climate periods.
xs: The **Little Ice Age** is placed about **1500-1850** — option **(3)**.
It is listed among the **natural** variations of climate.
xa: **Milankovitch cycles** (eccentricity, obliquity, precession) drive **ice-age cycles**.
**Volcanoes** cool climate through **SO2 + ash** aerosols.
**Continental drift** and **ocean currents** are other natural causes.

21.s:
Consider the following statements about solar output and recent global warming:
1. Satellite observations since 1978 show no net increase in solar output.
2. Recent warming can therefore not be explained by an increasing solar output.
3. Satellite observations establish that solar output has continuously declined since 1978.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The evidence indicates no net increase, not a continuous decline, in solar output since 1978.
21.tq: Reject the stronger but unsupported word ‘continuously’ in the third statement.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **satellites since 1978** show **no net increase** in solar output.
Statement 2 is correct: hence the **sun does not explain recent warming**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the record shows **no net increase**, not a continuous decline.
xa: **Milankovitch cycles** (orbital factors) drive **ice-age cycles**.
**Volcanoes:** **SO2 + ash** act as **cooling aerosols**.
IPCC **AR6**: warming had already reached **1.1 degC** in **2011-2020**.

21.s: Volcanic eruptions can produce a short-term cooling effect mainly because:
o: Volcanic gases permanently remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
Sulphur dioxide and ash form aerosols that reflect sunlight
Volcanic dust increases the absorption of solar radiation by the surface
Lava directly lowers ocean temperatures worldwide
21.x: Sulphur dioxide and ash generate cooling aerosols that reflect incoming sunlight.
21.tq: Connect the natural event with its atmospheric mechanism and radiative effect.
xs: **Sulphur dioxide and ash** form **aerosols that reflect sunlight** — option **(2)**.
The notes list **volcanoes** as a natural cause whose **SO2 + ash** act as **cooling aerosols**.
**Stratospheric aerosol injection** copies this **volcanic cooling** by forming **sulphuric-acid aerosols**.
xa: Its risk is **"termination shock"** — **rapid warming** if injection stops.
Other natural causes: **Milankovitch cycles**, **solar output**, **continental drift**, **ocean currents**.
**Little Ice Age:** about **1500-1850**.

21.s:

2. It conducts original climate research as its principal activity.
3. It assesses the existing scientific literature on climate change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: The IPCC has 195 members and assesses available scientific literature. It does not conduct research of its own as its principal activity.
21.tq: Separate the assessment function from the research function before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **IPCC** has **195 members**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it **does no research of its own**.
Statement 3 is correct: it **assesses** the existing **literature**.
xa: It shared the **Nobel Peace Prize 2007** with **Al Gore**.
**WG I** physical science basis; **WG II** impacts, adaptation, vulnerability; **WG III** mitigation.
The **AR7** cycle began in **July 2023**.

21.s: The Nobel Peace Prize awarded to the IPCC in 2007 was shared with which of the following persons?
21.x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.

xs: The IPCC shared the **Nobel Peace Prize 2007** with **Al Gore** — option **(2)**.
The IPCC itself **assesses** literature and does **no research of its own**.
xa: IPCC membership: **195**.

21.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (IPCC Working Group)
A. Working Group I
B. Working Group II
C. Working Group III

List-II (Subject)
1. Mitigation
2. Physical science basis

21.s:
Consider the following statements about the IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C (SR1.5):
1. It was published in 2018.
2. It stated that, at the current rate, warming is likely to reach 1.5°C between 2030 and 2052.
3. It stated that limiting warming to 1.5°C requires global CO2 emissions to fall about 45% from 2010 levels by 2050.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
21.x: Statement 1 is correct: SR1.5 came out in 2018. Statement 2 is correct: it put the 1.5°C crossing between 2030 and 2052 at the current rate. Statement 3 is wrong: the 45% cut from 2010 levels is needed by 2030; 2050 is the date for net zero. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses the true statement 2, and C and D include the false statement 3.
21.tq: SR1.5: 45% cut by 2030, net zero around 2050 — watch for the two dates being swapped.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **SR1.5** was published in **2018**.
Statement 2 is correct: warming likely reaches **1.5 degC between 2030 and 2052** at the current rate (APPSC GS 2022).
Statement 3 is wrong: the **45%** cut from **2010** levels is needed **by 2030**; **2050** is the date for **net zero**.
xa: ⚠ **SR1.5** = 1.5 degC between **2030 and 2052**; **AR6** = breach in the **early 2030s**.
**AR6** says emissions must **peak before 2025**.
**Net zero:** human emissions balanced by **removals** (sinks, capture).

21.s: In the context of climate policy, 'net zero' means that:
o: All greenhouse-gas emissions are stopped permanently.
Natural emissions are completely eliminated from the atmosphere.
Human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through sinks or capture.
Only carbon dioxide emissions are reduced to zero without removals.
21.x: Net zero is achieved when human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through natural sinks or technological capture, resulting in zero net addition.
21.tq: Apply the definition to distinguish net emissions from gross emissions.
xs: **Net zero** means **human-caused emissions** are **balanced by removals** through sinks or capture — option **(3)**.
The net addition to the atmosphere becomes **zero**; emissions need not stop entirely, so (1) is wrong.
xa: **SR1.5:** to limit warming to 1.5 degC, net zero is needed **around 2050**.
**SR1.5:** global CO2 must fall about **45%** from **2010** levels by **2030**.
**AR6:** emissions must **peak before 2025**, with **net zero by mid-century**.

21.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) Synthesis Report:
1. It was released on 20 March 2023.
2. Warming during 2011–2020 had already reached about 1.1°C.
3. It indicated that 1.5°C warming is likely to be breached in the early 2030s.
4. It stated that emissions may peak after 2035 without affecting the mid-century net-zero objective.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. AR6 indicated that emissions must peak before 2025; therefore statement 4 is incorrect.
21.tq: Find the single time-related reversal in the final statement.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **AR6 Synthesis Report** came out on **20 March 2023**.
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: warming had reached **1.1 degC** (**2011-2020**), and **1.5 degC** is likely breached in the **early 2030s**.
Statement 4 is wrong: AR6 says emissions must **peak before 2025**, with **net zero by mid-century**.
xa: ⚠ **SR1.5** (2018) gave **2030-2052** for reaching 1.5 degC; **AR6** gives the **early 2030s**.
**AR7** cycle began **July 2023**.
**AR6** also warns up to **25%** of mountain species face extinction.

21.s:
Consider the following statements about the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025:
1. Current policies would lead to about 2.8°C of warming.
2. Emissions must fall 35% (for 2°C) and 55% (for 1.5°C) by 2035 from 2019 levels.
3. Full implementation of NDCs would keep warming below 1.5°C.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
21.x: Statement 1 is correct: current policies point to about 2.8°C. Statement 2 is correct: cuts of 35% (2°C) and 55% (1.5°C) by 2035 from 2019 levels are needed. Statement 3 is wrong: full NDCs still give about 2.3-2.5°C, and a 1.5°C overshoot is very likely this decade. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 3 are wrong.
21.tq: Gap 2025: 2.8 current policy; 2.3-2.5 with NDCs.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: under **current policies** warming reaches **~2.8 degC**.
Statement 2 is correct: emissions must fall **35% (2 degC)** / **55% (1.5 degC)** by **2035** from **2019** levels.
Statement 3 is wrong: **full NDCs** still give **2.3-2.5 degC**; overshoot of **1.5 degC** is "very likely" this decade.
xa: **SR1.5** (**2018**): **1.5 degC** likely between **2030 and 2052**; **net zero around 2050**.
**AR6** (**20 March 2023**): warming already **1.1 degC**; 1.5 degC breach in the **early 2030s**; emissions must **peak before 2025**.
**COP31** meets in **Turkiye** in **November 2026**.

21.s: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2021 was awarded in part to which scientists for the physical modelling of Earth's climate?
21.x: Syukuro Manabe and Klaus Hasselmann shared the 2021 Physics Nobel (with Giorgio Parisi) for physical modelling of Earth's climate. Al Gore shared the 2007 Peace Prize with the IPCC, and Pachauri chaired the IPCC; Hansen, Mann, Arrhenius and Keeling are climate scientists who did not receive this prize.
21.tq: 2021 Physics = Manabe + Hasselmann (+ Parisi).
xs: **Syukuro Manabe and Klaus Hasselmann** won the **Nobel Prize in Physics 2021** for **physical modelling of Earth's climate** — option **(2)**.
They shared it with **Giorgio Parisi**.
**Al Gore** shared the **Nobel Peace Prize 2007** with the IPCC — a different prize.
xa: The **IPCC** has **195 members** and **assesses** literature.
IPCC **WG I** covers the **physical science basis**.

21.s:
Which of the following is a direct physical cause of sea-level rise associated with climate change?
1. Thermal expansion of seawater
2. Melting of ice
3. Increased snow albedo
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
