28.s:
The 2009 National Policy on Disaster Management emphasised which of the following?
1. Prevention and mitigation
2. Community participation
3. Mainstreaming disaster risk reduction
4. Exclusive dependence on post-disaster relief
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
28.x: The 2009 policy emphasised prevention, mitigation, community participation and mainstreaming disaster risk reduction. Exclusive dependence on post-disaster relief is contrary to this approach.
28.tq: Identify the policy-oriented statements and reject the extreme ‘exclusive’ approach.
xs: The **2009 NPDM** stressed **prevention, mitigation, community** and **mainstreaming DRR** — option **(2) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statement 4 is wrong: India's policy moved **away from relief-centric** response, so exclusive dependence on post-disaster relief contradicts it.
xa: The **DM Act 2005** made the same shift: **from relief-centric to proactive prevention, mitigation and preparedness**.
Criticism: spending is **still relief-centric** rather than mitigation-focused.
**APSDMA** too moved from **relief-centric to mitigation-centric**.

28.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Body)
a. NDMA
b. NEC
c. SDMA
d. DDMA
List-II (Head)
i. Chief Minister
ii. Union Home Secretary
iii. Prime Minister
iv. District Collector with an elected local representative as co-chairperson
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: NDMA is headed by the Prime Minister, NEC by the Union Home Secretary, SDMA by the Chief Minister, and DDMA by the District Collector with an elected local representative as co-chairperson.
28.tq: Start from the sure pair of NDMA and the Prime Minister, then eliminate incompatible codes.
xs: Correct code: **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**NDMA** — **Prime Minister**; **NEC** — **Union Home Secretary**.
**SDMA** — **Chief Minister**; **DDMA** — **Collector** with an elected local representative as **co-chairperson**.
xa: Sections: NDMA **s.3**, NEC **s.8**, SDMA **s.14**, DDMA **s.25**.
SDMA's State Executive Committee is under the **Chief Secretary**.
**APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister** under the **AP DM Rules 2007**.

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
28.x: NIDM is associated with Section 42. Section 44 deals with the National Disaster Response Force.
28.tq: Find the incorrect statutory section by comparing each body with its legal provision.
xs: **NIDM — Section 44** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
**NIDM** is **s.42**; **s.44** is the **NDRF** (force).
The others are right: **SDMA s.14**, **NDMA s.3**, **NEC s.8**.
xa: Funds: National Disaster Response Fund **s.46**, NDMF **s.47**, SDRF **s.48**.
Plans: hazard-specific **s.35**; Ministry DM Plans **s.37**.

28.s: Which statement regarding the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is correct?
o: It is a force recruited solely from state police departments.
It is a scientific body concerned only with satellite imaging.
It is composed exclusively of elected representatives of affected districts.
It is a specialist force drawn from central paramilitary forces and includes search-and-rescue teams, engineers and dog squads.
28.x: NDRF is a specialist force drawn from central paramilitary forces, with search-and-rescue teams, engineers and dog squads, functioning under the superintendence of NDMA.
28.tq: Choose the option that combines the force’s composition and specialist capabilities precisely.
xs: **NDRF** is a **specialist force** from the **central paramilitary forces**, with **search and rescue teams, engineers, dog squads** — option **(4)**.
It is not from state police, not a satellite body, and not made of elected representatives.
xa: It works under **NDMA superintendence**.
⚠ **NDRF** is both the **Force** and the **Fund** — acronym trap.
Gap: **SDRFs** not yet set up in all states.

28.s: A major institutional gap that can strain the NDRF during simultaneous disasters is that:
o: State Disaster Response Forces are not yet set up in all states
State authorities are prohibited from conducting disaster exercises
The NDRF has no search-and-rescue teams
The NDRF is not linked with any central authority
28.x: SDRFs have not yet been established in all states, increasing pressure on the NDRF when several disasters occur simultaneously.
28.tq: Identify the capacity gap that explains the operational consequence.
xs: **SDRFs are not yet set up in all states** — this strains NDRF in simultaneous disasters — option **(1)**.
NDRF does have **search and rescue teams** and is under **NDMA** superintendence, so options (3) and (4) are false.
xa: Suggested fix: **mandatory SDRFs** + **joint NDRF-SDRF training**.
The **DM (Amendment) Act 2025** makes a **mandatory SDRF** in every state.
Criticism list also notes **SDRFs not raised in all States**.

28.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
28.x: Section 46 relates to the National Disaster Response Fund, whereas the National Disaster Mitigation Fund is provided under Section 47.
28.tq: Find the swapped statutory sections by separating response funds from mitigation funds.
xs: **National Disaster Mitigation Fund — Section 46** is wrong — option **(4)**.
**NDMF** is **s.47**; **s.46** is the **National Disaster Response Fund**; the **SDRF** is **s.48**.
xa: Response funds = **relief**; mitigation funds = **long-term risk reduction**.
**NDMF** projects: **Rs 4,645 crore** approved for **9** states, including AP.
Mitigation funds are **underused**.

28.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF)?
o: It is a fund maintained jointly by PRIs and district administrations
It provides long-term financing exclusively for mitigation projects
It is the first fund used by every State for all local disasters
It is a Central fund that tops up the SDRF during severe calamities
28.x: The NDRF is a Central fund used to supplement or top up the State Disaster Response Fund during severe calamities.
28.tq: Distinguish response funding from long-term mitigation funding.
xs: The **National Disaster Response Fund** is a **central** fund that **tops up the SDRF** in **severe** calamities — option **(4)**.
The **first** fund for relief is the **SDRF**; long-term mitigation is for the **NDMF/SDMF**.
xa: National Disaster Response Fund: **s.46**.
SDRF Centre:State share **75:25** for general states.
⚠ **NDRF** = Force **and** Fund.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF):
1. It is constituted under Section 48 of the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
2. It is the first fund available for relief in notified disasters.
3. In general States, the Centre-State contribution ratio is 75:25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: All three statements are correct: the SDRF is associated with Section 48, serves as the first relief fund for notified disasters, and has a 75:25 Centre-State contribution ratio for general States.
28.tq: Check each fund against its section, purpose and financing ratio.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: SDRF is under **s.48**.
Statement 2: it is the **first fund** for relief in **notified disasters**.
Statement 3: Centre:State **75:25** for general states.
xa: States may use **up to 10% of SDRF** for **state-specific** disasters.
AP got **Rs 277.63 crore** (2025-26) + **Rs 479.01 crore** (2026-27) under SDRF/NDRF.
The **National Disaster Response Fund** tops up the SDRF in severe calamities.

28.s: The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are primarily intended for which purpose?
o: Payment of compensation to members of response forces
Immediate relief in notified disasters only
Financing only post-disaster reconstruction of roads
28.x: The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are intended for long-term risk reduction and mitigation rather than immediate relief alone.
28.tq: Apply the relief-versus-mitigation distinction.
xs: **National/State Disaster Mitigation Funds** are for **long-term risk reduction** — option **(1)**.
Immediate relief is the job of the **response funds** (SDRF/NDRF).
xa: NDMF is under **s.47**; the funds are **underused**.
**NDMF** projects: **Rs 4,645 crore** for **9** states, including AP.
AP allocated **Rs 521.17 crore** under **SDMF/NDMF**.

28.s:
With reference to disaster management funds, consider the following statements:
1. The National Disaster Response Fund and State Disaster Response Fund are meant for relief.
2. The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are meant for mitigation.
3. The abbreviation NDRF may refer both to a response force and to a response fund.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: The response funds support relief, the mitigation funds support mitigation, and NDRF is used for both the National Disaster Response Force and the National Disaster Response Fund.
28.tq: Separate response institutions from response funds and mitigation funds before choosing the combination.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Response** = National/State **Disaster Response Fund** (relief).
Statement 2: **Mitigation** = National/State **Disaster Mitigation Fund**.
Statement 3: **NDRF** is both the **Force** and the **Fund** — acronym trap.
xa: **16th FC** guidelines cover **2026-31**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about notified disasters:
1. The Finance Commission recommends the calamities to be covered and the Ministry of Home Affairs notifies them.
2. Heatwave and lightning are on the notified list.
3. Industrial chemical calamities are on the notified list.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: FC recommends, MHA notifies. Statement 2 is correct: heatwave and lightning are now notified. Statement 3 is wrong: no man-made calamity is notified. So '1 only' misses 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
28.tq: Notified list = natural hazards only; no man-made calamity.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: the **Finance Commission** recommends the calamities; **MHA notifies** them.
Statement 2: **heatwave** and **lightning** are on the list (added for **2026-31**).
Statement 3 wrong: **no man-made calamity** is notified.
xa: The list went from **12 to 14** categories, opening **SDRF/NDRF** and **SDMF** funding.
Others on the list: cyclone, drought, hailstorm, cloudburst, frost/cold wave, earthquake, flood, tsunami, landslide, avalanche, fire, pest attack.
**16th FC** guidelines cover **2026-31**.

28.s:
With reference to disaster management plans, consider the following statements:
1. Hazard-specific plans of the Union ministries are prepared under Section 35.
2. Ministry Disaster Management Plans are prepared under Section 37.
3. Both types of plans are prepared under Section 25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Hazard-specific plans are associated with Section 35 and Ministry Disaster Management Plans with Section 37. Section 25 concerns the DDMA, not these plans.
28.tq: Reject the statement that assigns planning provisions to the section dealing with the district authority.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **hazard-specific plans** are under **Sec 35**.
Statement 2: **Ministry DM Plans** are under **Sec 37**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Sec 25** is the **DDMA**, not these plans.
xa: NDMA's **"Resilient India 2047"** (**Jun 2026**) asks Union ministries for these plans.
NDMA (**s.3**) approves the **National Plan**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about Urban Disaster Management Authorities (UDMAs) under the Disaster Management (Amendment) Act, 2025:
1. A UDMA is headed by the Mayor of the city.
2. They are to be set up in every Municipal Corporation city except Delhi and Chandigarh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 2 is correct: UDMAs cover State capitals and Municipal Corporation cities, except Delhi and Chandigarh. Statement 1 is wrong: a UDMA is headed by the MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER, not the Mayor. Hence 2 only.
28.tq: UDMA head = Municipal Commissioner.
xs: Only **statement 2** is correct — option **(1) 2 only**.
Statement 2 is correct: **UDMAs** come up in every **Municipal Corporation** city **except Delhi and Chandigarh**.
Statement 1 is wrong: a UDMA is headed by the **Municipal Commissioner**, not the Mayor.
xa: The **2025 amendment** gives **statutory status** to the **NCMC** and the **High-Level Committee**.
It creates **national and state disaster databases** for data-driven planning.
It **updates definitions** of **risk** and **resilience**, aligning with **Sendai**.
Prep adds a **mandatory SDRF** in every state.

28.s:
Consider the following as features of the Disaster Management Amendment Act, 2025:
1. Creation of national and state disaster databases
2. Statutory status for the National Crisis Management Committee
3. Mandatory State Disaster Response Fund in every state
4. Strengthening of NDMA powers relating to minimum relief standards and audits
Which of the above are correct?
28.x: All four listed measures are features of the 2025 amendment, including disaster databases, statutory NCMC status, mandatory SDRF and stronger NDMA powers.
28.tq: Treat the option containing all four amendment features as a complete policy package.
xs: All four are features of the **DM (Amendment) Act 2025** — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
It adds **disaster databases**, **statutory status for the NCMC**, a **mandatory SDRF** in every state.
It gives **stronger NDMA powers**: **minimum relief standards, audits**.
xa: **Urban DM Authorities** in every Municipal Corporation city (except **Delhi and Chandigarh**).
Statutory definitions: **risk, resilience, recovery, evacuation**.
UDMAs are headed by the **Municipal Commissioner**.

28.s: Which one of the following is a PRE-DISASTER mitigation measure?
28.x: Retrofitting is undertaken before a disaster to strengthen existing structures and reduce potential damage. Damage assessment, compensation and psychosocial care belong to the post-disaster phase.
28.tq: Classify the measure by the phase in which it is undertaken.
xs: **Retrofitting** of buildings is a **pre-disaster mitigation** measure — option **(2)**.
**Damage assessment**, **compensation** and **psycho-social care** belong to **post-disaster recovery**.
xa: Other mitigation measures: **hazard mapping, embankments, land-use planning, building codes, afforestation**.
**Preparedness**: DM plans, **Aapda Mitra** training, **mock drills**, stockpiles, early warning (**CAP-SACHET**).
Modern view: phases are an **overlapping continuum**, not a line.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding preparedness measures:
1. Mock drills are a component of preparedness.
2. Stockpiling essential materials is a preparedness measure.
3. CAP-SACHET is associated with early warning dissemination.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Mock drills, stockpiles and early warning through CAP-SACHET are all preparedness measures undertaken before a disaster.
28.tq: Test a cluster of related components through coded combinations.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Mock drills** and **stockpiles** are **preparedness** measures.
**CAP-SACHET** is the **early warning** component of preparedness.
xa: **CAP (Common Alerting Protocol)** integrates **public warnings**.
**Aapda Mitra** community volunteers and the **National School Safety Programme** are preparedness tools.
IMD's **MHEW-DSS** (2024) reaches ~**80%** of the population.

28.s:
With reference to the disaster management cycle, consider the following statements:
1. Response includes restoring critical services.
2. Recovery and reconstruction may include compensation and psychosocial care.
3. Modern frameworks regard the phases as a strictly linear sequence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Response includes restoration of critical services, while compensation and psychosocial care are recovery measures. Modern frameworks treat the phases as an overlapping continuum rather than a strictly linear sequence.
28.tq: Use the extreme word ‘strictly’ to identify the incorrect statement.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: **response** includes **restoring critical services** (with rescue, shelter, food, medical aid).
Statement 2: **recovery** includes **compensation** and **psycho-social care**.
Statement 3 wrong: modern view sees phases as an **overlapping continuum**, not a line.
xa: Recovery also covers **damage assessment, livelihoods, "Build Back Better"**.
Response is by **NDRF** and the **armed forces**.
Some notes put response under **post-disaster**.

28.s: In the colour-coded warning system of the India Meteorological Department, the colour ORANGE indicates:
28.x: Green means all well, yellow means be aware, orange means be prepared and red means take action.
28.tq: Discriminate between closely related warning colours and their meanings.
xs: IMD **Orange** = **"Be prepared"** — option **(3)**.
**Green** = all well; **Yellow** = be aware; **Red** = take action.
xa: IMD runs **7 cyclone warning centres**, including **Visakhapatnam**.
**Damini** app gives **lightning** alerts.
IMD's 24-h cyclone track error fell **93 to 74 km** (**2013-2022**).

28.s:
Consider the following safety actions:
1. During a flood: move to higher ground and avoid walking or driving through flowing water.
2. During a cyclone warning: stand under a large tree until the storm passes.
3. Indoors during an earthquake: drop, cover and hold under a strong table, away from windows and staircases.
Which of the actions given above is/are correctly recommended?
28.x: Action 1 is correct: drop, cover, hold under a strong table, away from windows, balconies and staircases. Action 2 is wrong: during a cyclone one must move to a cyclone shelter or safer shelter and never stand under trees or in weak houses. Action 3 is correct: move to higher ground and avoid flowing water. Hence 1 and 3 only.
28.tq: Cyclone: shelter, never trees or the sea.
xs: Actions **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Action 1 is correct: in a **flood**, **move to higher ground** and avoid **flowing water**.
Action 2 is wrong: on a **cyclone warning**, **move to a cyclone shelter**; never stand **under trees** or in weak houses.
Action 3 is correct: indoors in an **earthquake**, **drop, cover, hold under a strong table**, away from windows and staircases.
xa: **Tsunami:** move **inland/uphill** immediately if the **sea recedes suddenly**.
Preparedness tools: **mock drills**, **Aapda Mitra** volunteers, **National School Safety Programme**.
**IMD colour code:** **Green** all well, **Yellow** be aware, **Orange** be prepared, **Red** take action.

28.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a preparedness tool for disaster safety awareness?
o: Encouraging people to enter flowing floodwater during exercises
28.x: Mock drills, Aapda Mitra volunteers and tsunami escape-route signage are preparedness tools; entering flowing floodwater is unsafe and is not a preparedness measure.
28.tq: Find the unsafe practice among recognised preparedness and awareness measures.
xs: **Encouraging people to enter flowing floodwater** is not a preparedness tool; it is unsafe, so option **(2)** is the answer.
The listed preparedness tools are **mock drills**, **Aapda Mitra** community volunteers, the **National School Safety Programme**, **tsunami escape-route signage** and awareness campaigns.
xa: Safe flood behaviour: move to **higher ground** and avoid walking or driving through flowing water.
In the DM cycle, **Preparedness** covers DM plans, training responders (**Aapda Mitra**), mock drills, stockpiles and early warning (**CAP-SACHET**).
**Community-based DRR through PRIs:** **Rs 507.37 crore**, run jointly by **MoPR + NDMA**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tsunami Ready programme in India:
1. It uses 12 indicators, and recognition is renewable every four years.
2. Recognition is verified by a board chaired by the Director General of NDRF.
3. India targets 100 tsunami-ready villages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: 12 indicators, renewable every 4 years. Statement 3 is correct: India targets 100 villages. Statement 2 is wrong: the National Tsunami Ready Recognition Board (MoES) is chaired by the Director, INCOIS. Hence 1 and 3 only.
28.tq: Tsunami Ready board = MoES, chaired by Director INCOIS.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **12 indicators**; recognition renewable every **4 years**.
Statement 2 is wrong: verification is by the **National Tsunami Ready Recognition Board** (**MoES**), chaired by the **Director, INCOIS**.
Statement 3 is correct: India targets **100** tsunami-ready villages.
xa: **INCOIS (Hyderabad)** houses the **Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre** (**2007**).
It alerts within **10 min** and serves **25** countries.
**Community-based DRR through PRIs:** **Rs 507.37 crore**, **20 states**, **81 districts**.

28.s:
Assertion (A): A sudden recession of the sea is treated as a warning sign requiring immediate movement inland or uphill.
Reason (R): A sudden recession of the sea may precede the arrival of a tsunami.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
28.x: Both statements are true, and the possibility that a sudden sea recession precedes a tsunami explains why immediate inland or uphill movement is advised.
28.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the recommended safety action.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes' tsunami drill: **move inland/uphill immediately if the sea recedes suddenly**, because the recession can come before the tsunami wave.
xa: Tsunamis are a **geological** hazard, with earthquakes, landslides and volcanoes.
Tsunami warning in India: **INCOIS, Hyderabad** (Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre, **2007**).
**Tsunami escape-route signage** is one of the listed preparedness tools.
Tsunami-ready villages are verified by the **National Tsunami Ready Recognition Board**, chaired by the **Director, INCOIS**.

28.s: The Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction programme through Panchayati Raj Institutions (Rs 507.37 crore) is jointly run by:
o: Ministry of Panchayati Raj and NDMA
Ministry of Rural Development and NIDM
Ministry of Earth Sciences and INCOIS
28.x: The CBDRR-through-PRIs programme is run jointly by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and NDMA, covering 20 States and 81 districts. The other pairs name bodies with different roles: response force, training, and tsunami warning.
28.tq: CBDRR via PRIs = MoPR + NDMA; 20 states, 81 districts.
xs: CBDRR through PRIs is jointly run by the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj and NDMA**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**NDRF** is the response force, **NIDM** does training and research, and **INCOIS** gives tsunami warnings: none runs this programme.
xa: Outlay: **Rs 507.37 crore**.
Coverage: **20 states**, **81 districts** (**20 GPs** per district), with **20 model GPs**.
Other community tools: **Aapda Mitra** volunteers, **mock drills**, the **National School Safety Programme**.

28.s: The nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility maps and the Landslide Atlas is:
28.x: The Geological Survey of India is the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility mapping and the Landslide Atlas.
28.tq: Match the specialised agency with its technical function.
xs: The **Geological Survey of India (GSI)** is the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility maps and the **Landslide Atlas**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**NCS** covers earthquakes, **IMD** covers cyclones and rain, and **CWC** covers river floods.
xa: GSI's **Bhukosh** portal hosts landslide-susceptibility maps of **4.3 lakh sq km**, mirrored to NDMA's GIS portal via WMS.
**Landslide Hazard Zonation** divides hill areas into homogeneous zones by susceptibility, hazard or risk; the maps are **probabilistic**.
For glacial lakes, NDMA tested an indigenous **GLOF alert at Sissu, HP**; ISRO made a **Glacial Lake Atlas**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about IMD's Multi-Hazard Early Warning Decision Support System (MHEW-DSS):
1. It is credited with zero casualties during Cyclones Hudhud and Fani.
2. It reaches about 80% of the population.
3. It was launched in 2024 under Mission Mausam as a webGIS multi-hazard warning platform.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
28.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: MHEW-DSS (IMD, 2024, Mission Mausam) is a webGIS platform reaching about 80% of the population. Statement 1 is NOT correct: the zero-casualty cases cited are Biparjoy (Gujarat) and Dana (Odisha). So only statement 1 is incorrect.
28.tq: MHEW-DSS zero casualties = Biparjoy + Dana.
xs: Only **statement 1** is NOT correct — option **(3) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is wrong: the zero-casualty cases are **Biparjoy** (**Gujarat**) and **Dana** (**Odisha**).
Statements 2 and 3 are correct: **MHEW-DSS** (**IMD, 2024, Mission Mausam**) is a **WebGIS** platform reaching about **80%** of the population.
xa: **Cyclone track error** (24 h) fell from **93 to 74 km**; (72 h) from **201 to 153 km**.
**Severe-weather forecasts** improved **40-50%**.
**Hudhud:** Oct **2014**, **Visakhapatnam**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre:
1. It is located at INCOIS, Hyderabad.
2. It was established in 2007.
3. It can issue alerts within about 10 minutes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: All three are correct: the ITEWC is at INCOIS Hyderabad, was set up in 2007, and issues alerts within 10 minutes, serving 25 countries. Every other option leaves out a true statement.
28.tq: ITEWC: INCOIS Hyderabad, 2007, 10 min, 25 countries.
xs: **All three statements are correct**, so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is the answer.
Statement 1: the ITEWC is at **INCOIS, Hyderabad**. Correct.
Statement 2: it was set up in **2007**. Correct.
Statement 3: it issues alerts within **10 min**. Correct.
xa: It serves **25** countries and monitored **32 major earthquakes in 2025**.
The **National Tsunami Ready Recognition Board** is chaired by the **Director, INCOIS**.
⚠ Tsunami = **INCOIS**; landslides = **GSI**; river floods = **CWC**.

28.s: Google Earth Engine is particularly useful in disaster management because it:
o: Processes large satellite-image archives for rapid flood mapping
Operates India’s network of cyclone shelters
Issues statutory evacuation orders to district authorities
28.x: Google Earth Engine is a cloud platform that processes extensive satellite-image archives and can support rapid flood mapping.
28.tq: Match the technology with its specific operational use.
xs: **Google Earth Engine** is a cloud platform that **processes large satellite-image archives for rapid flood mapping**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It does not run cyclone shelters, measure earthquake magnitude or issue evacuation orders.
xa: **Remote sensing** gives a fast, synoptic view: inundation mapping, damage assessment, flood-hazard zoning, drought early warning.
**GIS** overlays spatial data; its key use is **hazard mapping**.
**NDEM**, the GIS repository for the whole DM cycle, is maintained by **ISRO**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding hazard zonation:
1. Landslide Hazard Zonation divides hill areas into homogeneous zones.
2. Such zoning is based on the degree of susceptibility, hazard or risk.
3. Hazard-zonation maps are deterministic declarations that a disaster will certainly occur at a particular location.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hazard-zonation maps are probabilistic; they do not guarantee that a disaster will occur at a particular location.
28.tq: Reject the extreme interpretation that converts a probabilistic map into a certainty.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(1)** is the answer.
Statement 1: Landslide Hazard Zonation divides hill areas into **homogeneous zones**. Correct.
Statement 2: zoning is by degree of **susceptibility, hazard or risk**. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; hazard-zonation maps are **probabilistic**, not certain predictions.
xa: **GSI** is the nodal agency for landslide zonation, susceptibility maps and the **Landslide Atlas**.
GSI's **Bhukosh** portal covers **4.3 lakh sq km** of landslide-susceptibility maps.
**Seismic microzonation** is built into **Smart Cities** and **AMRUT**.

28.s:
Consider the following pairs (Tool — Use):
1. Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) — integrates public warnings
2. INSAT-3D/3DR — tracking cyclones
3. National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM) — GIS repository maintained by IMD
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
28.x: Pair 1 is correct: CAP integrates public warnings. Pair 2 is correct: INSAT-3D/3DR track cyclones. Pair 3 is wrong: NDEM, the GIS repository for the whole DM cycle, is maintained by ISRO, not IMD. So only two pairs are correct.
28.tq: NDEM = ISRO; CAP = alerts; INSAT-3D = cyclones.
xs: Pairs **1** and **2** are correct — option **(2) Only two**.
**CAP (Common Alerting Protocol)** integrates **public warnings**; **INSAT-3D/3DR** **track cyclones**.
Pair 3 is wrong: **NDEM**, the GIS repository for the whole DM cycle, is maintained by **ISRO**, not IMD.
xa: **Damini App** gives **lightning** alerts.
**Google Earth Engine** processes satellite archives for **rapid flood mapping**.
**ISRO Disaster Management Support Programme** covers floods, cyclones, droughts, forest fires, landslides, earthquakes.
**NADAMS** — **agricultural drought assessment**.

28.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
28.x: The Damini App provides lightning alerts. The other pairs assign disaster-management tools to unrelated functions.
28.tq: Start from the sure technology–function pair and eliminate mismatches.
xs: **Damini App — lightning alerts** is correctly matched, so option **(1)** is correct.
**INSAT-3D** tracks **cyclones**; **Bhukosh** is GSI's portal for **landslide-susceptibility maps**; **NDEM** is ISRO's GIS repository for the DM cycle.
xa: IMD's Lightning Detection System covers **104 locations**.
**Lightning** and **heatwaves** were added to notified disasters (**12 to 14** categories) for **2026-31**.
**CAP** (Common Alerting Protocol) integrates public warnings.

28.s: In flood management, a Geographic Information System (GIS) mainly helps authorities by:
o: Analysing flood patterns together with topography so that proactive action can be taken
Replacing the need for rainfall data
Issuing compensation cheques to flood victims
28.x: GIS stores and overlays spatial data, analysing flood patterns and topography for hazard mapping and proactive action. It is an analysis tool: it does not build embankments, it needs rainfall data rather than replacing it, and it does not pay compensation.
28.tq: GIS = overlay flood pattern + topography -> hazard mapping.
xs: GIS **analyses flood patterns together with topography** so authorities can act proactively, so option **(1)** is correct.
GIS is an analysis tool: it does not raise embankments, replace rainfall data or pay compensation.
xa: GIS stores, analyses and **overlays** remote-sensed and spatial data; key use = **hazard mapping** (earthquake, landslide, flood, fire).
**Google Earth Engine** processes satellite archives for **rapid flood mapping**.
River-flood warnings come from the **Central Water Commission**, which began scientific flood forecasting in **1958** on the Yamuna at Delhi.

28.s:
Which of the following functions falls within the mandate of APSDMA?
1. Running the State Emergency Operations Centre
2. Coordinating with districts
3. Operating early-warning systems
4. Planning post-disaster restoration
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: APSDMA runs the State Emergency Operations Centre, coordinates districts, operates early warnings and undertakes pre-disaster planning and post-disaster restoration.
28.tq: Group statutory functions across preparedness, response and recovery phases.
xs: **All four** are APSDMA functions, so option **(4)** "1, 2, 3 and 4" is correct.
APSDMA runs the **State Emergency Operations Centre**, coordinates **districts** and operates **early warning**.
Its mandate covers **pre-disaster** planning and **post-disaster** restoration.
xa: APSDMA is chaired by the **Chief Minister** under the **AP DM Rules 2007**.
It is the **apex statutory state body** for DM policy and plans.
AP moved from **relief-centric** to **mitigation-centric** DM and is seen as a national leader in DRR.

28.s: Which one of the following sets contains only measures used in cyclone risk reduction in Andhra Pradesh?
o: IMD warnings, cyclone shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves
Deep mining, dam demolition, desalination and river diversion
Only post-cyclone compensation and crop harvesting
Forest clearance, coastal construction and removal of mangroves
28.x: Cyclone risk reduction measures include IMD warnings, shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangrove protection or restoration.
28.tq: Select the complete set of coordinated mitigation and preparedness measures.
xs: AP's cyclone measures are **IMD warnings, cyclone shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Removing mangroves or doing only post-cyclone compensation goes against these measures.
xa: **Hudhud**: Oct **2014**, **Visakhapatnam**; **Michaung**: Dec **2023**, near **Bapatla**.
IMD has **7 cyclone warning centres**, including **Visakhapatnam**.
Cyclone safety: move to a **cyclone shelter**; never go to sea or stand under trees.

28.s:
Consider the following statements about cyclones that hit Andhra Pradesh:
1. Cyclone Hudhud made landfall near Visakhapatnam in October 2014.
2. Cyclone Michaung made landfall near Kakinada in December 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: Hudhud hit Visakhapatnam in October 2014. Statement 2 is wrong: Michaung (December 2023) made landfall near BAPATLA. Hence 1 only.
28.tq: Hudhud = Visakhapatnam 2014; Michaung = Bapatla 2023.
xs: Only **statement 1** is correct — option **(1) 1 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Hudhud** made landfall at **Visakhapatnam** in **Oct 2014**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Michaung** (**Dec 2023**) made landfall near **Bapatla**, not Kakinada.
xa: **APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister** under the **AP DM Rules 2007**.
APSDMA runs the **State Emergency Operations Centre**.
AP cyclone measures: **IMD warnings**, **cyclone shelters**, evacuation, shelter belts and **mangroves**.
**7 cyclone warning centres** include **Visakhapatnam**.

28.s: The change in Andhra Pradesh’s disaster-management approach is described as a shift from:
o: A mitigation-centric approach to a relief-centric approach
A district-centric approach to a village-centric approach only
A warning-based approach to a compensation-only approach
A relief-centric approach to a mitigation-centric approach
28.x: Andhra Pradesh has moved from a relief-centric approach towards a mitigation-centric approach and is regarded as a national leader in disaster-risk reduction.
28.tq: Test the direction of institutional change; reversed comparisons are a common trap.
xs: AP moved from a **relief-centric approach to a mitigation-centric approach**, so option **(4)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the direction of the shift.
xa: AP is regarded as a **national leader in DRR**.
The **DM Act 2005** made the same national shift: from relief-centric response to **prevention, mitigation and preparedness**.
⚠ Criticism nationally: spending is still **relief-centric** rather than mitigation-focused.

28.s: The Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules under which APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister were made in:
28.x: The Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules were made in 2007.
28.tq: Separate the State rules year from the Act, policy and plan years.
xs: The **AP DM Rules** were made in **2007**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**2005** is the DM Act, **2009** the National Policy on DM, **2016** the first NDMP.
xa: Under these rules **APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
APSDMA is the **apex statutory state body** for DM policy and plans.
Under the DM Act, the **SDMA** is set up under **s.14**; its State Executive Committee is under the **Chief Secretary**.

28.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Adding heatwaves and lightning raised India's notified-disaster categories from 12 to 14.
2. Their inclusion opens SDRF/NDRF and disaster-mitigation-fund support for them.
3. NDMA's 'Resilient India 2047' asks Union Ministries to prepare plans under Sections 46 and 48 of the DM Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: Statement 1 is correct: 12 to 14 categories. Statement 2 is correct: notification opens SDRF/NDRF and SDMF funding. Statement 3 is wrong: Resilient India 2047 asks for hazard-specific plans under Section 35 and Ministry DM Plans under Section 37; Sections 46 and 48 are the response funds. So '1 only' misses 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Statement 1: adding **heatwaves and lightning** raised notified categories from **12 to 14**. Correct.
Statement 2: notification opens **SDRF/NDRF and SDMF** funding. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; Resilient India 2047 asks for hazard plans under **Sec 35** and Ministry DM Plans under **Sec 37**. Sections **46** and **48** are the response funds.
xa: The new list applies to the **2026-31** award period under **16th FC** guidelines.
**No man-made calamity** is notified; states may spend **up to 10% of SDRF** on state-specific disasters.
SDRF Centre:State share is **75:25** for general states.

28.s: Which of the following is identified as a criticism or continuing challenge in India’s disaster-management system?
o: Excessive emphasis on mitigation expenditure over relief
Outdated India Disaster Resource Network data
Universal constitution of SDRFs in every State
Complete multi-hazard mapping across the country
28.x: The India Disaster Resource Network inventory is described as outdated. Other identified challenges include incomplete multi-hazard mapping, SDRFs not being raised in all States, and relief-centric spending.
28.tq: Select the genuine system deficiency among reversed or exaggerated claims.
xs: **Outdated India Disaster Resource Network data** is a listed criticism, so option **(2)** is correct.
The other options reverse the real problems: spending is still **relief-centric**, SDRFs are **not raised in all States**, and multi-hazard mapping is **incomplete**.
xa: Proposed fix: an annual NDMA **State Disaster Vulnerability Index**.
Suggested fix for the SDRF gap: **mandatory SDRFs** plus joint NDRF-SDRF training.
The **DM (Amendment) Act 2025** makes an SDRF **mandatory** in every state.

28.s: Which proposal has been suggested to improve comparative assessment of disaster vulnerability among States?
o: A biennial National Relief Expenditure Census
An annual NDMA State Disaster Vulnerability Index
28.x: A proposal has been made for an annual NDMA State Disaster Vulnerability Index.
28.tq: Identify the specific institutional proposal rather than a generic reform.
xs: The proposal is an **annual NDMA State Disaster Vulnerability Index**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The other options are not proposals in the notes.
xa: Listed criticisms: incomplete **multi-hazard mapping**, SDRFs not raised in all States, outdated **India Disaster Resource Network** data, relief-centric spending.
**Vulnerability** = exposure + inability to cope; **Hazard x Vulnerability = Disaster**.
Community vulnerability factors: **kutcha housing**, farm-labour dependence, thin health infrastructure, low crop-insurance cover, weak early warning.

28.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems and Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh receives 2–3 such systems annually, mainly from the Arabian Sea.
It receives 30–35 such systems annually, exclusively from the southern Bay of Bengal.
Such systems affect only the coastal districts and never the river basins.
It receives 13–14 such systems annually, mostly from the northern Bay of Bengal, affecting the Godavari and Krishna basins.
28.x: Andhra Pradesh is associated with 13–14 Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems annually, mostly from the northern Bay, which can flood the Godavari and Krishna basins.
28.tq: Check the frequency, source region and affected basins together.
xs: AP gets **13-14** Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems a year, mostly from the **northern Bay**, flooding the **Godavari-Krishna** basins, so option **(4)** is correct.
This was raised at the **IMD-Amaravati + NIDM** meeting near **Gannavaram**.
xa: AP flood alerts: **48-h** rain warnings and **6-h** flash-flood warnings, Vijayawada first.
**Godavari** flood relief camps were set up in **Jul 2026**.
AP funds: **Rs 277.63 crore** (2025-26) + **Rs 479.01 crore** (2026-27) under SDRF/NDRF; **Rs 521.17 crore** under SDMF/NDMF.

28.s:
Arrange the following disaster-response steps in the correct sequence:
A. Early warning
B. Evacuation
C. Rescue
D. Shelters
28.x: Response runs early warning, evacuation, rescue and shelters, that is A, B, C, D.
28.tq: Arrange steps from before to after impact.
n: During a disaster, early warning is followed by evacuation. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
During a disaster, evacuation is followed by rescue. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
During a disaster, rescue is followed by movement to shelters. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
During a disaster, shelters are followed by emergency medical or water supply. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xs: The sequence is **A, B, C, D** — option **(3)**.
During a disaster: **early warning → evacuation → rescue → shelters** → emergency medical or water supply.
xa: After a disaster: **relief → restoration → reconstruction → resilient rebuilding**.
The **community** is usually the **first responder**.
**Response** is **during or immediately after** — **time-critical**.

28.s: Which of the following represents the correct post-disaster management sequence?
28.x: After a disaster comes relief, then restoration, then reconstruction and finally resilient rebuilding.
28.tq: Arrange steps from immediate to long term.
n: After a disaster, relief is followed by restoration. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
After a disaster, restoration is followed by reconstruction. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
After a disaster, reconstruction is followed by resilient rebuilding. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xs: The post-disaster sequence is **relief → restoration → reconstruction → resilient rebuilding** — option **(3)**.
Relief comes first; **resilient rebuilding** is the last step.
xa: During-disaster sequence: **early warning → evacuation → rescue → shelters**.
**Post-disaster** stage covers **recovery**, **rehabilitation**, **reconstruction** — focus on **rebuild better**.
**Modern view:** phases form an **overlapping continuum**, not a line.

28.s: Which phase of disaster management aims to restore normal life and reduce future vulnerability?
28.x: Recovery aims to bring back normal life and lower future vulnerability through rehabilitation and reconstruction. Response is the immediate action, and mitigation reduces impact beforehand.
28.tq: Place each phase before, during or after the disaster.
n: Recovery aims to restore normal life. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Recovery aims to reduce future vulnerability. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Recovery aims to restore normalcy. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Recovery builds resilience. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: **Recovery** aims to **restore normal life** and **reduce future vulnerability** — option **(3)**.
**Response** is **immediate action** to **save lives**; **mitigation** **reduces risk** before a disaster.
xa: Recovery includes **rehabilitation**, **reconstruction**, **livelihood support**, **psycho-social care**.
Recovery is **long-term**, **builds resilience** — **Build Back Better**.
**Preparedness** is the **first and critical step**.

28.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The community is usually the first responder.
The Collector plays a pivotal role in disaster response.
The fire brigade alone has the basic responsibility for urban response.
The district administration has the basic responsibility in urban response.
28.x: Option C is incorrect: urban response is shared by civic bodies, the fire brigade and police, with the district administration in overall charge. The community is usually the first responder.
28.tq: Watch for 'alone'.
n: The community is usually the first responder. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Urban response involves civic authorities. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Urban response involves the fire brigade. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Urban response involves local police. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
The district administration has the basic responsibility during urban response. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
The Collector plays a pivotal role during urban response. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: **"The fire brigade alone has the basic responsibility"** is incorrect — option **(3)**.
**Urban response** involves **civic authorities**, the **fire brigade** and **local police**; the **district administration** has the **basic responsibility**.
The **community** is the **first responder** and the **Collector** plays a **pivotal role** — both correct.
xa: **DDMA** is headed by the **District Magistrate/Collector**.
**Search and Rescue** plays a major role **post-disaster**.
**SDRF** is the **first responder** within the state in the first **24–48 hours**.

28.s:
Assertion (A): Mitigation is considered the most cost-effective phase of disaster management.
Reason (R): Mitigation aims to reduce the severity or impact of a disaster.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
28.x: Both are true: mitigation is the most cost-effective phase because cutting a disaster's impact in advance costs less than relief and rebuilding later. R explains A.
28.tq: Ask whether reducing impact explains the saving.
n: Mitigation reduces the severity of a disaster. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Mitigation reduces the impact of a disaster. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Mitigation is the most cost-effective phase. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Mitigation aims to reduce disaster risk. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Mitigation aims to minimise future losses. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
**Mitigation** reduces **disaster risk** and the **severity/impact**, **minimising future losses** — the **most cost-effective** phase.
xa: Mitigation measures: **earthquake-resistant buildings**, **embankments**, **building codes**, **afforestation**, **insurance**, **hazard mapping**.
DM Act definition: measures **reducing the risk, impact or effects** of a disaster.
Mitigation is a **pre-disaster** phase with prevention and preparedness.

28.s:

I. It includes warning systems.
II. It includes evacuation arrangements.
III. It includes emergency resources and coordination.
IV. Its objective is to restore normal life after a disaster.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: I, II and III are correct: preparation covers warnings, evacuation plans, and emergency resources and coordination. IV is false because restoring normal life is the goal of recovery.
28.tq: Place each activity in its phase.
n: Preparation includes warning systems. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparation includes evacuation arrangements. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparation includes emergency resources. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparation includes coordination. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Recovery aims to restore normal life. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Recovery aims to restore normalcy. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — option **(4) I, II and III only**.
**Preparedness** includes **early warning systems**, **evacuation arrangements**, **emergency resources** and **coordination**.
IV is wrong: **restoring normal life** is the aim of **recovery**.
xa: Preparedness also covers **mock drills**, **stockpiling**, **Aapda Mitra** training, **Emergency Operation Centres**, **contingency plans**.
Preparedness is the **first and critical step**.
Prep early-warning tool: **CAP-SACHET**.

(b) Mitigation
(c) Preparedness

n: Prevention includes land-use zoning. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Prevention includes controlling industrial siting. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Mitigation includes earthquake-resistant buildings. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Mitigation includes hazard mapping. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparedness includes Early Warning Systems. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparedness includes mock drills. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response includes search and rescue. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response includes evacuation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Earthquake mitigation includes reframing building-construction guidelines. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Earthquake mitigation includes implementing building-construction guidelines. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Mitigation includes building codes. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
The during-crisis phase focuses on rescue. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Risk assessment leads to mitigation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Prevention occurs before a disaster. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Prevention aims to stop a hazard from becoming a disaster. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Mitigation occurs before a disaster. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparedness occurs before a disaster. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response occurs during or immediately after a disaster. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Prevention** — **land-use zoning**, **controlling industrial siting**; **mitigation** — **earthquake-resistant buildings**, **hazard mapping**.
**Preparedness** — **early warning systems**, **mock drills**; **response** — **search and rescue**, **evacuation**.
xa: **Recovery** — **rehabilitation**, **reconstruction**, **livelihood support**.
Prevention also includes **regulating deforestation**.
**Risk assessment** leads to **mitigation**.

28.s: Disaster management has how many phases?
28.x: Disaster management is commonly described in four phases: mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery, forming a continuous cycle.
28.tq: Recall the standard four-phase disaster management cycle.
n: Disaster management has four phases. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: Disaster management has **four phases** — option **(3) Four**.
The cycle is **continuous**: lessons from **recovery** lead to better **prevention**.
xa: ⚠ The notes' table lists **prevention**, **mitigation**, **preparedness**, **response** and **recovery**; Prep merges **Prevention/Mitigation** into one phase.
**Stages:** **pre-disaster**, **during-disaster**, **post-disaster**.
**Mitigation** is the **most cost-effective** phase.

28.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Community awareness programmes are a form of non-structural mitigation.
II. Education programmes are a form of non-structural mitigation.
III. Planting trees along coastal areas is a cyclone mitigation measure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: All three are correct: awareness and education are non-structural mitigation, and coastal tree belts reduce cyclone damage.
28.tq: Discriminate structural from non-structural mitigation.
n: Non-structural mitigation includes community awareness programmes. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Non-structural mitigation includes education programmes. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Cyclone mitigation includes planting trees along coastal areas. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: **All three** are correct — option **(1) I, II and III**.
**Community awareness** and **education** programmes are **non-structural mitigation**.
**Planting trees along coastal areas** is a **cyclone mitigation** measure.
xa: **Earthquake mitigation:** **reframing and implementing building-construction guidelines**.
**Risk assessment** leads to mitigation.
**Mangroves** **buffer** coastal hazards.

28.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Prevention includes regulating deforestation.
Statement B: Prevention is proactive and long-term.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
28.x: Both are true: prevention includes controlling deforestation, and it is proactive and long-term.
28.tq: Recall the nature of prevention.
n: Prevention includes regulating deforestation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Prevention is proactive and long-term. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
**Prevention** includes **land-use zoning**, **regulating deforestation** and **controlling industrial siting**.
Prevention aims to **stop a hazard from becoming a disaster** — **proactive and long-term**.
xa: Prevention, mitigation and preparedness are **pre-disaster** phases.
The post-2005 **three Ps:** **prevention**, **preparedness**, **proofing/mitigation**.
**Mitigation** is the **most cost-effective** phase.

28.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Preparedness includes Emergency Operation Centres.
II. Preparedness includes contingency plans.
III. Emergency Operation Centres are included under the recovery phase.
IV. Contingency plans are included under the response phase.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: I and II are correct: emergency operation centres and contingency plans are preparedness tools. III and IV are false because they put these tools in the wrong phases.
28.tq: Place each tool in its phase.
n: Preparedness includes Emergency Operation Centres. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparedness includes contingency plans. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: Statements **I and II** are correct — option **(1) I and II only**.
**Emergency Operation Centres** and **contingency plans** belong to **preparedness**.
III and IV are wrong: they place these tools in **recovery** and **response** instead.
xa: **Response:** **search and rescue**, **evacuation**, **first aid**, **temporary shelters**.
**Recovery:** **rehabilitation**, **reconstruction**, **psycho-social care**.
**APSDMA** runs the **State Emergency Operations Centre**.

28.s:
How many of the following are objectives or characteristics of the response phase?
1. Saving lives
2. Meeting basic needs
3. Providing first aid
4. Providing temporary shelters
5. Providing food and water
6. Maintaining law and order
7. Being time-critical
8. Being a long-term activity
28.x: Seven describe response: saving lives, basic needs, first aid, shelter, food and water, law and order, and being time-critical. Being long-term describes recovery.
28.tq: Discriminate time-critical response from long-term recovery.
n: Response aims to save lives. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response aims to meet basic needs. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response includes first aid. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response includes temporary shelters. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response includes food and water provision. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response includes maintaining law and order. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response is time-critical. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xs: **Seven** of the eight describe response — option **(3) Only seven**.
Response aims to **save lives** and **meet basic needs** — **first aid**, **temporary shelters**, **food and water**, **law and order** — and is **time-critical**.
**Long-term** describes **recovery**, not response.
xa: Response comes **during** or **immediately after** a disaster.
It also includes **search and rescue** and **evacuation**.
**NDRF** and armed forces do **search and rescue** (Prep).

(b) During-disaster stage
(c) Post-disaster stage

28.tq: Place each phase before, during or after the disaster.
n: The pre-disaster stage covers prevention, mitigation, and preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
The focus of the pre-disaster stage is risk reduction and readiness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
The during-disaster stage covers response. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]

28.x: Both are true: mitigation belongs to the pre-disaster phase because that phase is made up of prevention, mitigation and preparedness. R explains A.

28.s:

I. Hazard zonation mapping is used in prevention or mitigation.
II. Real-time damage assessment is used during response.
III. “Build Back Better” planning is associated with recovery or reconstruction.
IV. Evacuation route planning is an application of recovery or reconstruction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
28.x: I, II and III are correct: hazard zonation is prevention, real-time damage assessment is response, and 'build back better' is recovery. IV is false because evacuation route planning is preparedness.
28.tq: Place each GIS use in its phase.
n: GIS is used for hazard zonation mapping during prevention or mitigation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
GIS is used for evacuation route planning during preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
GIS is used for real-time damage assessment during response. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
GIS is used for “Build Back Better” planning during recovery or reconstruction. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
xs: Statements **I, II and III** are correct — option **(3) I, II and III only**.
**Hazard zonation mapping** — **prevention/mitigation**; **real-time damage assessment** — **response**; **"Build Back Better" planning** — **recovery**.
IV is wrong: **evacuation route planning** is a **preparedness** use.
xa: Preparedness also uses **resource mapping** and **early warning systems**.
Response also uses **search and rescue coordination**, **resource allocation**.
Prevention also uses **vulnerability assessment**, **risk mapping**, **land-use planning**.

29.s:
Consider the following statements about UNCLOS and maritime zones:
1. It set up the International Seabed Authority to regulate seabed mining beyond national jurisdiction.
2. A coastal State has full sovereignty, not merely sovereign rights, over its 200 nm Exclusive Economic Zone.
3. UNCLOS was adopted in 1982 and came into force in 1994.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
29.x: Statement 3 is correct: UNCLOS dates from 1982 and entered into force in 1994. Statement 1 is correct: it created the ISA for seabed mining beyond national jurisdiction. Statement 2 is wrong: full sovereignty applies only to the 12 nm territorial sea; in the 200 nm EEZ the State has sovereign rights over resources. So '3 only' misses statement 1, and options with statement 2 are wrong.
29.tq: 12 nm = sovereignty; 200 nm EEZ = sovereign rights only.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: UNCLOS set up the **International Seabed Authority (ISA)** for seabed mining **beyond national jurisdiction**.
Statement 2 is wrong: full **sovereignty** is only in the **12 nm** territorial sea; the **200 nm EEZ** gives **sovereign rights** only.
Statement 3 is correct: **UNCLOS** was adopted in **1982**, in force **1994**.
xa: **India's EEZ:** about **2.37 million sq km** — world's **18th largest**.
Indian law: **Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, EEZ and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976**.
Contiguous zone: **24 nm**.

29.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Territorial sea — Full sovereignty, subject to innocent passage
2. Contiguous zone — Enforcement of customs, fiscal, immigration and sanitary laws
3. High seas — Freedom of navigation, overflight and research

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
29.x: All three pairs are correct: the territorial sea (12 nm) gives full sovereignty subject to innocent passage; the contiguous zone (24 nm) lets the state enforce customs, fiscal, immigration and sanitary laws; and the high seas carry freedom of navigation, overflight and research.
29.tq: Match each zone with its distinctive legal right before selecting the coded combination.
xs: **All three pairs are correct**, so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is the answer.
Pair 1: **territorial sea** (**12 nm**) = full sovereignty, subject to **innocent passage**. Correct.
Pair 2: **contiguous zone** (**24 nm**) = enforce **customs, fiscal, immigration, sanitary** laws. Correct.
Pair 3: **high seas** = freedom of **navigation, overflight, research**. Correct.
xa: **EEZ** (**200 nm**): sovereign rights to explore, exploit and conserve all living and non-living resources.
**Continental shelf:** sovereign rights over **seabed and subsoil** resources, up to **350 nm** if extended.
India's law: **Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, EEZ and Other Maritime Zones Act, 1976**.

29.s:
With reference to the Exclusive Economic Zone, consider the following statements:

1. It extends up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline.
2. The coastal state has sovereign rights to explore, exploit and conserve living and non-living resources.
3. It includes the continental shelf beyond 200 nautical miles.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: The EEZ extends to 200 nautical miles and confers resource-related sovereign rights. It excludes the continental shelf beyond 200 nautical miles.
29.tq: Find the exclusion statement in a maritime-zone question.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(1)** is the answer.
Statement 1: the EEZ runs to **200 nm** from the baseline. Correct.
Statement 2: the coastal state has **sovereign rights** to explore, exploit and conserve living and non-living resources. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; the EEZ **excludes** the territorial sea and the **continental shelf beyond 200 nm**.
xa: India's EEZ: **~2.37 million sq km** (~**24 lakh sq km**), the world's **18th largest**.
⚠ EEZ gives **sovereign rights** only; full **sovereignty** applies in the **12 nm** territorial sea.
India's **EEZ Rules 2025**: an **Access Pass** is mandatory for mechanised and motorised vessels **>=24 m**.

29.s: India's Exclusive Economic Zone is about how large, and where does it rank in the world?
29.x: India's EEZ is about 2.37 million sq km (~24 lakh sq km), the world's 18th largest, much of it added by the Andaman-Nicobar and Lakshadweep islands. 1.6 million sq km is an older figure, 11,098 is the coastline length in km, and India is not 2nd.
29.tq: EEZ ~2.37 m sq km, 18th; older notes say 2.02/1.6.
xs: India's EEZ is **about 2.37 million sq km**, the world's **18th largest**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**1.6 million sq km** is an older figure, and **11,098** km is India's **coastline** length, not an area.
xa: That is about **24 lakh sq km**; older notes also say **2.02 million sq km**.
The **Andaman-Nicobar** and **Lakshadweep** islands add much of it.
GSI has surveyed **3,10,761 sq km** of a **5,89,160 sq km** EEZ target.

29.s: India's domestic law on maritime zones (territorial waters, continental shelf and EEZ) was enacted in:
29.x: The Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, EEZ and Other Maritime Zones Act was passed in 1976. 1982 and 1994 are when UNCLOS was adopted and came into force; 1956 is unrelated.
29.tq: Maritime Zones Act 1976 predates UNCLOS 1982.
xs: India's **Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, EEZ and Other Maritime Zones Act** was passed in **1976**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**1982** and **1994** are when UNCLOS was adopted and came into force.
xa: ⚠ The Indian Act (**1976**) came before UNCLOS (**1982**).
Territorial sea **12 nm**; EEZ **200 nm**.
The **OAMDR Act 2002** (amended **2023**) governs offshore mineral leases.

29.s:
Consider the following statements about seabed minerals:
1. Polymetallic nodules contain nickel, copper, cobalt and manganese.
2. Polymetallic sulphides contain silver, gold and platinum besides copper, zinc, lead and iron.
3. Rare earths do not occur on the seafloor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
29.x: Statement 1 is correct: nodules = nickel, copper, cobalt, manganese. Statement 2 is correct: sulphides carry copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver, gold and platinum. Statement 3 is wrong: rare earths do occur on the seafloor. So '1 only' misses 2, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.
29.tq: Nodules = Ni-Cu-Co-Mn; sulphides add precious metals.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Statement 1: nodules carry **nickel, copper, cobalt, manganese**. Correct.
Statement 2: sulphides carry copper, zinc, lead, iron, **silver, gold, platinum**. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; **rare earths do occur on the seafloor**.
xa: Polymetallic sulphides form at **hydrothermal vents on mid-ocean ridges** and are key for EVs, grids and solar.
**Gas hydrates** = methane ice in seabed sediments.
India's first ISA contract: **polymetallic nodules, Central Indian Ocean Basin** (**2002**).

29.s: India became the first Pioneer Investor in the Central Indian Ocean Basin in:
29.x: India became the first Pioneer Investor in the Central Indian Ocean Basin in 1987.
29.tq: Discriminate between the Pioneer Investor date and later ISA contract dates.
xs: India became the first **Pioneer Investor** in the **Central Indian Ocean Basin** in **1987**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**2002** is the year of India's ISA nodule contract; **1976** is the Maritime Zones Act; **1982** is UNCLOS adoption.
xa: Licences come from the **ISA**, set up under UNCLOS.
Later contracts: sulphides, Central and South West Indian Ridge (**2016**); sulphides, **Carlsberg Ridge** (**15 Sep 2025**).
**Matsya 6000** is designed to dive to **6,000 m** in the Central Indian Ocean.

Match List-I with List-II:

B. Polymetallic sulphides — Central and South West Indian Ridge

xs: Correct match: **A-1, B-2, C-3**, so option **(1)** is the answer.

29.s: Gas hydrates are best described as:
o: Methane ice occurring in seabed sediments
29.x: Gas hydrates are methane ice deposits occurring in seabed sediments.
29.tq: Distinguish a precise scientific definition from nearby marine substances.
xs: Gas hydrates are **methane ice in seabed sediments**, so option **(3)** is correct.
They are not solid petroleum, frozen seawater or beach salts.
xa: Explored under the **National Gas Hydrate Programme** in the **KG basin, Mahanadi and Andaman**.
Other seabed resources: **nodules** (nickel, copper, cobalt, manganese) and **polymetallic sulphides**.

29.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deep Ocean Mission:
1. It was approved in June 2021 with an outlay of ₹4,077 crore over five years.
2. Under it, the Samudrayaan submersible Matsya 6000 is designed to carry three crew to 6,000 m in the Central Indian Ocean.
3. Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
29.x: Statement 1 is correct: the mission was approved in June 2021 at ₹4,077 crore for five years. Statement 3 is wrong: the nodal ministry is the Ministry of Earth Sciences. Statement 2 is correct: Matsya 6000 is built to take 3 crew to 6,000 m. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 3 are wrong.
29.tq: Deep Ocean Mission = MoES, ₹4,077 crore, Matsya 6000.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Deep Ocean Mission** was approved in **June 2021** at **₹4,077 crore** over **five years**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Matsya 6000** (**Samudrayaan**) carries **3 crew** to **6,000 m**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the nodal ministry is the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, not Ports/Shipping.
xa: It is one of the nine **PM-STIAC** missions.
It has **six** focus areas, including **deep-sea mining** and a **manned submersible**.
**NIOT's Nellore** facility tests **nodule-mining crawlers** and **LTTD desalination**.

29.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deep Ocean Mission:

2. Its focus areas include deep-sea mining and a manned submersible.

Statements 2 and 3: focus areas include **deep-sea mining + manned submersible**, and **ocean climate advisory, biodiversity, ocean survey**. Correct.

Approved **June 2021**, **₹4,077 crore** over **5 years**, under **MoES**.
**NIOT's Nellore** seafront tests **LTTD desalination** and **wave-energy** units.

29.s:
Consider the following statements about offshore minerals:
1. Under the OAMDR Act 2002 (amended 2023), production leases for non-atomic minerals go to private firms only by auction.
2. The first tranche of 13 offshore blocks was auctioned under a composite licence.

xa: Offshore blocks: lime mud **3**, **heavy minerals 16** (handed to **DAE**), construction sand **9**, polymetallic crust/nodules **7**.
GSI survey: **3,10,761 sq km** covered of a **5,89,160 sq km** EEZ target.

Mumbai High, Cauvery, Chavara and Carlsberg Ridge
