xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Statement 1: **Gobi** = **cold, continental**, Mongolia and China. Correct.
Statement 2: **Taklamakan** = **Xinjiang, Tarim basin**. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; the Taklamakan is **cold, continental**.
xa: Hot deserts: **Sahara, Kalahari, Sonoran, Thar**.
**Atacama** is a cold-current coastal desert.
**Mongolian** plateau is intermontane, Central Asia.

31.s:
Consider the following statements about deserts:
1. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.
2. The Namib is one of the world's oldest deserts.
3. The Great Victoria is the largest desert in Australia.
4. The Thar extends through India and Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
31.x: All four statements are correct. The Sahara is the largest hot desert, the Namib is among the oldest, Great Victoria is Australia's largest desert, and the Thar lies in India and Pakistan.
31.tq: Test a cluster of desert attributes by checking size, age, country and extent separately.
xs: **All four statements are correct**, so option **(4)** "1, 2, 3 and 4" is the answer.
**Sahara** = largest hot; **Namib** = one of the oldest.
**Great Victoria** = Australia's largest (WA, SA); **Thar** = India (Rajasthan) and Pakistan.
xa: **Atacama** (Chile) is the **driest**.
Sahara countries include **Algeria, Libya, Egypt, Mali, Niger, Chad, Sudan**.
Aeolian landforms: **barchans, seifs, mushroom rocks, yardangs, zeugen, loess**.

31.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its aeolian landform?
31.x: Barchans are crescent-shaped sand dunes. Yardangs, mushroom rocks and loess are also aeolian features but do not have the descriptions given in the other options.
31.tq: Match the exact landform description instead of the general desert association.
xs: **Barchan — crescent-shaped dune** is correct, so option **(3)** is the answer.
**Loess, mushroom rocks and yardangs** are aeolian (wind) landforms, not volcanic cones, river terraces or limestone plateaus.
xa: Full list: **barchans, seifs, mushroom rocks, yardangs, zeugen, loess**.
**Nullarbor Plain** is a **limestone** plain on the Great Australian Bight.
⚠ Largest hot desert = **Sahara**; driest = **Atacama**.

31.s: The Terai is best described as the:
o: Limestone plain along the Great Australian Bight
Marshy zone south of the Bhabar in Nepal and the Himalayan foothills of India
31.x: The Terai is a marshy zone south of the Bhabar, occurring in Nepal and along India's Himalayan foothills.
31.tq: Distinguish regional physiographic names by their landform and location.
xs: The **Terai** is the **marshy zone south of the Bhabar** in **Nepal** and India's Himalayan foothills, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Lake Eyre basin** = lowest point of Australia; **Nullarbor** = limestone plain; **Levant** = eastern Mediterranean.
xa: The **Indo-Gangetic plain** is India's **youngest** physiographic division.

xs: **Kyiv** is on the **Dnieper**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Cologne** = Rhine; **Paris** = Seine; **Vienna** = Danube.
xa: Asked in APPSC-G1 **2022**.
The Dnieper rises in the **Valdai Hills** and drains into the **Black Sea**.
The **MV OMORFI** attack in the **Black Sea** killed an Indian crew member (Aug **2026**).

32.s: Budapest, Vienna and Bratislava are all cities situated on the:
32.x: Budapest, Vienna and Bratislava are important cities located on the Danube River.
32.tq: Recognise the cluster of cities belonging to one river basin.
xs: **Budapest, Vienna and Bratislava** are on the **Danube**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Paris** is on the **Seine**; **Cologne** on the **Rhine**; **New Orleans** on the **Mississippi**.
xa: **Belgrade** stands at the confluence of the **Sava and Danube**.
The Danube rises in the **Black Forest** and drains into the **Black Sea**.
It crosses the **most countries (10)**.

32.s: Belgrade is situated at the confluence of which two rivers?
32.x: Belgrade is located at the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers.
32.tq: Identify the confluence pair rather than only the larger river.
xs: **Belgrade** is at the confluence of the **Sava and Danube**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The other pairs are not linked to Belgrade in the notes.
xa: Other Danube cities: **Budapest, Vienna, Bratislava**.
The Danube passes **Serbia**, **Hungary**, **Austria**, **Slovakia**, **Romania**.
The **Dnieper** and **Dniester** also flow into the Black Sea.

32.s:
Match List-I (Waterfall) with List-II (Record):
List-I
(a) Angel Falls
(b) Victoria Falls
(c) Iguazu Falls
(d) Tugela Falls
List-II
(i) Largest waterfall system
(ii) Second highest waterfall
(iii) Highest waterfall, about 979 m
(iv) Largest sheet of falling water
32.x: Angel Falls on the Churun (Venezuela) is the highest at about 979 m (3,212 ft); Victoria Falls on the Zambezi is the largest sheet of falling water; Iguazu (Argentina-Brazil) is the largest fall system; Tugela in South Africa's Drakensberg is the second highest. So a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii. The other codes swap Angel with Tugela, Victoria with Iguazu, or Angel with Victoria.
32.tq: Angel highest, Tugela second; Victoria = sheet; Iguazu = system.
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Angel Falls** (river **Churun**, **Venezuela**) is the **highest**, about **979 m** (**3,212 ft**).
**Victoria Falls** on the **Zambezi** is the **largest sheet of falling water**; **Iguazu** (**Argentina-Brazil**) is the **largest fall system**.
**Tugela Falls** in South Africa's **Drakensberg** is the **second highest**.
xa: **Niagara Falls** (**USA-Canada**) lies **between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario**.
Angel Falls lies in the **Guiana Highlands** of Venezuela.
The **Zambezi** also has the **Kariba Dam** and forms part of the **Zambia–Zimbabwe boundary**.

32.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Niagara Falls lies between Lakes Erie and Ontario.
2. Iguazu Falls is situated between Argentina and Brazil.
3. Tugela Falls is located in the Drakensberg of South Africa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
32.x: All three statements are correct. Niagara is between Erie and Ontario, Iguazu is associated with Argentina and Brazil, and Tugela is in South Africa's Drakensberg.
32.tq: Combine location, neighbouring countries and physical-region clues.
xs: **All three statements are correct**, so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is the answer.
**Niagara** = between **Erie and Ontario**; **Iguazu** = **Argentina-Brazil**; **Tugela** = **Drakensberg**, South Africa.
xa: Iguazu is the **largest fall system**; Tugela the **second highest**.
The **Welland Canal** links Ontario and Erie, bypassing **Niagara Falls**.
**Angel Falls** is the highest (**3,212 ft**).

32.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lake Baikal is the deepest lake and the largest freshwater lake by volume.
2. The Caspian is the largest lake and is a freshwater lake.
3. Lake Superior, shared by the USA and Canada, is the largest freshwater lake by area.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Statement 1 is correct: Baikal is the deepest and largest by volume of fresh water. Statement 2 is wrong: the Caspian is the largest lake but it is saline. Statement 3 is correct: Superior (USA-Canada) is the largest freshwater lake by area. Hence 1 and 3 only.
32.tq: Volume = Baikal; area (fresh) = Superior; overall largest (saline) = Caspian.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(3)** is the answer.
Statement 1: **Baikal** is the **deepest** and largest freshwater lake **by volume**. Correct.
Statement 2: wrong; the **Caspian** is the largest lake but **saline**.
Statement 3: **Superior** (USA-Canada) is the largest freshwater lake **by area**. Correct.
xa: ⚠ Largest = Caspian (saline); largest fresh by area = Superior; by volume = Baikal.
The Caspian borders **Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan**.
**Victoria** is the **2nd-largest freshwater lake**.

32.s: Which one of the following lakes is the second-largest freshwater lake and is also associated with the source of the White Nile?
32.x: Lake Victoria, shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, is the second-largest freshwater lake and is associated with the source of the White Nile.
32.tq: Combine the superlative with the associated river-source clue.
xs: **Lake Victoria** is the **2nd-largest freshwater lake** and the source of the **White Nile**, so option **(3)** is correct.
It is shared by **Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania**.
xa: It lies **between the two branches** of the Rift Valley, not in the rift.
**Titicaca** = highest navigable lake; **Turkana** = largest desert lake.
The **Blue Nile** rises from **Lake Tana**.

32.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lake Titicaca (Peru-Bolivia) is the highest navigable lake.
2. Lake Turkana in Kenya is the largest desert lake.
3. Lake Van in Turkiye is the largest freshwater lake of Asia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Statement 1 is correct: Titicaca is the highest navigable lake. Statement 2 is correct: Turkana (Eastern Rift, Kenya) is the largest desert lake and is alkaline. Statement 3 is wrong: Lake Van is the largest alkaline lake, not a freshwater lake. Hence 1 and 2 only.
32.tq: Titicaca = highest navigable; Turkana = desert; Van = alkaline.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Statement 1: **Titicaca** (Peru-Bolivia) is the **highest navigable lake**. Correct.
Statement 2: **Turkana** (Kenya) is the **largest desert lake**. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; **Lake Van** is the largest **alkaline** lake.
xa: Turkana lies in the **Eastern Rift** and is also alkaline.
**Balkhash**: western half fresh, eastern half saline.
**Baikal** is the deepest lake.

32.s: Which statement correctly describes Lake Balkhash?
o: Its western half is saline and its eastern half is fresh.
Its western half is fresh and its eastern half is saline.
It is entirely saline and lies in Iran.
It is entirely freshwater and lies in Russia.
32.x: Lake Balkhash is in Kazakhstan; its western half is freshwater while its eastern half is saline.
32.tq: Watch for the reversal trap in two-part geographical comparisons.
xs: **Lake Balkhash** has a **fresh western half** and a **saline eastern half**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses it; the lake is in **Kazakhstan**.
xa: Kazakhstan also borders the **Caspian** (largest lake, saline).
**Lake Van** (Turkiye) is the largest **alkaline** lake.
**Baikal** (Russia, Siberia) is the deepest.

32.s:
Consider the following statements about the lakes of the Great Rift Valley:
1. They form a chain and are mostly freshwater.
2. Lake Malawi lies at the northern end of the chain.
3. Tanganyika, Albert, Edward and Kivu lie in the western branch.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Statement 1 is correct: they form a chain and are mostly freshwater. Statement 2 is wrong: Lake Malawi is at the southern end. Statement 3 is correct: Tanganyika, Albert, Edward and Kivu are in the western (Albertine) branch. Hence 1 and 3 only.
32.tq: Malawi = southern end; Victoria sits between the branches, not in the rift.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(3)** is the answer.
Statement 1: Rift Valley lakes form a **chain** and are **mostly freshwater**. Correct.
Statement 2: wrong; **Lake Malawi** is at the **southern end**.
Statement 3: **Tanganyika, Albert, Edward, Kivu** are in the **western (Albertine)** branch. Correct.
xa: **Kivu** lies on the **DRC-Rwanda** border.
**Lake Victoria** lies **between** the two branches.
APPSC-G1 **2024** key: statements **I-III** true.

32.s: Which one of the following statements about Lake Victoria is correct?
o: It lies in the western branch of the Great Rift Valley.
It lies between the two branches of the Great Rift Valley.
It is located entirely within the Eastern Rift.
It forms the southern end of the western branch.
32.x: Lake Victoria lies between the eastern and western branches of the Great Rift Valley rather than within either rift branch.
32.tq: Distinguish “between the branches” from “within a branch.”
xs: **Lake Victoria** lies **between the two branches** of the Great Rift Valley, so option **(2)** is correct.
It is **not in the rift**; the western branch holds **Tanganyika, Albert, Edward, Kivu**.
xa: **Lake Malawi** is at the **southern end** of the chain.
Victoria is the **2nd-largest freshwater lake** (Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania).
**Turkana** is in the **Eastern Rift**.

32.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lonar—largest freshwater lake of Andhra Pradesh
Chilika—largest freshwater lake of Andhra Pradesh
32.x: Chilika in Odisha is India’s largest lake. Kolleru is Andhra Pradesh’s largest freshwater lake, while Lonar is a meteorite-crater lake.
32.tq: Separate national, state-level and geological classifications before matching.
xs: **Chilika — largest lake of India** is correct, so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Kolleru** (AP) is the **largest freshwater lake**; **Lonar** is the **meteorite crater** lake.
xa: Chilika is in **Odisha**.
**Pulicat** (Tirupati district) is the **2nd largest brackish lagoon** after Chilika.
Pulicat is separated from the sea by **Sriharikota**.

32.s:
Consider the following statements about the Great Lakes of North America:
1. Lake Ontario is the smallest of them by area.
2. Lake Ontario is drained by the St Lawrence to the Atlantic.
3. Lake Ontario is the only Great Lake lying wholly in the USA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ontario is the smallest (19,011 sq km) and easternmost. Statement 2 is correct: it is drained by the St Lawrence to the Atlantic. Statement 3 is wrong: only Lake Michigan lies wholly in the USA. Hence 1 and 2 only.
32.tq: Michigan = only Great Lake wholly in the USA.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Statement 1: **Ontario** is the **smallest** by area (**19,011 sq km**). Correct.
Statement 2: it is drained by the **St Lawrence** to the **Atlantic**. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; **only Michigan** lies wholly in the USA.
xa: Ontario is also the **easternmost** Great Lake.
Shore cities: **Toronto, Hamilton, Rochester**.
A US order renamed Lake Ontario **"Lake America"** (**28 Aug 2026**).

32.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Lake Ontario:
1. It is the easternmost of the Great Lakes.
2. It is fed by the Niagara River.
3. It is connected to Lake Erie by the Welland Canal, which bypasses Niagara Falls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
32.x: All three statements are correct. Lake Ontario is easternmost, receives the Niagara River from Lake Erie, and is linked to Erie by the Welland Canal, which bypasses Niagara Falls.
32.tq: Check each statement against the lake's position, inflow and artificial navigation link.
xs: **All three statements are correct**, so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is the answer.
Ontario is **easternmost** and fed by the **Niagara River** (from Erie).
The **Welland Canal** links **Ontario-Erie**, bypassing **Niagara Falls**.
xa: Ontario is the **smallest** Great Lake (**19,011 sq km**).
It is drained by the **St Lawrence** to the Atlantic.
Order west to east: **Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario**.

32.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the Great Lakes of North America from west to east?
32.x: From west to east the Great Lakes are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario. Ontario is the easternmost and smallest; the other orders misplace Michigan, Huron or Erie.
32.tq: West to east: Superior-Michigan-Huron-Erie-Ontario (SMHEO).
xs: West to east: **Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario**, so option **(3)** is correct.
The other orders misplace Michigan, Huron or Erie.
xa: **Ontario** is the easternmost and smallest (**19,011 sq km**).
**Superior** is the largest freshwater lake by area.
Links: **St Marys** (Superior-Huron), **Mackinac** (Michigan-Huron), **Detroit** (Huron-Erie), **Welland** (Ontario-Erie).

32.s: The Dead Sea, shared by Jordan and Israel, is approximately how far below sea level at its lowest point on land?
32.x: The Dead Sea is the lowest point on land and lies about 1,385 feet below sea level according to the cited figure.
32.tq: Use the distinctive numerical figure and reject altered-value distractors.
xs: The **Dead Sea** lies about **1,385 feet** below sea level, the **lowest point on land**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It is shared by **Jordan and Israel**.
xa: It is fed by the **Jordan** river (Jordan Valley, rift).
Jordan's sole port is on the **Gulf of Aqaba** (Red Sea).
The **Red Sea** has **no major river** inflow.

32.s: Which statement regarding the Red Sea is correct?
o: It receives the Volga and Ural rivers and borders five Caspian states.
It has no major river inflow, and the Dahlak Archipelago lies near its Eritrean coast.
It is bordered by the United Kingdom and France and receives the Rhine.
It is drained mainly by the Danube and Dnieper.
32.x: The Red Sea has no major river inflow, and the Dahlak Archipelago is associated with Eritrea on its western side.
32.tq: Use the absence-of-a-major-river exception and the location clue together.
xs: The **Red Sea** has **no major river** inflow, and the **Dahlak archipelago** (Eritrea) lies in it, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Volga and Ural** feed the **Caspian**; **Rhine** feeds the **North Sea**; **Danube and Dnieper** feed the **Black Sea**.
xa: Red Sea borders: **Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea, Saudi Arabia, Yemen**.
The **Gulf of Aqaba** holds **Jordan's sole port**.
**Socotra** archipelago (UNESCO site) belongs to **Yemen**.

32.s: Which set contains only rivers that flow into the Mediterranean Sea?
32.x: The Nile, Rhone, Po and Ebro are listed as rivers flowing into the Mediterranean Sea.
32.tq: Classify each river by its mouth before selecting the complete set.
xs: The **Nile, Rhone, Po and Ebro** flow into the **Mediterranean**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Rhine, Elbe, Thames** go to the **North Sea**, **Vistula** to the **Baltic**; **Volga, Ural** go to the **Caspian**.
xa: **Gibraltar** (Spain-Morocco) links the Mediterranean and the **Atlantic**.
The Mediterranean borders **S Europe, N Africa and the Levant**.
The **Mississippi** drains into the **Gulf of Mexico**; the **Mekong** into the South China Sea.

32.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
32.x: The Black Sea receives the Danube, Dnieper and Dniester. The Jordan flows into the Dead Sea, while the Volga flows into the Caspian Sea.
32.tq: Find the option containing rivers belonging to two different seas.
xs: **Black Sea — Jordan and Volga** is wrong, so option **(2)** is the answer.
The Black Sea receives the **Danube, Dnieper, Dniester**; the **Jordan** feeds the **Dead Sea**; the **Volga** feeds the **Caspian**.
The rest are right: **Baltic** = Vistula, Oder; **Caspian** = Volga, Ural; **North Sea** = Rhine, Elbe, Thames.
xa: The **Baltic** is **brackish**.
The Black Sea is **meromictic**, salinity **17-18 ppt**.

32.s:
Consider the following statements about the Black Sea:
1. It is a meromictic sea.
2. Its salinity is about 17-18 ppt.
3. Iran is one of its bordering countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Black Sea is meromictic (its layers do not mix). Statement 2 is correct: its salinity is about 17-18 ppt. Statement 3 is wrong: it is bordered by Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia; Iran borders the Caspian. Hence 1 and 2 only.
32.tq: Black Sea neighbours: Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia, Georgia - no Iran.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Statement 1: the Black Sea is **meromictic**. Correct.
Statement 2: its salinity is **17-18 ppt**. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; its borders are **Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia, Georgia**; **Iran** borders the Caspian.
xa: It receives the **Danube, Dnieper, Dniester**.
The **Bosphorus** links it to the **Sea of Marmara**; the **Kerch** Strait to the **Sea of Azov**.

32.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic (Caribbean) with the Pacific and uses a lock system.
2. The Kiel Canal connects the North Sea with the Baltic Sea.
3. The Kiel Canal lies in Denmark.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Statement 1 is correct: Panama links the Atlantic (Caribbean) and Pacific with locks. Statement 2 is correct: Kiel links the North Sea and Baltic. Statement 3 is wrong: the Kiel Canal is in Germany. Hence 1 and 2 only.
32.tq: Kiel = Germany, North Sea-Baltic.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Statement 1: the **Panama Canal** links the **Atlantic (Caribbean)** and **Pacific** with a **lock system**. Correct.
Statement 2: the **Kiel Canal** links the **North Sea** and **Baltic**. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; the Kiel Canal is in **Germany**.
xa: The **Welland Canal** links Lakes **Ontario and Erie**.
The **Baltic** receives the **Vistula** and **Oder**.
**Greenland**, the largest island, belongs to **Denmark**.

32.s: Which strait connects the Andaman Sea, an arm of the Indian Ocean, with the South China Sea, an arm of the Pacific Ocean?
32.x: The Malacca Strait, between Malaysia and Indonesia, connects the Andaman Sea with the South China Sea.
32.tq: Use the connected-water-bodies method for identifying straits.
xs: The **Malacca Strait** (Malaysia-Indonesia) links the **Andaman Sea** with the **South China Sea**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Gibraltar** = Mediterranean-Atlantic; **Dardanelles** = Aegean-Marmara; **Bering** = Arctic-Pacific.
xa: **Hormuz** (Iran-Oman) links the **Persian Gulf** and **Gulf of Oman**.
**Indonesia** is the largest archipelagic country.
The **Mekong** also drains into the **South China Sea**.

32.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Strait of Gibraltar, between Spain and Morocco, connects the Mediterranean with the Atlantic.
2. The Kerch Strait, between Russia and Ukraine, connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov.
3. The Bering Strait connects the Arctic Ocean with the Atlantic Ocean.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Statement 1 is correct: Gibraltar (Spain-Morocco) links the Mediterranean and Atlantic. Statement 2 is correct: Kerch (Russia-Ukraine) links the Black Sea and Sea of Azov. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bering Strait (Russia-USA) links the Arctic with the Pacific. Hence 1 and 2 only.
32.tq: Bering = Arctic-Pacific, between Russia and Alaska.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Statement 1: **Gibraltar** (Spain-Morocco) links the **Mediterranean** and **Atlantic**. Correct.
Statement 2: **Kerch** (Russia-Ukraine) links the **Black Sea** and **Sea of Azov**. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; the **Bering** Strait (Russia-USA) links the **Arctic** and **Pacific**.
xa: **Bosphorus** = Black Sea-Marmara; **Dardanelles** = Aegean-Marmara (Turkiye).
**Malacca** links the Andaman Sea and South China Sea.
The **Kiel Canal** links the North Sea and Baltic.

32.s: Which of the following correctly represents the connections made by the Bosphorus and Dardanelles, respectively?
o: Aegean Sea–Black Sea; Marmara Sea–Mediterranean Sea
Black Sea–Marmara Sea; Aegean Sea–Marmara Sea
Black Sea–Sea of Azov; Aegean Sea–Black Sea
Marmara Sea–Red Sea; Black Sea–Aegean Sea
32.x: The Bosphorus connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara, while the Dardanelles connects the Aegean Sea with the Sea of Marmara.
32.tq: Discriminate between two closely related Turkish straits by their exact endpoints.
xs: **Bosphorus** = **Black Sea-Marmara**; **Dardanelles** = **Aegean-Marmara**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Both straits are in **Turkiye**.
**Black Sea-Sea of Azov** is the **Kerch** Strait.
xa: The **Taurus** range lies in southern Turkiye.
**Lake Van** (Turkiye) is the largest alkaline lake.
**Gibraltar** links the Mediterranean and Atlantic.

32.s: The Strait of Hormuz, the world's key oil route, connects which of the following water bodies?
o: Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
Black Sea and Sea of Marmara
Andaman Sea and South China Sea
32.x: Hormuz, between Iran and Oman, links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman. The Bosphorus links the Black Sea and Marmara, and Malacca links the Andaman Sea and South China Sea; the Red Sea-Gulf of Aden link is not Hormuz.
32.tq: Hormuz = Persian Gulf to Gulf of Oman, Iran-Oman.
xs: **Hormuz** links the **Persian Gulf** and the **Gulf of Oman**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It lies between **Iran and Oman** and is the world's key oil route.
**Black Sea-Marmara** is the **Bosphorus**; **Andaman Sea-South China Sea** is **Malacca**.
xa: Hormuz crisis: Iran is **not party to UNCLOS**, but **transit passage** is binding customary law (**5 Sep 2026**).
The **Red Sea** has no major river inflow.
**Malacca** (Malaysia-Indonesia) links the **Andaman Sea** and the **South China Sea**.

32.s: Which of the following island–country pairs is NOT correctly matched?
32.x: Normandy is a region of France. Kyushu belongs to Japan, Sardinia to Italy and Mallorca to Spain.
32.tq: Use the country–region distinction to detect the swapped location.
xs: **Normandy — Italy** is wrong, so option **(1)** is the answer; Normandy is a region of **France**.
The others are correct: **Sardinia** = Italy; **Mallorca** (Balearics) = Spain; **Kyushu** = Japan.
xa: **Honshu** is also in **Japan**.
Largest islands: **Greenland** (Denmark), **New Guinea**, **Borneo**, **Madagascar**.
**Socotra** archipelago (UNESCO site) = **Yemen**; largest archipelagic country = **Indonesia**.

32.s: Socotra archipelago, recognised as a UNESCO site, belongs to which country?
32.x: The Socotra archipelago is associated with Yemen and is identified as a UNESCO site.
32.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring countries of the Arabian Sea region.
xs: The **Socotra archipelago** (UNESCO site) belongs to **Yemen**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Eritrea** has the **Dahlak archipelago** in the Red Sea; Oman lies on the **Strait of Hormuz**.
xa: Yemen also borders the **Red Sea**, with Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea and Saudi Arabia.
Largest islands: **Greenland** (Denmark), New Guinea, Borneo, Madagascar.
Largest archipelagic country: **Indonesia**.

32.s:
Arrange the following islands in descending order of their geographical size:
A. Madagascar
B. Greenland
C. Borneo
D. New Guinea
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
32.x: The order is Greenland, New Guinea, Borneo and Madagascar.
32.tq: Apply the size hierarchy and identify the largest island first.
xs: Descending order: **Greenland, New Guinea, Borneo, Madagascar** = **B, D, C, A**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) puts New Guinea above Greenland; option (3) puts Borneo above New Guinea.
xa: **Greenland** belongs to **Denmark**.
**Indonesia** is the largest archipelagic country.
**Kyushu** and **Honshu** are Japanese islands; **Sardinia** is Italian.

32.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Greenland, the largest island, belongs to Denmark.
2. Indonesia is the largest archipelagic country.
3. Madagascar is larger than Borneo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Statement 1 is correct: Greenland (Denmark) is the largest island. Statement 2 is correct: Indonesia is the largest archipelagic country. Statement 3 is wrong: the order is Greenland, New Guinea, Borneo, Madagascar, so Borneo is larger. Hence 1 and 2 only.
32.tq: Island order: Greenland > New Guinea > Borneo > Madagascar.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Statement 1: **Greenland** (Denmark) is the largest island. Correct.
Statement 2: **Indonesia** is the largest archipelagic country. Correct.
Statement 3: wrong; the order is Greenland, New Guinea, **Borneo**, **Madagascar**, so Borneo is larger.
xa: **Mallorca** (Balearics) belongs to **Spain**.
**Socotra** archipelago = **Yemen**.
**Normandy** is a region of **France**.

32.s: With reference to the Strait of Hormuz crisis, which statement is correct?
o: Iran is a party to UNCLOS and transit passage is treaty law only.
Iran is not a party to UNCLOS and transit passage has no legal force.
Transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz is governed exclusively by the World Bank.
Iran is not a party to UNCLOS, but transit passage remains binding as customary international law.
32.x: Iran is not a party to UNCLOS; nevertheless, the principle of transit passage is binding as customary international law.
32.tq: Separate treaty membership from rules recognised as customary international law.
xs: **Iran is not a party to UNCLOS**, but **transit passage** remains binding as **customary international law**, so option **(4)** is correct.
Options (1) and (2) get Iran's status or the legal force wrong; the World Bank has no role.
xa: Date of the Hormuz crisis note: **5 Sep 2026**.
**Hormuz** (Iran-Oman) links the **Persian Gulf** and **Gulf of Oman**; world's key oil route.
**Malacca** (Malaysia-Indonesia) links the Andaman Sea and South China Sea.

32.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Pulicat Lagoon is correct?
o: It is the largest brackish lagoon in India and is separated from the sea by Chilika.
It is a freshwater lagoon fed only by the Godavari.
It is the second largest brackish lagoon after Chilika and is separated from the sea by Sriharikota.
It lies entirely within the Krishna delta and has no sea barrier.

Statement 3: wrong; the **Durand Line** dates to **1893**; the **Shimla Convention 1914** produced the **McMahon Line**.
xa: The Durand Line was a **buffer vs Russia** (British India-Afghanistan).

**Rayalaseema** is bordered by **Tamil Nadu** in the **south**, **Karnataka** in the **west** and **Telangana** in the **north**.
xa: **Andhra Pradesh** is bounded by **Chhattisgarh** and **Odisha** in the north and the **Bay of Bengal** in the east.
**Karnataka** borders the most southern states — **Goa**, **Maharashtra**, **Telangana**, **AP**, **TN**, **Kerala**.
The Puducherry enclave **Yanam** lies within **Andhra Pradesh** (Godavari delta).

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the dimensions of the Himalayas:
1. They cover an area of about 15 lakh sq km.
2. They are about 500 km wide in Kashmir and narrow to about 200 km in Arunachal Pradesh.
3. They extend for about 2,414 km from Nanga Parbat to Namcha Barwa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 3 is correct: the arc runs about 2,414 km from Nanga Parbat (west) to Namcha Barwa (east). Statement 2 is correct: the width falls from about 500 km in Kashmir to 200 km in Arunachal. Statement 1 is wrong: the Himalayas cover about 5 lakh sq km. So '3 only' misses statement 2, and options with statement 1 are wrong.
34.tq: 2,414 km long; wide in Kashmir, narrow in Arunachal; ~5 lakh sq km.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: the Himalayas cover about **5 lakh sq km**, not 15 lakh.
Statement 2: the width is **500 km in Kashmir** and **200 km in Arunachal**.
Statement 3: the length is **2,414 km** from **Nanga Parbat to Namcha Barwa**.
xa: IYB 2026 gives the length as "about **2,400 km**", depth **240-320 km**.
The Himalayas are **wider in Kashmir**, **narrower in the North-East**; folds of Himadri are **asymmetrical**.
Uplift ran through the **Tertiary** (**Eocene to Pliocene**, ~**60-7 million years ago**).
**Western end** = **Nanga Parbat**; **eastern end** = **Namcha Barwa**.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the structure of the Himalayas:
1. The folds of the Himadri are asymmetrical.
2. The steep slope of the Himalayas faces the plains.
3. The gentler slope faces Tibet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. The Himadri has asymmetrical folds; the Himalayan slope towards the plains is steeper, while the Tibetan side is gentler.
34.tq: Test the complete structural pattern and avoid reversing the two slopes.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the folds of the **Himadri** are **asymmetrical** — correct.
Statement 2: the **steep slope** faces the **plains** — correct.
Statement 3: the **gentle slope** faces **Tibet** — correct.
xa: The **Himadri core** is **granite**.
APPSC-G1 2024 key: the Himalayas are **wider in Kashmir**, **narrower in the North-East**.
**Himadri** is the **loftiest and oldest** Himalayan range, averaging **over 6,000 m**.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the origin of the Himalayas:
1. They were uplifted from Tethys sediments during the Tertiary (Eocene to Pliocene).
2. The Indian plate collided with the Eurasian plate about 4-5 crore years ago.
3. The Himalayas have stopped rising.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 1 is correct: uplift from Tethys sediments, Eocene to Pliocene (~60-7 million years ago). Statement 2 is correct: India-Eurasia collision about 4-5 crore years ago. Statement 3 is wrong: the Himalayas are still rising. Hence 1 and 2 only.
34.tq: Collision continues, so the Himalayas still rise.
xs: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: uplift of **Tethys sediments** in the **Tertiary**, **Eocene to Pliocene** (~**60-7 million years** ago).
Statement 2 correct: the **Indian plate** collided with **Eurasia** about **4-5 crore years** ago.
Statement 3 wrong: the Himalayas are **still rising**.
xa: The **Trans-Himalayas** (Tibetan Himalaya) were formed **before** the Himalayas.
The **Shiwalik** consists of simple **'Jura'-type folds** of river deposits.
Length **2,414 km**; area about **5 lakh sq km**.

34.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the three longitudinal parallel ranges of the Himalayas?
34.x: The three principal longitudinal parallel ranges are Himadri or Greater Himalaya, Himachal or Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik or Outer Himalaya.
34.tq: Separate the longitudinal-range classification from the regional west-to-east classification.
xs: The three longitudinal parallel ranges are **Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik** — option **(3)**.
**Himadri** = Greater, **Himachal** = Lesser, **Shiwalik** = Outer Himalaya.
**Punjab, Kumaon, Nepal** (and Assam) are **regional** divisions; **Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar** are **Trans-Himalayan** ranges.
xa: **Northernmost** of the three = **Himadri**, not the Shiwalik (APPSC-GS 2025).
**Himadri**: loftiest and oldest, average **over 6,000 m**.
**Shiwalik**: youngest and narrowest, width **15-50 km**, average **1,300 m**.
**Purvanchal** is one of the **3** northern mountain groups, not a parallel range.

34.s: Approximately what proportion of India's area is occupied by plains according to the stated relief-share classification?
34.x: Plains form the largest relief division of India and account for about 43 percent of the country’s area.
34.tq: Choose the precise approximate share and avoid shifting the stated percentage by ten points.
xs: **Plains** occupy about **43 percent** of India's area — option **(3)**.
They form the **largest** relief portion of India (APPSC-GS 2024 key).
xa: **Shiwalik** debris helped build the **Indo-Gangetic plain**.
The Himalayas cover about **5 lakh sq km**.
The Himalayas form India's **northern boundary** and a **climatic barrier**.

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the parallel ranges of the Himalayas:
1. The Karakoram is part of the Trans-Himalaya.
2. The Ladakh Range continues eastwards into Tibet as the Kailash Range.
3. The Zaskar Range lies south of the Karakoram and is separated from the Pir Panjal by the Kashmir Valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. Karakoram and Zaskar are Trans-Himalayan ranges, Ladakh continues as Kailash in Tibet, and the Kashmir Valley separates Zaskar from Pir Panjal.
34.tq: Check each range by its position and continuation before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Karakoram** is a **Trans-Himalayan** range (home of **K2**) — correct.
Statement 2: the **Ladakh** range continues into Tibet as the **Kailash** range — correct.
Statement 3: **Zaskar** is Trans-Himalayan; the **Kashmir Valley** separates **Pir Panjal** from it — correct.
xa: Karakoram glaciers: **Siachen, Rimo, Baltoro**.
The **Trans-Himalayas** were formed **before** the Himalayas.
**Ladakh Plateau** is the **highest plateau** in India.

34.s:
Arrange the following Himalayan ranges from north to south:
A. Himachal
B. Karakoram
C. Shiwalik
D. Himadri
E. Ladakh
34.x: From north to south, the sequence is Karakoram, Ladakh, Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik.
34.tq: Fix the northernmost Trans-Himalayan range first, then move southward through the three principal Himalayan ranges.
xs: North to south: **Karakoram, Ladakh, Himadri, Himachal, Shiwalik** — option **(1) B, E, D, A, C**.
Karakoram, Ladakh and Zaskar are **Trans-Himalayan**, so they lie north of the **Himadri**.
Of the three parallel ranges, **Himadri** is northernmost and **Shiwalik** is outermost.
xa: **Himadri** averages **over 6,000 m**; **Shiwalik** averages **1,300 m**.
**Himachal** includes **Pir Panjal**, **Dhauladhar**, **Mussoorie** and **Mahabharat** (Nepal).
**Zaskar** lies between Ladakh and the Himadri; the **Kashmir Valley** separates it from Pir Panjal.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the Himalayan ranges:
1. The Himadri is the loftiest and oldest range and has a granite core.
2. The Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest range, averaging about 1,300 m.
3. The Shiwalik is the northernmost of the three parallel ranges.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Himadri is loftiest, oldest, over 6,000 m on average, with a granite core. Statement 2 is correct: the Shiwalik is youngest and narrowest (15-50 km), about 1,300 m. Statement 3 is wrong: the northernmost of the three is the Himadri; the Shiwalik is the outermost (southernmost). Hence 1 and 2 only.
34.tq: North to south: Himadri, Himachal, Shiwalik.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Himadri** is the **loftiest and oldest** range, with a **granite** core.
Statement 2 correct: **Shiwalik** is the **youngest and narrowest**, averaging **1,300 m**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **northernmost** parallel range is the **Himadri**, not the Shiwalik (APPSC-GS 2025).
xa: **Shiwalik** width: **15-50 km**; simple **'Jura'-type folds** of river deposits.
**Himadri** averages **over 6,000 m**; its folds are **asymmetrical**.
⚠ **Nanda Devi** and **Trisul** belong to the **Greater Himalaya**, not the Middle Himalaya.

34.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Himachal or Lesser Himalaya?
o: Pir Panjal — Jhelum-Beas sector — approximately 300 km
34.x: Pir Panjal is a major range of the Himachal Himalaya extending for about 300 km in the Jhelum-Beas sector. Dhauladhar, Mussoorie and Mahabharat are also associated with the Lesser Himalaya.
34.tq: Pair the range with the correct parallel belt and approximate extent.
xs: **Pir Panjal** of the Himachal (Lesser) Himalaya spans the **Jhelum-Beas** sector for about **300 km** — option **(1)**.
**Karakoram** and **Ladakh** are **Trans-Himalayan**, not Himachal ranges.
**Mahabharat** (Nepal) belongs to the **Himachal**, not the Shiwalik.
xa: Other Himachal ranges: **Dhauladhar**, **Mussoorie**, **Mahabharat**.
Pir Panjal passes: **Banihal** (**2,833 m**, Jammu-Srinagar) and **Rohtang** (**3,978 m**, Kullu-Lahaul-Spiti).
The **Kashmir Valley** separates **Pir Panjal** from the **Zaskar**.

34.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Trans-Himalaya?
o: It was formed after the main Himalayan ranges and contains the lowest plateau of India.
It was formed before the Himalayas, and the Ladakh Plateau is the highest plateau in India.
It lies south of the Himadri and is younger than the Shiwalik.
It consists only of the Shiwalik and Himachal ranges.
34.x: The Trans-Himalaya formed before the Himalayas. The Ladakh Plateau is regarded as the highest plateau in India.
34.tq: Use the age comparison and the distinctive superlative associated with the Ladakh Plateau.
xs: The Trans-Himalaya was **formed before the Himalayas**, and the **Ladakh Plateau** is the **highest plateau in India** — option **(2)**.
It lies **north** of the Himadri, so it is not south of it nor younger than the Shiwalik.
It comprises **Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar** — not the Shiwalik and Himachal.
xa: The Trans-Himalaya is also called the **Tibetan Himalaya**.
**K2** (Godwin Austen) in the Karakoram is the **2nd highest** peak in the world.
The **Ladakh** range continues into Tibet as the **Kailash** range.

34.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the standard west-to-east regional division of the Himalayas with their bounding rivers?
o: Punjab Himalaya—Indus to Sutlej; Kumaon Himalaya—Sutlej to Kali; Nepal Himalaya—Kali to Teesta; Assam Himalaya—Teesta to Dihang
Punjab Himalaya—Indus to Beas; Kumaon Himalaya—Beas to Kali; Nepal Himalaya—Kali to Teesta; Assam Himalaya—Teesta to Dihang
Punjab Himalaya—Jhelum to Sutlej; Kumaon Himalaya—Sutlej to Gandak; Nepal Himalaya—Gandak to Teesta; Assam Himalaya—Teesta to Lohit
Punjab Himalaya—Indus to Kali; Kumaon Himalaya—Kali to Teesta; Nepal Himalaya—Teesta to Dihang; Assam Himalaya—Dihang to Lohit
34.x: The standard Burrard boundaries are Indus–Sutlej, Sutlej–Kali, Kali–Teesta and Teesta–Dihang. The Punjab Himalaya is sometimes extended up to the Beas in some accounts, but Sutlej is the standard boundary.
34.tq: Start from the sure river pair and eliminate options that shift the regional boundaries.
xs: Standard divisions: Punjab **Indus-Sutlej**, Kumaon **Sutlej-Kali**, Nepal **Kali-Teesta**, Assam **Teesta-Dihang** — option **(1)**.
These are the **Burrard** boundaries, running west to east.
⚠ Some notes end the Punjab Himalaya at the **Beas**, but the standard boundary is the **Sutlej**.
xa: Punjab Himalaya peaks: **Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi, Haramosh**; mainly **sedimentary** rocks.
Kumaon: **Nanda Devi, Trisul, Panchchuli**; lakes **Nainital, Bhimtal**.
Nepal Himalaya: **Everest, Kanchenjunga, Dhaulagiri**.
Assam Himalaya ends at the **Namcha Barwa** knee-bend.

34.s: The Punjab Himalaya is chiefly associated with which of the following groups of peaks?
34.x: Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi and Haramosh are prominent peaks of the Punjab or Kashmir-Himachal Himalaya.
34.tq: Use the regional-division cluster to associate each division with its characteristic peaks.
xs: The Punjab Himalaya holds **Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi and Haramosh** — option **(3)**.
**Nanda Devi, Trisul, Panchchuli** are **Kumaon** peaks; **Everest, Kanchenjunga, Dhaulagiri** are **Nepal** Himalaya peaks.
**Namcha Barwa** is Assam Himalaya; **Kailash** is Trans-Himalaya.
xa: Punjab Himalaya lies between the **Indus and Sutlej**; mainly **sedimentary** rocks.
**Nanga Parbat** (PoK) marks the **western end** of the Himalayas.
⚠ Some notes end the Punjab Himalaya at the **Beas**; standard = **Sutlej**.

34.s: The Himalayan range takes a sharp knee-bend near Namcha Barwa at the
34.x: The Himalaya makes a knee-bend at the Dihang gorge near Namcha Barwa and then turns southwards as the Purvanchal hills.
34.tq: Associate the distinctive geomorphic change in direction with its exact gorge and peak.
xs: The Himalaya makes its knee-bend at the **Dihang gorge** near **Namcha Barwa** — option **(4)**.
After the bend it turns **south** as the **Purvanchal** hills.
**Nathu La** is a pass in Sikkim, not a gorge; the **Sutlej** and **Kali** are boundaries of regional divisions.
xa: Purvanchal heights range **500-3,000 m**.
The **Assam Himalaya** spans **Teesta-Dihang (Brahmaputra)**.
**Namcha Barwa** (Tibet, China) is the **eastern end** of the Himalayas.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about Himalayan peaks:
1. Kamet is a peak of the Himadri in the Kumaon (Garhwal) Himalaya, Uttarakhand.
2. Nanda Devi belongs to the Middle (Lesser) Himalaya.
3. Dhaulagiri lies in the Nepal Himalaya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kamet is in the Himadri, Kumaon/Garhwal, Uttarakhand. Statement 2 is wrong: Nanda Devi belongs to the Greater Himalaya (Himadri), a common trap in notes that place it in the Middle Himalaya. Statement 3 is correct: Dhaulagiri is in the Nepal Himalaya. Hence 1 and 3 only.
34.tq: Nanda Devi and Trisul = Greater Himalaya, not Middle.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Kamet** is in the **Himadri**, **Kumaon (Garhwal)**, Uttarakhand.
Statement 2 wrong: ⚠ **Nanda Devi** belongs to the **Greater Himalaya**, not the Middle Himalaya.
Statement 3 correct: **Dhaulagiri** lies in the **Nepal Himalaya**.
xa: **Trisul** is also a **Greater Himalaya** peak, often wrongly put in the Middle Himalaya.
**Nanda Devi** = highest peak **wholly in India**; **Kanchenjunga** = highest in India.
**Kailash** lies in the **Trans-Himalaya**, Tibet.

34.s: Which of the following statements regarding Kanchenjunga is correct?
o: It is wholly within Nepal and belongs to the Punjab Himalaya.
It marks the western end of the Assam Himalaya in Tibet.
It lies in the Himadri on the India-Nepal boundary and is the highest peak in India.
It is located in the Karakoram under Pakistan-China control.
34.x: Kanchenjunga belongs to the Himadri and lies on the India-Nepal boundary. It is the highest peak in India, although it is not wholly within India; the highest peak wholly in India is Nanda Devi.
34.tq: Distinguish “highest peak wholly in India” from the highest peak associated with India’s claim.
xs: **Kanchenjunga** lies in the **Himadri** on the **India-Nepal** boundary and is the **highest peak in India** — option **(3)**.
It belongs to the **Nepal Himalaya**, not the Punjab Himalaya; it is not in the Karakoram.
The Assam Himalaya's end is **Namcha Barwa**, not Kanchenjunga.
xa: ⚠ Highest **wholly in India** = **Nanda Devi** (Uttarakhand).
**K2** (Godwin Austen) is the **2nd highest** in the world.
Highest range of Assam: **Barail**.

34.s: Godwin Austen, commonly known as K2, is correctly described as
o: a peak of the Himadri, 8,586 metres high, wholly within Uttarakhand
a peak of the Nepal Himalaya, 8,611 metres high, wholly within Nepal
a peak of the Karakoram, 8,611 metres high, under Pakistan-China control and second highest in the world
a peak of the Assam Himalaya, 8,586 metres high, located in Tibet
34.x: Godwin Austen or K2 is 8,611 metres high and belongs to the Karakoram. It lies in territory under Pakistan-China control and is the world’s second-highest peak.
34.tq: Separate the peak’s height, range, political control and world ranking instead of relying on a single superlative.
xs: **K2** is a **Karakoram** peak, **8,611 m**, under **Pakistan/China** control and **2nd highest in the world** — option **(3)**.
India claims it; it is not in the Himadri, Nepal or Assam Himalaya.
xa: The **Karakoram** is a **Trans-Himalayan** range with the **Siachen, Rimo, Baltoro** glaciers.
**Kanchenjunga** = highest in India; **Nanda Devi** = highest wholly in India.
**Ladakh Plateau** is the highest plateau in India.

34.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nanga Parbat — eastern end of Assam Himalaya — China
Namcha Barwa — eastern end of Assam Himalaya — Tibet
Dhaulagiri — western end of Punjab Himalaya — Pakistan
34.x: Namcha Barwa marks the eastern end of the Assam Himalaya and is located in Tibet, China. Nanga Parbat marks the western end of the Himalayan arc in the Punjab Himalaya.
34.tq: Use the western-end/eastern-end contrast to eliminate the swapped peak-location pairs.
xs: **Namcha Barwa** marks the **eastern end** of the **Assam Himalaya** in **Tibet** — option **(2)**.
**Nanga Parbat** is the **western end** (PoK, Pakistan), not the eastern end.
**Dhaulagiri** is in the **Nepal Himalaya**; **Kailash** is in the **Trans-Himalaya** (Tibet).
xa: The Himalaya bends at the **Dihang gorge** near Namcha Barwa and turns south as **Purvanchal**.
Length from Nanga Parbat to Namcha Barwa: **2,414 km**.
Assam Himalaya: **Teesta to Dihang (Brahmaputra)**.

34.s: The Kumaon Himalaya is particularly associated with which of the following glaciers?
34.x: Pindari, Milam and Kafni glaciers are associated with the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand.
34.tq: Test a distinctive list through direct recall rather than confusing it with Trans-Himalayan glaciers.
xs: The Kumaon Himalaya has the **Pindari, Milam and Kafni** glaciers — option **(2)**.
**Siachen, Rimo, Baltoro** are **Karakoram** glaciers.
**Gangotri** is in the **Greater Himalaya**, source of the **Bhagirathi**.
xa: Kumaon lies between the **Sutlej and Kali** in **Uttarakhand**.
Kumaon peaks: **Nanda Devi, Trisul, Panchchuli**.
Kumaon lakes: **Nainital, Bhimtal**.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about glaciers:
1. Siachen Glacier is situated in the Karakoram Range, in the Nubra region.
2. Siachen marks the northern limit of Ladakh.
3. Baltoro, Biafo and Hispar glaciers are located in Gilgit-Baltistan in the Karakoram region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. Siachen lies in the Karakoram's Nubra region and marks Ladakh's northern limit, while Baltoro, Biafo and Hispar are in the Karakoram sector of Gilgit-Baltistan.
34.tq: Group glaciers by their range and position before evaluating the statements.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Siachen** is in the **Karakoram (Nubra)** — correct.
Statement 2: Siachen marks the **northern limit of Ladakh** — correct (IYB 2026).
Statement 3: **Baltoro, Biafo, Hispar** lie in **Gilgit-Baltistan (PoK)** in the Karakoram — correct.
xa: **Rimo** is another Karakoram glacier.
**Gangotri** (Greater Himalaya) is the source of the **Bhagirathi** at **Gaumukh**.
Kumaon glaciers: **Pindari, Milam, Kafni**.

34.s: Gangotri Glacier is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Pir Panjal Range and source of the Chenab
Kumaon Range and source of the Mandakini
Greater Himalaya and source of the Bhagirathi
34.x: Gangotri Glacier is located in the Greater Himalaya of Uttarakhand and is the source of the Bhagirathi at Gaumukh.
34.tq: Match the glacier with both its range and its associated river source.
xs: **Gangotri** lies in the **Greater Himalaya** and is the **source of the Bhagirathi** — option **(4)**.
Its snout is at **Gaumukh**, in **Uttarakhand**.
**Nubra** is the Karakoram region of **Siachen**, not Gangotri.
xa: Kumaon glaciers: **Pindari, Milam, Kafni**.
Karakoram glaciers: **Siachen, Rimo, Baltoro, Biafo, Hispar**.
⚠ **Nanda Devi** and **Kamet** (Uttarakhand) are also in the **Himadri**.

34.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of avalanche-prone Himalayan passes?
o: Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana
Banihal, Shipki La, Nathu La and Bomdi La
Lipulekh, Banihal, Zoji La and Shipki La
Rohtang, Nathu La, Bomdi La and Lipulekh
34.x: Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana are identified as avalanche-prone passes.
34.tq: Identify the complete group rather than selecting a familiar individual pass.
xs: The avalanche-prone passes are **Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana** — option **(1)**.
Each other group mixes in passes like **Banihal**, **Nathu La**, **Bomdi La** or **Lipulekh** that are not on this list.
xa: **Rohtang** (HP, **3,978 m**) is crossed by the **Atal Tunnel**.
**Nathu La** (Sikkim) links **Gangtok** with Tibet via the **Chumbi valley**.
**Lipulekh** (Uttarakhand) is on the **Kailash-Mansarovar** route.

34.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nathu La — Gangtok-Tibet route through the Chumbi Valley
34.x: Nathu La (Sikkim) links Gangtok with Tibet through the Chumbi Valley. The Gangtok-Tibet route is Nathu La's, not Zoji La's (Zoji La is the Srinagar-Leh pass); the Tawang-Lhasa route is Bomdi La's, not Shipki La's; and the Jammu-Srinagar route is Banihal's, not Bomdi La's.
34.tq: Start from the sure pass–route pair and eliminate the swapped connections.
xs: **Nathu La** (Sikkim) links **Gangtok** with Tibet through the **Chumbi Valley** — option **(2)**.
The **Tawang-Lhasa** route is **Bomdi La**'s (Arunachal Pradesh).
The **Jammu-Srinagar** route is **Banihal**'s (Pir Panjal).
xa: **Lipulekh** (Uttarakhand): **India-Nepal-China** tri-junction, **Kailash-Mansarovar** route.
**Rohtang** (HP): **Kullu - Lahaul-Spiti**.
**Zoji La** is avalanche-prone, with **Khardung La, Rohtang, Mana**.

34.s:
With reference to Himalayan passes, consider the following statements:
1. Rohtang Pass is located in Himachal Pradesh in the Pir Panjal Range and connects Kullu with Lahaul-Spiti.
2. Lipulekh Pass is located in Uttarakhand and forms part of the India-Nepal-China tri-junction route.
3. Bomdi La provides the route between Tawang and Lhasa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three are correct: Rohtang (Pir Panjal, HP, 3,978 m) links Kullu with Lahaul-Spiti; Lipulekh in Uttarakhand lies at the India-Nepal-China tri-junction on the Kailash-Mansarovar route; and Bomdi La in Arunachal Pradesh is on the Tawang-Lhasa route. Hence 1, 2 and 3.
34.tq: Split the options by verifying the pass, state and route combination.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: **Rohtang** (HP, **Pir Panjal**, **3,978 m**) links **Kullu - Lahaul-Spiti** — correct.
Statement 2: **Lipulekh** (Uttarakhand) is at the **India-Nepal-China tri-junction** — correct.
Statement 3: **Bomdi La** (Arunachal Pradesh) is on the **Tawang - Lhasa** route — correct.
xa: Lipulekh is on the **Kailash-Mansarovar** route.
**Atal Tunnel** runs under **Rohtang**.
**Nathu La** links **Gangtok** with Tibet via the **Chumbi valley**.

34.s: Which one of the following pairs of tunnels and passes is correctly matched?
34.x: The Atal Tunnel runs under the Rohtang Pass (Pir Panjal, HP), and the Jawahar Tunnel is at the Banihal Pass (Jammu-Srinagar). The other pairs swap the tunnels or name Nathu La, which has no such tunnel.
34.tq: Atal = Rohtang (HP); Jawahar = Banihal (J&K).
xs: The **Atal Tunnel** runs under the **Rohtang Pass** — option **(3)**.
The **Jawahar Tunnel** is at **Banihal**, so options pairing Atal with Banihal or Jawahar with Rohtang are swapped.
xa: **Banihal** (J&K, Pir Panjal, **2,833 m**) links **Jammu - Srinagar**.
**Rohtang** (HP, Pir Panjal, **3,978 m**) links **Kullu - Lahaul-Spiti**.
Rohtang is avalanche-prone, with **Zoji La, Khardung La, Mana**.

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the Purvanchal hills:
1. Patkai Bum lies in Arunachal Pradesh along the Myanmar border.
2. The Barail range links the Naga and Mizo hills and is the highest range of Assam.
3. The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills lie in Mizoram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: Statement 1 is correct: Patkai Bum is in Arunachal Pradesh on the Myanmar border. Statement 2 is correct: Barail links Naga and Mizo hills and is Assam's highest range. Statement 3 is wrong: Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills form the Shillong Plateau in Meghalaya; Mizoram has the Mizo (Lushai) hills. Hence 1 and 2 only.
34.tq: Garo-Khasi-Jaintia = Meghalaya (Shillong Plateau).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Patkai Bum** is in **Arunachal Pradesh**, running NE-SW along the **Myanmar** border.
Statement 2 correct: **Barail** links the **Naga and Mizo** hills and is the **highest range of Assam**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Garo, Khasi, Jaintia** are in **Meghalaya** (Shillong Plateau); Mizoram has the **Mizo (Lushai)** hills.
xa: **Naga Hills** — Nagaland; **Manipur Hills** — Manipur (**Loktak Lake**).
**Molasse basin** lies in **Mizoram** (soft unconsolidated deposits).
Purvanchal heights: **500-3,000 m**.

34.s: Which of the following statements about the Purvanchal hills is correct?
o: They extend from Kashmir to Himachal Pradesh without entering the North-East.
They are the southern continuation of the Himalayas after the Dihang knee-bend and generally range from 500 to 3,000 metres in height.
They are formed by a westward turn of the Himalayas at the Sutlej gorge.
They consist exclusively of the Shiwalik hills of Uttarakhand.
34.x: After the knee-bend near Namcha Barwa and the Dihang gorge, the Himalayas turn south as the Purvanchal hills. Their heights generally range from 500 to 3,000 metres.
34.tq: Apply the direction-change clue and the elevation range to identify the Purvanchal description.
xs: Purvanchal is the **southern continuation** of the Himalayas after the **Dihang knee-bend**, **500-3,000 m** high — option **(2)**.
The bend is near **Namcha Barwa** in the east, not at the Sutlej; the hills lie in the **North-East**.
xa: **Garo-Khasi-Jaintia** and **Naga** hills run **east-west**; **Mizo** and **Rakhine** run **north-south**.
**Barail** (Assam) links the Naga and Mizo hills.
Purvanchal is one of the **3** northern mountain groups.

34.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the alignment of the major Purvanchal hill groups?
o: Garo-Khasi-Jaintia run east-west, while the Mizo and Rakhine hills run north-south.
All the hill groups run exclusively west-east.
All the hill groups form a single east-west range without intersection.
Naga and Mizo hills run east-west, while Garo-Khasi-Jaintia run north-south.
34.x: The Garo-Khasi-Jaintia and Naga hills generally run east-west, joining the north-south Mizo and Rakhine hills. The specified contrast is correctly stated in option a.
34.tq: Compare the two directional alignments rather than treating all North-Eastern hills as one trend.
xs: **Garo-Khasi-Jaintia** (and Naga) hills run **east-west**, joining the **north-south Mizo and Rakhine** hills — option **(1)**.
So the hill groups do not all run one way; option **(4)** reverses the alignment.
xa: **Garo, Khasi, Jaintia** are in **Meghalaya** (Shillong Plateau).
**Mizo (Lushai) Hills** — **Mizoram**; **Patkai Bum** — Arunachal Pradesh.
The knee-bend is at the **Dihang gorge** near **Namcha Barwa**.

34.s: The Molasse Basin in the Indian Himalayan context is associated with
34.x: The Molasse Basin is associated with Mizoram and consists of soft, unconsolidated deposits.
34.tq: Pair the basin with its state and characteristic material.
xs: The **Molasse basin** is in **Mizoram**, of **soft unconsolidated deposits** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS 2025).
The **granite** core belongs to the **Himadri**, not the Molasse basin.
xa: **Mizoram** has the **Mizo (Lushai) Hills**.
**Barail** links the **Naga and Mizo** hills — highest range of **Assam**.
**Manipur Hills** hold **Loktak Lake**.

34.s:
The Himalayas are significant to India because they
1. form India's northern boundary.
2. act as a climatic barrier.
3. have contributed debris that helped build the Indo-Gangetic Plain through the Shiwalik system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. The Himalayas define India's northern boundary, act as a climatic barrier, and Shiwalik debris contributed to the formation of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
34.tq: Treat geographical significance as a cause-and-effect set rather than as isolated facts.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the Himalayas form India's **northern boundary** — correct.
Statement 2: they act as a **climatic barrier** — correct.
Statement 3: **Shiwalik** debris built the **Indo-Gangetic plain** — correct.
xa: **Plains** form about **43%** of India's area.
Western end **Nanga Parbat**; eastern end **Namcha Barwa**.
**Himadri** is oldest and loftiest vs **Shiwalik** youngest and narrowest.

34.s:
Arrange the following Himalayan peaks from east to west:
A. Mount Everest
B. Nanda Devi
C. Namcha Barwa
D. Kanchenjunga
34.x: From east to west the order is Namcha Barwa, Kanchenjunga, Everest, Nanda Devi, that is C, D, A, B.
34.tq: Picture the peaks along the Himalaya from east to west.
n: The east-to-west Himalayan peak order is Namcha Barwa, Kanchenjunga, Mount Everest, and Nanda Devi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Kanchenjunga is located in Sikkim and Nepal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Nanda Devi is located in Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Mount Everest is located in Nepal and Tibet. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Namcha Barwa is located in Tibet. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Mount Everest is located in Nepal and China’s Tibet region. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Kanchenjunga is located in Sikkim and Nepal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
xs: East to west the order is **Namcha Barwa, Kanchenjunga, Mount Everest, Nanda Devi** (**C, D, A, B**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Namcha Barwa** (Tibet, near **Arunachal Pradesh**) marks the **eastern end** of the Himalayas.
**Kanchenjunga** (**Sikkim–Nepal**) lies east of **Everest** (**Nepal–Tibet**), and **Nanda Devi** (**Uttarakhand**) lies furthest west.
xa: ⚠ **Kanchenjunga** = highest in India; **Nanda Devi** = highest **wholly** in India.
**Nanga Parbat** marks the **western end**.
⚠ **Nanda Devi** and **Trisul** belong to the **Greater Himalaya**, not the Middle Himalaya.

The **Barail** (Assam) links the **Naga** and **Mizo** hills.

Zoji La is on the Srinagar-Leh route. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Baralacha La is on the Manali-Leh route. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Shipki La is on the Himachal Pradesh-Tibet route. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]

**Baralacha La** — **Manali-Leh route**; **Shipki La** — **Himachal Pradesh-Tibet route** (**Kinnaur**).
xa: **Ladakh** passes: **Karakoram Pass**, **Zoji La**, **Tanglang La**, **Aghil**.
**Rohtang** (**3,978 m**) links **Manali** with **Lahaul-Spiti**; the **Atal Tunnel** runs under it.
**Avalanche-prone passes**: **Zoji La**, **Khardung La**, **Rohtang**, **Mana**.

34.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Lipulekh Pass is located in Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, and is associated with the India–China border and the Kailash–Mansarovar route.
Jelep La is in Sikkim and is associated with the Eastern Sikkim–Lhasa route.
Niti Pass is in Uttarakhand and is associated with the Uttarakhand–Myanmar border.

n: The location of Lipulekh Pass is Pithoragarh in Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Lipulekh Pass is on the India-China border. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Lipulekh Pass is on the Kailash-Mansarovar route. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Jelep La is a major pass in Sikkim. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Jelep La connects Eastern Sikkim and Lhasa. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Niti is a major pass in Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Niti Pass is on the Uttarakhand-Tibet route. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Nathu La is a major pass in Sikkim. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Nathu La is associated with India and China. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Nathu La is associated with the Chumbi Valley. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Lipulekh is a major pass in Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Niti Pass ... associated with the Uttarakhand–Myanmar border**" — so option **(3)** is the answer.
**Niti Pass** is on the **Uttarakhand-Tibet route**, not the Myanmar border.
**Lipulekh** (**Pithoragarh**) — **India-China border**, **Kailash-Mansarovar route**; **Jelep La** — **Eastern Sikkim–Lhasa**; **Nathu La** — **India–China**, **Chumbi Valley**.
xa: The **India-Myanmar border** passes are **Diphu La** and **Pangsau**.
**Uttarakhand** passes: **Lipulekh**, **Mana**, **Niti**, **Kingri-Wingri**, **Muling La**.

Statement B: **Thalghat** and **Bhor Ghat** are in **Maharashtra**.

xs: **Mana Pass** connects **India (Uttarakhand) and Tibet** — so option **(4)** **Uttarakhand–Tibet** is correct.

34.s: Bum La is located on which border?

n: Bum La is on the India-China border. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
xs: **Bum La** lies on the **India-China border** near **Tawang**, Arunachal Pradesh — so option **(3)** is correct.

xa: **Bomdila** (**West Kameng**) is on the **Arunachal-Tibet route**.

34.s:
Consider the following statements:

II. K2 is 8,611 m high and is located in the Karakoram on the Pakistan–China border.
III. Kangchenjunga is 8,586 m high and is located in the Himalayas on the India–Nepal border.
IV. Lhotse is 8,485 m high and is located in the Himalayas on the Nepal–China border.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
34.x: I, II and III are correct: Everest 8,849 m, K2 8,611 m and Kangchenjunga 8,586 m are placed correctly. IV is false because Lhotse is 8,516 m; 8,485 m is Makalu.
34.tq: Discriminate close peak heights.
n: Mount Everest is the highest peak of the Himalayas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Mount Everest is 8,849 m high. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
K2 is 8,611 m high. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
K2 is located in the Karakoram range. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
K2 is located on the Pakistan–China border. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Kangchenjunga is 8,586 m high. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Kangchenjunga is located in the Himalayas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Kangchenjunga is located on the India–Nepal border. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Lhotse is 8,516 m high. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Lhotse is located in the Himalayas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Lhotse is located on the Nepal–China border. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
xs: Statements **I, II and III only** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
I: **Mount Everest** (**8,849 m**) lies between **Nepal** and **China's Tibet region**.
II: **K2** — **8,611 m**, **Karakoram**, **Pakistan–China**. III: **Kangchenjunga** — **8,586 m**, **India–Nepal**.
IV is wrong: **Lhotse** is **8,516 m**; **8,485 m** is **Makalu**.
xa: K2 is also called **Godwin Austen** — **2nd highest in the world**.
**Lhotse** and **Makalu** both lie on the **Nepal–China** border.
**Siachen**, **Rimo** and **Baltoro** glaciers lie in the **Karakoram**.
