xa: Greek name **Acesines**; Vedic name **Asikni**.
**Chenab** is the **largest tributary of the Indus**.
Chenab projects: **Baglihar, Salal, Dul Hasti** (J&K).

36.s: Which one of the following statements about the course of the Indus is correct?
o: It flows northwest between Ladakh and Zaskar, turns south at Nanga Parbat and enters the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
It flows east through Assam and enters Bangladesh as the Jamuna.
It rises at Gomukh and meets the Yamuna at Prayagraj.
It flows southeast between the Aravalli and Vindhya ranges before entering the Bay of Bengal.
36.x: The Indus flows northwest between Ladakh and Zaskar, turns south at Nanga Parbat through an antecedent gorge and meets the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
36.tq: Trace the river course directionally and distinguish it from the Brahmaputra and Ganga systems.
xs: The **Indus** flows between **Ladakh and Zaskar**, turns south at **Nanga Parbat** and enters the **Arabian Sea** near **Karachi** — option **(1)**.
It turns south through an **antecedent gorge**.
Entering Bangladesh as the **Jamuna** is the **Brahmaputra**; rising at **Gomukh** is the **Bhagirathi**.
xa: Indus source: **Singge Khabab**, Kailash range (**5,182 m**).
Its largest tributary is the **Chenab**.
Tributaries W to E: **Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej**.

36.s: Salal, identified as India’s first project in the region under the Indus Waters Treaty, is a hydropower project on the
36.x: The Salal project is a 690 MW NHPC project on the Chenab and is identified as India’s first project in the region under the treaty.
36.tq: Match a project with the river on which it is situated.
xs: **Salal** is a **690 MW** NHPC project on the **Chenab** — option **(3)**.
It is India's **first project** in the region under the **IWT** (Jan 2026).
xa: Other Chenab projects: **Baglihar** and **Dul Hasti** (J&K).
Under the **IWT 1960**, the **Chenab** is a **western** river (primarily Pakistan).
**Bhakra** is on the **Sutlej**; **Pandoh** on the **Beas**.

36.s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, 1960, which group of rivers is allocated to India as the 'eastern rivers'?
36.x: The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej go to India, while the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab go primarily to Pakistan. The other options mix eastern and western rivers.
36.tq: East (India): Ravi-Beas-Sutlej; West (Pakistan): Indus-Jhelum-Chenab.
xs: The **eastern rivers** **Ravi, Beas and Sutlej** go to India — option **(2)**.
The **western rivers** **Indus, Jhelum and Chenab** go primarily to Pakistan; the other options mix the groups.
xa: The treaty dates from **1960**.
**Salal** (Chenab) is India's first project in the region under the **IWT**.
IIT-Gandhinagar study (**1980-2021**): Indus flows **+8%** vs Ganga **-17%**.

36.s: According to the cited IIT-Gandhinagar study for 1980–2021, the flow of the Indus increased by approximately
36.x: The study reported an approximately 8 per cent increase in Indus flows, while Ganga flows declined by about 17 per cent during the period.
36.tq: Separate the increase figure from the contrasting decline figure in a paired statistic.
xs: The Indus flow rose by about **8 per cent** — option **(1)**.
The same study (**1980-2021**) found the **Ganga** flow fell by **17%**.
xa: IWT **1960**: eastern rivers **Ravi, Beas, Sutlej** → India.
Western rivers **Indus, Jhelum, Chenab** → primarily Pakistan.
The **Ganga** basin covers about **9,51,600 sq km**.

36.s: At which place do the headstreams Bhagirathi and Alaknanda unite before the river acquires the name Ganga?
36.x: Bhagirathi and Alaknanda unite at Devprayag. Downstream of this confluence, the river is called the Ganga.
36.tq: Directly identify the place associated with a river confluence.
xs: **Bhagirathi** and **Alaknanda** join at **Devprayag**, where the river becomes the **Ganga** — option **(3)**.
These two are the Ganga's **headstreams**; the river is called the Ganga only **from Devprayag**.
xa: The **Bhagirathi** rises at **Gomukh**, **Gangotri** glacier.
**Tehri** dam is on the **Bhagirathi** (Uttarakhand).
The Ganga is navigable up to **Prayagraj**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements about the lower course of the Ganga:
1. It swings south at the Farakka barrage.
2. Its left arm at Farakka is the Bhagirathi-Hooghly.
3. Its right arm, the Padma, reaches the Bay of Bengal under the name Padma.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Ganga swings south at Farakka. Statement 2 is correct: the left arm is the Bhagirathi-Hooghly. Statement 3 is wrong: the Padma joins the Brahmaputra and Meghna and enters the Bay as the Meghna. So 1 and 2 only.
36.tq: Farakka: left Hooghly, right Padma; the mouth is called the Meghna.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the Ganga swings south at the **Farakka barrage** (WB).
Statement 2 correct: the **left arm** is the **Bhagirathi-Hooghly**.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Padma** joins the **Brahmaputra and Meghna** and enters the Bay as the **Meghna**.
xa: The Brahmaputra (**Jamuna**) joins the Padma at **Goalundo**.
The **Barak** is the **Meghna**'s headstream.
**Mahananda** is the **easternmost** Ganga tributary.

36.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ganga:
1. Its basin covers about 9,51,600 sq km in total.
2. It drains nearly 40% of India's area.
3. It is navigable only up to Farakka.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the basin is about 9,51,600 sq km and drains nearly 40% of India. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ganga is navigable up to Prayagraj. So 1 and 2 only.
36.tq: Ganga basin ~40% of India; navigable up to Prayagraj.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: basin about **9,51,600 sq km**.
Statement 2 correct: it drains nearly **40%** of India's area.
Statement 3 wrong: the Ganga is navigable up to **Prayagraj**, not just Farakka.
xa: ⚠ Length: **2,525 km** (APP: **2,465 km** total, **2,071 km** in India).
The **Yamuna** is the **westernmost and longest** tributary (PYQ 2025).
**Namami Gange** (**2014**) is implemented by the **NMCG**.

36.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the bank of the Ganga on which it is classified as a tributary?
36.x: Damodar is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga. Gomti, Kosi and other listed Himalayan tributaries are left-bank tributaries, while Son is a right-bank tributary.
36.tq: Use bank-side classification to separate geographically close tributaries.
xs: **Damodar** is a **right-bank** (Peninsular) tributary — option **(3)**.
**Gomti** and **Kosi** are **left-bank** (Himalayan) tributaries.
**Son** is a **right-bank** tributary, not left.
xa: Right bank: **Yamuna, Tons, Son, Punpun, Damodar**.
Left bank: **Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Mahananda**.
The Damodar rises at **Tori, Chota Nagpur**; **Tilaiya** is on its **Barakar** tributary.

36.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Son — joins the Ganga near Maner
Yamuna — joins the Ganga at Prayagraj
Ramganga — joins the Ganga near Farrukhabad
36.x: The Gandak enters India at Valmikinagar, not Raxaul. Ramganga joins near Farrukhabad, Yamuna at Prayagraj and Son near Maner.
36.tq: Find the wrong location attached to a tributary.
xs: **Gandak — enters India at Raxaul** is wrong — option **(1)**: the Gandak enters at **Valmikinagar**.
**Son** joins near **Maner**, **Yamuna** at **Prayagraj**, **Ramganga** at **Farrukhabad** — correct.
xa: Gandak = **Narayani** in Nepal; **Sadanira** of the **Shatapatha Brahmana**.
Nepal flash floods raised the **Narayani-Gandak**, with alerts in Bihar and UP (28 Aug 2026).
The **Ramganga** rises near **Nainital**.

36.s: The Son is regarded as the second-largest right-bank tributary of the Ganga after the Yamuna. It joins the Ganga near
36.x: The Son is the second-largest right-bank tributary after the Yamuna and joins the Ganga near Maner, close to Patna.
36.tq: Combine rank and confluence location to identify a tributary.
xs: The **Son** joins the Ganga near **Maner, Patna** — option **(3)**.
**Farrukhabad** is the **Ramganga** confluence; **Etawah** is where the **Chambal** joins the Yamuna; **Hamirpur** is the **Betwa**'s.
xa: The Son rises at **Amarkantak**.
Bihar-Jharkhand MoU on Son water: **5.75 MAF** Bihar + **2 MAF** Jharkhand of **7.75 MAF** (**1973** **Bansagar Accord**).
**Rihand** (G.B. Pant Sagar), on the Son system, is the **largest artificial lake by volume**.

36.s: Gandak is known as which of the following names in Nepal?
36.x: The Gandak is known as Narayani in Nepal. Sadanira is its name in the Shatapatha Brahmana.
36.tq: Discriminate between regional and historical names of the same river.
xs: In Nepal the Gandak is the **Narayani** — option **(2)**.
**Sadanira** is its name in the **Shatapatha Brahmana**, not in Nepal.
The **Karnali** is the **Ghaghara**, a Mansarovar-area river.
xa: The Gandak enters India at **Valmikinagar**.
It is a **left-bank** (Himalayan) tributary of the Ganga.
Confluence order: **Ghaghara → Son → Gandak → Kosi**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements about the tributaries of the Yamuna:
1. The Chambal rises near Mhow (MP) and joins the Yamuna from the right bank.
2. The Hindon is a right-bank tributary of the Yamuna.
3. The Betwa joins the Yamuna at Hamirpur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Statement 1 is correct: Chambal rises at Mhow and is a right-bank tributary (joins in Etawah). Statement 2 is wrong: the Hindon is the left-bank tributary. Statement 3 is correct: the Betwa joins at Hamirpur. So 1 and 3 only.
36.tq: Yamuna right bank = Chambal, Betwa, Sindh, Ken (from the south); left bank = Hindon.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(3) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **Chambal** rises at **Mhow** (MP), joins from the **right** in **Etawah**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Hindon** is the **left-bank** tributary of the Yamuna.
Statement 3 correct: the **Betwa** joins at **Hamirpur**.
xa: Other right-bank Yamuna tributaries: **Sindh, Ken**.
The Yamuna rises at **Yamunotri** and joins the Ganga at **Prayagraj**.
The Yamuna is the **westernmost and longest** Ganga tributary.

36.s: Which one of the following is both the westernmost and the longest tributary of the Ganga?
36.x: The Yamuna, rising at Yamunotri and joining at Prayagraj, is the westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga. The Son is the second-largest right-bank tributary; the Ghaghara and Ramganga are left-bank Himalayan tributaries.
36.tq: Westernmost = Yamuna; easternmost = Mahananda.
xs: The **Yamuna** is the **westernmost and longest** Ganga tributary — option **(3)** (PYQ 2025).
The **Son** is the **2nd largest right-bank** tributary after the Yamuna.
**Ghaghara** and **Ramganga** are **left-bank** Himalayan tributaries.
xa: **Mahananda** is the **easternmost** Ganga tributary.
Yamuna right-bank tributaries: **Chambal, Betwa, Sindh, Ken**; left bank: **Hindon**.
⚠ PYQ 2024: **Burhi Dihing** and **Dhansiri** are **Brahmaputra** tributaries, not the Ganga's.

36.s:
Arrange the following tributaries of the Ganga in the order of their confluence below Prayagraj (west to east):
A. Gandak
B. Son
C. Kosi
D. Ghaghara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
36.x: Below Prayagraj the order is Tons, Gomti, Ghaghara, Son, Gandak, Kosi and Mahananda. So Ghaghara (D), Son (B), Gandak (A), Kosi (C): D, B, A, C. The other codes misplace the Son or the Ghaghara.
36.tq: Tons-Gomti-Ghaghara-Son-Gandak-Kosi-Mahananda: only Tons and Son come from the right.
xs: Order: **Ghaghara → Son → Gandak → Kosi** — option **(1) D, B, A, C**.
Full order below Prayagraj: **Tons (R) → Gomti (L) → Ghaghara (L) → Son (R) → Gandak (L) → Kosi (L) → Mahananda (L)**.
xa: The **Son** joins near **Maner, Patna**.
The **Kosi** is the "**Sorrow of Bihar**".
**Mahananda** is the last and **easternmost** tributary.

36.s: The Brahmaputra rises at which glacier in the Kailash range?
36.x: The Brahmaputra rises at the Chemayungdung Glacier in the Kailash range, east of Lake Mansarovar.
36.tq: Distinguish the source glacier of one Himalayan river from those of other major rivers.
xs: The Brahmaputra rises at the **Chemayungdung Glacier** in the **Kailash range**, east of Mansarovar — option **(2)**.
**Gangotri** is the **Bhagirathi**'s source.
xa: In Tibet it is the **Tsangpo / Yarlung Zangbo**.
It turns south at **Namche Barwa**.
Length **2,900 km**; only **885 km** in India.

36.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Brahmaputra is correct?
1. It is about 2,900 km long.
2. Only about 885 km of its course lies in India.
3. It is ranked ninth in the world by volume.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
36.x: All three statements are correct: the Brahmaputra is about 2,900 km long, has an approximately 885 km course in India, and ranks ninth globally by volume.
36.tq: Combine length, national-stretch and world-rank figures in a coded question.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The Brahmaputra is **2,900 km** long — correct.
Only **885 km** lies in India — correct.
By **volume** it is the **9th largest** river in the world — correct.
xa: Navigable **1,280 km** up to **Dibrugarh**.
**Majuli** (upper Assam) is the **largest riverine island** in the world (**60 km x 20 km**).
Floods make it the "**sorrow of Assam**".

36.s: At which place does the Brahmaputra turn southward after flowing through Tibet?
36.x: The river, known as the Tsangpo or Yarlung Zangbo in Tibet, turns south at Namche Barwa.
36.tq: Associate a major change in river direction with its landmark location.
xs: The **Tsangpo** turns south at **Namche Barwa** — option **(2)**.
It enters Arunachal Pradesh as the **Dihang/Siang** via the **Dihang gorge**.
**Pasighat** is where **Dibang** and **Lohit** join; **Dhubri** marks the entry to Bangladesh.
xa: **Nanga Parbat** is where the **Indus** turns south.
Names: **Tsangpo** (Tibet) → **Dihang/Siang** → **Brahmaputra** (Assam) → **Jamuna** (Bangladesh).
It joins the Ganga (**Padma**) at **Goalundo**.

36.s: The Dihang becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam after the confluence of which rivers near Pasighat/Sadiya?
36.x: Dibang and Lohit join the Dihang near Pasighat/Sadiya, after which the combined river is called the Brahmaputra.
36.tq: Identify the tributaries responsible for a change in the river’s regional name.
xs: **Dibang** and **Lohit** join the **Dihang** near **Pasighat/Sadiya** — option **(1)**.
The combined river is the **Brahmaputra**, running down the **Assam valley**.
The **Rangeet** joins the **Teesta**; **Subansiri, Manas, Kameng, Sankosh** are right-bank tributaries in Assam.
xa: The Dihang enters via the **Dihang gorge** after turning at **Namche Barwa**.
Navigable **1,280 km** up to **Dibrugarh**.
**Majuli** lies in upper Assam.

36.s: Which one of the following is a right-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra?
36.x: Subansiri is a northern, Himalayan or right-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra. Burhi Dihing, Dhansiri and Dikhu are southern or left-bank tributaries.
36.tq: Apply the river-bank convention to distinguish northern and southern tributaries.
xs: **Subansiri** is a **right-bank** (north, Himalayan) tributary — option **(4)**.
**Burhi Dihing, Dhansiri, Dikhu** are **left-bank** (south) tributaries.
⚠ UPSC notes label Subansiri/Manas "left"; the standard convention treats the **north bank as right**.
xa: Other right-bank tributaries: **Kameng (Jia Bhareli), Manas, Puthimari, Pagladiya, Sankosh**.
The **Teesta** joins in **Bangladesh**.
**Dhansiri** rises in the **Nagaland hills**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements about the Teesta:
1. It is approximately 414 km long.
2. It rises at Tso Lhamo Lake in North Sikkim.
3. Rangeet is its largest tributary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: All three statements are correct. The Teesta is about 414 km long, rises at Tso Lhamo Lake and has the Rangeet as its largest tributary.
36.tq: Test a river through a combination of length, source and largest-tributary facts.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Teesta** is **414 km** long — correct.
It rises at **Tso Lhamo lake** in **North Sikkim** — correct.
Its largest tributary is the **Rangeet** — correct.
xa: The Teesta joins the Brahmaputra in **Bangladesh**.
The draft **2011** Teesta sharing treaty is still **stalled** (Jul 2026).
The Teesta is a **right-bank** tributary of the Brahmaputra.

36.s: The Brahmaputra is called the ‘sorrow of Assam’ mainly because of its:
36.x: The Brahmaputra is called the ‘sorrow of Assam’ because of the floods it causes.
36.tq: Link the descriptive epithet with the principal physical hazard caused by the river.
xs: The Brahmaputra is the "**sorrow of Assam**" because of its **floods** — option **(2)**.
Debate: the floods are partly **man-made** — roads without drainage, **deforestation**, **silted channels** (13 Aug 2026).
xa: It has many tributaries: right bank **Subansiri, Manas**; left bank **Burhi Dihing, Dhansiri**.
The **Kosi** is the "**Sorrow of Bihar**".
**Majuli** is the largest riverine island.

36.s: The Barak River, rising in the Manipur hills, is described as the headstream of the:
36.x: The Barak rises in the Manipur hills and is described as the headstream of the Meghna.
36.tq: Distinguish the Barak–Meghna relationship from the Brahmaputra–Jamuna relationship.
xs: The **Barak**, rising in the **Manipur hills**, is the **Meghna**'s headstream — option **(4)**.
The Ganga-Brahmaputra waters enter the Bay of Bengal as the **Meghna**.
xa: The **Padma** is the Ganga's right arm into Bangladesh.
The **Bhagirathi-Hooghly** is the Ganga's left arm at **Farakka**.
The Brahmaputra (**Jamuna**) joins the Padma at **Goalundo**.

36.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pangong Tso — Freshwater lake of Uttarakhand
Loktak — Freshwater lake with floating phumdis
Tso Moriri — Freshwater lake of Manipur
36.x: Loktak Lake in Manipur is a freshwater lake noted for its floating phumdis. Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri are in Ladakh, while Roopkund is in Uttarakhand.
36.tq: Use the lake–state–water-type combination to reject mismatched pairs.
xs: **Loktak** (Manipur) is a **freshwater** lake with floating **phumdis** — option **(2)**.
**Pangong Tso** and **Tso Moriri** are **brackish** lakes of **Ladakh**.
**Roopkund** is a glacial "skeleton lake" of **Uttarakhand**.
xa: Loktak holds the **Keibul Lamjao** NP.
**Wular** (J&K) is the **largest freshwater lake** of India, fed by the **Jhelum**.
**Tso Moriri** is a **Ramsar site**.

36.s: Which of the following statements regarding Tso Moriri is correct?
o: It is a freshwater lake in Manipur associated with Keibul Lamjao National Park.
It is the largest freshwater lake of India, fed by the Jhelum.
It is a glacial skeleton lake in the Kumaon region.
It is a brackish lake in Ladakh and is a Ramsar site.
36.x: Tso Moriri is a brackish lake in Ladakh and has Ramsar-site status.
36.tq: Identify the precise location–water type–status combination.
xs: **Tso Moriri** is a **brackish** lake in **Ladakh** and a **Ramsar site** — option **(4)**.
**Keibul Lamjao** is on **Loktak** (Manipur); the largest freshwater lake fed by the Jhelum is **Wular**.
The skeleton lake is **Roopkund** (Uttarakhand).
xa: **Pangong Tso** (Ladakh, shared with Tibet) is also brackish/saline.
**Loktak** has floating **phumdis**.
**Bhimtal** (Kumaon) is freshwater.

36.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Wular — Jammu and Kashmir — largest freshwater lake of India
36.x: Wular is located in Jammu and Kashmir and is the largest freshwater lake of India; it is not a brackish high-altitude lake of Ladakh.
36.tq: Find the location and water-type reversal in the incorrectly matched pair.
xs: **Wular — Ladakh — brackish** is wrong — option **(4)**: Wular is in **J&K**, the **largest freshwater lake** of India.
**Roopkund** (glacial skeleton lake) and **Bhimtal** (freshwater) are in **Uttarakhand** — correct.
xa: Wular is fed by the **Jhelum**.
Ladakh's brackish lakes: **Pangong Tso** and **Tso Moriri**.
**Loktak** (Manipur) has floating **phumdis**.

36.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
36.x: The Bhakra Project is built on the Sutlej. Pandoh is on the Beas, Tehri on the Bhagirathi and Tilaiya on the Barakar.
36.tq: Match each project with its river and reject the options formed by swapping neighbouring Himalayan rivers.
xs: **Bhakra** is on the **Sutlej** (HP) — option **(1)**.
**Pandoh** is on the **Beas**; **Tehri** on the **Bhagirathi**; **Tilaiya** on the **Barakar**.
xa: The **Sirhind Canal** draws from the **Sutlej** at **Ropar** (Punjab).
Chenab projects: **Baglihar, Salal, Dul Hasti**.
**Rihand** is on the Rihand (**Son** system), UP.

36.s: Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti projects are associated with which river?
36.x: Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti are projects on the Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir.
36.tq: Group the three projects sharing one river instead of treating them as separate river associations.
xs: **Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti** are on the **Chenab** (J&K) — option **(3)**.
**Bhakra** is on the **Sutlej**; **Pandoh** on the **Beas**; **Tehri** on the **Bhagirathi**.
xa: **Salal** (**690 MW**, NHPC) is India's first project in the region under the **IWT**.
The Chenab forms from **Chandra + Bhaga** at **Tandi**.
The Chenab is a **western river** under the IWT.

36.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
36.x: The Rihand Project is on the Rihand River of the Son system in Uttar Pradesh, not on the Chenab. Tilaiya is on the Barakar, Sirhind Canal draws from the Sutlej, and the Indira Gandhi Canal draws from the Sutlej-Beas system.
36.tq: Find the project–river mismatch, especially where a familiar Himalayan river is substituted for the actual river.
xs: **Rihand Project — Chenab** is wrong — option **(4)**: Rihand is on the **Rihand** (**Son** system) in **UP**.
**Tilaiya** is on the **Barakar** (Damodar system); **Sirhind Canal** draws from the **Sutlej** — correct.
xa: **Rihand** (**G.B. Pant Sagar**) is the **largest artificial lake by volume**.
Chenab projects: **Baglihar, Salal, Dul Hasti**.
Tilaiya is in **Jharkhand**.

36.s: The Namami Gange programme is implemented by the
36.x: The National Mission for Clean Ganga implements the Namami Gange programme. The programme was launched as a flagship initiative in 2014.
36.tq: Apply the 'who implements the programme?' method to distinguish the executing body from related institutions.
xs: **Namami Gange** is implemented by the **National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG)** — option **(1)**.
The **Global River Cities Alliance** was launched **by** the NMCG; it does not implement Namami Gange.
xa: Namami Gange was launched as a flagship in **2014**.
The Alliance was launched at **COP28, Dubai (Dec 2023)**.
Polluted stretch = **BOD > 3 mg/L**; **Maharashtra** has the most.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Global River Cities Alliance was launched by the National Mission for Clean Ganga.
2. It was launched at COP26 in Glasgow.
3. Maharashtra has the highest number of polluted river stretches.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
36.x: Statement 1 is correct: NMCG launched the Global River Cities Alliance, extending the River Cities Alliance of Indian cities. Statement 2 is wrong: it was launched at COP28 in Dubai (December 2023). Statement 3 is correct: Maharashtra has the most polluted stretches (BOD > 3 mg/L). Hence 1 and 3 only.
36.tq: GRCA: NMCG, COP28 Dubai, Dec 2023.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the **NMCG** launched the **Global River Cities Alliance**.
Statement 2 wrong: it was launched at **COP28, Dubai (Dec 2023)**, not COP26.
Statement 3 correct: **Maharashtra** has the most polluted stretches (**BOD > 3 mg/L**).
xa: The Alliance extends the **River Cities Alliance** of Indian cities.
**Namami Gange** launched in **2014**.
Indus flows **+8%** vs Ganga **-17%** (IIT-Gandhinagar).

36.s:
Which of the following factors has been identified as partly contributing to the man-made component of Brahmaputra floods?
1. Roads constructed without adequate drainage
2. Deforestation
3. Silted river channels
4. Increased formation of glacial cirques
Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: Roads without adequate drainage, deforestation and silted channels are cited as partly man-made contributors to Brahmaputra flooding. Glacial cirques are not included among these factors.
36.tq: Separate human-induced flood factors from an unrelated glacial landform.
xs: **Roads without drainage**, **deforestation** and **silted channels** are the cited man-made factors — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only** (13 Aug 2026).
**Glacial cirques** are not among the factors the notes list.
xa: Brahmaputra floods make it the "**sorrow of Assam**".
Navigable **1,280 km** up to **Dibrugarh**.
**Majuli** (upper Assam) is the **largest riverine island** in the world.

36.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with a distinctive geographical description?
36.x: Majuli is identified as the largest riverine island. Mahananda is the easternmost Ganga tributary, Yamuna the westernmost, and Loktak is a freshwater lake of Manipur.
36.tq: Compare several superlatives and distinctive descriptions while rejecting reversed directional labels.
xs: **Majuli** is the **largest riverine island** in the world — option **(4)**.
The **Yamuna** is the **westernmost** tributary and the **Mahananda** the **easternmost** — options (1) and (3) swap them.
**Loktak** is a **freshwater** lake of **Manipur**, not a saline lake of Ladakh.
xa: Majuli lies in **upper Assam**, **60 km x 20 km**.
Ladakh's brackish lakes: **Pangong Tso** and **Tso Moriri**.
Loktak has floating **phumdis** and **Keibul Lamjao** NP.

36.s: The 2026 Bihar-Jharkhand MoU on sharing the waters of the Son, which ended a 25-year dispute, divides the 7.75 MAF available under which agreement?
36.x: The MoU allots 5.75 MAF to Bihar and 2 MAF to Jharkhand out of the 7.75 MAF set under the 1973 Bansagar Accord. The Indus Waters Treaty is with Pakistan, and the Ganga and Mahakali treaties are with Bangladesh and Nepal.
36.tq: Son water: Bansagar Accord 1973; Bihar 5.75 + Jharkhand 2 = 7.75 MAF.
xs: The **7.75 MAF** comes from the **1973** **Bansagar Accord** — option **(2)**.
The MoU gives **5.75 MAF** to **Bihar** and **2 MAF** to **Jharkhand**, ending a **25-year** dispute (1 Sep 2026).
The **Indus Waters Treaty, 1960** splits the **Indus** rivers, not the Son.
xa: The **Son** rises at **Amarkantak** and joins the Ganga near **Maner, Patna**.
**Rihand** (G.B. Pant Sagar), on the **Son** system, is the **largest artificial lake by volume**.
IWT: eastern rivers **Ravi, Beas, Sutlej** → India.

36.s: The Bhagirathi originates from which of the following places?
36.x: The Bhagirathi rises at Gomukh in Uttarkashi district. The Alaknanda rises at Satopanth and the Yamuna at Yamunotri.
36.tq: Recall the source of each river.
n: Bhagirathi originates at Gomukh in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Alaknanda originates at Satopanth Glacier above Badrinath. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Yamuna originates at Yamunotri Glacier on the western slopes of Banderpunch Peak. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Son originates at Amarkantak Hill. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: The **Bhagirathi** originates at **Gomukh** in **Uttarkashi district**, Uttarakhand — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Yamunotri Glacier** is the **Yamuna**'s source; **Amarkantak Hill** is the **Son**'s source.
**Satopanth Glacier** above **Badrinath** is the source of the **Alaknanda**.
xa: The **Alaknanda** and **Bhagirathi** meet at **Devprayag** to form the **Ganga**.
**Uttarkashi** is situated on the Bhagirathi; the **Tehri** dam is across it.
The Ganga **enters the plains at Haridwar**.

36.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: In Bangladesh, the Ganga is known as the Padma.
The Ganga flows through Farakka in West Bengal before entering Bangladesh.
In Bangladesh, the Ganga is known as the Jamuna.
The Ganga enters the plains at Haridwar.
36.x: Option C is incorrect: in Bangladesh the Ganga is the Padma; the Jamuna there is the Brahmaputra. Farakka and Haridwar are right.
36.tq: Discriminate the Bangladeshi names of rivers.
n: Ganga enters the plains at Haridwar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Ganga flows through Farakka in West Bengal before entering Bangladesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Ganga is known as Padma in Bangladesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**In Bangladesh, the Ganga is known as the Jamuna**" — so option **(3)** is the answer.
In **Bangladesh** the Ganga is the **Padma**; **Jamuna** is the **Brahmaputra**'s name there.
The Ganga does enter the plains at **Haridwar** and flows through **Farakka** (**West Bengal**) before entering Bangladesh.
xa: At **Farakka barrage** the left arm is the **Bhagirathi-Hooghly**; the right arm the **Padma**.
The Padma joins the Brahmaputra at **Goalundo**, entering the **Bay of Bengal** as the **Meghna**.
The Ganga is **navigable up to Prayagraj**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Ghaghra originates at Mapchachungo Glacier.
II. The Sharda joins the Ghaghra in the plains.
III. The Ghaghra meets the Ganga at Revilganj in Saran, Bihar.
IV. The Ramganga joins the Ganga near Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
36.x: All four are correct: the Ghaghra rises at Mapchachungo, takes in the Sharda and meets the Ganga at Revilganj, and the Ramganga joins near Kannauj.
36.tq: Recall the confluence of each river.
n: Ghaghra originates at Mapchachungo Glacier. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Sharda joins Ghaghra in the plains. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Ghaghra meets Ganga at Revilganj in Saran district, Bihar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Ramganga joins Ganga near Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: **All four statements (I, II, III and IV)** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
I: the **Ghaghra** originates at **Mapchachungo Glacier**. II: the **Sharda** (**Kali**) joins it **in the plains**.
III: the **Ghaghra** meets the Ganga at **Revilganj** in **Saran district**, **Bihar**.
IV: the **Ramganga** joins the Ganga **near Kannauj**, Uttar Pradesh.
xa: ⚠ Other notes say the **Ramganga** joins at **Farrukhabad**.
The **Gandak** joins at **Sonpur** near **Patna**; it is the **Narayani** in Nepal.
The **Kosi** has the **Sun Kosi**, **Arun Kosi** and **Tamur Kosi** as tributaries.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Mahananda is the last left-bank tributary of the Ganga.
Statement B: The Mahananda joins the Ganga in West Bengal.

Which of the following is correct?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
36.x: Both are true: the Mahananda is the last left-bank tributary of the Ganga and joins it in West Bengal.
36.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Mahananda is the last left-bank tributary of Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Mahananda joins Ganga in West Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Mahananda** is the **last left-bank tributary** of the Ganga and **joins it in West Bengal**.
xa: The Mahananda is the **easternmost** Ganga tributary; the **Yamuna** is the **westernmost**.
Left-bank tributaries: **Ramganga**, **Gomati**, **Ghaghara**, **Gandak**, **Kosi**, **Mahananda**.
Confluence order below Prayagraj ends **Gandak → Kosi → Mahananda**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Yamuna is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga.
II. Son is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga.
III. Damodar flows into the Hugli.
IV. Chambal is a right-bank tributary of the Yamuna.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
36.x: All four are correct: the Yamuna and Son are right-bank Ganga tributaries, the Damodar flows into the Hugli and the Chambal joins the Yamuna from the right.
36.tq: Discriminate left-bank from right-bank tributaries.
n: Yamuna is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Son is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Damodar flows into the Hugli. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Chambal is a right-bank tributary of the Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
xs: **All four statements (I, II, III and IV)** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
I and II: the **Yamuna** and **Son** are **right-bank** (Peninsular) tributaries of the Ganga.
III: the **Damodar** **flows into the Hugli**.
IV: the **Chambal** is a **right-bank** tributary of the **Yamuna**.
xa: The **Yamuna** is the **longest tributary** of the Ganga; the **Son** is the 2nd largest right-bank tributary.
The **Barakar** is the Damodar's **main tributary** — the **Barakar–Damodar–Hugli chain**.
The **Damodar** rises at **Khamarpat Hill** and flows through a **rift valley**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:

o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false

Statement A is false, Statement B is true
36.x: Both are true: the Yamuna rises at Yamunotri on Banderpunch, and the Chambal passes Sawai Madhopur and Dholpur before joining the Yamuna.

n: Yamuna originates at Yamunotri Glacier on the western slopes of Banderpunch Peak. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chambal flows through Sawai Madhopur in Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chambal flows through Dholpur in Rajasthan before joining Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chambal joins Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement A: the **Yamuna** originates at **Yamunotri Glacier** on the **western slopes** of **Banderpunch Peak**.
Statement B: the **Chambal** joins the **Yamuna** (in **Etawah**) after its course through Rajasthan.
xa: The **Chambal** rises at **Mhow**, MP.
The **Yamuna** and **Ganga** meet at **Prayagraj**.
The **Chambal Valley** projects serve **Madhya Pradesh** and **Rajasthan**; the Chambal is known for **ravines**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Chambal, Sind, Betwa and Ken join the Yamuna on its right bank.
Statement B: The Hindan joins the Yamuna on its left bank.

Which of the following is correct?
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
36.x: Both are true: the peninsular rivers Chambal, Sind, Betwa and Ken join the Yamuna from the right (south), while the Hindan joins it from the left in western Uttar Pradesh.
36.tq: Peninsular tributaries join the Yamuna from the south, the right bank.
n: Tons is a left-bank tributary of the Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Hanuman Ganga is a left-bank tributary of the Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Sasur Khaderi is a left-bank tributary of the Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement A: **Chambal**, **Sindh**, **Betwa** and **Ken** are **right-bank** tributaries of the Yamuna.
Statement B: the **Hindon** joins as a **left-bank** tributary.
xa: Other left-bank tributaries: **Tons**, **Hanuman Ganga**, **Sasur Khaderi**.
The **Betwa** joins at **Hamirpur**; the **Matatila** project lies on it.
The **Chambal** joins in **Etawah**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements about the Brahmaputra:
I. In Tibet, it is known as Tsangpo or Sanpu.
II. In Arunachal Pradesh, it is known as Dihang.
III. In Bangladesh, it is known as Jamuna.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
36.x: All three are correct: the Brahmaputra is the Tsangpo in Tibet, the Dihang in Arunachal and the Jamuna in Bangladesh.
36.tq: Recall the regional names of the Brahmaputra.
n: Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo or Sanpu in Tibet. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Brahmaputra is called Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Brahmaputra is called Jamuna in Bangladesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: **All three statements (I, II and III)** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
I: in **Tibet** it is the **Tsangpo** or **Sanpu** (**Yarlung Zangbo**).
II: in **Arunachal Pradesh** it is the **Dihang** (**Siang**).
III: in **Bangladesh** it is the **Jamuna**.
xa: It turns south at **Namche Barwa**; the **Dibang** and **Lohit** join near **Pasighat/Sadiya**.
It is navigable **1,280 km** up to **Dibrugarh**; called the "**sorrow of Assam**".
**Majuli** is a river island in the Brahmaputra in **Assam**.

36.s:
How many of the following are direct tributaries of the Brahmaputra?
1. Manas
2. Kopili/Kapili
3. Rangeet
4. Kishanganga
36.x: Two are direct Brahmaputra tributaries: the Manas and the Kopili. The Rangeet joins the Teesta (not the Brahmaputra directly), and the Kishanganga joins the Jhelum.
36.tq: Separate direct tributaries from sub-tributaries and from Indus-system rivers.
n: Manas is a tributary of Brahmaputra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Kopili, or Kapili, is a tributary of Brahmaputra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Rangeet is a tributary of Teesta. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Kishanganga is a tributary of Jhelum. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: **Only two** — the **Manas** and **Kopili/Kapili** — are direct Brahmaputra tributaries, so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Rangeet** is a tributary of the **Teesta** (its largest tributary), not of the Brahmaputra directly.
The **Kishanganga** is a tributary of the **Jhelum** (**Neelum** in Pakistan).
xa: Major Brahmaputra tributaries: **Dibang**, **Lohit**, **Subansiri**, **Kameng**, **Sankosh**, **Manas**, **Burhi Dihing**, **Dhansiri**, **Kopili**, **Teesta**.
The **Teesta** rises at **Tso Lhamo lake** and joins the Brahmaputra in **Bangladesh**.
The **Kameng** is also called the **Jia Bharali**.

36.s:

List-I
(a) Sankosh — origin
(b) Sankosh — joins
(c) Sankosh — boundary it marks
(d) Teesta — states through which it flows

List-II

36.x: The Sankosh rises in northern Bhutan, joins the Brahmaputra and marks the Assam–West Bengal boundary, while the Teesta flows through Sikkim and West Bengal, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
36.tq: Separate a river's source, its confluence and the boundary it forms.
n: Sankosh originates in northern Bhutan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Sankosh joins Brahmaputra near the Assam–West Bengal border. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Sankosh forms the boundary between Assam and West Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Teesta flows through Sikkim and West Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Sankosh** originates in **northern Bhutan**, **joins the Brahmaputra** and marks the **Assam–West Bengal** boundary.
The **Teesta** flows through **Sikkim and West Bengal**.
xa: The Teesta (**414 km**) joins the Brahmaputra in **Bangladesh**; the draft **2011** sharing treaty is stalled.
The **Rangeet** (Sikkim) is the Teesta's largest tributary.
The **Sankosh** is a **right-bank** (north, Himalayan) tributary, like the **Subansiri** and **Manas**.

36.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Jhelum — origin
(b) Jhelum — course
(c) Jhelum — entry into Pakistan
(d) Kishanganga — name in Pakistan

List-II
(i) Verinag at the foot of the Pir Panjal
(ii) Srinagar and Wular Lake
(iii) Deep and narrow gorge
(iv) Neelum
36.x: The Jhelum rises at Verinag, flows through Srinagar and Wular Lake and enters Pakistan through a deep gorge, and the Kishanganga is the Neelum there, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
36.tq: Recall the course of the Jhelum.
n: Jhelum originates at Verinag at the foot of the Pir Panjal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Jhelum flows through Srinagar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Jhelum flows through Wular Lake. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Jhelum enters Pakistan through a deep and narrow gorge. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Kishanganga is called Neelum in Pakistan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: The correct match is **a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Jhelum** rises at **Verinag** at the foot of the **Pir Panjal** and flows through **Srinagar** and **Wular Lake**.
It **enters Pakistan** through a **deep and narrow gorge**; the **Kishanganga** is called **Neelum** in Pakistan.
xa: The Greek name of the Jhelum is **Hydaspes**; its Vedic name **Vitasta**.
**Wular** is the **largest freshwater lake** of India, fed by the Jhelum.
Under the **Indus Waters Treaty 1960**, the **Jhelum** is a **western river** (primarily Pakistan).

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Ravi joins the Chenab in Pakistan.
II. The Chenab receives the Jhelum and the Ravi.
III. The Sutlej receives the Chenab and joins the Indus.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
36.x: All three are correct: the Ravi joins the Chenab, which also takes the Jhelum, and the combined flow joins the Sutlej before reaching the Indus.
36.tq: Recall the order of the Indus tributaries.
n: Ravi joins Chenab in Pakistan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chenab receives Jhelum. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chenab receives Ravi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Sutlej receives Chenab. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Sutlej joins Indus. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: **All three statements (I, II and III)** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
I: the **Ravi joins the Chenab** in **Pakistan**.
II: the **Chenab receives the Jhelum and the Ravi**.
III: the **Sutlej receives the Chenab** and **joins the Indus**.
xa: The **Chenab** is the **largest tributary** of the Indus — formed by **Chandra + Bhaga at Tandi**.
⚠ **Hydaspes** = Jhelum; **Hyphasis** = Beas; **Acesines** = Chenab.
The **Indus** reaches the **Arabian Sea** near **Karachi**.

36.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Chenab is the largest tributary of the Indus.
In Pakistan, Kishanganga is known as Neelum.
Sutlej is a tributary of the Indus.
Kishanganga is a tributary of the Sutlej.

n: Chenab is the largest tributary of the Indus. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Kishanganga is known as Neelum in Pakistan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Sutlej is a major tributary of the Indus. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Kishanganga is a tributary of the Jhelum. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Chenab is a major tributary of the Indus. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Kishanganga is a tributary of the Sutlej**" — so option **(4)** is the answer.
The **Kishanganga** is a **tributary of the Jhelum**, called **Neelum** in Pakistan.
The **Chenab** is the **largest tributary** of the Indus, and the **Sutlej** joins the Indus — both correct.
xa: The **Sutlej**'s tributaries are the **Beas**, **Spiti** and **Baspa**.

The **Zanskar** joins the Indus at **Nimu**; **Leh** lies on the Indus's **right bank**.

36.s: Which irrigation project supplies Chennai?
36.x: The Telugu Ganga Project carries Krishna water to Chennai.

n: Telugu Ganga Project supplies Chennai. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
xs: The **Telugu Ganga Project** (**Andhra Pradesh**) **supplies Chennai** — so option **(1)** is correct.

Damodar Valley Project is located in Jharkhand and West Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]

Tungabhadra Project is constructed across the Tungabhadra River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
Hirakud Project is constructed across the Mahanadi River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
Rihand Project is constructed across the Rihand River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
xs: The correct match is **a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Srisailam** — **Krishna**; **Tungabhadra** — **Tungabhadra**.
**Hirakud** — **Mahanadi**; **Rihand** — **Rihand** (Son system).
xa: **Rihand** lies in **Uttar Pradesh**; **Hirakud** in **Odisha**.
The **Son**'s tributaries include the **Rihand**, **Johilla**, **Gopad**, **Kanhar** and **North Koel**.
The **Mandal** project lies on the **North Koel**.

36.s: The Kosi Project is located in which combination of places?
36.x: The Kosi Project is shared by Bihar and Nepal.
36.tq: Recall the states of each project.
n: Kosi Project is located in Bihar and Nepal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
xs: The **Kosi Project** lies in **Bihar and Nepal** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**MP and Rajasthan** — **Chambal**; **AP and Karnataka** — **Tungabhadra**; **Jharkhand and West Bengal** — **Damodar Valley**.
xa: The **Kosi** is the "**Sorrow of Bihar**".
Its tributaries are the **Sun Kosi**, **Arun Kosi** and **Tamur Kosi**.
The **Kosi** plain of north Bihar is a huge **megafan**.

36.s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Tungabhadra Project is located in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.
Statement B: Chambal Valley Project is located in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
o: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
36.x: Both are true: Tungabhadra serves AP and Karnataka, and the Chambal Valley Project serves MP and Rajasthan.
36.tq: Check each statement separately.
n: Tungabhadra Project is located in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
Chambal Valley Project is located in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement A: the **Tungabhadra** project lies in **Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka**.
Statement B: the **Chambal Valley** project lies in **Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan**.
xa: **Telugu Ganga** (AP) **supplies Chennai**.
**Hirakud** and the **Mahanadi Project** are in **Odisha**.
The **Kosi** project is shared by **Bihar and Nepal**.

n: Matatila Project is constructed across the Betwa River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]

37.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Himalayan rivers from Peninsular rivers?
o: Himalayan rivers form only estuaries, whereas Peninsular rivers form only deltas.
Himalayan rivers are seasonal, whereas Peninsular rivers are perennial.
Himalayan rivers generally have deep antecedent gorges, whereas Peninsular rivers have broad or shallow graded valleys.
Himalayan rivers have fixed straight courses, whereas Peninsular rivers meander extensively.
37.x: Himalayan rivers are generally perennial and form deep antecedent gorges, while Peninsular rivers are usually seasonal and flow through broad, shallow, graded valleys.
37.tq: Compare the two river systems feature by feature.
xs: Himalayan rivers cut **deep antecedent gorges**; Peninsular rivers have **broad, shallow, graded valleys** — option **(3)**.
Himalayan rivers are **perennial** and Peninsular rivers **seasonal** — option (2) reverses this.
Himalayan rivers **meander and shift**; Peninsular rivers have **fixed, straight courses** — option (4) reverses this.
xa: Mouths: Himalayan rivers form **large deltas**; Peninsular rivers form **deltas (east)** or **estuaries (west)**.
Himalayan rivers are fed by **rain + snowmelt**; Peninsular rivers are **monsoon-fed**.
Use: Himalayan — **irrigation and navigation**; Peninsular — **hydropower**.

37.s:
Antecedent rivers are those which:
1. Rise in the Trans-Himalaya.
2. Maintain their courses by cutting gorges as mountain ranges rise.
3. Are represented by the Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: Antecedent rivers rise in the Trans-Himalaya and retain their courses by cutting through rising ranges. Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra are examples.
37.tq: Test definition, process and examples together.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Antecedent rivers **rise in the trans-Himalaya** — correct.
They kept their course by **cutting gorges** as the ranges rose — correct.
Examples: **Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra** — correct.
xa: Himalayan rivers are **perennial** (rain + snowmelt).
Peninsular rivers are **older**, with graded valleys.
Himalayan rivers have **meandering, shifting** courses in the plains.

37.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the east-flowing rivers of Peninsular India is correct?
o: They generally form large deltas at their mouths.
They invariably flow through rift valleys and form estuaries.
They all originate in the Eastern Ghats.
They are short and swift and are mainly used for natural harbours.
37.x: East-flowing rivers generally drain into the Bay of Bengal and form large deltas. West-flowing rivers more commonly form estuaries and support hydropower and natural harbours.
37.tq: Use the mouth feature to separate east-flowing rivers from west-flowing rivers.
xs: East-flowing Peninsular rivers form **large deltas** — option **(1)**.
**Rift valleys** and **estuaries** belong to the west-flowing **Narmada and Tapi**.
**Short and swift** rivers giving natural harbours are the **west-flowing** ones.
xa: East-flowing examples: **Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi, Pennar, Palar, Vamsadhara, Nagavali**.
⚠ East-flowing = **deltas + irrigation**; west-flowing = **estuaries + hydropower**.
The **Godavari delta** is **Konaseema**, with **7 distributaries**.

37.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of west-flowing rivers?
37.x: Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati and Mahi flow westwards towards the Arabian Sea. The other groups contain east-flowing rivers.
37.tq: Classify the entire group by its drainage direction before examining individual rivers.
xs: **Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati, Mahi** all flow **west** to the Arabian Sea — option **(2)**.
**Pennar, Palar, Vamsadhara, Nagavali** and **Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi** flow **east**.
Option **(4)** mixes east-flowing Godavari and Krishna with west-flowing **Periyar** and **Sharavati**.
xa: Other west-flowing rivers: **Periyar, Mandovi, Sharavati**.
West-flowing rivers form **estuaries, not deltas** → natural harbours.
**Narmada** (**1,312 km**) is the longest west-flowing river.

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Narmada is the longest west-flowing river of India (about 1,312 km).
2. The Tapi is the second longest west-flowing river and reaches the sea at Suvali near Surat.
3. The Tapi flows through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: Statement 1 is correct: Narmada (1,312 km) is the longest west-flowing river. Statement 2 is correct: Tapi (724 km) is second and meets the sea at Suvali near Surat. Statement 3 is wrong: the Tapi's rift valley lies between the Satpura and Ajanta ranges; the Vindhya-Satpura rift is the Narmada's. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.
37.tq: Narmada: Vindhya-Satpura; Tapi: Satpura-Ajanta - one range down.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Narmada** (**1,312 km**) is the **longest west-flowing** river.
Statement 2 correct: **Tapi** (**724 km**) is second and reaches the sea at **Suvali near Surat**.
Statement 3 wrong: the Tapi rift is between **Satpura and Ajanta**; Vindhya-Satpura is the **Narmada**'s.
xa: The Tapi rises at **Multai** tank, **Satpura** plateau (Betul, MP).
**Tapti Basin Mega Recharge**: **MP and Maharashtra** MoU (PYQ 2025).
City pair: **Tapi-Surat**.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about rivers that cross a line of latitude twice:
1. The Congo crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.
2. The Mahi crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat.
3. The Limpopo of Africa crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice and drains into the Indian Ocean.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
37.x: Statement 2 is correct: the Mahi crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice and enters the Gulf of Khambhat. Statement 3 is correct: the Limpopo ('Crocodile River') crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice and drains into the Indian Ocean. Statement 1 is wrong: the Congo crosses the Equator twice, not the Tropic of Cancer. So 2 and 3 only; '2 only' leaves out true statement 3, while '1 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 1.
37.tq: Mahi - Cancer, Congo - Equator, Limpopo - Capricorn: one river per line.
xs: Statements **2** and **3** are correct — so option **(2) 2 and 3 only** is the answer.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **Congo** crosses the **Equator twice**, not the Tropic of Cancer.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Mahi** crosses the **Tropic of Cancer twice** and enters the **Gulf of Khambhat**.
Statement 3 is correct: the **Limpopo** (Africa) crosses the **Tropic of Capricorn twice** and drains into the **Indian Ocean**.
xa: The Limpopo is associated with the name "**Crocodile River**".
⚠ Sources differ on the Mahi's origin: **Banswara district (Rajasthan)** in one set of notes, **Madhya Pradesh** in another.
The Mahi flows **southwest**, through **Rajasthan** and **Gujarat**, to the **Gulf of Khambhat**.

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
2. Banas is an east-flowing river originating in the Aravallis.
3. Sahibi is a north-flowing river originating in the Aravallis.
4. Sabarmati is a west-flowing river originating in the Aravallis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: All four statements are correct. The Aravallis give rise to west-flowing Luni and Sabarmati, east-flowing Banas and north-flowing Sahibi; Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
37.tq: Use directional classification to verify each Aravalli-born river.
xs: All four are correct — option **(4) 1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Luni** ends in the **Rann of Kutch** — correct.
Aravalli-born rivers: **west** — Luni, Sabarmati; **east** — Banas; **north** — Sahibi — correct (VIS 2026).
xa: **Sabarmati** flows past **Ahmedabad**.
The Luni is an Aravalli-born **desert** river.
The **Mahi** crosses the **Tropic of Cancer twice**.

37.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Narmada — Marble Rocks and Dhuandhar Falls near Jabalpur
37.x: Luni is an Aravalli-born desert river that ends in the Rann of Kutch, not the Gulf of Khambhat. Narmada, Tapi and Periyar are correctly matched with the other descriptions.
37.tq: Use the destination trap to distinguish inland-drainage Luni from west-flowing rivers reaching the sea.
xs: **Luni — Gulf of Khambhat** is wrong — option **(3)**: the Luni ends in the **Rann of Kutch**.
**Tapi** — Suvali near Surat; **Periyar** — Kerala, **Mullaperiyar** dam; **Narmada** — **Dhuandhar** near **Jabalpur** — correct.
xa: The river reaching the **Gulf of Khambhat** is the **Mahi**.
**Dhuandhar** falls lie at the **Marble Rocks** (MP).
Other Narmada falls: **Kapildhara, Dhardi**.

37.s: The Narmada and Son rivers originate from which of the following places?
37.x: Both the Narmada and Son originate at Amarkantak in the Maikal range of Madhya Pradesh.
37.tq: Link the common source with the two rivers rather than selecting a source associated with only one river.
xs: **Narmada** and **Son** rise at **Amarkantak** in the **Maikal** range (MP) — option **(4)**.
**Multai** is the **Tapi**'s source; **Sihawa** the **Mahanadi**'s; **Mahabaleshwar** the **Krishna**'s.
xa: The Narmada flows west through a **rift valley** between the Vindhyas and Satpuras.
The Son flows north to the Ganga as a **right-bank** tributary.
**Narmada and Kaveri** basins are about the same size.

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
37.x: The Krishna originates at Mahabaleshwar. The Brahmagiri hills at Talakaveri are the source of the Kaveri.
37.tq: Find the swapped source by comparing the Western Ghats source points.
xs: **Krishna — Brahmagiri hills** is wrong — option **(4)**: the Krishna rises at **Mahabaleshwar** ("Krishna Kund").
**Mahanadi — Sihawa**, **Tapi — Multai tank**, **Pennar — Nandi hills** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **Brahmagiri** = two sources: **Kaveri** (Talakaveri, Kodagu) and **Godavari** (Nashik).
The Western Ghats are the "**Water Tower of Peninsular India**".
The **Pennar** is the lifeline of **Rayalaseema**.

37.s:
Which of the following rivers originate in the Eastern Ghats?
1. Vamsadhara
2. Nagavali
3. Machkund
4. Sileru
5. Sabari
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
37.x: Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Machkund, Sileru and Sabari are all listed as rivers originating in the Eastern Ghats.
37.tq: When every listed item belongs to the same source region, select the complete combination.
xs: All five rise in the **Eastern Ghats** — option **(4) 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5**.
**Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Machkund, Sileru, Sabari** are listed together.
xa: **Sileru** is a tributary of the **Sabari**; its upper course is the **Machkund**.
The **Sabari** joins the Godavari near **Kunavaram/K.R. Puram**.
**Vamsadhara** (AP-Odisha): tribunal **2010**, award **2017**.

37.s: The Western Ghats are called the ‘Water Tower of Peninsular India’ mainly because they provide the sources of which group of rivers?
37.x: The Western Ghats are described as the Water Tower of Peninsular India because they provide the sources of the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri river systems.
37.tq: Connect the descriptive geographical title with the river systems originating in the region.
xs: The Western Ghats are the "**Water Tower of Peninsular India**" for the **Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri** — option **(1)**.
**Narmada** rises at **Amarkantak**; **Luni, Sabarmati, Banas** rise in the **Aravallis**.
xa: **Godavari**: Brahmagiri-**Trimbakeshwar** hills (Nashik).
**Krishna**: **Mahabaleshwar**; **Kaveri**: **Brahmagiri / Talakaveri** (Kodagu).
**Mahanadi** rises at **Sihawa** (Chhattisgarh).

37.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the longest Peninsular rivers in descending order?
37.x: The order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (about 1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (858 km) and Tapi (724 km).
37.tq: Compare adjacent river lengths instead of relying only on whether they flow east or west.
xs: Order: **Godavari > Krishna > Narmada > Mahanadi > Tapi** — option **(3)**.
xa: The Godavari is the **2nd longest** river in India.
The **Kaveri** is **805 km**.
**Ganga** (**2,525 km**) is India's longest river.

37.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the relative size of river basins in Peninsular India:
1. The Godavari basin is larger than the Krishna basin.
2. The Krishna basin is larger than the Mahanadi basin.
3. The Narmada and Kaveri basins are approximately equal in size.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: The relative order is Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi, while the Narmada and Kaveri basins are approximately equal in size.
37.tq: Use the comparison chain and identify the coded combination.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Basin ranking: **Godavari → Krishna → Mahanadi**.
The **Narmada and Kaveri** basins are about the **same size**.
xa: The **Godavari** basin is the **second largest** (~**10%** of India).
Largest basin: **Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna**.
~**75%** of AP lies in the **Godavari, Krishna and Pennar** basins.

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Brahmaputra is longer overall than the Ganga.
2. Only about 885 km of the Brahmaputra lies in India.
3. The Ganga is regarded as India's longest river.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: The Brahmaputra is about 2,900 km long overall, but only 885 km lies in India. The Ganga, at 2,525 km, is considered India's longest river.
37.tq: Separate overall length from length within India.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **Brahmaputra** (**2,900 km**) is longer overall than the Ganga — correct.
Only **885 km** of it lies in **India** — correct.
The **Ganga** is **India's longest river** — correct.
xa: ⚠ Trap: overall length vs length **in India**.
**Godavari** (**1,465 km**) is the 2nd longest in India.

37.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Indravati — Godavari
2. Tel — Mahanadi
3. Kabini — Krishna
4. Tungabhadra — Krishna
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
37.x: Indravati is a tributary of the Godavari, while Tel and Tungabhadra are tributaries of the Mahanadi and Krishna respectively. Kabini is a right-bank tributary of the Kaveri, not the Krishna.
37.tq: Split the options by checking the easily confusable river–tributary pair.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct — option **(2) 1, 2 and 4 only**.
**Indravati — Godavari** (left bank) and **Tel — Mahanadi** (right bank) — correct.
**Kabini** is a right-bank tributary of the **Kaveri**, not the Krishna — wrong.
**Tungabhadra** is the **largest** Krishna tributary — correct.
xa: Kaveri tributaries: left **Hemavathi, Shimsha, Arkavathi**; right **Kabini, Bhavani, Amaravati**.
⚠ Largest tributary: Godavari = **Pranhita**; Krishna = **Tungabhadra**.
Mahanadi left bank: **Seonath, Hasdeo**.

37.s: With reference to the Godavari, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Pravara, Manjira and Manair are its right-bank tributaries.
Purna, Pranahita and Sabari are its right-bank tributaries.
Tungabhadra is its largest left-bank tributary.
Tel is its principal right-bank tributary.
37.x: Pravara, Manjira and Manair join the Godavari from the right bank. Purna, Pranahita, Indravati and Sabari are its important left-bank tributaries.
37.tq: Test the left-bank and right-bank classification directly.
xs: **Pravara, Manjira, Manair** are the Godavari's **right-bank** tributaries — option **(1)**.
**Purna, Pranhita, Sabari** join from the **left** bank.
**Tungabhadra** is a **Krishna** tributary; **Tel** is a **Mahanadi** tributary.
xa: Largest Godavari tributary: **Pranhita** (**Wardha + Wainganga**), joining near **Kaleshwaram**.
**Indravati** (left bank) rises in **Kalahandi**, Odisha, and flows through **Bastar**.
**Kinnerasani** is also listed among Godavari tributaries.

37.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
37.x: Ghataprabha is a right-bank tributary of the Krishna. Tungabhadra is also a right-bank tributary, Sheonath is a left-bank tributary of the Mahanadi, and Bhavani is a right-bank tributary of the Kaveri.
37.tq: Find the correctly matched river and bank among reversed bank classifications.
xs: **Ghataprabha** is a **right-bank** tributary of the **Krishna** — option **(3)**.
**Tungabhadra** is also **right-bank**, not left.
**Sheonath** is a **left-bank** Mahanadi tributary; **Bhavani** is a **Kaveri** tributary.
xa: Krishna right bank: **Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Koyna**.
Krishna left bank: **Bhima, Dindi, Musi**.
⚠ PYQ 2025: **Ghataprabha** is a Krishna tributary, not the Godavari's.

37.s: The Godavari river is popularly known as which of the following?
37.x: The Godavari is known as Dakshin Ganga or Dakshina Ganga. The name Dakshina Ganga is also used for the Kaveri in some references.
37.tq: Discriminate between similar names associated with Peninsular rivers.
xs: The Godavari is called "**Dakshin/Dakshina Ganga**" — option **(2)**.
⚠ Some notes also use the name for the **Kaveri**.
xa: The Godavari is the **longest peninsular river** (**1,465 km**).
Delta: **Konaseema**; mouth near **Antharvedi**.
City: **Godavari-Rajamahendravaram**.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about the Godavari delta:
1. It is known as the Konaseema delta.
2. It has seven distributaries, including the Gautami, Vasishta and Vainateya.
3. The Bhagirathi is one of its distributaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Godavari delta is Konaseema. Statement 2 is correct: it has 7 distributaries - Gautami, Vasishta, Vainateya, Tulya, Bharadwaja, Kaushika and Athreya. Statement 3 is wrong: the Bhagirathi is a Himalayan headstream of the Ganga, not a Godavari distributary. So 1 and 2 only (B); A leaves out true statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
37.tq: Seven Godavari mouths, all named after rishis (Gautami, Vasishta...).
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1 correct: the Godavari delta is **Konaseema**.
Statement 2 correct: **7 distributaries** — **Gautami, Vasishta, Vainateya**, Tulya, Bharadwaja, Kaushika, Athreya.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Bhagirathi** is a Ganga headstream rising at **Gomukh**.
xa: The delta's mouth is near **Antharvedi**.
Godavari floods (Jul 2026): **5.2 lakh cusecs** released at **Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage, Dowleswaram**.
**150 relief camps** were set up in Polavaram district.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pranhita river:
1. It is the largest tributary of the Godavari and joins it from the left bank.
2. It is formed by the confluence of the Wardha and the Manjira.
3. It joins the Godavari near Kaleshwaram.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
37.x: Statement 1 is correct: Pranhita is the largest (left-bank) tributary of the Godavari. Statement 2 is wrong: Pranhita is formed by the Wardha and the Wainganga; the Manjira is a right-bank tributary of the Godavari. Statement 3 is correct: it joins the Godavari near Kaleshwaram. So only 1 and 3 (B); A, C and D all include the false statement 2.
37.tq: Pranhita = Wardha + Wainganga, meets Godavari at Kaleshwaram; Manjira is on the other (right) bank.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Pranhita** is the **largest**, **left-bank** Godavari tributary.
Statement 2 wrong: it is formed by **Wardha + Wainganga**; the **Manjira** is a **right-bank** tributary.
Statement 3 correct: it joins near **Kaleshwaram**.
xa: ⚠ Largest tributary: Godavari = **Pranhita**; Krishna = **Tungabhadra**.
The **Wainganga** joins the Godavari via the Pranhita.
⚠ Some notes say the **Sileru** joins the Pranhita.

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Indravati — joins the Krishna at Sangameswaram
Sabari — joins the Godavari near Kunavaram
Manjira — rises in the Sinkaram hills
Pranhita — joins the Godavari near Nizamabad
37.x: The Sabari joins the Godavari near Kunavaram in Andhra Pradesh. Sangameswaram is where the Tungabhadra (not the Indravati) joins the Krishna, and the Pranhita joins the Godavari near Kaleshwaram, not Nizamabad.
37.tq: Start with the sure river–confluence pair and reject swapped locations.
xs: The **Sabari** joins the Godavari near **Kunavaram** (K.R. Puram) — option **(2)**.
**Sangameswaram** is where the **Tungabhadra** joins the Krishna, not the Indravati.
The **Pranhita** joins near **Kaleshwaram**, not Nizamabad.
xa: The Sabari rises in the **Eastern Ghats**, Odisha.
**Sileru** (upper course **Machkund**) joins the Sabari at the **AP-Chhattisgarh-Odisha tri-junction**.
The Sabari is a **left-bank** Godavari tributary.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tungabhadra:
1. It is formed by the union of the Tunga and the Bhadra.
2. It is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna.
3. It joins the Krishna at Sangameswaram (Nandyal).
4. Vedavathi (Hagari) and Handri are its tributaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
37.x: Statement 1 is correct: Tunga + Bhadra form the Tungabhadra. Statement 2 is wrong: it is the largest RIGHT-bank tributary of the Krishna. Statement 3 is correct: it joins the Krishna at Sangameswaram in Nandyal. Statement 4 is correct: Vedavathi (Hagari) and Handri are its own tributaries. So 1, 3 and 4 only (B); A, C and D include the false statement 2 (C also leaves out true 1 and 3).
37.tq: Krishna's big right-bank feeder is the Tungabhadra; its left bank has Bhima and Musi.
xs: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct — option **(2) 1, 3 and 4 only**.
Statement 1 correct: **Tunga + Bhadra** form the Tungabhadra.
Statement 2 wrong: it is the **largest right-bank** tributary of the Krishna.
Statements 3 and 4 correct: joins at **Sangameswaram (Nandyal)**; own tributaries **Vedavathi (Hagari)** and **Handri**.
xa: Tungabhadra: **531 km**, ~**149 km** in AP.
**Raichur doab** lies between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra**.
**Vedavathi** joins the Tungabhadra at **Siruguppa**.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the winds called monsoons?
o: Local winds confined to the coastal districts of India
Primary planetary winds that blow permanently in one direction
Upper-air winds that never reach the land surface
Seasonal or periodic secondary winds that reverse direction with the season
38.x: Monsoons are seasonal or periodic secondary winds. Their direction reverses with the change of season; they are not primary planetary winds.
38.tq: Distinguish monsoons from primary winds by their periodic reversal and classification.
xs: Monsoons are **seasonal/periodic secondary winds** that **reverse direction** with the season — option **(4)**.
They are **not primary (planetary)** winds — ⚠ "primary winds" was the false statement in PYQ G2 2023.
They blow **sea → land in summer** and **land → sea in winter**.
xa: The word comes from Arabic **"Mausim"** (season).
Monsoons lie mainly in the tropics between **20°N and 20°S**.
Their distribution is controlled mainly by **relief**.

38.x: Statement 1 is correct: monsoons lie mainly within 20°N-20°S. Statement 2 is wrong: the monsoon is not steady and is unequally distributed, with breaks and variability. Statement 3 is correct: relief mainly controls its distribution. So 1 and 3 only (B); A leaves out true statement 3, C and D include the false statement 2.
38.tq: 'Equally distributed' is the classic false statement (PYQ 2022).
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.

Statement 3 correct: distribution is controlled mainly by **relief**.
xa: The monsoon is marked by **breaks** and **variability**.
Its sudden onset is the "**burst**" (first week of June).

38.s: The word 'monsoon' is derived from the Arabic word 'Mausim', which means
38.x: 'Mausim' is Arabic for season, reflecting the seasonal reversal of these winds. The word does not mean rain, wind or sea, though monsoons bring rain and are winds that blow from the sea in summer.

xs: Arabic **"Mausim"** means **season** — option **(3)**.

38.s: According to the classical thermal theory of the monsoon, the summer monsoon is produced primarily because:
o: The ITCZ remains fixed south of the equator throughout the year.
Land heats faster than the sea, creating a low-pressure area over land that draws moist winds from the sea.
The Himalayas generate a cold high-pressure area over northern India in summer.
The sea heats faster than the land, creating a permanent low over the ocean.
38.x: Sir Edmund Halley's thermal theory, proposed in 1686, attributes the monsoon to differential heating of land and sea. Summer heating creates a low over land that attracts moist maritime winds.
38.tq: Apply the pressure-gradient logic of differential heating rather than memorising only the theory’s name.
xs: **Land heats faster than sea**, creating a **summer low over land** that draws moist sea winds — option **(2)**.
This is the classical **thermal** theory of Sir Edmund **Halley** (**1686**); the pattern reverses in winter.
The sea does not heat faster; in summer the **high** lies over the sea.
xa: The **dynamic theory** explains the monsoon by the northward shift of the **ITCZ**.
**Tibetan plateau** heating creates an upper-air anticyclone and a stronger **TEJ**.
**Mascarene High** near **Madagascar** drives **cross-equatorial flow**.

38.s: The dynamic or ITCZ theory explains the southwest monsoon mainly through:
o: The cooling of the Tibetan Plateau during the summer months.
The northward shift of the ITCZ over the Ganga plain, drawing south-east trade winds across the equator as south-westerlies.
The southward shift of the ITCZ over the Indian Ocean during summer.
The permanent eastward movement of the subtropical westerly jet over peninsular India.
38.x: In summer, the ITCZ shifts northward over the Ganga plain as the monsoon trough. South-east trades cross the equator and are deflected to become south-westerly winds.
38.tq: Follow the movement of the pressure belt and the cross-equatorial wind path.
xs: The **ITCZ** shifts **north** over the **Ganga plain** as the **monsoon trough**, pulling **SE trades** across the equator as **SW winds** — option **(2)**.
Its **N-S swings** set the rainfall (UPSC CSAT).
A **southward** ITCZ shift is the opposite of the summer pattern.
xa: During **breaks**, the trough shifts to the **Himalayan foothills**.
**STJ** north of the Himalayas → **onset**; back south → **withdrawal**.
Thermal theory: Sir Edmund **Halley**, **1686**.

38.s:

38.x: All three statements are correct. The northward shift of the subtropical westerly jet is associated with onset, while its return south of the Himalayas accompanies withdrawal; the tropical easterly jet extends from the South China Sea to East Africa.
38.tq: Combine onset, withdrawal and jet-stream path statements before selecting the coded option.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
The **subtropical westerly jet (STJ)** shifts **north of the Himalayas** in summer → **onset** — correct.
The **TEJ** runs from the **South China Sea to East Africa** — correct.
The STJ's return **south** → **withdrawal** — correct.
xa: The **TEJ** coincides with the **SW monsoon**.
**Tibetan plateau** heating strengthens the **TEJ**.
In the retreating monsoon the **TEJ disappears**.

38.s: The heating of the Tibetan Plateau contributes to the southwest monsoon by:

Blocking all cross-equatorial winds in the Arabian Sea
Creating a permanent surface high and weakening the tropical easterly jet

xs: Tibetan heating creates an **upper-air anticyclone** and a **stronger Tropical Easterly Jet** — option **(1)**.

xa: A **permanent high** lies in the **S Indian Ocean** (UPSC).

38.s:

2. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole can offset the effect of El Niño.

38.tq: 'Unfavourable' can only mean bad for the monsoon - it stalls it.

Statement 1 correct: **El Nino weakens**; **La Nina strengthens/aids** the monsoon.
Statement 2 correct: a **positive IOD** can offset El Nino.
Statement 3 wrong: an **unfavourable MJO** phase **stalls** the monsoon.

IMD forecast ~**90% of LPA** (Jun 2026).
