3. Gujarat has the largest number of Jains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kerala has the largest number of Christians, though Christians are a majority only in Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya. Statement 2 is correct: Maharashtra has the most Buddhists, following Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur (1956). Statement 3 is wrong: Maharashtra, not Gujarat, has the largest number of Jains. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options with statement 3 are wrong.
67.tq: Largest NUMBER differs from majority/highest SHARE: Christians-Kerala, Buddhists and Jains-Maharashtra.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
1: **Kerala** has the largest number of **Christians** — correct.
2: **Maharashtra** has the most **Buddhists** — correct (UPSC **2001**).
3: Wrong — **Maharashtra**, not Gujarat, has the most **Jains**.
xa: Largest number of Muslims: **Uttar Pradesh**.
Christian majority: **Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya**.
Buddhists' Maharashtra concentration stems from **Ambedkar**'s **1956** Nagpur conversion.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious composition of India:
1. Buddhists form the highest share of the population in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.
2. Sikhs constitute a majority only in Punjab.
3. Jains have their highest population share in Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: All three statements are correct. Buddhist share is highest in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh; Punjab is the only Sikh-majority State; and Jain share is highest in Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat.
67.tq: Check each community against its highest share and majority status before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
Buddhists' highest share: **Sikkim** and **Arunachal Pradesh**; Sikh majority only in **Punjab**; Jains' highest share: **Maharashtra, Delhi, Gujarat**.
xa: Largest number of Buddhists: **Maharashtra**.
Sikhs ≈ **57.7%** of Punjab.
Map questions pair **Ladakh/Sikkim** with Buddhists.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the majority status of religions in India?
o: Sikhs are a majority in Punjab, Haryana and Delhi.
Christians are a majority in Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya.
Muslims are a majority in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
Buddhists are a majority in Maharashtra and Sikkim.
67.x: Christians are a majority in Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya. Sikhs are a majority only in Punjab, while Muslims are not a majority in Uttar Pradesh or Bihar and Buddhists do not form a majority in Maharashtra or Sikkim.
67.tq: Separate majority status from concentration or largest absolute population.
xs: **Christians** are a majority in **Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya** — option **(2)** is correct.
Sikhs are a majority **only in Punjab**; Muslims a majority in **Lakshadweep** and **J&K**; Buddhists are not a majority in Maharashtra or Sikkim.
xa: Nagaland about **88%**, Mizoram **87%**, Meghalaya **75%** Christian.
⚠ **Arunachal Pradesh** is not Christian-majority (≈ **30%**).
Largest number of Christians: **Kerala**.

67.s: Which one of the following statements about Arunachal Pradesh is correct?
o: Hindus are the only major religious group in the State.
Christians constitute more than 50 percent of its population.
It is the only Sikh-majority State in India.
Christians are the largest single group but constitute only about 30 percent.
67.x: Christians are the largest single religious group in Arunachal Pradesh, but they constitute only about 30 percent and therefore do not form a majority.
67.tq: Distinguish the largest single group from a group holding more than half the population.
xs: In **Arunachal Pradesh**, Christians are the **largest single group** but only ≈ **30%** — option **(4)** is correct.
So it is **not Christian-majority**; Punjab is the only **Sikh-majority** state.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes list Arunachal among Christian-majority states.
Arunachal is one of the **8** states/UTs where Hindus are below **50%**.
Buddhists have their **highest share** in Arunachal and **Sikkim**.

67.s: Which of the following correctly states the fuller list of States/Union Territories where Hindus are below 50 percent, although the material notes that no other religion has a majority in some of them?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Kerala, West Bengal, Punjab, Delhi, Goa and Sikkim
Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Jammu and Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Punjab
Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya only
67.x: The fuller eight-unit list is Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Jammu and Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Punjab. The shorter five-State list excludes Lakshadweep, Arunachal Pradesh and Manipur.
67.tq: Handle a confusable five-versus-eight list by identifying the additional units explicitly included in the fuller version.
xs: The fuller list: **Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya, J&K, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Punjab** — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (4) is the **older "five States"** list, which omits Lakshadweep, Arunachal and Manipur.
In those three Hindus are below **50%** but no other religion has a majority.
xa: Hindus are absent as a majority along the **Indo-Bangladesh/Pak borders** and NE hill states.
Muslim majority: **Lakshadweep**, **J&K**.
Sikh majority: **Punjab** only.

67.s: Which State has the largest number of Muslims in India according to Census 2011?
67.x: Uttar Pradesh has the largest Muslim population by number. Jammu and Kashmir (about 68%) and Lakshadweep (about 97%) have Muslim majorities, but a high share is not the same as the largest number; West Bengal and Kerala also have large Muslim populations but fewer than Uttar Pradesh.
67.tq: Largest number: Muslims UP, Christians Kerala, Buddhists and Jains Maharashtra.
xs: **Uttar Pradesh** has the largest number of Muslims — option **(4)** is correct.
**J&K** and **Lakshadweep** have Muslim **majorities**, but not the largest numbers.
xa: J&K about **68%** Muslim; Lakshadweep about **97%**.
Concentrations also in **West Bengal, Kerala, Bihar, Maharashtra, Delhi**.
Islam spread via **Arab merchants**, the **Turkish Sultanate**, **Mughals** and **Sufis**.

67.s: The concentration of Buddhists in Maharashtra is particularly associated with which event?
o: The migration of Sikhs to Delhi
Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur in 1956
The arrival of Arab merchants on the western coast
The spread of Christianity by Portuguese missionaries
67.x: Maharashtra's large Buddhist population is linked to Dr B. R. Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur in 1956.
67.tq: Link a distinctive demographic concentration with its stated historical cause.
xs: Buddhism's **Maharashtra** concentration stems from **Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur** in **1956** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Arab merchants** spread Islam and the **Portuguese** spread Christianity — neither explains Buddhist numbers.
xa: Maharashtra has the **largest number of Buddhists** (UPSC **2001**).
Buddhists' highest share: **Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh**.
Buddhist growth **2001-11**: **6.1%**.

67.s: Which one of the following statements regarding religious settlement patterns is correct?
o: Sikhs are concentrated mainly in the north-eastern hills.
Jains are mainly concentrated in remote hill regions.
Muslims often live in majority neighbourhoods for reasons including security and cultural preservation.
Christians are predominantly urban in all concentration areas.
67.x: Muslims often live in majority neighbourhoods because of security concerns, cultural preservation and rental discrimination. Jains are associated mainly with urban trading communities, and Christians are mostly rural.
67.tq: Use the social-geographical explanation rather than merely recalling a location.
xs: **Muslims** often live in **majority neighbourhoods** for **security**, **cultural preservation** and owing to **rental discrimination** — option **(3)** is correct.
Sikhs are in Punjab, Haryana, Delhi; Jains are **urban** trading communities; Christians are **mostly rural**.
xa: Non-Hindu majorities along the **Indo-Bangladesh/Pak borders**.
Muslim share rose due to **fertility, not religion**.
Christians are concentrated in **NE hills** and the **west coast**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about the Muslim share of India's population:
1. Muslim fertility is now rising and the gap with Hindus is widening.
2. The rise is explained by poorer economic status and lower female education, not by religion as such.
3. It rose from about 10 per cent in 1951 to about 14 per cent in 2011.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statement 3 is correct: about 10 per cent (1951) to about 14 per cent (2011). Statement 2 is correct: the notes attribute it to poorer economic status and lower female education ('fertility, not religion'). Statement 1 is wrong: Muslim fertility is now falling fast and the gap with Hindus is closing. So '2 and 3 only'.
67.tq: Fertility gap tracks income and female education, and it is closing.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: **Muslim fertility is now falling fast** and the **gap with Hindus is closing**.
Statement 2 is correct: the rise reflects **poorer economic status** and **lower female education** — "fertility, not religion".
Statement 3 is correct: Muslim share rose from **10% (1951)** to **14% (2011)**.
xa: Muslim share 2001 → 2011: **13.4% to 14.2%**; growth **24.6%** (highest).
Hindu share fell **80.5% to 79.8%** — first time below 80%.
**Jains** grew slowest (**5.4%**).
Muslims are the **largest minority**: **17.22 crore**.

67.s: Which of the following statements regarding the historical diffusion of Islam and Christianity in India is correct?
o: Islam spread only through Portuguese missionaries.
Christianity reached India through Arab merchants and the Turkish Sultanate alone.
Islam spread through Arab merchants, the Turkish Sultanate, Mughals and Sufis, while Christianity was associated with St Thomas, the Portuguese and Francis Xavier.
Both religions spread exclusively through modern urban migration.
67.x: Islam arrived with Arab merchants and later spread through the Turkish Sultanate, Mughals and Sufis. Christianity was associated with St Thomas, the Portuguese and Francis Xavier.
67.tq: Test a multi-stage historical sequence and reject exclusive wording such as 'only' and 'exclusively'.
xs: Islam spread via **Arab merchants**, **Turkish Sultanate**, **Mughals**, **Sufis**; Christianity via **St Thomas**, the **Portuguese** and **Francis Xavier** — option **(3)** is correct.
The other options mix up the agents or wrongly claim modern migration.
xa: **St. Thomas** arrived in **52 AD**.
Missionaries shaped **coastal Andhra** through schools, hospitals and printing.
Anti-conversion laws: **Odisha** (**1967**) and **MP** (**1968**) first.

67.s: Which pair of anti-conversion laws and years is correctly matched?
67.x: Odisha enacted an anti-conversion law in 1967 and Madhya Pradesh followed in 1968. They were the first States associated with such laws.
67.tq: Start from the sure year-State pair and avoid shifting adjacent years between States.
xs: Anti-conversion laws: **Odisha — 1967**; **Madhya Pradesh — 1968** — option **(1)** is correct.
They were the **first** such laws.
xa: Mid-**2026**: **13 of 28 States** enforce such laws.
**Ambedkar**'s **1956** Nagpur conversion shaped Maharashtra's Buddhists.
Christianity arrived in **52 AD** (St. Thomas).

67.s: According to Census 2011 figures for residual Andhra Pradesh, which of the following is the correct order of religious shares from highest to lowest?
67.x: In residual Andhra Pradesh, Hindus accounted for about 90.9 per cent, Muslims about 7.3 per cent and Christians about 1.4 per cent.
67.tq: Compare the percentage shares and identify the descending order.
xs: Residual AP: **Hindus** about **90.9%** > **Muslims** about **7.3%** > **Christians** about **1.4%** — option **(4)** is correct.
Options placing Christians above Muslims ignore that Christians are only about **1.4%**.
xa: AP Christians (**2024-25**): **6.82 lakh**.
Christians concentrate in **coastal districts and tribal agency areas**.
Muslims concentrate in **Rayalaseema**: **Kurnool, YSR Kadapa, Anantapur**.

67.s: The Christian population in Andhra Pradesh is concentrated mainly in:
o: The coastal districts and tribal agency areas
Only the metropolitan region of Visakhapatnam
67.x: The Christian population of Andhra Pradesh is concentrated in the coastal districts and tribal agency areas. It is not confined to Rayalaseema or a single metropolitan region.
67.tq: Use the location clue and reject options that impose an unsupported exclusive concentration.
xs: AP's Christians are concentrated in **coastal districts and tribal agency areas** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Rayalaseema** districts have the highest **Muslim** share instead.
xa: AP Christians: **6.82 lakh** (≈ **1.4%**).
Missionaries shaped **coastal Andhra** (schools, hospitals, printing).
**Christian Bhavan** at **Adavithakkellapadu** (Guntur).

67.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the minority population of Andhra Pradesh?
1. It is mostly urban.
2. It contains a large Below-Poverty-Line segment.
3. It has a low share in economic support schemes.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
67.x: All three statements correctly describe the minority population of Andhra Pradesh in APSES 2024–25: it is mostly urban, has a large Below-Poverty-Line segment and has a low share in economic support schemes.
67.tq: Test a cluster of linked social indicators without reversing their direction.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** is correct.
AP's minorities (**2024-25**) are **mostly urban**, with a **large BPL segment** and a **low share in economic support schemes**.
xa: AP has a **State Minorities Commission**, separate **Minorities** and **Christian Minorities Finance Corporations**, and a **Waqf Board**.
Minority allocation (**2026-27**): **₹5,434 crore → ₹6,090 crore**.
**Urdu** declared **second official language** (**17 Mar 2026**).

67.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the highest Muslim population shares are associated with which group of districts?
67.x: The highest Muslim shares in Andhra Pradesh are associated with the Rayalaseema districts of Kurnool, YSR Kadapa and Anantapur.
67.tq: Match the religious concentration with the correct regional district group.
xs: AP's highest Muslim shares are in **Rayalaseema**: **Kurnool, YSR Kadapa, Anantapur** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Coastal** districts and tribal agency areas host the Christians.
xa: AP Muslims about **7.3%**.
AP Waqf Board pays **₹10,000/month** to Imams, **₹5,000** to Mouzzans.
**1,652** pilgrims approved for **Haj 2025**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the central minority scholarship schemes:
1. The Pre-matric Scholarship covers Classes IX and X.
2. The Post-matric Scholarship is for students whose parental income is below Rs 2.5 lakh.
3. The Merit-cum-Means Scholarship (2007) is for professional and technical UG-PG courses.
4. The scholarships are paid through NSP 2.0 and DBT, with 50% earmarked for girls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Pre-matric covers Classes IX-X, Post-matric has a Rs 2.5 lakh income ceiling, and Merit-cum-Means (2007) covers professional/technical UG-PG. Statement 4 is wrong: payment is through NSP 2.0 and DBT, but 30% (not 50%) is earmarked for girls. So '1, 2 and 3 only' is right; '1 and 2 only' misses 3, and the options with 4 are wrong.
67.tq: Remember 30% for girls; 2.5 lakh ceiling; MCM 2007.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2)** is correct.
1: **Pre-matric** covers Classes **IX-X** — correct; 2: **Post-matric** income limit **₹2.5 lakh** — correct.
3: **Merit-cum-Means** (**2007**) = professional/technical UG-PG — correct.
4: Wrong — **30%**, not 50%, is earmarked for **girls**.
xa: Paid via **NSP 2.0** and **DBT**.
**Aadhaar-based One Time Registration** from **2024-25**.
AP (April **2026**) fast-tracked DBT of post-matric scholarships.

67.s: Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) was formerly known as:
67.x: PMJVK was formerly called the Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MsDP).
67.tq: Discriminate between similarly associated minority welfare programmes by their former names.
xs: **PMJVK** was formerly the **Multi-sectoral Development Programme** (**MsDP**) — option **(4)** is correct.
It funds infrastructure, unlike scholarship or skill schemes; it is **centrally sponsored**.
xa: Revised from **2022-23** to cover **all districts** incl. **112** Aspirational Districts.
Its focus is **Minority Concentration Areas**.
**2024-25**: projects worth **₹646.91 crore** approved.

67.s: Jiyo Parsi is intended to address:
o: The educational backwardness of Urdu-speaking students
The decline of the Parsi population
The infrastructure gap in Minority Concentration Areas
67.x: Jiyo Parsi targets the decline of the Parsi population.
67.tq: Match a distinctive scheme name with its narrowly defined target group.
xs: **Jiyo Parsi** targets the **decline of the Parsi population** — option **(3)** is correct.
Urdu coaching is run by the **AP Urdu Academy**; Haj aid by the **Haj Committee**; MCA infrastructure by **PMJVK**.
xa: **PMJVK** (formerly **MsDP**) funds infrastructure in **Minority Concentration Areas**.
**Central Waqf Council** = statutory, **1964**.
Latest notified minority: **Jains (2014)**.

67.s: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body established in:
67.x: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body dating from 1964.
67.tq: Use direct institutional year recall while separating the Council from later Waqf legislation.
xs: The **Central Waqf Council** is statutory, set up in **1964** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is a central body, separate from the state-level **AP State Waqf Board**.
xa: **Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025 / UMEED**: notified **5 April 2025**, in force **8 April 2025**.
The Act applies the **Limitation Act** and audits waqfs earning over **₹1 lakh**.
AP Waqf Board surveyed un-notified waqf properties: **7,005** of **10,522**.

67.s: Which one of the following is NOT a provision or associated feature mentioned in relation to the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 and UMEED?
o: Mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of its income
Uploading property data on the UMEED portal within six months
Audit of waqfs earning over ₹1 lakh
67.x: The stated audit requirement applies to waqfs earning over ₹1 lakh; a mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of income is not specified.
67.tq: Find the option that extends a qualified provision into an absolute one.
xs: **Mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of income** is not a provision — option **(2)** is correct.
The audit applies only to waqfs **earning over ₹1 lakh**.
The **Limitation Act** applies, and property data go on the **UMEED portal** within **6** months — both are provisions.
xa: Notified **5 April 2025**; in force **8 April 2025**.
**Central Waqf Council** dates from **1964**.
AP Waqf Board pays **₹10,000/month** to Imams.

67.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Andhra Pradesh body/scheme)
a. AP State Minorities Finance Corporation
b. AP State Christian Minorities Finance Corporation
c. AP State Waqf Board
d. AP State Haj Committee

List-II (2024-25 fact)
i. 1,652 pilgrims approved for Haj 2025
 ii. Post-matric RTF of ₹36.34 crore to 50,767 beneficiaries
 iii. ₹10,000 per month to Imams and ₹5,000 to Mouzzans
 iv. ₹150.92 crore allocation and Jerusalem pilgrimage assistance

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
67.x: The Minorities Finance Corporation corresponds to post-matric RTF, the Christian Corporation to ₹150.92 crore and pilgrimage assistance, the Waqf Board to payments to Imams and Mouzzans, and the Haj Committee to 1,652 pilgrims.
67.tq: Start from the distinctive Haj-pilgrim and Waqf honorarium pairs, then complete the matching.
xs: **Minorities FC-RTF, Christian FC-₹150.92 cr, Waqf Board-Imam honorarium, Haj Committee-1,652 pilgrims** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Minorities FC**: post-matric RTF **₹36.34 cr** to **50,767**; **Christian FC**: **₹150.92 cr** + Jerusalem aid.
**Waqf Board**: **₹10,000/month** to Imams, **₹5,000** to Mouzzans; **Haj Committee**: **1,652** pilgrims for Haj **2025**.
xa: Minorities FC also pays **NTR Bharosa** **₹1,362.81 cr** to **3,26,617** minority pensioners.
Christian FC: **₹5,000** honorarium to pastors of **8,427** churches.

67.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent Andhra Pradesh minority-related measures is correct?
o: ₹1,800 crore a year was allocated to Imams and Mouzams, and Urdu ceased to have official status.
₹180 crore a year was allocated only to pastors, and Telugu was declared the second official language.
₹18 crore a year was allocated to Imams and Mouzams, and Urdu was declared the third official language.
₹180 crore a year was allocated to Imams and Mouzams, and Urdu was declared the second official language.
67.x: The annual allocation for Imams and Mouzams was stated as ₹180 crore, and Urdu was declared the second official language of Andhra Pradesh.
67.tq: Combine the correct amount with the correct language-status fact and reject altered scale or status.
xs: **₹180 crore** a year goes to **Imams and Mouzams**, and **Urdu** was declared the **second official language** — option **(4)** is correct.
The other options change the amount, the beneficiaries or the language's status.
xa: Urdu became second official language on **17 Mar 2026**.
Minority allocation **₹5,434 crore → ₹6,090 crore**.
AP Waqf Board: **₹10,000/month** to Imams, **₹5,000** to Mouzzans.

67.s: Which one of the following accurately describes the status of the Uniform Civil Code in the context stated?
o: Uttarakhand’s UCC has been in force since January 2025; Bills passed by Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh await Presidential assent.
UCC has been in force in all NDA-ruled States since January 2025; no State Bills await assent.
Only Assam’s Bill awaits Presidential assent, while Uttarakhand’s UCC has not yet commenced.
Uttarakhand, Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh all implemented their UCC laws in 2024.
67.x: Uttarakhand’s UCC came into force in January 2025, while the Bills of Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh were awaiting Presidential assent.
67.tq: Separate an enacted and operative law from Bills that have only been passed and await assent.
xs: **Uttarakhand**'s UCC is in force since **January 2025**; **Assam, Gujarat, MP** Bills await **Presidential assent** — option **(1)** is correct.
So UCC is not in force in all NDA states, and the three states have not implemented it.
xa: Union Home Minister: UCC in all **21** NDA-ruled States by **2029**.
NCM Chairperson: **Harjit Singh Grewal** (**Jul 2026**).
Census **2027** asks the religion and birthplace of both parents.

67.s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised primarily because it:
o: Gives the Centre unbridled power to notify minorities, despite the state-level identification approach associated with T.M.A. Pai.
Transfers all minority identification powers exclusively to State Commissions.
Requires every minority community to be identified only through a census conducted by the Supreme Court.
Prevents the Centre from notifying any minority community.
67.x: The criticism is that Section 2(c) gives the Centre unbridled power to notify minorities, whereas T.M.A. Pai is associated with state-level identification.
67.tq: Match the legal criticism with the correct authority and constitutional interpretation.
xs: **Section 2(c)** gives the Centre "**unbridled power**" to notify minorities, against the **T.M.A. Pai** **state-level** identification test — option **(1)** is correct.
It does not hand powers to State Commissions or bar the Centre from notifying.
xa: Latest notified minority: **Jains (2014)**.
Religious minorities are only about **5%** of higher-judiciary appointees.
"**Demography**" narrative vs **fertility** data is another debate.

67.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relevant minority institutions and facts in Andhra Pradesh?
o: AP has only a Waqf Board; Christians number 6.28 lakh and Urdu is the third official language.
AP has a State Minorities Commission, but Urdu is not an official language and Christians number 8.62 lakh.
AP has only a Central Minorities Commission and no separate Christian Finance Corporation or Waqf Board.
AP has a State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations, and a Waqf Board; Christians number 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
67.x: Andhra Pradesh has the stated State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations and a Waqf Board; its Christian population is 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
67.tq: Check the complete institutional and numerical combination rather than one isolated fact.
xs: AP has a **State Minorities Commission**, separate **Minorities** and **Christian Minorities Finance Corporations**, a **Waqf Board**; Christians **6.82 lakh**; **Urdu** second official language — option **(4)** is correct.
**6.28** and **8.62 lakh** are distorted figures; Urdu is the **second**, not third, official language.
xa: Christians ≈ **1.4%** of AP.
Urdu declared second official language on **17 Mar 2026**.
AP also has a **Haj Committee** and an **Urdu Academy**.

67.s: The Census 2027 enumeration schedule includes which of the following?
o: Only the six notified religions, without any parental information
The six religions plus ‘other religion’, along with the religion and birthplace of both parents
Only ‘No Religion’ and ‘Other Religion’, along with the birthplace of grandparents
The six religions plus caste, but no question on birthplace
67.x: The Census 2027 schedule lists the six religions and ‘other religion’, and asks the religion and birthplace of both parents.
67.tq: Watch for omissions and substitutions in a list-based enumeration question.
xs: Census **2027** lists **six religions + "other religion"** and asks the **religion and birthplace of both parents** — option **(2)** is correct.
It asks about **parents**, not grandparents, and keeps the **six religions**.
xa: Census **2011** first offered a **"No Religion"** option.
Six major religions: **Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain**.
**ORP** = **Other Religions and Persuasions** (**0.7%** in **2011**).

67.s: Which notified minority community is the latest among the following, with notification in 2014?
67.x: Jains were notified as a minority community in 2014 and are the latest notified minority among the communities mentioned.
67.tq: Use chronology and distinguish the latest notified community from older notified groups.
xs: **Jains** were the latest notified minority, in **2014** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Christians**, **Parsis** and **Buddhists** were notified earlier.
xa: Jains: **0.4%** of India; lowest growth **5.4%**.
Jains have the **highest literacy** (about **95%**).
Most Jains live in **Maharashtra**.

67.s: Who was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a full three-year term in July 2026?
67.x: Harjit Singh Grewal was appointed NCM Chairperson for a full three-year term in July 2026. T.M.A. Pai is the Supreme Court case on State-level identification of minorities, Virginius Xaxa chaired the 2013 committee on tribal status, and K.S. Singh led AnSI's People of India project.
67.tq: NCM Chairperson (Jul 2026): Harjit Singh Grewal.
xs: **Harjit Singh Grewal** became NCM Chairperson for a full **3**-year term in **Jul 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
**T.M.A. Pai** is a judgment on minority identification; **Xaxa** and **K.S. Singh** are tribal/anthropology figures.
xa: **Section 2(c)** of the NCM Act gives the Centre power to notify minorities.
Latest notified minority: **Jains (2014)**.
AP has its own **State Minorities Commission**.

67.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Census 2011:
1. The literacy rate was 74.04 per cent.
2. India's total population was 121.09 crore.
3. The decadal population growth (2001-11) was 21.54 per cent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statement 2 is correct: 121.09 crore. Statement 3 is wrong: decadal growth in 2001-11 was 17.64 per cent; 21.54 per cent was the 1991-2001 figure. Statement 1 is correct: literacy was 74.04 per cent (male 82.14, female 65.46). So '1 and 2 only'.

Statement 3 is wrong: decadal growth 2001-11 was **17.64%**.

68.s: The Dardic branch, including Kashmiri, belongs to which language family?

68.s: The Austro-Asiatic language family in India is represented by which of the following branches?
68.x: The Austro-Asiatic family includes the Munda branch, with languages such as Santhali and Mundari, and the Mon-Khmer branch, including Khasi.

68.s:

68.s: Which one of the following statements about Santhali is correct?

68.tq: Combine script, creator and amendment-year facts to reject near-miss options.

68.s:

2. Hindi and English are the official languages of the Union.
3. A State is constitutionally required to adopt Hindi as its only official language.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: States may choose their own official language or languages, while Hindi and English are the Union’s official languages. A State is not required to adopt Hindi as its only official language.
68.tq: Identify the extreme word ‘only’ in the false statement about State language choice.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1)** is correct.
1: Each State **chooses its own** official language(s) — correct (**Art. 345**).
2: **Hindi + English** are Union official languages — correct (UPSC).
3: Wrong — no State must adopt Hindi alone.
xa: AP: **Telugu and Urdu** (**2019** PYQ).
Meghalaya: **English** + **Khasi and Garo**.
**Official Languages Act, 1963** kept English after **1965**.

68.s:
Consider the following statements about the Munshi-Ayyangar formula:
1. It prohibited all provinces from using English for official purposes.
2. It was adopted on 14 September 1949, a date now observed as Hindi Diwas.
3. It provided a 15-year transition for Hindi in Devanagari to become the Union's official language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
68.x: Statement 2 is correct: adopted on 14 September 1949 (Hindi Diwas). Statement 3 is correct: Hindi in Devanagari became the Union's official language with a 15-year transition, and 14 languages were placed in the Eighth Schedule. Statement 1 is wrong: provinces were free to choose a regional language or English. So '2 and 3 only'.
68.tq: Munshi-Ayyangar: 14 Sept 1949, 15-year transition, provinces free to use English.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: provinces were **free to choose a regional language or English**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **Munshi-Ayyangar formula** was adopted on **14 September 1949** — now **Hindi Diwas**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Hindi in Devanagari** became the Union's official language with a **15-year transition**.
xa: The formula recognised **14** languages in the Eighth Schedule.
**Official Languages Act, 1963** kept English in use after **1965**.
**Art. 343**: official language of the Union — Hindi in Devanagari.
**Art. 351**: Union's duty to develop Hindi.

68.s: The Official Languages Act, 1963 is significant because it:
o: Required every State to adopt the three-language formula
Continued the use of English alongside Hindi after 1965
Removed Hindi from the Union’s official-language framework
Made Sanskrit the sole official language of the Union
68.x: The Official Languages Act, 1963 continued English in use alongside Hindi after 1965.
68.tq: Identify the legal effect of the Act rather than confusing it with the original constitutional transition plan.
xs: The **Official Languages Act, 1963** kept **English** in use **after 1965**, alongside **Hindi** — option **(2)** is correct.
The three-language formula came from the **NPE 1968**, not this Act.
xa: **Munshi-Ayyangar** formula gave a **15-year** transition.
Union: **Hindi + English**.
**Art. 344**: Official Language Commission.

B. Article 344
C. Article 345
D. Article 351

o: Article 350A — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 350B — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 351 — Union’s duty to develop Hindi

The Special Officer is under **Art. 350B**; **350A** = **mother-tongue instruction at primary stage**.
**351** (develop Hindi) and **343** (Union language) are correct.

**Art. 394A**: authoritative translation of the Constitution.

68.s: Which one of the following is the correct present list of languages added by the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003?
68.x: The 92nd Amendment Act, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule.

68.s: The 96th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 changed the name of which language in the Eighth Schedule?

xs: The **96th Amendment** (**2011**) changed "**Oriya**" to "**Odia**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It renamed a language already in the Schedule; it did not add one.

Eighth Schedule: **14** originally, **22** now.

68.tq: Use the constitutional-provision trap by separating linked Articles from other language provisions.
xs: The Eighth Schedule is linked with **Articles 344(1) and 351** — option **(1)** is correct.
**344** = Official Language Commission; **351** = Union's duty to develop Hindi drawing on **Eighth Schedule languages**.
xa: **Art. 394A**: authoritative translation — a benefit of inclusion.
**Art. 343**: Union language; **Art. 345**: State language.
Eighth Schedule: **14** originally, **22** now.

68.s: Which one of the following statements about English and the Eighth Schedule is correct?
o: English was included in the original Schedule but removed in 1992.
English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.
English was added by the 92nd Amendment along with Santhali.
English is one of the 22 scheduled languages by convention.
68.x: English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.
68.tq: Test the distinction between official use of English and its constitutional Schedule status.
xs: **English has never been** in the Eighth Schedule — option **(2)** is correct.
It is an official language of the Union with Hindi, but not a scheduled language.
xa: "**NOT** in the Eighth Schedule" PYQs: **Bhojpuri**, **English**.
**Official Languages Act, 1963** kept English after **1965**.
Meghalaya and **Nagaland** use **English** officially.

68.s: The 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule cover approximately what percentage of the population's mother tongues?
68.x: The 22 scheduled languages cover the mother tongues of approximately 96.71 percent of the population.
68.tq: Distinguish the current coverage figure from the earlier 91 percent figure.
xs: The **22** scheduled languages cover **96.71 percent** (**96.71%**) of mother tongues — option **(3)** is correct.
Earlier, **18** languages covered **91%** (before **2003**).
xa: **99 languages** remain outside (**Jul 2025**).
Hindi alone = **43.6%**.
Census **2011**: **121** languages.

68.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gor Boli or Lambadi?
o: It is an Austroasiatic language written in Ol Chiki.
It is a Tibeto-Burman language confined to the North-East.
It is a Dravidian language with a widely standardised script of its own.
It is an Indo-Aryan language spoken by Banjaras and has no script of its own.
68.x: Gor Boli or Lambadi is Indo-Aryan, is spoken by Banjaras across several States, and has no script of its own.
68.tq: Separate language family, community, geographical spread and script.
xs: **Gor Boli (Lambadi)** is **Indo-Aryan**, spoken by **Banjaras**, with **no script of its own** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is written in **Telugu, Devanagari, Kannada**; **Ol Chiki** belongs to Santhali.
xa: Banjaras live in **AP, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan**.
Demand for Eighth Schedule inclusion continues (**23 Jul 2026**).
**Halbi** is also Indo-Aryan.

68.s: A language community seeks authoritative translation of the Constitution under Article 394A, interpretation in Parliament and central development funds. These are principally associated with:
o: Recognition as a non-scheduled Census language
Classification as a dialect under Hindi
Recognition by the People's Linguistic Survey alone
68.x: Interpretation in Parliament, authoritative constitutional translation under Article 394A and central development funds are stated benefits associated with Eighth Schedule inclusion.
68.tq: Apply the listed benefits to identify the relevant constitutional status.
xs: **Art. 394A** translation, Parliament interpretation and central funds come with **inclusion in the Eighth Schedule** — option **(3)** is correct.
Non-scheduled Census languages and PLSI listing give no such benefits.
xa: Other benefits: **Sahitya Akademi** recognition, option in the **UPSC** Indian-language paper.
**No fixed criteria** for inclusion.
**22** scheduled languages now.

68.s:
Arrange the following languages in chronological order of their recognition as classical languages of India:
A. Kannada
B. Sanskrit
C. Odia
D. Tamil
68.x: Tamil was recognised in 2004, Sanskrit in 2005, Kannada in 2008 and Odia in 2014.
68.tq: Fix the earliest and latest entries first, then place the intervening years.
xs: The correct order is **Tamil – Sanskrit – Kannada – Odia** (D, B, A, C) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tamil** was the **first** classical language (**2004**), followed by **Sanskrit** (**2005**).
**Kannada** was recognised in **2008** (with Telugu) and **Odia** in **2014**.
xa: **Telugu** was recognised in **2008** together with Kannada; **Malayalam** in **2013**.
India now has **11** classical languages; **Pali and Prakrit** are the only ones **outside** the Eighth Schedule.
⚠ Trap: "Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Odia were all recognised in 2008" is **wrong**.
Classical status is granted by the **Government of India**.

68.s:
With reference to the revised criteria for classical languages in 2024, consider the following statements:
1. Knowledge texts were added to the scope of eligible literature.
2. Both prose and poetry were recognised in the revised formulation.
3. Epigraphic evidence was added as a consideration.
4. The requirement that the tradition must be original and not borrowed was retained without change.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The revised criteria dropped the requirement that the tradition must be ‘original, not borrowed’, so statement 4 is false.
68.tq: Watch for a statement that changes a reported revision into a continuation of the old rule.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: the **2024 revision** added **knowledge texts** — correct.
Statement 2: these knowledge texts cover both **prose and poetry** — correct.
Statement 3: **epigraphic evidence** was added — correct.
Statement 4 is wrong: the revision **dropped** the **"original, not borrowed"** rule.
xa: Core criterion: **high antiquity** — early texts **1,500-2,000 years** old.
Another criterion: a **rich ancient literary tradition** regarded as heritage.
India has **11** classical languages; status is granted by the **Government of India**.
**Granth Kutir** at Rashtrapati Bhavan holds books in all **11** classical languages.

68.s: The status of a classical language is granted by:
68.x: Classical-language status is granted by the Government of India, not by an individual State Government or an academic institution.
68.tq: Apply the ‘who grants or authorises this?’ authority test.
xs: Classical-language status is granted by the **Government of India** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is not a power of a **State Government**, the **UGC** or the **Sahitya Akademi**.
⚠ Trap in the notes: "the **Government of Uttar Pradesh** granted it" is **wrong**.
xa: **Tamil** was the first classical language (**2004**); **Sanskrit** followed in **2005**.
**Pali and Prakrit** are the only classical languages outside the **Eighth Schedule**.

68.s:
Which of the following statements regarding classical languages is correct?
1. India has 11 classical languages.
2. Telugu, Marathi and Bengali are among the classical languages.
3. Pali and Prakrit are the only classical languages outside the Eighth Schedule.

68.tq: Combine a numerical fact with list-membership statements and identify the complete combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is correct.
Statement 1: India has **11** classical languages.
Statement 2: **Telugu, Marathi and Bengali** are all classical languages (BPSC 2025 "more than one of the above").
Statement 3: **Pali and Prakrit** are the only classical languages **outside the Eighth Schedule**.
xa: **Telugu** became classical in **2008** along with **Kannada**.
**Tamil** (**2004**) was the first; **Sanskrit** (**2005**) the second.
**Granth Kutir** at Rashtrapati Bhavan holds about **2,300 books and 50 manuscripts** in all 11 classical languages.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Goa — Konkani, with Marathi also used

68.tq: Start with the sure state-language pair and eliminate the swapped state associations.
xs: **Goa – Konkani** (with **Marathi** also used) is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Ladakh** (Regulation 2025): English, Hindi, Urdu, **Bhoti, Purgi**.
**AP**: **Telugu and Urdu** (2019 PYQ answer).

68.s: Which of the following languages are declared official languages of Meghalaya along with English?
68.x: Meghalaya has English as an official language, with Khasi and Garo also declared official languages.

xs: Meghalaya declared **Khasi and Garo** official languages along with **English** — so option **(2)** is correct.

**Bhoti and Purgi** are Ladakh's; **Konkani/Marathi** are Goa's; **Nepali/Lepcha** are Sikkim's.

**Khasi and Garo** are among the languages still **pending** for the Eighth Schedule.
Khasi's Mon-Khmer link is evidence the **Meghalaya plateau** was once part of peninsular India.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the language arrangement introduced or reported for the concerned region?
o: Ladakh — English, Hindi, Urdu, Bhoti and Purgi
Kerala — Khasi and Garo as associate official languages
Meghalaya — Tamil and Kannada for notified minority areas
Sikkim — English, Urdu, Bhoti and Purgi only

xs: **Ladakh – English, Hindi, Urdu, Bhoti and Purgi** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
This list comes from the **Official Languages Regulation 2025** (14 Jan 2026).
**Khasi and Garo** associate status belongs to **Meghalaya**, not Kerala.
**Tamil and Kannada** for notified minority areas belongs to **Kerala**, not Meghalaya.
xa: **Kerala's Malayalam Language Bill 2025** lets Tamil/Kannada minorities in notified areas correspond in their own languages.

**Art. 345**: State Legislature adopts the State official language(s).

68.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Census 2011 recorded about 26% of Indians as bilingual.
2. Census 2011 recorded about 26% of Indians as trilingual.

68.x: Statement 1 is correct: about 26% were bilingual in Census 2011. Statement 2 is wrong: only about 7% were trilingual. Statement 3 is correct: the three-language formula came with NPE 1968 after the Kothari Commission. So '1 and 3 only' is right; '1 only' misses 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
68.tq: 26% bilingual, 7% trilingual; three-language formula = NPE 1968 (Kothari).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: Census 2011 recorded about **26%** as **bilingual** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: only about **7%** were **trilingual**.
Statement 3: the **three-language formula** came with the **National Policy on Education 1968**, after the **Kothari Commission** — correct.
xa: The three-language formula remains a live dispute (**Jun 2026**).
**Art. 350A**: instruction in the **mother tongue at primary stage**.
Critics say the Census **understates English bilingualism**.

68.s: India has approximately how many languages listed in UNESCO’s Atlas of Endangered Languages?
68.x: India has about 197 languages listed in UNESCO’s Atlas of Endangered Languages, the highest number for any country.
68.tq: Use the precise numerical figure and eliminate nearby altered values.
xs: India has about **197** languages in the **UNESCO Atlas** of endangered languages — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is the **most of any country**.
xa: **SPPEL (2013)** protects languages with **fewer than 10,000 speakers**; run by **CIIL, Mysuru**.
Threats: **globalisation + English**, **migration/nuclear families**, **no mother-tongue schooling**, **lack of scripts**.
**Kerala** published dictionaries of endangered **Mavila** and **Malaveduvan** (Kannur-Kasaragod).

68.s:

3. It covers languages having fewer than 1,000 speakers.

68.x: Statement 1 is correct: SPPEL is a Union Education Ministry scheme of 2013. Statement 2 is correct: it is run by CIIL, Mysuru. Statement 3 is wrong: it covers languages with fewer than 10,000 speakers, not 1,000. So '1 and 2 only' is right; the other options include the wrong statement 3.
68.tq: SPPEL: 2013, CIIL Mysuru, below 10,000 speakers.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: **SPPEL** is a **Union Education Ministry** scheme of **2013** — correct.
Statement 2: it is run by **CIIL, Mysuru** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: SPPEL covers languages with **fewer than 10,000 speakers**, not 1,000.
xa: India has about **197** endangered languages in the UNESCO Atlas — the most of any country.
The Census also treats **10,000+ speakers** as the cut-off for counting a "language".
**CESCT**, a wing of **CIIL Mysuru**, was moved to **Nellore**.

68.s: Which State published a comprehensive bilingual tribal dictionary series for preserving vanishing tribal languages?
68.x: Odisha published a comprehensive bilingual tribal dictionary series for preserving vanishing tribal languages.

xs: **Odisha** published a comprehensive **bilingual tribal dictionary** series — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2019 PYQ).

**Kerala** produced dictionaries only of **Mavila** and **Malaveduvan**.

**Kui/Kuvi** is spoken by the **Kandhas of Odisha** (Dongria Kondh).
**SPPEL (2013)** is run by **CIIL, Mysuru**.

68.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a threat to endangered tribal languages?
o: Availability of scripts for tribal languages
Dominance of English on the internet
Absence of schooling in the mother tongue
68.x: Availability of scripts is not a threat; rather, the lack of scripts for tribal languages is identified as a threat. Migration, nuclear families, English dominance and lack of mother-tongue schooling are threats.
68.tq: Find the single reversed or negative formulation among otherwise valid threats.
xs: **Availability of scripts** is not a threat — the threat is the **lack of scripts** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Listed threats: **globalisation + English** (incl. **internet dominance of English**), **migration, nuclear families**, **no mother-tongue schooling**.
xa: **SPPEL (2013)** protects languages with fewer than **10,000** speakers.
**Adi Vaani** (2026): India's first **AI translation platform** for tribal languages.

68.s: Bhasha Sangam, launched in 2018, was associated with which initiative?
68.x: Bhasha Sangam was a 2018 initiative under Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat.
68.tq: Match a named initiative with its parent programme and year.
xs: **Bhasha Sangam (2018)** comes under **Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Under it, **school students** learn simple sentences in all **22 scheduled languages**.
xa: **SPPEL** (**2013**) protects endangered languages; run by **CIIL, Mysuru**.
**Adi Vaani** (2026): first AI translation platform for tribal languages.
**"Jago"** (26 Aug 2026): AI assistant by the **Tribal Affairs Ministry**.

68.s: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022 is associated with which development?
o: Making Urdu the second official language statewide
Recognition of Telugu as a classical language
Creation of the Telugu Language Commission
Moving the Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Telugu to Nellore

**Telugu's classical status** came in **2008**, and the move of **CESCT to Nellore** is a separate step.
xa: The CM **confirmed** Urdu as the second official language (17 Mar 2026).
**AP State Urdu Academy**: free computer training in **36 centres** (2024-25).
**P. Trivikram Rao** heads the **Mandali Venkata Krishna Rao Official Language Commission**.

68.s:
Which of the following statements about Telugu is correct?

Statement 1: Telugu is **Dravidian** (**South-Central** branch).
Statement 2: it has been a **classical language since 2008**.
Statement 3: it is one of the **22 scheduled languages**.

68.x: The Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Telugu was moved to Nellore.

xs: **CESCT** was moved to **Nellore** — so option **(4)** is correct.

xa: Telugu has been a **classical language since 2008**.
AP made **Telugu Mahotsavam** an **annual event** (announced at **Undavalli Caves**).

68.s:
Consider the following statements about Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy:
1. He designed a script for the Savara language and prepared Savara-Telugu dictionaries and a Savara manual.

3. He is regarded as the father of the Vyavaharika (colloquial) Telugu movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
68.x: Statement 3 is correct: Gidugu led the Vyavaharika (colloquial) Telugu movement. Statement 2 is wrong: 29 August, Telugu Language Day, is Gidugu's own birth anniversary. Statement 1 is correct: he designed a script for Savara and prepared Savara-Telugu dictionaries and a Savara manual. So '1 and 3 only'.
68.tq: Gidugu: colloquial Telugu, 29 August, Savara script.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Gidugu** designed a script for **Savara** and prepared **Savara-Telugu dictionaries** and a **Savara manual**.
Statement 2 is wrong: **Telugu Language Day (29 August)** is **Gidugu's** own birth anniversary.
Statement 3 is correct: he is the father of the **Vyavaharika (colloquial) Telugu** movement.
xa: **Savara (Sora)** is an **Austro-Asiatic, Munda** language of the Srikakulam-Vizianagaram hills.
Telugu became a **classical language in 2008**; **CESCT** moved to **Nellore**.
First fully Telugu inscription: **Kalamalla (575 CE, Renati Cholas, Kadapa)**.
Earliest Telugu word: **"Nagabu"** (Amaravati inscription).

68.x: Statement 1 is correct: 'Nagabu' appears in the Amaravati inscription. Statement 2 is correct: the Kalamalla inscription of 575 CE by the Renati Cholas is the first fully Telugu inscription. xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: the earliest Telugu word **"Nagabu"** is in the **Amaravati inscription** — correct.
Statement 2: the **Kalamalla inscription (575 CE)** of the **Renati Cholas** is the first fully Telugu inscription — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: Kalamalla is in **Kadapa**, not the Krishna-Godavari delta.
xa: Telugu is called the **"Italian of the East"**.
The **Coastal (Krishna-Godavari)** dialect is the base of **standard Telugu**.
Telugu has been **classical since 2008**.

68.s: Telugu is popularly known as the:
68.x: Telugu is popularly called the ‘Italian of the East’.

xs: Telugu is called the **"Italian of the East"** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes give no such epithet as "Sanskrit of the South", "Latin" or "Greek of the East" for Telugu.
xa: Earliest Telugu word: **"Nagabu"** (**Amaravati** inscription).
