69.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Political stability at origin — Push factor
69.x: Political instability, not political stability, is a push factor. Education is a pull factor, while monsoon failure and poor rural infrastructure push people away from the origin.
69.tq: Find the wrongly matched pair by separating adverse origin conditions from attractive destination conditions.
xs: **Political stability at origin – Push factor** is wrong — so option **(4)** is correct.
The push factor is political **instability**, along with conflict and persecution.
**Poor rural infrastructure** and **monsoon failure** are push factors; **education** is a pull factor — all correct.
xa: Pull factors: **jobs, higher wages**, **health care**, **security**, amenities.
**Drought in the Sahel** is cited as an environmental factor.
**Information networks** (Keralites, Sikhs) also drive migration.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about rural-to-urban migration:
1. High labour demand in cities can encourage it.
2. Unbalanced rural-urban development can encourage it.
3. Lack of rural employment opportunities can encourage it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: All three conditions encourage rural-to-urban migration: cities generate labour demand, regional development is uneven, and rural areas may offer few employment opportunities.
69.tq: Recognise multiple simultaneous causes and select the comprehensive coded option.
xs: All three encourage rural-to-urban migration — so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is correct (**BPSC 2024 PYQ**).
**High labour demand in cities**, **unbalanced rural-urban development** and **few rural jobs** are all causes.
xa: Rural-to-urban migration is **male**-dominated, for **employment**, and **drives urbanisation**.
About **26%** of the population is aged 10-24; job search drives rural-urban moves.
Distress migration from **Rayalaseema** and north coastal AP goes to **Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai**.

69.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its role in migration?
o: Keralites and Sikhs — Information networks influencing migration
Drought in the Sahel — Pull factor of higher wages
Adulthood — Least mobile stage of life
69.x: Information networks associated with groups such as Keralites and Sikhs can influence migration. Adults are generally the most mobile, while drought and conflict are adverse conditions that push migration.
69.tq: Match examples with the type of factor or demographic influence they represent.
xs: **Keralites and Sikhs** illustrate **information networks** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Drought in the Sahel** is an **environmental** push, not a pull of higher wages.
**Adults** are the **most mobile**, not the least.
**Conflict** is a **push** factor at origin, not a destination amenity.
xa: Pull factors: **jobs, higher wages, education, health care**.
**Place utility** = desirability of a destination.
Push: **low farm productivity**, **monsoon failure**, **poverty**.

69.s: Who propounded the Push-Pull Theory of migration in “A Theory of Migration” published in 1966?
69.x: Everett S. Lee propounded the push-pull theory in his 1966 work, “A Theory of Migration”.
69.tq: Link the theory, title and year with its proponent.
xs: **Everett S. Lee** gave the **push-pull theory** in "A Theory of Migration" (**1966**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**E.G. Ravenstein** gave the **laws of migration** (**1885, 1889**).
**Wilbur Zelinsky** – **mobility transition model**; **Griffith Taylor** – **migration zone theory**.
xa: Lee's name tied to migration theory was asked in **UPPSC 2017**.
⚠ **Notestein and Thompson** → demographic transition; **Doubleday** → diet-based population theory.
**Place utility** = desirability of a destination.

69.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

a. Laws of migration — E.G. Ravenstein
b. Mobility transition model — Wilbur Zelinsky
c. Migration zone theory — Griffith Taylor
d. Place utility — Desirability of a destination
69.x: Ravenstein is associated with the laws of migration, Zelinsky with the mobility transition model, Taylor with migration zone theory, and place utility with the desirability of a destination.
69.tq: Start from a sure scholar-theory pair and verify the remaining associations.
xs: All four pairs are correct — so option **(4)** "a, b, c and d" is correct.
**Laws of migration** – **E.G. Ravenstein** (1885, 1889); **mobility transition model** – **Wilbur Zelinsky**.
**Migration zone theory** (racial) – **Griffith Taylor**; **place utility** – desirability of a destination.
xa: **Push-pull theory** – **Everett S. Lee** (**1966**).
**Counter-urbanisation** = movement from urban to rural areas.
⚠ **Notestein and Thompson** = demographic transition, not migration.

69.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Everett S. Lee — Demographic transition theory
69.x: Everett S. Lee is associated with migration theory, not demographic transition theory. Notestein and Thompson are linked to demographic transition, while Doubleday is associated with a diet-based population theory.
69.tq: Use the confusable-theorist trap by separating migration theory from demographic transition.
xs: **Everett S. Lee – Demographic transition** is wrong — so option **(4)** is correct.
Lee is linked to **migration theory** (push-pull, **1966**).
**Notestein and Thompson** → **demographic transition**; **Doubleday** → **diet-based population theory** — correctly matched.
xa: This trap appeared in **UPPSC 2017**.
**Ravenstein** – **laws of migration**; **Zelinsky** – **mobility transition model**.
**Griffith Taylor** – **migration zone theory**.

69.s: The Nationwide Migration Survey conducted by MoSPI for July 2026–June 2027 is significant because it is:
o: The first international migration survey since 1951
The first full migration survey since 2007–08
The first survey limited to seasonal agricultural labour
The first Census survey based only on place of birth
69.x: The MoSPI Nationwide Migration Survey for July 2026–June 2027 is the first full migration survey since 2007–08.
69.tq: Link the survey period with its historical significance and avoid confusing it with Census methods.
xs: It is the **first full migration survey since 2007-08** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **MoSPI Nationwide Migration Survey (NSO)** runs **July 2026-June 2027**.
xa: It redefines **short-term migration** as **15 days-6 months** (earlier 1-6 months).
A **migrant** = **Usual Place of Residence** differs; **6-month** rule.
**Census 2027** will also record migration.

69.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the earlier and revised definitions of short-term migration in the MoSPI survey?
o: Earlier: less than 15 days; revised: more than 6 months
69.x: The earlier definition covered 1–6 months, whereas the revised definition covers 15 days–6 months.
69.tq: Use the changed boundary value to discriminate between two otherwise similar definitions.
xs: Earlier **1-6 months**; revised **15 days-6 months** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option 2 reverses the old and new definitions.
xa: The **MoSPI** survey runs **July 2026-June 2027**, first full survey since **2007-08**.
Migrant = **Usual Place of Residence** differs, using the **6-month** rule.
**PLFS 2020-21** overall migration rate: **28.9%**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about migration in Census 2011:
1. By place of last residence, 455.8 million people were migrants, about 37.6% of the population of 121 crore.
2. Of these migrants, 141.2 million had moved during 2001-11.
3. Inter-state migrants numbered fewer than 1 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is correct: 455.8 million migrants by place of last residence, about 37.6% of 121 crore. Statement 2 is correct: 141.2 million had moved during 2001-11. Statement 3 is wrong: there were over 4.1 crore inter-state migrants. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3; '1 and 2 only' is right.
69.tq: Remember the chain 455.8 million total, 141.2 million in the decade, 4.1 crore inter-state.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: **455.8 million** migrants by **place of last residence** = about **37.6%** of 121 crore — correct.
Statement 2: **141.2 million** moved during **2001-11** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: there were **over 4.1 crore** inter-state migrants.
xa: **Rural to rural** was the **largest stream** in **2011**.
**PLFS 2020-21**: overall migration rate **28.9%**.
**Census 2027** will give fresh migration data.

69.s: Which of the following is the correct order of the leading out-migration states mentioned in the data?
o: Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, followed by Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
Maharashtra and Delhi, followed by Gujarat and Haryana
Kerala and Andhra Pradesh, followed by Tamil Nadu and Gujarat
Punjab and West Bengal, followed by Delhi and Maharashtra
69.x: Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are the leading out-migration states, followed by states including Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. The other options mainly describe destination states or reverse the source-state pattern.
69.tq: Start with the leading pair and distinguish source-state ordering from destination-state lists.
xs: **Bihar and Uttar Pradesh**, followed by **Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh**, are source states — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Maharashtra, Delhi, Gujarat, Haryana** are **destination** states.
**Kerala, AP, Tamil Nadu** also appear among destinations.
xa: Other source states: **Uttarakhand, J&K, West Bengal, Punjab, Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, AP**.
**Delhi** and **Maharashtra** lead in-migration.
Census 2011: **over 4.1 crore** inter-state migrants.

69.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the leading in-migration destinations listed in the migration data?
o: Delhi, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala
Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh
Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Punjab
69.x: The listed leading in-migration destinations include Delhi, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala.
69.tq: Recall the destination-state cluster and avoid mixing it with the source-state cluster.
xs: **Delhi, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala** are destination states — so option **(1)** is correct.
**UP, Bihar, Odisha, Rajasthan, MP, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal** are **source** states.
xa: **Delhi** and **Maharashtra** lead in-migration; **Haryana, Karnataka, Punjab** are also destinations.
**UP** and **Bihar** lead out-migration.
World: highest migrant share – **UAE**; largest number – **Europe**; highest percentage – **Oceania**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about the demographic consequences of migration:
1. Population grows at the source area and falls at the destination.
2. Source areas are often left with an ageing population and a higher share of women.
3. Uneven change in constituency populations makes migration relevant to delimitation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is wrong: it is reversed; population grows at the destination and falls at the source. Statement 2 is correct: the source is left with ageing people and more women. Statement 3 is correct: uneven constituency populations matter for delimitation. So '1 and 2 only', '1 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' all wrongly include statement 1; '2 and 3 only' is right.
69.tq: Check the direction: destinations gain, sources lose.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong (reversed): population **grows at the destination** and **falls at the source**.
Statement 2: the source is left with **ageing** people and **more women** — correct.
Statement 3: uneven constituency populations matter for **delimitation** (Delimitation Bill 2026) — correct.
xa: Migration **distorts the age-sex structure** at origin and destination.
Workers move from **high-fertility** to ageing **low-fertility** states.
Social side: **"sons of the soil"** hostility, slums, **"dual city"**.

69.s: The term “social remittances” in the context of migration refers to:
o: Remittance of only foreign currency to the source region
Tax collected from inter-state migrant workers
Compulsory welfare payments made by the destination government
Transfer of skills and ideas by migrants
69.x: Social remittances refer to the transfer of skills, knowledge and ideas by migrants. They are distinct from monetary remittances.
69.tq: Discriminate between monetary remittances and social remittances.
xs: **Social remittances** = **skill transfer** by migrants — so option **(4)** is correct.
They are listed under **economic** consequences alongside money **remittances**.
xa: India's remittances hit **USD 135 billion** in **FY2024-25**.
Remittances increasingly come from **skilled professionals** in developed countries rather than West Asia.
Global remittances: **USD 905 billion** (2024).

69.s: The expression “son of the soil” hostility is associated with:
o: Hostility towards migrants in the destination region
Transfer of skills from destination to source
Cultural exchange between migrants and local people
69.x: “Son of the soil” hostility denotes opposition to migrants by local populations in destination areas, including hostility expressed against groups such as “Bihari bhaiya”.
69.tq: Direct recall of a characteristic social consequence.
xs: **"Sons of the soil"** = **hostility towards migrants** at the destination — so option **(1)** is correct.
Example: hostility against **"Bihari bhaiya"**; it is a **social** consequence.
**Skill transfer** is "social remittances"; **cultural mixing** is a separate positive effect.
xa: Other social effects: **slums**, **"dual city"/"double city"**, **ghettoisation**.
**M.S. Gore**: family ties kept even in **nuclear households**.
**ONORC** gives **ration portability** — an unrelated scheme.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about migrant workers during the COVID-19 lockdown:
1. About 122 million jobs were lost.
2. It exposed job insecurity and wage exploitation of migrants.
3. It showed that migrant workers were fully covered by social security.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is correct: about 122 million jobs were lost. Statement 2 is correct: the lockdown exposed job insecurity and wage exploitation. Statement 3 is wrong: it exposed the absence of social security for migrants. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3; '1 and 2 only' is right.
69.tq: The lockdown exposed gaps; any statement claiming full protection is the false one.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: about **122 million job losses** — correct.
Statement 2: it exposed **job insecurity** and **wage exploitation** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: it exposed **no social security** for migrants.
xa: Migrants also miss **voting**; portability (**ONORC, EPF**) is patchy.
**e-Shram** (**2021**): **31.78 crore** registered by **July 2026**.
**OSH Code 2020** covers **self-migrating workers** and portability of **PDS**.

69.s: The Inter-State Migrant Workmen (RECS) Act, 1979 has been subsumed in the:
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
69.x: The Inter-State Migrant Workmen (RECS) Act, 1979 is now subsumed in the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020.
69.tq: Discriminate between the four labour codes by matching the subject matter.
xs: The 1979 Act is subsumed in the **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **OSH Code** merges **13 laws**.
It is one of the **4 Labour Codes** (consolidating 29 laws), in force from **November 2025**.
xa: OSH Code covers **self-migrating workers** with an annual **lump-sum travel allowance**.
It provides portability of **PDS** and **social security**.
The 1979 Act required registration for **5 or more** inter-state migrants.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, 1979:
1. An establishment had to register only if it employed 20 or more inter-State migrant workers.
2. Weak enforcement has been a recognised gap in the Act.
3. Workers were entitled to a displacement allowance of 50 per cent of monthly wages and a journey allowance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is wrong: registration was required for establishments with 5 or more inter-State migrant workers (contractors also needed licences). Statement 3 is correct: displacement allowance of 50 per cent of monthly wages plus journey allowance. Statement 2 is correct: poor enforcement is a known gap. So '2 and 3 only'. The Act is now subsumed in the OSH Code, 2020.
69.tq: 1979 Act: 5+ migrants, 50% displacement allowance, weakly enforced.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: registration applied to establishments with **5 or more** inter-state migrants, not 20.
Statement 2 is correct: **weak enforcement** is a known gap.
Statement 3 is correct: a **displacement allowance (50% of monthly wages)** + **journey allowance**.
xa: The Act is now **subsumed in the OSH Code, 2020**, which merges **13 laws**.
The **4 Labour Codes** came into force in **November 2025**.
The OSH Code covers **self-migrating workers** and gives an annual **lump-sum travel allowance**.
**e-Shram portal (2021)**: **31.78 crore** registered by **July 2026**.

69.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature mentioned in relation to migrant workers under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020?
o: Coverage of workers who migrate on their own
Portability of PDS and social security across States
Abolition of all contractor licensing requirements
69.x: The OSH Code covers workers who migrate on their own, provides for annual travel allowance and supports portability of PDS and social security. Abolition of all contractor licensing requirements is not a stated feature.
69.tq: Find the option that goes beyond the stated provisions of the Code.
xs: **Abolition of all contractor licensing** is not an OSH Code feature — so option **(4)** is correct.
The OSH Code covers **self-migrating workers**, gives an annual **lump-sum travel allowance** and portability of **PDS** and social security.
xa: The **OSH Code** merges **13 laws**; it is one of the **4 Labour Codes**.
The Labour Codes came **into force in November 2025**.
The 1979 Act it replaced required **contractors** to hold **licences**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC):
1. It provides NFSA ration portability, so migrants can draw rations anywhere in India.
2. It is operational only in the 28 States and not in the Union Territories.
3. Biometric failures and data mismatches between States remain problems.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is correct: ONORC gives NFSA ration portability anywhere. Statement 2 is wrong: it works in all 36 States/UTs (with 99.9% Aadhaar seeding). Statement 3 is correct: biometric failures and inter-state data mismatches persist. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 2; '1 and 3 only' is right.
69.tq: ONORC covers all 36 States/UTs; the problems are technical, not coverage.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: **ONORC** gives **NFSA ration portability** — migrants draw rations anywhere.
Statement 2 is wrong: it works in **all 36 States/UTs**.
Statement 3: **biometric failures** and **data mismatches** between states are problems — correct.
xa: Aadhaar seeding is **99.9%**.
**e-Shram portal** (**2021**) is a **"One-Stop-Solution"** for unorganised workers.
Migrant portability (**ONORC, EPF**) remains **patchy**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code:
1. It is one of the four Labour Codes.
2. The four Labour Codes consolidated 29 laws.
3. It came into force in November 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: The OSH Code is one of four Labour Codes; together they consolidated 29 laws and came into force in November 2025.
69.tq: Check the institutional status, number of laws and effective date together.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is correct.
Statement 1: the **OSH Code** is one of the **4 Labour Codes**.
Statement 2: the four codes **consolidated 29 laws**.
Statement 3: they came **into force in November 2025**.
xa: The **OSH Code** itself **merges 13 laws**, including the **Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, 1979**.
It covers **self-migrating workers** and gives an annual **lump-sum travel allowance**.
It provides portability of **PDS** and **social security**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about the e-Shram portal:
1. It is a One-Stop-Solution for unorganised workers, linked to 15 central schemes.
2. About 31.78 crore unorganised workers were registered on it by July 2026.
3. It is available in 22 languages through DigiLocker.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is correct: e-Shram (2021) is a One-Stop-Solution linked to 15 central schemes, with a gig and platform worker module. Statement 2 is correct: 31.78 crore were registered by July 2026. Statement 3 is wrong: the 22 languages come through BHASHINI, not DigiLocker. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3; '1 and 2 only' is right.
69.tq: Languages = BHASHINI; a swapped platform name is a common trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: **e-Shram** (**2021**) is a **"One-Stop-Solution"** for unorganised workers, linked to **15 central schemes** — correct.
Statement 2: **31.78 crore** registered by **July 2026** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **22 languages** come via **BHASHINI**, not DigiLocker.
xa: e-Shram has a **gig and platform worker** module.
**ONORC** works in **all 36 States/UTs** with **99.9%** Aadhaar seeding.
**PDOT** (MEA, **Jan 2018**) trained **1,72,220** emigrant workers by 31 Dec 2024.

69.s: The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration was adopted at:
69.x: The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration was adopted at Marrakech in December 2018.
69.tq: Use the place–date pair to eliminate nearby international venues and years.
xs: The **GCM** was adopted at **Marrakech in December 2018** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was then **endorsed by the UN General Assembly**.
xa: It is **non-binding**.
**Not all** UN members adopted it — the **US** stayed out.
It covers **international** migration only, not **internal displacement**.
⚠ In **UPSC 2023**, **none** of the GCM statements were correct.

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration:
1. It was endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly.
2. It is legally binding on all adopting countries.
3. It covers international migration, but not internal displacement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: The Compact was endorsed by the UN General Assembly and covers international migration only. It is non-binding, so statement 2 is false.
69.tq: Identify the false legal-status statement and distinguish international migration from internal displacement.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: the GCM was **endorsed by the UN General Assembly** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: the GCM is **non-binding**.
Statement 3: it covers **international** migration only, **not internal displacement** — correct.
xa: Adopted at **Marrakech in December 2018**.
**Not all** UN members adopted it — the **US** stayed out.
Exam traps test **"all countries"**, **"legally binding"** and **"internal migration"** — all false.

69.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the geographical pattern of international migrants?
o: Europe has the highest migrant share, UAE has the largest number of migrants, and Asia has the highest percentage
UAE has the highest migrant share, Europe has the largest number of migrants, and Oceania has the highest percentage of migrants
Oceania has the highest migrant share, Europe has the largest number of migrants, and UAE has the highest percentage
Qatar has the highest migrant share, Oceania has the largest number of migrants, and Europe has the highest percentage
69.x: The UAE has the highest migrant share of population, Europe has the largest number of migrants, and Oceania has the highest percentage of migrants.
69.tq: Keep absolute number, population share and regional percentage as separate comparisons.
xs: **UAE** – highest migrant share; **Europe** – largest number; **Oceania** – highest percentage — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Largest number = **Europe**; highest percentage = **Oceania** — options 1, 3, 4 mix these up.
xa: The **UAE** and **Europe** answers come from **UPPSC 1999**.
Gulf states **UAE, Qatar and Kuwait** lead in migrant share.
About **3.5 million** Indians live in the **UAE**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about the World Migration Report 2026:
1. It is published by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and is the 13th edition.
2. It is an annual report, brought out every year since 2000.
3. It reports more than 120 million forcibly displaced people and 65.8 million internal displacements caused by disasters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is correct: IOM (founded 1951) publishes it and 2026 is the 13th edition. Statement 2 is wrong: the report is biennial (every two years) since 2000, not annual. Statement 3 is correct: more than 120 million forcibly displaced and 65.8 million disaster-induced internal displacements. So '1 only' leaves out a true statement, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 2; '1 and 3 only' is right.
69.tq: WMR is biennial, not annual: a one-word trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: published by **IOM** (founded **1951**); **13th edition** — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: the report is **biennial** since **2000**, not annual.
Statement 3: more than **120 million** forcibly displaced; **65.8 million** disaster displacements — correct.
xa: People living outside their country of birth are now **3.7%**; the **"2%"** claim is outdated.
It reconfirmed India as the **top remittance recipient** (**USD 137 billion, 2024**).
It ranks India's diaspora as the **largest in the world**.

69.s:
With reference to the Indian diaspora, consider the following statements:
1. India has the largest diaspora in the world.
2. The number of Indians living abroad is over 35 million.
3. About 3.5 million Indians are in the United Arab Emirates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: India is reported to have the world’s largest diaspora, numbering over 35 million people abroad, including about 3.5 million in the UAE.
69.tq: Combine the population figures with the country-specific figure.
xs: All three are correct — so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is correct.
India has the **largest diaspora in the world** (WMR 2026).
**Over 35 million** Indians live abroad, about **3.5 million** of them in the **UAE**.
xa: **India-UAE** is the **5th** largest global migration corridor — mostly workers.
**India-US** (**6th**) is mostly **skilled workers + students**.
Telugu communities live in **195 countries**; AP runs **NRT networks in 148**.

69.s: The remittance pattern of India in FY 2024–25 was increasingly associated with:
o: A complete cessation of remittances from developed countries
Skilled professionals in developed countries rather than only workers in West Asia
Only agricultural labourers in neighbouring countries
Only unskilled workers in the Gulf region
69.x: India received a record USD 135 billion in FY 2024–25, with an increasing contribution from skilled professionals in developed countries rather than mainly from West Asia.
69.tq: Identify the changing source and skill profile of remittances.
xs: Remittances increasingly come from **skilled professionals in developed countries** rather than **West Asia** — so option **(2)** is correct.
India received a record **USD 135 billion** in **FY2024-25**.
xa: In **2024**, India received **USD 137 billion** — top recipient (WMR 2026).
**India-US** corridor (**6th**) is mostly **skilled workers + students**.
Global remittances: **USD 905 billion** (2024).

69.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India’s position in global remittances in 2024?
o: India was the second-largest recipient, with US$97 billion
India was the top recipient, with US$75 billion
India was outside the top five recipients, with US$137 billion
India was the top recipient and the only country receiving more than US$100 billion, with US$137 billion
69.x: India remained the top remittance recipient in 2024, receiving US$137 billion and being the only country to receive more than US$100 billion.
69.tq: Check rank, exclusivity and amount together because each is a possible trap.
xs: India was the **top recipient** and the **only country above USD 100 billion**, with **USD 137 billion** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The figure is from the **World Migration Report 2026** (IOM).
xa: India's record: **USD 135 billion** in **FY2024-25**.
Global remittances: **USD 905 billion**; **USD 685 billion** to low- and middle-income countries.
India also has the **largest diaspora** — over **35 million**.

69.s: The Pre-Departure Orientation Training (PDOT), launched in January 2018, is run by which ministry and for whom?
o: Ministry of External Affairs, for emigrants going to ECR countries
Ministry of Labour and Employment, for inter-State migrant workers
Ministry of Education, for Indian students going abroad
Ministry of Home Affairs, for refugees entering India
69.x: PDOT is the MEA's programme (Jan 2018) for emigrant workers going to Emigration Check Required (ECR) countries; about 1,72,220 were trained by 31 Dec 2024. It is not a Labour Ministry scheme for inter-State migrants, not meant for students, and has nothing to do with refugees coming into India.
69.tq: PDOT = MEA, ECR emigrants, 2018.
xs: **PDOT** is run by the **Ministry of External Affairs** for **emigrants to ECR countries** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It began in **Jan 2018**; **1,72,220** emigrant workers were trained by 31 Dec 2024.
It is not a Labour Ministry scheme for inter-state migrants, nor for students or refugees.
xa: **e-Shram** (**2021**) is the portal for **unorganised workers**.
**APNRT** is AP's **diaspora agency**; it ran a help desk for Telugus stranded in the Gulf.
**Konaseema** sent about **15,000** workers to the **GCC** by Dec 2025.

69.s: Which group of districts in Andhra Pradesh is identified as a major source of domestic workers and unskilled labour migrating to the Gulf countries?
o: East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna
69.x: Anantapur, Kadapa and Chittoor in Rayalaseema are identified as important source districts for domestic workers and unskilled labour migrating to the Gulf.
69.tq: Use the source-region clue to distinguish Rayalaseema districts from other Andhra Pradesh regions.
xs: **Anantapur, Kadapa and Chittoor** (**Rayalaseema**) send Gulf **domestic workers and unskilled labour** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Srikakulam-Vizianagaram-Visakhapatnam** is **Uttarandhra**, from where **distress/seasonal** migration occurs.
xa: **Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema** (Godavari delta) sent about **15,000** workers to the GCC; **over 70%** were young women.
Rayalaseema also sees **distress migration** to **Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai**.
Telugu diaspora: Gulf (**Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain**) + **USA**.

69.s: Seasonal labour migration from Andhra Pradesh is particularly associated with which of the following areas?
o: The forest districts of southern Telangana
Only the urban districts of Coastal Andhra
69.x: Seasonal labour leaves drought-prone Rayalaseema as well as the north-coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh.
69.tq: Identify the paired geographical regions rather than choosing an option narrowed by the word 'only'.
xs: Seasonal labour leaves **drought-prone Rayalaseema** and **north-coastal districts** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Godavari delta** (Konaseema) is known for **Gulf** migration of women, not seasonal labour.
xa: **Srikakulam fishermen** migrate to the **Gujarat coast**.
Rayalaseema + north coastal AP see **distress migration** to Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai.
The CM said the **Bhogapuram airport** would end migration from **Uttarandhra**.

69.s: Srikakulam fishermen are specifically reported to migrate seasonally to which destination?
69.x: Srikakulam fishermen migrate seasonally to the Gujarat coast.
69.tq: Test the migrant-origin and destination pair directly; the location is the key discriminator.
xs: **Srikakulam fishermen** migrate to the **Gujarat coast** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Srikakulam lies in the **Kalinga/Uttarandhra** north-coastal region.
xa: **Seasonal labour** also leaves **drought-prone Rayalaseema** and north-coastal districts.
**Rayalaseema** (Anantapur, Kadapa, Chittoor) sends Gulf domestic and unskilled workers.
About **25 lakh** AP migrant workers were reportedly affected by the **SIR** of electoral rolls.

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding migration from Konaseema:
1. About 15,000 jobseekers had gone to GCC countries by December 2025.
2. Over 70 per cent of them were women.
3. The migration was exclusively for highly skilled professional employment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the migrants were mostly women working as housemaids, and cases of exploitation were reported.
69.tq: Reject the extreme occupational claim and retain the supported figure and gender-share statements.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: about **15,000** jobseekers went to the **GCC** by **Dec 2025** — correct.
Statement 2: **over 70%** were **women** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: they were mostly **housemaids**, with **exploitation** cases — not skilled professionals.
xa: The data come from the **Konaseema Centre for Migration**.
Konaseema district is **Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema** in the **Godavari delta**.
**APNRT** is the state's **diaspora agency**.

69.s: The Chief Minister stated that migration from Uttarandhra would 'become a thing of the past' with the construction of which infrastructure project?
69.x: The statement linked the expected reduction in migration from Uttarandhra to the new Bhogapuram airport.
69.tq: Match the policy statement with the specific infrastructure project named in it.
xs: The CM linked it to the new **Bhogapuram airport** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He said migration from **Uttarandhra** "will become a thing of the past" (2 Aug 2026).
xa: **Uttarandhra/north coastal AP** sees **distress** and **seasonal** migration.
**Srikakulam fishermen** go to the **Gujarat coast**.
New **industrial nodes** aim to slow distress migration to **Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai**.

69.s: Migration is regarded as the main component of the difference between rural and urban growth because:
o: natural increase differs little between rural and urban areas
all rural migrants move only to metropolitan cities
natural increase is absent in rural areas but very high in urban areas
urban areas have no migration-related population increase
69.x: Migration is the main component of the rural-urban growth difference because natural increase differs little between rural and urban areas.
69.tq: Link the cause with the demographic comparison instead of choosing absolute statements about rural or urban growth.
xs: **Natural increase differs little** between rural and urban areas — so option **(1)** is correct.
Hence **migration** is the main component of the **rural vs urban growth difference**.
xa: **Rural to urban** migration **drives urbanisation**.
Population **grows at the destination** and **falls at the source**.
Workers move from **high-fertility** to ageing **low-fertility** states.

69.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: APNRT — Gulf help desk for stranded Telugus
NSO — Telugu diaspora network in 148 countries
69.x: APNRT, the AP Non-Resident Telugu Society, ran the help desk for Telugus stranded in the Gulf (Mar 2026). The other pairs are wrong: IOM publishes the World Migration Report, the NSO/MoSPI runs the Nationwide Migration Survey, and the NRT networks in 148 countries are run by the AP government.
69.tq: Start from the sure organisation-function pair and eliminate swapped institutional roles.
xs: **APNRT – Gulf help desk for stranded Telugus** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**IOM** publishes the **World Migration Report**, not anything on the SIR.
**NRT networks in 148** countries are run by the **AP government**; **MoSPI/NSO** runs the **Nationwide Migration Survey**.
xa: **APNRT** = **AP Non-Resident Telugu Society**, the state's diaspora agency (3 Mar 2026).
Telugu communities live in **195 countries**.
The **MoSPI** survey runs **July 2026-June 2027**.

70.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
70.x: Only 1901 — 10.84% is correct. The other pairs attach later figures to the wrong year: 1931 was 11.99% (17.97% was 1961), 1961 was 17.97% (27.81% was 2001), and 2001 was 27.81% (31.16% was 2011).
70.tq: Match each census year with its percentage and eliminate shifted values.
xs: **1901 – 10.84%** urban is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: 2011 urban population: **37.71 crore (377.1 million)**.
Phases: **slow 1901-31**, **medium 1931-61**, **rapid 1961 onwards**.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about the phases of urban growth in India:
1. 1901-1931 was the slow phase, with urban growth of about 0.35% a year.
2. 1931-1961 was the rapid phase of urban growth.
3. In the phase from 1961 onwards, urban population rose from 78.94 million to 377.11 million.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: Statement 1 is correct: 1901-31 was the slow phase (about 0.35% a year). Statement 2 is wrong: 1931-61 was the medium phase (towns 2,049 to 2,330); the rapid phase began in 1961. Statement 3 is correct: from 1961, urban population rose from 78.94 to 377.11 million (+262%). So '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 2; '1 and 3 only' is right.
70.tq: Slow-medium-rapid splits at 1931 and 1961.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: **1901-31** was the **slow** phase, about **0.35%** a year — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: **1931-61** was the **medium** phase (towns **2,049 → 2,330**); the rapid phase began in **1961**.
Statement 3: from 1961, urban population rose **78.94 → 377.11 million** (**+262%**) — correct.
xa: In **1931**, **33.46 million** people lived in **2,049** towns.
Urban population in **1961**: **78.94 million**.

70.s: India's urban population is projected to reach approximately what level by 2031?
70.x: India's urban population is projected to reach about 60 crore by 2031.
70.tq: Use the projected absolute population figure, not the separate percentage projection.
xs: Urban population is projected at **about 60 crore by 2031** — so option **(3)** is correct.
In **2011** it was **37.71 crore** (31.16% of the population).
xa: More than **50%** of Indians are projected to be urban by **2050**.
**EAC-PM** satellite data put urbanisation as high as **63% in 2015**.
Cities cover **3%** of India's land but produce about **60% of GDP**.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about the World Cities Report 2026:
1. It was brought out by UN-Habitat and released at the World Urban Forum in Baku.
2. It says about 40% of people (about 3.4 billion) face housing shortages.
3. It says about 110 million people live in slums or informal settlements.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: Statement 1 is correct: UN-Habitat released it at the World Urban Forum, Baku. Statement 2 is correct: about 40% (~3.4 billion) face housing shortages. Statement 3 is wrong: about 1.1 billion, not 110 million, live in slums or informal settlements. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3; '1 and 2 only' is right.
70.tq: Watch billion vs million: 3.4 billion short of housing, 1.1 billion in slums.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: the **World Cities Report 2026** is by **UN-Habitat**, released at the World Urban Forum, **Baku** — correct.
Statement 2: about **40% (~3.4 billion)** face **housing shortages** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: about **1.1 billion** (not 110 million) live in **slums or informal settlements**.
xa: **UN-Habitat** has its headquarters in **Nairobi** and was set up in **1978**.
AP signed an **MoU with UN-Habitat** for a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in **Amaravati**.
Census 2011: **6.54 crore** people in Indian slums.

70.s: The number of towns in India rose from about ______ in 1901 to ______ in 2011.
70.x: India had about 1,827 towns in 1901 and 7,935 in 2011. 2,049 was the number of towns in 1931 and 5,161 the total in 2001; 1,362 -> 3,894 is the rise in census towns (2001-11); 3,799 -> 4,041 is the rise in statutory towns (2001-11).
xs: Towns rose from about **1,827** (1901) to **7,935** (2011) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**2,049** is the 1931 count; **5,161** is the 2001 total.
xa: Roughly **9,000** towns today; only about **500** are large cities.

70.s:
Consider the following statements about India's urban growth during 2001-2011:
1. Urban population rose from 286 million to 377.1 million, an increase of about 41.8%.
2. The urban share of population rose from 27.81% to 31.16%.
3. For the first time since Independence, the absolute increase in urban population exceeded the rural increase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: Statement 1 is wrong: urban population did rise from 286 to 377.1 million, but that is about +31.8%, not 41.8%. Statement 2 is correct: urban share went from 27.81% to 31.16%. Statement 3 is correct: urban areas added about 91 million, more than rural areas, a first since Independence. So '1 and 2 only', '1 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' all wrongly include statement 1; '2 and 3 only' is right.
70.tq: 31.8% is the decadal growth, 31.16% the urban share; a changed digit marks the false statement.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: urban population rose **286 → 377.1 million**, which is **+31.8%**, not 41.8%.
Statement 2: urban share **27.81% → 31.16%** — correct.
Statement 3: **first time since Independence** the absolute urban increase (**91.0 million**) exceeded rural (**90.4 million**) — correct.
xa: ⚠ **31.80%** is **decadal growth**; **31.16%** is the **urban share**.
Main reason: **reclassification of rural areas as urban** (census towns **1,362 → 3,894**).

70.s: Which one of the following was the principal reason for the sharp increase in India's urban population during 2001–2011?
o: Reclassification of erstwhile rural areas as urban
Reduction in the number of census towns
70.x: The principal reason was the reclassification of rural areas as urban. Census towns increased from 1,362 to 3,894 during this period.
70.tq: Identify the main cause instead of choosing a related but unsupported demographic factor.
xs: The main reason was **reclassification of erstwhile rural areas as urban** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-G1 2017).
**Census towns** rose from **1,362 to 3,894** — they increased, not fell.
xa: Components of urban growth: **natural increase** + **rural-urban migration** + **new towns / reclassification**.
Urban population rose **+31.8%**, to **377.1 million**.
⚠ Trap: "1,362 to **3,784**" is a misprint; the Census figure is **3,894**.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the components of urban growth:
1. Natural increase in population
2. Net rural-urban migration
3. Reclassification of rural areas as urban
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: Natural increase, rural-urban migration and reclassification or creation of new towns are the three identified components of urban growth.
70.tq: Check whether all three recognised components are included before selecting the complete combination.
xs: All three are components — so option **(4)** "1, 2 and 3" is correct.
Urban growth = **natural increase** + **rural-urban migration** + **new towns / reclassification**.
xa: In 2001-11, **reclassification** was the main reason for the jump.
**Migration** is the main reason urban and rural growth differ.
**MoHUA** told Parliament the **1981** Census Town criteria are outdated, yet the RGI will **retain them for Census 2027**.

70.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the figures 31.80% and 31.16% associated with urbanisation in India?
o: 31.80% is the rural share and 31.16% is the decadal urban growth
31.80% is the decadal urban growth and 31.16% is the 2011 urban share
31.80% is the 2011 urban share and 31.16% is the rural share
Both figures represent the 2011 urban share
70.x: 31.80% is the 2001-11 decadal growth of urban population (286 to 377.1 million), while 31.16% is the urban share of India's population in Census 2011; confusing the two is a common trap.
70.tq: Separate two look-alike percentages by asking what each percentage measures.
xs: **31.80%** is the **decadal urban growth**; **31.16%** is the **2011 urban share** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: "31.80% of total population" is wrong — that figure is growth (286 → 377.1 million).
xa: Rural share in 2011: **68.84%** (833.1 million).
Urban increase **91.0 million** > rural **90.4 million** — a first since Independence.

70.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a cause of urbanisation in India?
o: Pressure of population on rural land
70.x: Growth of industry and trade, pressure on rural land, low farm productivity, services and transport are identified causes. The complete disappearance of transport services is not a cause stated in this context.
70.tq: Find the extreme reversal of a recognised development factor.
xs: **Complete disappearance of transport services** is not a cause — so option **(3)** is correct.
Causes (APPSC 2008, "all of the above"): **industry and trade**, **pressure on rural land**, **low farm productivity**, **services and transport**.
xa: Push factors: **monsoon failure**, **rural unemployment**.
Pull factors: **jobs**, **health and education**, **transport links**.
**Industrialisation** creates urban jobs.

70.s: The description of urban growth as ‘top-heavy’ primarily refers to which of the following?
o: Class I cities hold about 70% of the urban population.
Million-plus cities account for less than 10% of the urban population.
Rural settlements contain about 70% of the total population.
Class VI towns contain about 70% of the urban population.
70.x: Urban growth is termed top-heavy because Class I cities contain about 70% of the urban population.
70.tq: Translate the descriptive term into its associated quantitative meaning.
xs: "Top-heavy" means **Class I cities hold about 70% of the urban population** — so option **(1)** is correct.
This is from the **Economic Survey 2025-26**.
xa: Class I = **1,00,000 and above**.
Of roughly **9,000** towns, only about **500** are large cities.
**53** million-plus cities/UAs in 2011, up from **35** in 2001.

70.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Class)
a. Class I
b. Class II
c. Class V
d. Class VI
List-II (Population)
i. Less than 5,000
ii. 50,000–99,999
iii. 1,00,000 and above
iv. 5,000–9,999
70.x: Class I is 1,00,000 and above, Class II is 50,000–99,999, Class V is 5,000–9,999 and Class VI is below 5,000.
70.tq: Start from the sure extreme pairs and then verify the remaining class thresholds.
xs: **a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: **Class I** cities hold about **70%** of urban population (top-heavy).
Million-plus city = **10 lakh** or more people.

70.s: Which one of the following is a statutory town?
o: Any continuous urban spread formed by two contiguous towns
Only a village satisfying the three Census Town criteria
Any area that is not classified as rural
A place notified with a municipality, corporation, cantonment board or notified town area committee
70.x: A statutory town is a place notified with a municipality, municipal corporation, cantonment board or notified town area committee and run by a ULB.
70.tq: Distinguish administrative status from Census-based demographic classification.
xs: A **statutory town** has a **municipality, corporation, cantonment board or notified town area committee** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is **notified by the State** and run by a **ULB**.
A **continuous urban spread** of contiguous towns is an **urban agglomeration**; "any area not rural" is not the definition.
xa: **Rural** = any area that is **not urban**.

70.s: An urban agglomeration is best defined as:
o: Any urban area with one lakh or more population
A rural cluster displaying urban occupational structure
A statutory town administered by a municipal corporation only
A continuous urban spread comprising a town with outgrowths or two or more contiguous towns
70.x: An urban agglomeration is a continuous urban spread consisting of a town and its outgrowths or two or more contiguous towns.
70.tq: Use the definition's structural elements—continuity, outgrowths and contiguity—to reject partial descriptions.
xs: An **urban agglomeration** = **town + outgrowths**, or **two or more contiguous towns** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**1 lakh or more** defines a **Class I** town; a **rural cluster with urban traits** is the **Rurban** idea.
xa: **Million-plus/metropolitan city** = **10 lakh** or more people.
**53** million-plus cities/UAs in 2011.
**Greater Mumbai** was the largest UA in 2011 (**18.4 million**).

70.s: Under Article 243P, a metropolitan area means an area having a population of:
70.x: Article 243P defines a metropolitan area as an area with a population of 10 lakh or more.
70.tq: Pair the constitutional Article with its population threshold.
xs: Under **Art. 243P**, a metropolitan area has **10 lakh or more** people — so option **(2)** is correct.
This was inserted by the **74th Amendment**.
xa: **Art. 243ZE**: a **Metropolitan Planning Committee** for every metropolitan area.
**Two-thirds** of MPC members are elected by elected municipal members and panchayat chairpersons.
The 74th Amendment inserted **Part IXA** (Art. **243P-243ZG**) and the **Twelfth Schedule** (**18** functions).

70.s: Which of the following correctly represents the change in the total number of towns between 2001 and 2011?
70.x: The total number of towns increased from 5,161 in 2001 to 7,935 in 2011. The other figures refer to statutory and census towns separately.
70.tq: Match the correct pair of years with the total-town figures, not subgroup figures.
xs: Total towns rose **5,161 → 7,935** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**3,799 → 4,041** is **statutory towns**; **1,362 → 3,894** is **census towns**.
xa: About **1,827** towns in **1901**.
The jump in **census towns** reflects **reclassification** of rural areas.

70.s:
Consider the following estimates of 'hidden urbanisation' in India:
1. The World Bank (2010) put 55.3% of Indians in urban-like areas.
2. The EAC-PM estimate of about 63% urbanisation in 2015 was based on Census Town criteria.
3. Janaagraha's ASICS 2023 found far more urbanisation than the Census shows.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: Statement 1 is correct: the World Bank (2010) estimated 55.3% in urban-like areas. Statement 2 is wrong: the EAC-PM's 63% (2015) figure was based on satellite data, not Census Town criteria. Statement 3 is correct: ASICS 2023 shows far more urbanisation than the Census. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 2; '1 and 3 only' is right.
70.tq: Link each estimate to its source: World Bank 55.3%, EAC-PM satellite 63%, Janaagraha ASICS.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: the **World Bank (2010)** put **55.3%** in **"urban-like"** areas — correct.
Statement 2 is wrong: **EAC-PM's 63% (2015)** was based on **satellite data**, not Census Town criteria.
Statement 3: **Janaagraha's ASICS 2023** shows far more urbanisation than the Census — correct.
xa: The **Census definition** makes urbanisation look slow; the UN **"Degree of Urbanisation"** method would count peri-urban areas.
The **1981** Census Town criteria will still be **retained for Census 2027**.
Official 2011 urban share: **31.16%**.

70.s: Between Census 2001 and Census 2011, the number of census towns in India rose from:
70.x: Census towns rose from 1,362 to 3,894. 3,799 to 4,041 is the rise in statutory towns; '1,362 to 3,784' is a misprinted figure (trap); 5,161 to 7,935 is the rise in total towns.
70.tq: Census towns 2011 = 3,894 (not 3,784).
xs: Census towns rose **1,362 → 3,894** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2017 PYQ).
**3,799 → 4,041** is statutory towns; **5,161 → 7,935** is total towns.
⚠ "**1,362 to 3,784**" is a misprinted figure — a trap.
xa: This rise shows **reclassification** was the main reason for the 2001-11 urban jump.
The **1981** Census Town criteria are criticised for **male bias** and **uniform thresholds**.
The RGI will **retain them for Census 2027**.

70.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
70.x: Ankleshwar is identified as a mining or collection town. Gandhinagar is administrative, Jamshedpur is industrial and Tirupati is religious or cultural.
70.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate towns belonging to other functional categories.
xs: **Mining town – Ankleshwar** is correct — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
**Jamshedpur** is **industrial**, **Gandhinagar** is **administrative**, **Tirupati** is **religious/cultural**.
xa: Garrison town in the same key: **Udhampur**.
Other mining towns: **Raniganj, Hazaribagh, Khammam, Digboi, Jharia**.
**Jamshedpur** is also a **planned industrial town**.

70.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
70.x: Vijayawada is classified as a transport or trade town. Udhampur, Bhadrachalam and Pilani represent garrison, religious and educational functions respectively.
70.tq: Find the town whose functional category belongs to a neighbouring group.
xs: **Resort/tourist – Vijayawada** is wrong — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Vijayawada** is a **transport/trade (market) town**, like Guntur.
**Pilani** – educational, **Udhampur** – garrison, **Bhadrachalam** – religious: correct.
xa: Resort towns: **Shimla, Ooty, Araku, Darjeeling, Kodaikanal, Mount Abu**.
**Vijayawada** is one of AP's **million-plus UAs** (2011) with Visakhapatnam.
Educational towns: **Aligarh, Pilani, Roorkee, Varanasi**.

70.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of diversified towns?
70.x: Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai are diversified towns. Shimla, Ooty and Araku are resort towns; Raniganj, Digboi and Khammam are mining/collection towns; Tirupati, Varanasi and Rameswaram are religious/cultural towns.
70.tq: Identify the common functional category shared by all members of one set.
xs: **Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai** are **diversified** towns — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Shimla, Ooty, Araku** are **resort** towns; **Raniganj, Digboi, Khammam** are **mining**.
**Tirupati, Varanasi, Rameswaram** are **religious/cultural**.
xa: The same three are **modern/British**-origin towns, with Surat and hill stations.
Mumbai and Kolkata are **mega cities** (**10 million** or more) with Delhi.
Madras was the **first municipal corporation** (**1688**).

70.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the historical period of origin?
70.x: Hyderabad is listed among medieval towns. Post-1947 planned towns include Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar, Gandhinagar and Dispur.
70.tq: Use the historical-period trap of assigning a medieval town to the post-1947 category.
xs: **Post-1947 planned – Hyderabad** is wrong — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hyderabad** is a **medieval** town, like Delhi, Jaipur, Lucknow, Agra.
**Kolkata** – modern/British, **Jaipur** – medieval, **Pataliputra** – ancient: correct.
xa: Post-1947 planned: **Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar, Gandhinagar, Dispur**.
Ancient: **Varanasi, Prayagraj, Pataliputra, Madurai**.
Hyderabad's 2011 city (**GHMC**) population was about **68 lakh**.

70.s: Which one of the following is the correct descending order of the first three urban agglomerations by population in 2011?
70.x: The 2011 order was Greater Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata, with populations of approximately 18.4, 16.3 and 14.1 million respectively.
70.tq: Use the first-place and second-place comparison to separate the close alternatives.
xs: 2011 order: **Greater Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Populations: **18.4**, **16.3** and **14.1** million.
In **2001** Kolkata was ahead of Delhi; in **2011** **Delhi overtook Kolkata**.
xa: Only these three are **mega cities** (**10 million** or more).
Next: **Chennai 8.7**, **Bengaluru 8.5**, **Hyderabad 7.7**, **Ahmedabad 6.4**.
**53** million-plus cities/UAs in 2011.

70.s: In the 2011 ranking of urban agglomerations, which city overtook Kolkata compared with the older 2001 order?

71.x: A megalopolis is a chain of merged metropolitan areas; umland is a town's surrounding hinterland; a conurbation is a continuously merged urban area; and a primate city dominates the next city by several times.
71.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes that reverse the closely related urban-form definitions.
xs: **A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Megalopolis** – chain of merged metropolitan areas; **Umland** – area surrounding a town, linked to it.
**Conurbation** – continuous urban area from merging towns; **Primate city** – several times larger than the next city.
xa: ⚠ **Gottmann** = megalopolis; **Geddes** = conurbation; **Jefferson** = primate city.
**Umland** is a **German term** for a town's **hinterland** (UPPSC 2017).
**Megacity** = **10 million+** (1 crore+) people.

71.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
71.x: The concept of the primate city is associated with Mark Jefferson. Rakesh Mohan is associated with three processes of Indian urbanisation.
71.tq: Find the wrong scholar-term association rather than judging the urban definitions.
xs: **Primate city – Rakesh Mohan** is wrong — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **primate city** concept belongs to **Mark Jefferson**.
**Conurbation – Patrick Geddes**, **Umland – German term**, **Megalopolis – Jean Gottmann** are correct.
xa: Gottmann's megalopolis example: the US north-east seaboard, **Boston-Washington**.
**Megalopolis – Gottmann** was asked in **UPPSC 2023**.
A primate city **dominates** the country's urban system.

71.s: The change from Tokyo to Jakarta as the world's most populous city is attributed mainly to:
o: The exclusion of all satellite towns from Jakarta
A new city-definition method in WUP 2025
A change in the boundary of Asia
71.x: The change is attributed to the new city-definition method adopted in World Urbanisation Prospects 2025, rather than a sudden demographic collapse of Tokyo.
71.tq: Distinguish a methodological change from an actual population event.
xs: The change is due to **a new city-definition method in WUP 2025** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**WUP 2025** (UN DESA) now ranks **Jakarta** first, then **Dhaka, Tokyo, New Delhi (4th)**.
xa: Earlier lists had **Tokyo** as the largest city (**APPSC 2018** key).
The **largest city of Asia** = largest of the world under the current list (**Jakarta**; formerly Tokyo).
Cities hold **45%** of the world's **8.2 billion** people.

71.s: A city with a population of 10 million or more is generally classified as a:
71.x: A megacity has a population of 10 million or more, equivalent to one crore or more. A million-plus city has a lower threshold of 10 lakh or more.
71.tq: Discriminate between the 10-million megacity threshold and the 1-million-plus-city threshold.
xs: A city of **10 million or more** is a **Megacity** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That equals **1 crore+** people.
A **million-plus / metropolitan** city has only **10 lakh** or more.
xa: India's 2011 megacities: **Greater Mumbai**, **Delhi**, **Kolkata**.
India's urban population is projected at **951 million by 2050**.
A **primate city** is several times larger than the next city.

71.s: According to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025, which is the correct order of the four most populous cities in the world?
71.x: The order is Jakarta, Dhaka, Tokyo and New Delhi. New Delhi occupies the fourth position in this listing.
71.tq: Use sequence recall and check the first and fourth positions before resolving the middle pair.
xs: WUP 2025 order: **Jakarta, Dhaka, Tokyo, New Delhi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**New Delhi** is **4th**.
xa: The change came from a **new city-definition method**.
⚠ Earlier lists: **Tokyo 1st**, **Delhi 2nd**, **Mumbai 7th**, **Kolkata 10th**.
**WUP 2025** is published by **UN DESA**.

71.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Metropolitan region or city)
A. Mumbai Metropolitan Region
B. Kolkata Metropolitan Area
C. Chennai Metropolitan Area
D. Delhi

xs: **A-4, B-2, C-3, D-1** — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Chennai – CMDA (1974)**; **Delhi – DDA (1957)**.
xa: The **DDA** was India's **first UDA**.
AP: **Visakhapatnam – VMRDA**; **Amaravati – APCRDA**.

71.s:
Consider the following pairs of region and planning authority:
1. Visakhapatnam (Vizag Economic Region) — VMRDA
2. Amaravati — APCRDA
3. Chennai Metropolitan Area — KMDA

Pair 3 is wrong: Chennai is planned by CMDA (1974); KMDA (1970) is Kolkata's authority. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' leaves out a correct pair, and the options with pair 3 include a wrong pair.
71.tq: Match the city's first letter: K-MDA Kolkata, C-MDA Chennai, VMRDA Vizag, APCRDA Amaravati.
xs: Pairs **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding metropolitan growth patterns identified in the Economic Survey 2025-26:

2. The expansion of these cities has been predominantly horizontal.
3. The administrative city always corresponds exactly to the economic metropolitan region.

71.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Survey observes that the administrative city no longer matches the economic metropolitan region, so statement 3 is false.
71.tq: Find the reversed statement about the administrative boundary and economic metro region.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: in **16 major cities** the **periphery grew faster than the core** (2000-2020, night-time lights) — correct.

71.s: Which of the following correctly represents the participating units of the National Capital Region (NCR)?
o: NCT of Delhi and parts of Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh
NCT of Delhi and parts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan
Delhi, Rajasthan, Punjab and Madhya Pradesh
Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
71.x: The NCR comprises the NCT of Delhi and parts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. Punjab and Madhya Pradesh are not participating units of the NCR.
71.tq: Use the constituent-state trap by distinguishing neighbouring states that are outside the NCR.
xs: The NCR is **NCT of Delhi + parts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Punjab and Madhya Pradesh are not in the NCR** (UPPSC 2008, 2017).
xa: Haryana towns: **Rohtak, Karnal**, Panipat, Sonipat, Gurugram, Faridabad.
UP towns: **Khurja**, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Noida; Rajasthan: **Alwar**.

71.s: The National Capital Region Planning Board was established under which Act?
71.x: The NCR Planning Board was set up under the NCRPB Act of 1985.

xs: The **NCR Planning Board** was set up under the **NCRPB Act, 1985** — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: NCRPB approved four greenfield **"Namo Cities"** (Jun 2026).

71.s: How does the United Nations treatment of the Delhi urban region differ from the Census treatment?
o: The Census includes only Delhi and Gurugram, whereas the UN includes only Noida and Ghaziabad.

xs: The **UN** treats **Delhi-Gurugram-Noida-Ghaziabad-Faridabad** as **one agglomeration**; the **Census** counts them **separately** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option 3 reverses the two approaches.
xa: **WUP 2025** ranks **New Delhi 4th** in the world.
**Gurugram, Faridabad** are Haryana's NCR towns; **Noida, Ghaziabad** are UP's.
**Delhi** is the **most polluted capital**.

71.s: Which one of the following towns is NOT a part of the National Capital Region (NCR)?
71.x: Ambala is not in the NCR (UPPSC 2011 trap). Rohtak and Karnal are in the Haryana part of the NCR, and Khurja (Bulandshahr) is in the UP part.
71.tq: NCR trap: Ambala is out; Rohtak, Karnal, Khurja are in.
xs: **Ambala** is **not** in the NCR — so option **(4)** is correct (**UPPSC 2011** trap).
**Rohtak** and **Karnal** are in the **Haryana** part; **Khurja** (**Bulandshahr**) in the **UP** part.
xa: Rajasthan's NCR town: **Alwar**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about municipal solid waste (MSW) in India:
1. India generates about 62 million tonnes of MSW a year.
2. About 30% of MSW is collected and 70% is processed.
3. Cities produce more than 1.5 lakh tonnes of MSW per day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: Statement 1 is correct: about 62 million tonnes a year. Statement 2 is wrong: it is the reverse, about 70% is collected and only 30% processed. Statement 3 is correct: cities produce more than 1.5 lakh tonnes a day (SBM-U). So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and the options with statement 2 include a wrong statement.
71.tq: Collection (70%) is always larger than processing (30%).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: about **62 million tonnes** of MSW a year — correct.
Statement 2 is reversed: about **70%** is **collected** and only **30%** **processed**.
Statement 3: cities produce more than **1.5 lakh tonnes/day** (SBM-U) — correct.
xa: **DRAP** targets **214** legacy dumpsites by **Dec 2026**.
Megacities need stronger **Metropolitan Waste Management Authorities**.
**Swachh Survekshan** (run by **MoHUA**, conducted by **QCI**) ranks cities on cleanliness.

71.s: Which of the following statements regarding urban pollution is correct?
o: Eight of the world's ten most polluted cities are in India, and Kolkata is the most polluted capital.
Eight of the world's ten most polluted cities are in India, and Delhi is the most polluted capital.
Ten of the world's ten most polluted cities are in India, and Delhi is the least polluted capital.
Six of the world's ten most polluted cities are in India, and Mumbai is the most polluted capital.
71.x: Eight of the world's ten most polluted cities are in India, and Delhi is identified as the most polluted capital.
71.tq: Check both parts of the compound statement: the number of Indian cities and the capital-city identification.
xs: **8 of the world's 10 most polluted cities** are in India and **Delhi** is the **most polluted capital** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is not Kolkata or Mumbai, and not all ten cities.
xa: **PARIVARTAN** (**₹9,585 crore**) will replace about **2.07 lakh** old trucks and buses in the NCR.
The **urban heat island** comes from **dense construction, asphalt**, lost tree cover.
Commuters lose **1.5-2 hours** a day in traffic.

71.s: Which comparison regarding the availability of urban planners is correct?
o: India has one planner per 5,000 people, compared with one per lakh in developed countries.
India has one planner per lakh people, compared with one per 5,000 people in developed countries.
Both India and developed countries have one planner per lakh people.
Both India and developed countries have one planner per 5,000 people.
71.x: India has approximately one planner per one lakh people, whereas developed countries have about one planner per 5,000 people.
71.tq: Watch for the reversed ratio trap between India and developed countries.
xs: India has **one planner per 1 lakh** people vs **one per 5,000** in developed countries — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option 1 reverses the two figures; the source is **NITI Aayog**.
xa: Commuters lose **1.5-2 hours** a day (**BCG**).
ES 2025-26 wants a statutory city plan and a **unified metropolitan authority**.
Cities are **"administered, not governed"** (ES).

71.s: Which approach is favoured for addressing informality in large cities?
o: Suspend land-market reforms until urbanisation stops
Integrate informality and reform land markets, including addressing dead capital and using Bhu-Aadhaar
Restrict all migrant employment to the formal sector immediately
Eradicate all informal settlements without integration
71.x: The Economic Survey favours integrating informality rather than eradicating it and recommends land-market reforms involving issues such as dead capital and Bhu-Aadhaar.
71.tq: Select the policy approach that follows the stated reform principle rather than the extreme eradication option.
xs: ES 2025-26: **integrate informality** and **reform land markets** (**"dead capital"**, **Bhu-Aadhaar**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It favours **integrating informality rather than eradicating it**.
xa: Social problems of big cities: **slums**, **migrant pressure**, **crime**, **informal jobs**.
ES argues for a **unified metropolitan authority**.
Census 2011: **6.54 crore** in slums.

71.s: The slum population constituted approximately what percentage of India's urban population according to Census 2011?
71.x: Slum dwellers accounted for about 17.4% of India's urban population in Census 2011.
71.tq: Identify the precise percentage rather than the nearest-looking estimate.
xs: Slum dwellers were about **17.4%** of urban population — so option **(3)** is correct.
Census 2011 counted **6.54 crore** in slums.
xa: **Maharashtra** had the largest slum population; **undivided AP** the highest share (**about 36%**).
**World Bank**: **177 million** slum dwellers, most of any country.
**Greater Visakhapatnam** had the highest share of slum households (**about 44%**).

71.s:
With reference to slums in Census 2011, consider the following statements:
1. Maharashtra had the largest slum population among the States.
2. Greater Mumbai had the largest slum population among million-plus cities.
3. Greater Mumbai had the highest share of slum households among million-plus cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Maharashtra (State) and Greater Mumbai (million-plus city) had the largest slum populations. Statement 3 is wrong: the highest share of slum households was in Greater Visakhapatnam (about 44%), ahead of Mumbai (about 41%). So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options with statement 3 include a wrong statement.
71.tq: Largest number = Mumbai/Maharashtra; highest share = Visakhapatnam/undivided AP.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Maharashtra** had the largest slum population (state) — correct.
Statement 2: **Greater Mumbai** had the largest among million-plus cities — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: the highest **share** was **Greater Visakhapatnam** (**about 44%**) vs Mumbai (**about 41%**).
xa: ⚠ Largest **number** = **Maharashtra / Greater Mumbai**; highest **share** = **Undivided AP / Greater Visakhapatnam**.
Undivided AP: about **36%** of urban population in slums.
Slums = about **17.4%** of urban population.

71.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the slum population in Census 2011?
o: Maharashtra had the highest share of its urban population living in slums.
Undivided Andhra Pradesh had the highest share of its urban population living in slums.
Greater Mumbai had the highest share of slum households among million-plus cities.
The slum population constituted less than 10% of India's urban population.
71.x: Undivided Andhra Pradesh had the highest share of its urban population living in slums, at about 36%.
71.tq: Separate absolute size from percentage share.
xs: **Undivided Andhra Pradesh** had the highest share of urban population in slums (**about 36%**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Maharashtra** had the largest slum **number**, not share.
The highest share of slum households among million-plus cities was **Greater Visakhapatnam**, not Mumbai.
Slums were about **17.4%** of urban population — not under 10%.
xa: Census 2011: **6.54 crore** slum dwellers.
**World Bank**: **177 million** (broader definition).
**Greater Mumbai** had the largest slum population among million-plus cities.

71.s: Which of the following is NOT a major cause of urban flooding identified in the context of expanding cities?
o: Construction over lakes, wetlands and floodplains
Replacement of permeable soil by concrete
71.x: Urban flooding is associated with construction over water bodies and floodplains, concretisation of soil and blocked drains. Expansion of natural vegetation cover is not listed as a cause.
71.tq: Find the one option that does not fit the cause-effect group.
xs: **Expansion of natural vegetation cover** is not a cause — so option **(4)** is correct.
Causes: **built-over lakes, wetlands and floodplains**, **concrete replacing permeable soil**, **blocked drains**.
xa: **Bengaluru**: built-up land **8% (1973) → about 74% (2013)**.
**Visakhapatnam**: flash floods after only a few hours of rain.
Vegetation loss also feeds the **urban heat island**.

71.s: Which combination best explains the urban heat island effect?
o: Low building density, irrigated fields and cool winds
Open wetlands, permeable soil and increased tree cover
Dense construction, asphalt surfaces and loss of tree cover
Reduced construction, bare rock and expanded forests
71.x: Dense construction, asphalt and the loss of tree cover trap heat and intensify the urban heat island effect.
71.tq: Select the complete causal combination rather than an isolated factor.
xs: **Dense construction, asphalt and lost tree cover** trap heat — so option **(3)** is correct.
Open **wetlands**, **permeable soil** and **more trees** would reduce, not cause, the effect.
xa: A **UEA** study of **104** cities found **Patiala** could warm at **double** the projected rate.
**Bengaluru** vegetation fell from **68%** to under **15%**.
**Delhi** is the **most polluted capital**.

71.s:

Statement 1: run by **MoHUA**, conducted by **QCI** — correct.
Statement 2: began **2016 with 73 cities** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: **4,589 cities** were surveyed in **2024-25**.
xa: It is the **world's largest cleanliness survey**.
**Indore** topped the 10 lakh+ Super Swachh League for the **8th time**.

Four greenfield cities, on the **TOD** model around **Namo Bharat (RRTS)** corridors (Jun 2026).

71.s: Which institutional reform has been advocated for megacities instead of merely simplifying compliance procedures?
o: Replacement of municipal bodies by cantonment boards
Transfer of all waste functions to panchayats
71.x: The suggested reform is to establish stronger Metropolitan Waste Management Authorities for megacities rather than rely only on simplified compliance.

72.s:
Consider the following statements about the Human Development Reports:
1. They are published by the World Bank.
2. The first Human Development Report was published in 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
72.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the HDRs are published by the UNDP, not the World Bank. Statement 2 is correct: the first HDR came out in 1990. So '2 only'; '1 only' and 'Both' wrongly accept statement 1, and 'Neither' rejects the correct statement 2.
72.tq: HDR = UNDP, first in 1990 (Mahbub ul Haq with Amartya Sen).
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — so option **(2)** "2 only" is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: the HDR is published by the **UNDP**, not the World Bank.
Statement 2: the **first HDR** came out in **1990** — correct.
xa: The HDR was conceived by **Mahbub ul Haq** with **Amartya Sen**.

72.s:
Consider the following statements about the human development approach:
1. Amartya Sen described capabilities as the substantive freedoms people have to lead lives they value.
2. Mahbub ul Haq conceived the Human Development Report in association with Amartya Sen.
3. Amartya Sen's book 'Development as Freedom' was published in 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
72.x: Statement 2 is correct: the Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq conceived the HDR with Amartya Sen. Statement 1 is correct: Sen defined capabilities as substantive freedoms to lead lives people value. Statement 3 is wrong: 'Development as Freedom' came out in 1999; 1990 is the year of the first HDR. So '1 and 2 only'; '2 only' misses statement 1, and the options with statement 3 include a wrong statement.
72.tq: 1990 = first HDR; 1999 = Development as Freedom; 1998 = Sen's Nobel.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Amartya Sen** described capabilities as **substantive freedoms** to lead lives people value.
Statement 2 is correct: **Mahbub ul Haq** conceived the **HDR**, with Sen as co-conceiver.
Statement 3 is wrong: **"Development as Freedom"** came out in **1999**; **1990** is the year of the **first HDR**.
xa: Sen won the Nobel in Economics in **1998**.
The HDR is published by **UNDP**.
Core idea: development = **enlargement of human choices**, not just income.
First **NHDR of India**: **2001**.

72.s:
Consider the following statements about the human development approach:
1. Amartya Sen received the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1998.
2. Development is viewed as the enlargement of human choices.
3. National income alone is treated as the complete test of development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
72.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the approach evaluates people and their capabilities rather than national income alone.
72.tq: Reject the extreme reduction of a multidimensional approach to a single income measure.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1: **Amartya Sen** won the **Nobel in Economics** in **1998** — correct.
Statement 2: development = **enlargement of human choices** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: the test of development is **people and their capabilities**, not national income alone.
xa: Two countries with the **same GNI per capita** can reach different outcomes.
Sen's **"Development as Freedom"** appeared in **1999**.
**Growth** is quantitative; **development** is quantitative + qualitative.

72.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Economic growth is primarily quantitative and is associated with income.
2. Human development includes both quantitative and qualitative dimensions.
3. Literacy, health and non-discrimination are only instruments of development and not constituents of development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
