75.tq: GCC 1956; Dhebar (PTG) 1973; PVTG 2006.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **GCC** was set up in **1956**; **1973** is the year the **Dhebar** PTG category came.
Statement 2 is correct: **"GCC Araku Valley Coffee"** is its trademark; it sells under the **"Girijan"** brand.
Statement 3 is correct: it procures **MFP** and agricultural produce, runs **interior PDS depots**, gives **credit**.
xa: GCC put **Rs 250.76 cr** into the tribal economy in 2024-25; runs **16 petrol bunks**.
**CTUAP** permanent campus: **Kondakarakam, Vizianagaram**.
**Samatha judgment (1997)** barred leasing Scheduled Area land to non-tribals and private miners.
**1/70 Regulation** bars land transfers from tribals to non-tribals in Scheduled Areas.

75.s: The Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh was established under which legislation?
75.x: CTUAP was set up under the Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2019, as required by the 13th Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act.
75.tq: Distinguish the establishing legislation from related regional legislation.
xs: **CTUAP** was set up by the **Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2019** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It fulfilled a requirement of the **13th Schedule** of the **AP Reorganisation Act**.

xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **1/70 Regulation** = AP Scheduled Area Land Transfer Regulation **1 of 1959**, amended by **1 of 1970**.

the Kannada areas going to Andhra and the Telugu areas to Mysore
76.x: In 1953, Bellary taluk was divided linguistically: Telugu-speaking areas went to Andhra and Kannada-speaking areas went to Mysore.
76.tq: Track the direction of transfer for each linguistic area.
xs: In **1953**, **Bellary taluk** was split by language: **Telugu areas to Andhra**, **Kannada areas to Mysore** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the split.
xa: **Anantapur** and **Kurnool** border Karnataka and have **Kannada** pockets.
**Chittoor / Tirupati** border Tamil Nadu (**Tamil**); **Srikakulam** borders Odisha (**Odia**).

76.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the recognition of Classical Languages is correct?
o: The Government of Uttar Pradesh granted Classical Language status to Telugu.
Tamil was recognised in 2008, after Telugu.
Telugu and Kannada were recognised in 2008, while Tamil was the first in 2004.
Malayalam and Odia were recognised in 2008 along with Telugu.
76.x: Tamil was the first, receiving recognition in 2004. Telugu and Kannada received it in 2008; the granting authority was the Union Government, not Uttar Pradesh.
76.tq: Trap the swapped year and wrong authority in a recognition-related statement.
xs: **Tamil** was the first classical language (**2004**); **Telugu and Kannada** followed in **2008** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Option (1) is wrong: the granting authority is the **Government of India**, not "Govt of Uttar Pradesh".
Option (4) is wrong: **Malayalam = 2013**, **Odia = 2014**.
xa: **Sanskrit** was declared in **2005**.
**2024**: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali (total **11**).

76.s: Telugu was one of the original how many languages included in the Eighth Schedule?
76.x: Telugu was one of the original 14 languages included in the Eighth Schedule.
76.tq: Distinguish the original count from later additions.
xs: Telugu was one of the **original 14** languages of the **Eighth Schedule** — so option **(2)** is correct.
No other count of the original Eighth Schedule appears in the notes.
xa: Telugu became a **classical language** in **2008**, with Kannada.
Telugu is the most widely spoken **Dravidian** language, **4th** in India (2011).

76.s: The languages recognised as classical languages in 2024 are:
o: Marathi, Assamese, Bengali, Tamil and Sanskrit
Marathi, Konkani, Pali, Prakrit and Bengali
Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali and Nepali
Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali
76.x: The 2024 additions were Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali.
76.tq: Test a complete named list rather than relying on recognition of a single language.
xs: The **2024** classical languages are **Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Tamil** and **Sanskrit** were declared in **2004 / 2005**.
xa: The 2024 additions took the total to **11**.
**Telugu, Kannada = 2008**; **Malayalam = 2013**; **Odia = 2014**.

76.s: In the TMA Pai case, whether a linguistic minority exists is judged at which level?
76.x: The TMA Pai case held that a linguistic minority is determined at the State level.
76.tq: Apply the judicial principle to the correct territorial unit.
xs: In the **TMA Pai** case, a linguistic minority is judged at the **State level** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is not judged at the district, village or national level.
xa: Current relevance: the **Supreme Court** questioned **CBSE** calling English "non-native".
AP's language pockets: **Odia** (Srikakulam), **Tamil** (Chittoor), **Kannada** (Anantapur, Kurnool).

77.s:
Consider the following statements about urbanisation in Andhra Pradesh (Census 2011):
1. AP was the most urbanised of the southern States.
2. Tamil Nadu's urban share (over 50 per cent) was well above AP's.
3. About 29.47 per cent of AP's population was urban, below the all-India figure of 31.16 per cent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statement 3 is correct: AP was 29.47 per cent urban against India's 31.16 per cent. Statement 1 is wrong: AP was the least urbanised southern State (APPSC G2 2017). Statement 2 is correct: Tamil Nadu is over 50 per cent urban. So '2 and 3 only'; '3 only' and '2 only' each miss a correct statement, and '1 only' picks the wrong one.
77.tq: AP 29.47% < India 31.16%: least urbanised in the South.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: AP was the **least urbanised southern state** (APPSC G2 2017).
Statement 2 is correct: **Tamil Nadu** is **over 50%** urban.
Statement 3 is correct: AP **29.47%** urban vs all-India **31.16%**.
xa: AP urban growth 2001-11 ≈ **33%** vs total growth **9.21%**.
AP's largest city: **Visakhapatnam** ("City of Destiny").
AP has **123** ULBs, incl. **17 Municipal Corporations**.

77.s: Between 2001 and 2011, which of the following best describes population growth in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Urban population increased by about 33%, while rural population increased by about 1.5%.
Urban population increased by about 1.5%, while rural population increased by about 33%.
Both urban and rural populations increased by about 33%.
Both urban and rural populations declined.
77.x: Urban population increased from 109.56 lakh to 146.10 lakh, about 33%, whereas rural population rose from 344.41 lakh to 349.67 lakh, about 1.5%.
77.tq: Use the contrasting growth rates to identify the correct urban-rural comparison.
xs: In 2001-11, **urban population rose about 33%** (**109.56 → 146.10 lakh**) while **rural rose about 1.5%** (**344.41 → 349.67 lakh**) — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps the two rates.
xa: Urban growth drove AP's low overall growth of **9.21%**.
⚠ 2011 urban growth ≈ **33%** vs total **9.21%**.
The **16th FC**'s **Urbanisation Premium** rewards merging peri-urban villages into ULBs.

77.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the planning approach described for Andhra Pradesh's peri-urban areas?
o: Urbanisation Premium — merging peri-urban villages into Urban Local Bodies
Urbanisation Premium — converting all municipalities into gram panchayats
Metro-region planning — restricting development to rural areas
Peri-urban planning — excluding villages from ULB boundaries
77.x: The 16th Finance Commission's Urbanisation Premium rewards the merger of peri-urban villages into Urban Local Bodies.
77.tq: Match the policy instrument with its stated institutional purpose.
xs: The **16th Finance Commission's Urbanisation Premium** rewards **merging peri-urban villages into ULBs** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It favours expanding ULB boundaries, not excluding villages or converting towns to gram panchayats.
xa: AP's urban population grew about **33%** in 2001-11.
AP has **123** ULBs (AP Survey 2025-26).

77.s: As per the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission answer key for 2011 data, how many cities of Andhra Pradesh had a population of more than one lakh?
77.x: The APPSC-GS 2019 answer key gives the number of Andhra Pradesh cities with more than one lakh population in 2011 as 32.
77.tq: Separate the population-count figure from the figures for municipal corporations, municipalities and nagar panchayats.
xs: AP had **32** cities with more than **1 lakh** people in 2011 (APPSC-GS 2019 answer key) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**17** is the number of **Municipal Corporations**; **30** nagar panchayats; **76** municipalities.
xa: **Visakhapatnam** is the largest city; it and **Vijayawada** are million-plus.
**AMRUT** covers ULBs of **1 lakh+**.

77.s: Andhra Pradesh has how many Urban Local Bodies, and what is their composition?
77.x: Andhra Pradesh has 123 ULBs comprising 17 corporations, 76 municipalities and 30 nagar panchayats.
77.tq: Check both the total and its component counts to detect reversed or altered composition.
xs: AP has **123** ULBs: **17 Municipal Corporations**, **76 municipalities**, **30 nagar panchayats** (AP Survey 2025-26) — option **(4)**.
Option (1) swaps the corporation and nagar panchayat counts.
xa: ⚠ APSES 2024-25 counted **79** municipalities.
Water supplied: **2,048 MLD** across **123** ULBs; sewage treated **613 MLD**.
**Anna Canteens**: **204** running across the ULBs.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding urban centres of Andhra Pradesh (Census 2011):
1. Visakhapatnam is the largest city of the State.
2. Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada are the State's million-plus urban agglomerations.
3. Tirupati is a million-plus urban agglomeration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Visakhapatnam is AP's largest city (APPSC-GS 2019 key), and Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada are the State's million-plus agglomerations. Statement 3 is wrong: Tirupati is a major centre but not million-plus. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' leaves out statement 2, and the options with statement 3 include a wrong statement.
77.tq: AP million-plus (2011) = Visakhapatnam + Vijayawada only.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Visakhapatnam** is AP's largest city (APPSC-GS 2019 key).
Statement 2 is correct: **Visakhapatnam + Vijayawada** are AP's **million-plus** agglomerations.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Tirupati** is a major centre but not million-plus — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: AP had **32** cities above **1 lakh** in 2011.
Tirupati is the "**Temple City**".

77.s:
Match the following nicknames with the corresponding cities:

List-I (Nickname)
A. City of Destiny
B. Andhra Paris
C. Temple City
D. Cultural Capital of the Andhras

List-II (City)
1. Tirupati
2. Tenali
3. Visakhapatnam
4. Rajamahendravaram

Codes:
A  B  C  D
 a. 3  2  1  4
 b. 2  3  4  1
 c. 3  1  2  4
 d. 4  2  1  3
77.x: Visakhapatnam is the City of Destiny, Tenali is Andhra Paris, Tirupati is the Temple City and Rajamahendravaram is the Cultural Capital of the Andhras.
77.tq: Begin with the sure nickname–city pair and use elimination for the remaining pairs.
xs: **City of Destiny = Visakhapatnam**, **Andhra Paris = Tenali**, **Temple City = Tirupati**, **Cultural Capital of the Andhras = Rajamahendravaram** — so **A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4**, option **(1)**.
The first two pairs were asked in APPSC **2025** and **2019** PYQs.
xa: Rajahmundry's title comes from **Rajaraja Narendra**'s **Eastern Chalukya** court.
**Amaravati** is called the "**People's Capital**".

77.s: The title ‘Cultural Capital of the Andhras’ associated with Rajamahendravaram is linked to which historical court?
o: The court of Pulakesin II of the Chalukyas
The court of Rajaraja Narendra of the Eastern Chalukyas
The court of Gautamiputra Satakarni of the Satavahanas
The court of Krishnadevaraya of the Vijayanagara Empire
77.x: Rajamahendravaram, also known as Rajahmundry, received the title in connection with Rajaraja Narendra’s Eastern Chalukya court.
77.tq: Apply the wrong-ruler trap by matching the title with the correct historical court.
xs: Rajamahendravaram's "**Cultural Capital**" title comes from **Rajaraja Narendra**'s **Eastern Chalukya** court — so option **(2)** is correct.
The notes link no other court to the title.
xa: **Tenali** = "**Andhra Paris**"; **Tirupati** = "**Temple City**".
**Godavari UDA** covers **Kakinada-Rajamahendravaram**.

77.s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes APCRDA and VMRDA?
1. APCRDA is concerned with planning the Amaravati capital region.
2. VMRDA is concerned with planning the Visakhapatnam metropolitan region.
3. VMRDA was formed in 2018 from VUDA.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
77.x: All three statements are correct. APCRDA plans the Amaravati capital region, while VMRDA plans the Visakhapatnam metropolitan region and was formed from VUDA in 2018.
77.tq: Separate institutions by jurisdiction and formation history.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **APCRDA** plans the **Amaravati** capital region (Guntur, Palnadu, Bapatla).
Statement 2 is correct: **VMRDA** plans the **Visakhapatnam metropolitan region**.
Statement 3 is correct: VMRDA was formed in **2018** from **VUDA** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: APCRDA was set up under the **APCRDA Act, 2014**.
VMRDA runs the "**Green Triangle**" eco-tourism project.

77.s: Which of the following authority-city pairs is NOT correctly matched?
77.x: Godavari UDA is associated with Kakinada-Rajamahendravaram, not Visakhapatnam. VMRDA is the authority for Visakhapatnam.
77.tq: Find the one swapped city-authority pair by checking the regional jurisdiction of each authority.
xs: **Godavari UDA — Visakhapatnam** is wrong: Godavari UDA covers **Kakinada-Rajamahendravaram** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**VMRDA** (Visakhapatnam), **TUDA** (Tirupati) and **APCRDA** (Amaravati) are correctly matched.
xa: AP has **21 UDAs**.
Town and Country Planning officials are deputed between them.

77.s: The Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) was set up under which law?
o: AP Metropolitan Region and Urban Development Authorities Act, 2018
77.x: APCRDA was constituted under the APCRDA Act, 2014, to plan the Amaravati capital region. 2018 is when VMRDA was formed from VUDA; the AP Reorganisation Act bifurcated the State; the 2019 Act set up the Central Tribal University.
77.tq: APCRDA = APCRDA Act 2014; VMRDA = 2018 from VUDA.
xs: **APCRDA** was set up under the **APCRDA Act, 2014** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**2018** is when **VMRDA** was formed from VUDA; the **2019** Central Universities (Amendment) Act set up **CTUAP**.
xa: APCRDA covers the **Amaravati** capital region (**Guntur, Palnadu, Bapatla**).
Capital area: **Vijayawada-Guntur-Tenali-Mangalagiri**, chosen for its **central location**.

77.s: Which economic region consists of 10 districts and has a target of USD 750–800 billion by 2047?
77.x: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region consists of 10 districts and has a target of USD 750–800 billion by 2047.
77.tq: Match the region with both its district count and long-term target.
xs: The **Visakhapatnam Economic Region** has **10** districts and a target of **USD 750-800 bn by 2047** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was prepared with **NITI Aayog**.
**Amaravati ER** has **9** districts; **Tirupati ER** has **10**, but without that target in the notes.
xa: **Budget 2026-27**: **City Economic Regions ₹5,000 crore each**.
The **Bhogapuram-Vizag "twin cities"** coastal corridor is planned.

77.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
77.x: Kopparthy is in Kadapa and belongs to VCIC. Orvakal in Kurnool is the node associated with the Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridor.
77.tq: Find the wrong node-district-corridor combination by checking all three elements.
xs: **Kopparthy — Kurnool — Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridor** is wrong: **Kopparthy** is in **Kadapa**, on the **VCIC** — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The **Hyderabad-Bengaluru** node is **Orvakal (Kurnool)**.
**Bhogapuram-Vizag "twin cities"** coastal corridor is planned (17 Feb 2026).
xa: Economic regions: **Visakhapatnam**, **Amaravati**, **Tirupati**.
Major centres listed alongside: **Kurnool**, Nellore, Kakinada, Guntur.

77.s: Which of the following sets contains all the Smart Cities of Andhra Pradesh listed under the Smart Cities Mission?
77.x: The Smart Cities of Andhra Pradesh are Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati and Amaravati.
77.tq: Check the complete membership of a State-wise scheme list rather than identifying only one city.
xs: AP's Smart Cities are **Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati** and **Amaravati** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Vijayawada, Guntur, Kurnool, Nellore, Rajamahendravaram** are not on the list.
xa: Smart Cities Mission (**Jun 2015**): **100** cities; **₹48,000 crore** central share.
**Kakinada Smart City Corporation** built heliports (Apr 2026).
Amaravati is also AP's **HRIDAY** city.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about urban schemes:
1. The Smart Cities Mission was launched in June 2015 for 100 cities.
2. The central share under the Smart Cities Mission was ₹1 lakh crore.
3. AMRUT covers 485 cities, including ULBs of one lakh or more population.
4. AMRUT was extended up to September 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
77.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct: the Smart Cities Mission began in June 2015 for 100 cities; AMRUT covers 485 cities and was extended to September 2025. Statement 2 is wrong: the Smart Cities central share was ₹48,000 crore; ₹1 lakh crore is the AMRUT outlay. Hence options B, C and D, which include statement 2, are wrong.
77.tq: Do not swap the outlays: Smart Cities ₹48,000 crore (central share), AMRUT ₹1 lakh crore.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Smart Cities** began in **Jun 2015** for **100** cities.
Statement 2 is wrong: its central share was **₹48,000 crore**; **₹1 lakh crore** is **AMRUT**'s outlay.
Statements 3 and 4 are correct: **AMRUT** covers **485** cities and was extended to **Sep 2025** — so **1, 3 and 4 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **HRIDAY (2015)** covers heritage cities — **Amaravati** in AP.
**SBM-U 2.0**: "**Garbage Free**" status for all cities by **2026**.

77.s: Which one of the following is the HRIDAY town in Andhra Pradesh?
77.x: Amaravati is the heritage city covered in Andhra Pradesh under HRIDAY.
77.tq: Distinguish the heritage-city scheme from the Smart Cities and AMRUT city lists.
xs: AP's **HRIDAY** heritage city is **Amaravati** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati** are **Smart Cities**, not HRIDAY towns.
xa: HRIDAY was launched in **2015**.
HRIDAY cities are also eligible under **AMRUT**.

77.s: The principal target of SBM-U 2.0, implemented during October 2021–2026, is to provide which status to all cities?
77.x: SBM-U 2.0 aims to give all cities Garbage Free status by 2026.
77.tq: Use the scheme’s defining objective to distinguish it from HRIDAY, AMRUT and Smart Cities.
xs: **SBM-U 2.0** (**Oct 2021-2026**) aims at "**Garbage Free**" status for all cities by **2026** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Heritage status is **HRIDAY**'s domain; Smart City status is the **Smart Cities Mission**'s.
xa: **94.62%** of AP's wards have door-to-door collection; **49.32%** achieve 100% source segregation.
Complexes producing **>100 kg** of waste a day must set up their own processing.

77.s: In the AMRUT Ease of Living Index, 2018, Andhra Pradesh was followed by which two States in the ranking?
77.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked first, followed by Odisha and Madhya Pradesh in the AMRUT Ease of Living Index 2018.
77.tq: Test the precise order of States rather than merely identifying the top-ranked State.
xs: In the **AMRUT Ease of Living Index (2018)**, **AP ranked 1st**, followed by **Odisha and Madhya Pradesh** (APPSC G1 2019 PYQ) — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses Odisha and Madhya Pradesh.
xa: Economic Survey 2025-26 ease-of-living top-10 includes **Tirupati** and **Vijayawada**.
AMRUT covers **485** cities.

77.s: Which of the following pairs was included among the top-ten cities in the Economic Survey 2025-26 ease-of-living list?
77.x: Tirupati and Vijayawada were included in the top-ten ease-of-living cities listed in the Economic Survey 2025-26.
77.tq: Identify the exact pair appearing in a ranked list and avoid substituting other major cities.
xs: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** ease-of-living top-10 includes **Tirupati and Vijayawada** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The list runs: **Pune, Navi Mumbai, Greater Mumbai, Tirupati** ... **Vijayawada, Bhopal**.
xa: **AMRUT Ease of Living Index (2018)**: AP ranked **1st**.
Tirupati is the "**Temple City**" and a **Smart City**.

77.s:
Consider the following statements about slums in Census 2011:
1. Undivided Andhra Pradesh had about 1.02 crore slum dwellers.
2. Undivided Andhra Pradesh had the highest number of slum dwellers among all States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statement 1 is correct: undivided AP had about 1.02 crore slum dwellers in Census 2011. Statement 2 is wrong: AP was second, after Maharashtra. So only option A fits; B, C and D wrongly accept statement 2 or reject statement 1.
77.tq: Slums 2011: Maharashtra first, undivided AP second (about 1.02 crore).
xs: Statement 1 is correct: undivided AP had about **1.02 crore** slum dwellers in **Census 2011**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was **second**, after **Maharashtra** — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: No slum figure for residual AP is given in the notes.
Urban flooding causes: **unplanned growth**, **lost wetlands**, **blocked drains**, **concretisation**.

77.s: The principal watercourse associated with flooding in Vijayawada is the:
77.x: Vijayawada floods are associated with the Budameru rivulet.
77.tq: Use the exact local watercourse rather than selecting the larger nearby river.
xs: **Vijayawada floods** are linked to the **Budameru rivulet** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The notes link no Vijayawada flood to the other rivers.
xa: An **AI flood-forecasting system** by **RTGS + APSDMA + IIT Gandhinagar** gives **48-hour** rain and **6-hour** flash-flood warnings.
It is to be extended to **all ULBs** (Jul 2026).

77.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Census definition of an urban area used in the context described?
o: Population of 5,000 or more, 75% or more male workers outside agriculture, and density of 400 or more persons per sq km
Population of 2,000 or more, 75% or more male workers outside agriculture, and density of 200 or more persons per sq km
Population of 5,000 or more, 50% or more male workers outside agriculture, and density of 400 or more persons per sq km
Population of 10,000 or more, 50% or more male workers outside agriculture, and density of 200 or more persons per sq km
77.x: The stated Census criteria are at least 5,000 people, at least 75% of male workers outside agriculture, and at least 400 persons per square kilometre.
77.tq: Match all three thresholds exactly; a change in any one threshold makes the option incorrect.
xs: Census "**urban**" = **5,000+** people, **75%+** of male workers **outside agriculture**, and **400+** persons per sq km — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other options change one or more of these thresholds.
xa: AP's urban share (2011): **29.47%** vs India **31.16%**.
⚠ **Census Town** criteria still undercount AP's urban spread.

77.s: Andhra Pradesh signed an MoU with UN-Habitat in July 2026 for establishing a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs at:
77.x: The Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs is to be established at Amaravati under the MoU with UN-Habitat.
77.tq: Identify the location associated with the named institutional initiative.
xs: The **UN-Habitat** MoU (Jul 2026) sets up a **Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs** at **Amaravati** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It supports **SURGE AP, RISE AP, UPLIFT AP**.
xa: Amaravati's physical progress was only **6.84%** (Survey 2025-26), with land-pooling grievances.
Amaravati is AP's **HRIDAY** and **Smart City**.

77.s:
Assertion (A): Flash floods in Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada are linked to urban environmental and drainage problems.
Reason (R): Loss of wetlands and blocked drains reduce the capacity of urban areas to absorb and convey excess water.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
77.x: Both statements are true, and the loss of wetlands and blocked drains directly explain the increased flood vulnerability of the two cities.
77.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the urban-flood assertion.
xs: **A** is true: **flash floods** in **Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada** stem from urban drainage problems.
**R** is true and is the correct **explanation** of A: **lost wetlands + blocked drains** cause the flash floods — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: Other causes: **unplanned growth** and **concretisation**.
Vijayawada floods are linked to the **Budameru** rivulet.
The AI flood-forecasting system is by **RTGS + APSDMA + IIT Gandhinagar**.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the construction of the Human Development Index:
1. The education dimension is measured by the adult literacy rate and gross enrolment.
2. Income is measured by GNI per capita (PPP), entered as a logarithm.
3. Since 2010 the HDI has been the geometric mean of the health, education and income indices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
78.x: Statement 3 is correct: the geometric mean replaced the arithmetic mean in 2010 (the first HDR was in 1990). Statement 1 is wrong: education is measured by mean years and expected years of schooling; literacy and gross enrolment were dropped in 2010. Statement 2 is correct: income is GNI per capita at PPP, in log form. So '2 and 3 only'; the other options include the wrong statement 1.
78.tq: After 2010: geometric mean + MYS/EYS; literacy is out.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: education is measured by **mean + expected years of schooling**, not literacy and gross enrolment.
Statement 2 is correct: income = **GNI per capita, PPP**, entered as a **log**.
Statement 3 is correct: since **2010** the HDI is the **geometric mean** of the three indices.
xa: Health is measured by **life expectancy**.
The first HDR came out in **1990** (UNDP), conceived by **Mahbub ul Haq** with **Amartya Sen**.
**NHDR 2001**: AP's HDI **0.416** vs India **0.472** — AP **below India's**.
**AP Human Development Report 2007** was prepared by **CESS, Hyderabad**.

78.s: The Andhra Pradesh Human Development Report, 2007 was prepared by:
o: Centre for Economic and Social Studies, Hyderabad
78.x: The AP Human Development Report 2007 was prepared by the Centre for Economic and Social Studies in Hyderabad.
78.tq: Who-prepared-what trap.
xs: The **AP Human Development Report 2007** was prepared by the **Centre for Economic and Social Studies (CESS), Hyderabad** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Institute for Competitiveness** co-produces the **Social Progress Index**; **NITI Aayog** produces the **SDG India Index**.
xa: The **NHDR 2001** was by the **Planning Commission**; AP ranked **10th** there.
AP's NHDR 2001 HDI: **0.416** vs India **0.472**.

78.s: Which of the following correctly represents the relative position of Kerala and Goa in the latest sub-national HDI comparison?
o: Goa is below 0.70 and Kerala ranks 24th
Kerala is above 0.86 but Goa is below 0.70
Both are below 0.70 and Kerala ranks last
Both are above 0.86 and Kerala ranks second
78.x: Goa and Kerala both recorded HDI values above 0.86, and Kerala ranked second.
78.tq: Comparison-table based elimination using value and rank together.
xs: In the **2023** sub-national HDI, **Goa and Kerala** are both **above 0.86**, with **Kerala 2nd** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**24th** is **Assam**'s rank (**0.699**), not Kerala's.
xa: **India**: **0.732**; **Tamil Nadu 0.787**; **West Bengal 0.719**.
The notes do not give AP's 2023 sub-national HDI value or rank.

78.s: According to the National Human Development Report 2001 of the Planning Commission, the HDI of Andhra Pradesh was
78.x: In NHDR 2001 AP's HDI (0.416) was below India's (0.472), and AP ranked 10th among major States. The first option reverses the two figures, the second wrongly makes them equal, and 0.385 is not the cited value.
xs: In **NHDR 2001**, AP's HDI was **lower than India's**: **0.416** against **0.472** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the two figures; option (2) wrongly makes them equal.
xa: AP ranked **10th** among major states in NHDR 2001.
Exam angle: "AP's HDI in NHDR 2001 was ... India's" → **less than**.
Latest (**2023**) India HDI: **0.732**.

78.s: Andhra Pradesh occupied which position in the Social Progress Index released in December 2022?
78.x: Andhra Pradesh was placed 23rd in the Social Progress Index of December 2022.
78.tq: Direct recall of an index rank.
xs: AP was **23rd** in the **Social Progress Index (Dec 2022)** (APPSC-GS 2022 key) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**9th** is AP's **SDG India Index** and **MPI** rank.
xa: The SPI is by the **Institute for Competitiveness + Social Progress Imperative**.
⚠ Summary: SDG score **74**, Mission Antyodaya **61**, SPI **23rd**.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission Antyodaya:
1. It is a convergence framework of the Ministry of Rural Development that ranks gram panchayats on an annual survey.
2. It is a healthcare mission that ranks hospitals annually.
3. Andhra Pradesh's state average score under it was 61.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
78.x: Statement 2 is wrong: calling Mission Antyodaya a healthcare mission is the standard trap. Statement 1 is correct: it is MoRD's convergence framework ranking gram panchayats through an annual survey. Statement 3 is correct: AP's state average score was 61 (APPSC-GS 2018 key). So '1 and 3 only'.
78.tq: Antyodaya = rural development, gram panchayats; AP score 61.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Mission Antyodaya** is the **Ministry of Rural Development**'s **convergence framework** ranking **gram panchayats** on an annual survey.
Statement 2 is wrong: ⚠ calling it a **healthcare mission** is the standard trap.
Statement 3 is correct: AP's **state average score** was **61** (APPSC-GS 2018 key).
xa: **Social Progress Index (Dec 2022)**: AP **23rd**.
**SDG India Index 2023-24**: AP score **74**, **9th**, **Front Runner**; **SDG 7 – 1st**.
SDG Index top: **Kerala and Uttarakhand 79**; bottom: **Bihar 57**.
AP **GSDP rank**: **8th**.

78.s: According to the SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh had which of the following status?
o: Score 74, rank 9 and Front Runner State
Score 84, rank 5 and Front Runner State
78.x: Andhra Pradesh scored 74, ranked ninth, and was classified as a Front Runner in the SDG India Index 2023-24.
78.tq: Combine score, rank and category to prevent partial recall from producing the answer.
xs: In the **SDG India Index 2023-24**, AP scored **74**, ranked **9th**, and is a **Front Runner** (65-99) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**79** is the top score (**Kerala and Uttarakhand**), not AP's.
xa: The index is NITI Aayog's **4th edition** (July 2024), with **113 indicators** and **16** goals.
AP is **1st** on **SDG 7**, **2nd** on SDG 14, **3rd** on SDG 1 (APSES 2024-25).
Bottom: **Bihar 57**.

78.s:
With reference to the SDG India Index 2023-24 (NITI Aayog), consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh ranked first on SDG 7.
2. Kerala and Uttarakhand topped the index with a score of 79.
3. Bihar was at the bottom with a score of 57.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three are correct: AP was 1st on SDG 7 (and 2nd on SDG 14, 3rd on SDG 1), Kerala and Uttarakhand topped at 79, and Bihar was last at 57. Each of the other options leaves out one correct statement.
78.tq: SDG India Index 2023-24: AP 74 (9th, Front Runner), 1st on SDG 7.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: AP ranked **1st** on **SDG 7**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Kerala and Uttarakhand** topped with **79**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Bihar** was last with **57** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: AP: score **74**, **9th**, **Front Runner**.
AP was also **2nd** on SDG 14 and **3rd** on SDG 1.

78.s: As per the APSES 2024–25 assessment, Andhra Pradesh was placed as the ______ least-poor State in India.
78.x: Andhra Pradesh was ranked as the 9th least-poor State according to the stated assessment.
78.tq: Directly identify the rank associated with Andhra Pradesh.
xs: AP is the **9th** least-poor state (APSES 2024-25; CDI also lists AP 9th) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**8th** is AP's **GSDP** rank; **10th** its NHDR 2001 HDI rank.
xa: ⚠ AP is **9th** in both the **SDG India Index** and **MPI**.

78.s: Which of the following correctly states Andhra Pradesh's MPI position in the NITI Aayog National MPI for 2019-21?
78.x: Andhra Pradesh's MPI was 0.025 and its multidimensional poverty headcount was 6.06%, compared with India's 14.96%.
78.tq: Paired-value discrimination between State and national figures.
xs: AP's **MPI (2019-21)** was **0.025** with a **headcount ratio of 6.06%** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**0.053** was AP's MPI in **2015-16**; **14.96%** is **India's** headcount.
xa: AP's MPI fell by about **50%**.
AP is the **9th** least-poor state.
Lowest-poverty district: **West Godavari 2.42%**.

78.s: Which district had the lowest multidimensional poverty percentage among the following districts of Andhra Pradesh?
78.x: West Godavari had the lowest listed multidimensional poverty percentage at 2.42%, followed by Guntur, Krishna and Chittoor.
78.tq: Rank-order comparison among nearby district values.
xs: **West Godavari** had the lowest poverty, **2.42%** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is followed by **Guntur 4.36%**, **Krishna 4.38%**, **Chittoor 5.66%**.
xa: AP's overall MPI headcount: **6.06%** vs India **14.96%**.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI):
1. It uses four dimensions and sixteen indicators.
2. India's multidimensional poverty headcount fell from 29.17 per cent in 2013-14 to 11.28 per cent in 2022-23.
3. About 24.82 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty, as per NITI's January 2024 estimate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
78.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the National MPI has three dimensions and twelve indicators. Statement 2 is correct: the headcount fell from 29.17 per cent (2013-14) to 11.28 per cent (2022-23). Statement 3 is correct: 24.82 crore escaped poverty (NITI, Jan 2024). So '2 and 3 only'.
78.tq: National MPI: 3 dimensions, 12 indicators; 29.17% -> 11.28%; 24.82 crore out.
xs: Statements **2 and 3 only** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: the **National MPI** uses **3 dimensions** and **12 indicators**.
Statement 2 is correct: headcount fell from **29.17% (2013-14)** to **11.28% (2022-23)**.
Statement 3 is correct: **24.82 crore** escaped poverty (NITI, **Jan 2024**).
xa: AP headcount **6.06%** vs India **14.96%** — AP **9th** least poor.
AP rural MPI headcount **7.71%**; urban **2.20%**; intensity **41.12%**.
Lowest-poverty district: **West Godavari 2.42%**.

78.s: According to the cited estimates, the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe shares in Andhra Pradesh's population are respectively:
78.x: Scheduled Castes account for 17.08% and Scheduled Tribes for 5.53% of Andhra Pradesh's population.
78.tq: Confusable-pair discrimination between SC and ST percentages.
xs: AP's **SC** share is **17.08%** and **ST** share **5.53%** (APSES 2024-25) — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses the two; **4.21%** is AP's share of **India's SCs**.
xa: AP's SC population (Census 2011): **84.69 lakh**.
Some notes give the ST count as **26.31 lakh (5.3%)**.

78.s: The Scheduled Caste population of Andhra Pradesh was approximately how much according to Census 2011 data?
78.x: The Scheduled Caste population was 84.69 lakh, constituting 4.21% of India's Scheduled Caste population.
78.tq: Magnitude and unit discrimination.
xs: AP's **SC population** (Census 2011) was **84.69 lakh** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**84.69 crore** is the wrong unit; **26.31 lakh** is an older **ST** figure.
xa: It equals **4.21%** of India's SCs.
SCs form **17.08%** of AP's population.

78.s:
With reference to the 28 districts of Andhra Pradesh (Census 2011 recast), consider the following statements:
1. Polavaram has the lowest urbanisation, while Visakhapatnam has the highest.
2. Markapuram has the lowest population.
3. SPSR Nellore has the highest population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
78.x: Statement 3 is correct: SPSR Nellore is most populous (24.17 lakh). Statement 2 is wrong: the least populous is Polavaram (3.49 lakh), not Markapuram. Statement 1 is correct: Polavaram is least urbanised (2.84 per cent) and Visakhapatnam most (89.69 per cent). So '1 and 3 only'.
78.tq: Polavaram is lowest in population, urbanisation and density; lowest literacy is ASR.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Polavaram** is least urbanised (**2.84%**); **Visakhapatnam** most (**89.69%**).
Statement 2 is wrong: the least populous is **Polavaram (3.49 lakh)**, not Markapuram.
Statement 3 is correct: **SPSR Nellore** is most populous (**24.17 lakh**).
xa: ⚠ **Polavaram** = lowest in population, urbanisation and density (**54/sq km**).
Highest density: **Visakhapatnam (1,870/sq km)**.
Literacy: highest **Visakhapatnam (79.05%)**; lowest **Alluri Sitarama Raju (44.67%)**.
Old 13-district map: densest **Krishna (518)**.

78.s: Which of the following is the correct statement regarding literacy variation among the 28 districts of Andhra Pradesh?
o: SPSR Nellore had the highest literacy at 79.05%, while Markapuram had the lowest at 44.67%.
Visakhapatnam had the highest literacy at 89.69%, while Polavaram had the lowest at 2.84%.
Alluri Sitarama Raju had the highest literacy at 79.05%, while Visakhapatnam had the lowest at 44.67%.
Visakhapatnam had the highest literacy at 79.05%, while Alluri Sitarama Raju had the lowest at 44.67%.
78.x: Visakhapatnam recorded the highest literacy, 79.05%, and Alluri Sitarama Raju the lowest, 44.67%.
78.tq: Avoiding swapped district and indicator values.
xs: **Visakhapatnam** had the highest literacy (**79.05%**) and **Alluri Sitarama Raju** the lowest (**44.67%**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**89.69%** and **2.84%** in option (2) are **urbanisation** figures, not literacy.
xa: ⚠ Lowest literacy = **ASR**, but lowest population, urbanisation and density = **Polavaram**.
AP does better on health (**MMR 30, IMR 19**) than on literacy.

78.s:
Consider the following statements about Talliki Vandanam:
1. It is the successor to Amma Vodi.
2. It gives Rs 15,000 per child per year to the mother.
3. It covers only government schools.
4. The assistance is calculated per mother, irrespective of the number of children.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Talliki Vandanam succeeded Amma Vodi and gives Rs 15,000 per child per year to the mother (Classes 1-12). Statement 3 is wrong: it covers government and private schools. Statement 4 is wrong: unlike Amma Vodi it is calculated per child, not per mother. So only two are correct.
78.tq: Per child, govt + private, Classes 1-12, Rs 15,000.
xs: **Only two** statements are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Talliki Vandanam** is the **successor to Amma Vodi**.
Statement 2 is correct: it gives **₹15,000 per child per year** to the mother.
Statement 3 is wrong: it covers **government + private schools**, Classes **1-12**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the assistance is **per child**, not per mother.
xa: **₹10,090 crore** went to mothers of **67.27 lakh** students (1 Jan 2026).
**Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** (former Aarogyasri): cashless care for **1.43 crore families**, **3,257 procedures**.
AP Budget 2026-27 gives **₹4,000 crore** to NTR Vaidya Seva.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva?
o: A school assistance scheme providing ₹15,000 per child per year
A district development programme covering 112 districts and 49 indicators
A housing scheme covering 7.60 lakh houses through PMAY convergence
A cashless healthcare scheme covering 1.43 crore families and 3,257 procedures
78.x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, formerly Aarogyasri, provides cashless care to 1.43 crore families and covers 3,257 procedures.
78.tq: Use the renamed-scheme trap and match the scheme with its distinctive coverage figures.
xs: **Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** (former **Aarogyasri**) gives **cashless care** to **1.43 crore families**, covering **3,257 procedures** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **₹15,000 per child per year** scheme is **Talliki Vandanam**, not Vaidya Seva.
xa: AP Budget 2026-27 gives Vaidya Seva **₹4,000 crore**.
AP's health figures: **MMR 30**, **IMR 19**.

78.s: In the March 2026 Aspirational Districts Programme rankings, which Andhra Pradesh district stood first in India in the Basic Infrastructure theme?
78.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju district stood first in India in the Basic Infrastructure theme in the March 2026 ADP rankings.
78.tq: Match the district with the specific ADP theme and ranking distinction.
xs: **Alluri Sitarama Raju (ASR)** topped the **ADP Basic Infrastructure** theme (Mar 2026 rankings) — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes name no other AP district for this ranking.
xa: ⚠ ASR also has AP's **lowest literacy** (**44.67%**).
Lowest population, urbanisation and density in the 28-district map: **Polavaram**.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the cited human-development indicators of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Health indicators are weaker than literacy, with MMR 44.67 and IMR 30
The State performs better on literacy, while MMR is 19 and IMR is 30
The State performs better on health, with MMR 30 and IMR 19, while the lowest district literacy is 44.67%
MMR, IMR and the lowest district literacy are all approximately 30
78.x: The comparative figures given are MMR 30 and IMR 19 for health, while the lowest district literacy figure cited is 44.67 percent, indicating relatively better performance on health than literacy.
78.tq: Check both the direction of comparison and the exact figures before selecting the option.
xs: AP does **better on health** (**MMR 30, IMR 19**) than on literacy (lowest district **ASR 44.67%**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps MMR and IMR and wrongly says literacy is the stronger side.
xa: Highest district literacy: **Visakhapatnam (79.05%)**.
**Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** covers **1.43 crore families**.

78.s: Why are IHDI and district-level indices considered useful alongside the Human Development Index in assessing Andhra Pradesh?
o: Because HDI hides inequality within a State
Because district-level indices measure only population size
Because IHDI replaces all district-level data with national averages
Because HDI measures only infrastructure and excludes health
78.x: HDI can conceal inequalities within a State; therefore, the Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index and district-level indices provide a more differentiated assessment.
78.tq: Apply the limitation of an aggregate index to the need for disaggregated measures.
xs: **HDI hides intra-state inequality**, hence **IHDI** and **district-level indices** — so option **(1)** is correct.
District indices show the gaps, e.g. literacy **79.05%** (Visakhapatnam) vs **44.67%** (ASR).
xa: HDI = **geometric mean** of health, education and income (since **2010**).
⚠ **Polavaram** is lowest in population, urbanisation and density.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
79.x: Cement manufacturing is a secondary-sector activity. Transport is tertiary, research and development is quaternary, and top decision-making is quinary.
79.tq: Use the activity-to-sector match and watch for neighbouring-sector substitutions.
xs: **Cement manufacturing** is a **secondary sector** activity — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Transport** is **tertiary** (APPSC-GS 2018 key); **research and development** is **quaternary**; top government decision-making is **quinary**.
xa: Primary = **agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining and quarrying** (direct use of nature).
Quaternary also covers **IT, education, consulting** (knowledge).
Quinary workers are called "**gold collar**".

79.s: Mining is classified differently in two commonly used contexts. Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Mining is a secondary activity and has no separate weight in the IIP.
Mining is a primary activity, but GVA reporting places it in the broad Industry sector.
Mining is a quinary activity because it involves technical expertise.
Mining is a tertiary activity and is reported under services in GVA.
79.x: By the nature of the activity, mining is primary because it extracts resources from nature. In GVA reporting it is included in the broad Industry sector.
79.tq: Separate classification by activity from classification used in economic reporting.
xs: **Mining** is a **primary** activity, but **GVA reporting** places it in the broad **Industry** sector (AP Survey) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) is wrong: mining has its own weight in the revised **IIP** — **11.05%**.
xa: The **APPSC-G2 2008** key left this question unanswered.
Mining is an **extractive industry**, like capture fishing, hunting and lumbering.

79.s: Which of the following pairs represents the oldest primary activities?
79.x: Hunting and gathering are regarded as the oldest primary activities because they involve direct dependence on nature for subsistence.
79.tq: Identify the historically earliest activities through their direct dependence on nature.
xs: **Hunting and gathering** are the **oldest primary activities** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Manufacturing is secondary; banking and trade tertiary; research and consulting quaternary.
xa: **Extractive industries** take what nature provides: **mining, capture fishing, hunting, lumbering**.
**Genetic industries** breed plants and animals: **agriculture**, animal husbandry, fish farming.

79.s: Which one of the following is NOT an extractive industry?
79.x: Animal husbandry is a genetic industry because it involves breeding and rearing animals. Mining, capture fishing and lumbering take resources provided by nature and are extractive industries.
79.tq: Find the activity that involves breeding rather than extraction.
xs: **Animal husbandry** is a **genetic** industry (breeding animals), not extractive — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Capture fishing, mining, lumbering** (and hunting) are **extractive** — they take what nature provides.
xa: Genetic industries: **agriculture**, animal husbandry, **fish farming** (UPPSC 2016 key: **Agriculture**).
⚠ **Capture fishing** = extractive, but **fish farming** = genetic.

79.s:
Consider the following pairs of collar-colour terms and workers:
1. Red collar — Primary-sector outdoor workers
2. Blue collar — Office and professional service workers
3. Pink collar — Nursing, teaching and clerical jobs
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
79.x: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct: red collar means primary-sector outdoor workers and pink collar means service jobs long held mostly by women, such as nursing, teaching and clerical work. Pair 2 is wrong: blue collar means manual, factory and construction workers; office and professional workers are white collar. So A, C and D, which include pair 2, are wrong.
79.tq: Blue = manual/factory; white = office. Watch for the blue-white swap.
xs: Pair 1 is correct: **red collar** = primary-sector (outdoor) workers.
Pair 2 is wrong: **blue collar** = **manual, factory and construction** workers; office and professional workers are **white collar**.
Pair 3 is correct: **pink collar** = **nursing, teaching, clerical** jobs long held mostly by women — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Green collar** = environment and renewable-energy jobs; **gold collar** = quinary decision-makers.
In **2025** the **UAE** overtook Saudi Arabia as the top destination for Indian blue-collar workers.

79.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the collar-colour term?
o: Green collar — Environment and renewable-energy jobs
Red collar — Office and professional services
79.x: Green-collar work is associated with environmental protection and renewable energy. White-collar work refers to office and professional services, red-collar work to primary-sector outdoor activities, and gold-collar work to top decision-makers and experts.
79.tq: Use elimination by matching each colour with its occupational domain.
xs: **Green collar** = **environment and renewable-energy jobs** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**White collar** = office and professional services; **red collar** = primary-sector outdoor work; **gold collar** = top decision-makers and experts, not manual workers.
xa: **Blue collar** = manual, factory and construction workers.
**Pink collar** = nursing, teaching, clerical jobs.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about the unorganised sector:
1. It commonly consists of small and scattered units.
2. Its workers may face irregular pay and lack of social security.
3. It is defined primarily by public ownership rather than by regulation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Small scattered units, irregular pay and lack of security are features of the unorganised sector. Public versus private is a separate classification based on ownership, not the organised–unorganised distinction.
79.tq: Reject the ownership-based confusion and retain the regulatory characteristics.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the unorganised sector has **small scattered units**, **irregular pay** and **no security**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **ownership** defines **public vs private**, not organised vs unorganised — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: AP informal employment: **62.3% rural** vs **45.6% urban** (AP Survey 2025-26).
**e-Shram**: **54%** of registered workers are women.

79.s: The Fisher-Clark thesis describes structural transformation as the movement of labour and output from
79.x: The thesis states that as income rises, labour and output generally move from the primary sector to the secondary sector and then to the tertiary sector.
79.tq: Test the direction of structural transformation as an ordered sequence.
xs: The **Fisher-Clark thesis**: as income rises, labour and output move **primary to secondary to tertiary** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the order.
xa: Proposed by **Allan Fisher (1935)** and **Colin Clark (1940)**.
Developed countries: services ≈ **70-80% of GDP** (World Bank).

79.s: India’s experience of ‘premature deindustrialisation’ refers primarily to the fact that India
o: moved directly from agriculture to a large manufacturing base
skipped the mass factory-job stage to a considerable extent
79.x: Premature deindustrialisation indicates that India did not pass through a large mass factory-employment phase before the expansion of services.
79.tq: Apply the concept to the structural sequence rather than interpreting the term literally.
xs: **Premature deindustrialisation** means India **skipped the mass factory-job stage** — so option **(4)** is correct.
India has only **2.9%** of global **manufacturing value added**.
xa: Counterpoint: organised manufacturing jobs rose **6% in FY24** (about **10 lakh**) (Economic Survey 2025-26).
AP's manufacturing is about **11% of GSDP** — the "**missing middle**".

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s structural transformation:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a services-led economy.
2. Manufacturing accounts for only about 11 per cent of GSDP.
3. Industrial Policy 4.0 for 2024–29 seeks to help fill the manufacturing gap.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: AP is described as services-led, with manufacturing at about 11% of GSDP. Industrial Policy 4.0 for 2024–29 is intended to address this ‘missing middle’.
79.tq: Combine the structural diagnosis, numerical share and policy response.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: AP is **services-led**.
Statement 2 is correct: manufacturing is only about **11% of GSDP**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Industrial Policy 4.0 (2024-29)** aims to fill this "**missing middle**" — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: AP GVA 2025-26: agriculture **33%**, industry **24%**, services **43%**.
India's manufacturing = **14.7%** of the economy (new GDP series).

79.s:
Consider the following statements about global sectoral patterns:
1. In developed countries, services account for about 70-80 per cent of GDP.
2. In developed countries, the quaternary and quinary sectors are shrinking.
3. In developing countries, the primary sector is still large in employment, while services grow faster than industry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Statement 1 is correct: services form about 70-80 per cent of GDP in developed countries (World Bank). Statement 2 is wrong: the quaternary and quinary sectors are growing there. Statement 3 is correct: developing countries still have a large primary-sector workforce while services outpace industry. So '1 and 3 only'.
79.tq: Developed: services 70-80% of GDP and knowledge sectors growing.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: in developed countries services ≈ **70-80% of GDP** (World Bank).
Statement 2 is wrong: the **quaternary + quinary** sectors are **growing** there.
Statement 3 is correct: developing countries keep a **large primary workforce** while **services grow faster than industry**.
xa: **Fisher-Clark thesis**: as income rises, labour and output move **primary → secondary → tertiary**.
India's deviation: **"premature deindustrialisation"** — only **2.9%** of global manufacturing value added.
India GVA 2024-25: services **52.9%**, industry **25.8%**, agriculture **21.4%**.
AP GVA 2025-26: **33% / 24% / 43%**; AP employment in agriculture **45.6%**.

79.s: Which sector accounted for the largest share of India’s GVA in 2024–25, on the new 2022–23 base?
79.x: The tertiary or services sector accounted for 52.9% of India’s GVA in 2024–25. The primary and secondary shares were 21.4% and 25.8% respectively.
79.tq: Match the sector with its correct GVA percentage rather than its employment share.
xs: The **tertiary sector** had the largest share of India's GVA in 2024-25: **52.9%** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Primary was **21.4%** and secondary **25.8%**.
**45.6%** is AP's **agriculture employment** share (PLFS 2023-24), not India's GVA.
xa: The base year moved to **2022-23** (Feb 2026).
AP's GVA: agriculture **33%**, industry **24%**, services **43%**.

79.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the broad sectoral pattern in both India and Andhra Pradesh?
o: Industry leads in both GVA and employment.
Agriculture leads in GVA, while services lead in employment.
Services lead in GVA, while agriculture leads in employment.
Services lead in both GVA and agriculture remains negligible in employment.
79.x: Services have the largest GVA share, whereas agriculture accounts for the largest share of employment in both India and Andhra Pradesh.
79.tq: Compare the leading sector in output with the leading sector in employment.
xs: In both India and AP, **services lead in GVA** while **agriculture leads in employment** — so option **(3)** is correct.
India: services **52.9%** of GVA; about **46.1%** of workers in agriculture.
AP: services **43%** of GVA; agriculture **45.6%** of employment.
xa: AP services employ only **31.6%** of workers.
e-Shram has **31 crore+** unorganised workers registered.

79.s: The new GDP series released in February 2026 is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: GDP levels 3–4% higher, manufacturing 21.4%, FY26 growth 6.2%
GDP levels 3–4% lower, manufacturing 14.7%, FY26 growth 7.6%
GDP levels unchanged, manufacturing 11%, FY26 growth 7.6%
GDP levels 3–4% lower, manufacturing 25.8%, FY26 growth 8.1%
79.x: The new GDP series placed GDP levels 3–4% lower, measured manufacturing at 14.7% of the economy and reported FY26 growth at 7.6%.
79.tq: Link several figures to the correct statistical series instead of mixing indicators.

79.s: Which statement best explains why Andhra Pradesh is described as more agrarian than India as a whole?

80.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the geographical origin of crops:
1. Coffee is included among the Old World crops.
2. Cocoa is included among the New World crops.
3. Rubber is included among the Old World crops.
4. Chilli is included among the New World crops.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Coffee is an Old World crop, while cocoa, rubber and chilli are New World crops. Therefore, statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, whereas statement 3 is false.
80.tq: Split the statements by checking each crop against the Old World–New World classification.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **coffee** is an **Old World** crop.
Statements 2 and 4 are correct: **cocoa** and **chilli** are **New World (Americas)** crops.
Statement 3 is wrong: **rubber** is a **New World** crop — so **1, 2 and 4 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Old World: **wheat, barley, rice, sugarcane, tea, coffee**.
New World: **maize, potato, tomato, tobacco, cocoa, rubber, cassava, groundnut, chilli**.
This is the standard **Columbian-exchange** pattern.

80.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Type of farming)
a. Plantation farming
b. Mixed farming
c. Commercial grain farming
d. Intensive subsistence farming

List-II (Characteristic region)
i. North-West Europe and eastern North America
ii. Monsoon Asia
iii. Prairies, Steppes, Pampas and Downs
iv. Malaysia, Brazil and India

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
80.x: Plantation farming is associated with Malaysia, Brazil and India; mixed farming with north-west Europe and eastern North America; commercial grain farming with the listed grassland regions; and intensive subsistence farming with monsoon Asia.
80.tq: Start with the distinctive plantation and mixed-farming pairs, then complete the code.
xs: **Plantation** — Malaysia, Brazil, India (iv); **Mixed** — NW Europe, eastern North America (i).
**Commercial grain** — Prairies, Steppes, Pampas, Downs (iii); **Intensive subsistence** — Monsoon Asia (ii) — so **a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii**, option **(1)**.
xa: Intensive subsistence: small plots, heavy labour, **high yield per ha** (wet paddy).
Commercial grain farming is **wheat**, mechanised and **extensive**.

80.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes intensive farming from extensive farming?
o: Intensive farming uses large areas with low input, whereas extensive farming uses small plots with high input.
Intensive farming uses high input per unit of land, whereas extensive farming uses large areas with relatively low input.
Extensive farming is confined to plantation estates, whereas intensive farming is confined to deserts.
Both systems necessarily use equal labour and capital per unit of land.
80.x: Intensive farming applies high labour and capital input to a unit of land, while extensive farming operates over larger areas with comparatively low input per unit of land.
80.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by checking input per unit of land against area.
xs: **Intensive** = **high input per unit of land**; **extensive** = **large areas with low input** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the two.
xa: Intensive subsistence farming: **Monsoon Asia** (wet paddy).
Extensive commercial grain farming: **Prairies, Steppes, Pampas, Downs**.

80.s: Derwent Whittlesey’s classification of world agricultural regions, published in 1936, identified how many regions?
80.x: Derwent Whittlesey mapped 13 agricultural regions in 1936. His classification remains a standard reference in agricultural geography.
80.tq: Use the distinctive classification count and publication year as paired numerical clues.
xs: **Derwent Whittlesey (1936)** mapped **13** agricultural regions — so option **(3)** is correct.
**4** is the number of **macro agricultural regions of India** (**Sengupta and Sdasyuk**).
xa: Whittlesey's **Mediterranean** region: winter rain, **viticulture**, citrus, olives.
His **Oriental intensive** region: Monsoon Asia, wet paddy.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about Mediterranean agriculture in Whittlesey's scheme:
1. It is found in the Mediterranean basin, California, central Chile, the south-western Cape and south-western Australia.
2. These regions receive most of their rain in summer.
3. Viticulture, citrus fruits and olives are typical of this agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the listed areas form the Mediterranean region, and viticulture, citrus and olives are its typical crops. Statement 2 is wrong: Mediterranean regions get winter rain, not summer rain. So A, B and D, which include statement 2, are wrong.
80.tq: Mediterranean = winter rain + grapes, citrus, olives; the Prairies are not part of it.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Mediterranean basin, California, central Chile, the SW Cape and SW Australia**.
Statement 2 is wrong: these regions get **winter rain**, not summer rain.
Statement 3 is correct: **viticulture, citrus, olives** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: **Viticulture** = grape cultivation.
Whittlesey mapped **13** regions (**1936**).

80.s: Oriental intensive farming is primarily associated with which of the following regions and characteristics?
o: The Mediterranean basin; winter rainfall and olives
The Prairies; mechanised wheat and high output per worker
The Pampas; extensive cattle ranching and low labour input
Monsoon Asia; wet paddy, high output per hectare and low output per worker
80.x: Oriental intensive farming belongs to monsoon Asia. It is characterised by wet-paddy cultivation, high output per hectare and relatively low output per worker.
80.tq: Contrast output per hectare with output per worker to identify the oriental intensive system.
xs: **Oriental intensive** farming = **Monsoon Asia**, **wet paddy**, **high output per hectare, low output per worker** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Winter rain and olives = **Mediterranean**; mechanised wheat = **commercial grain** (Prairies).
xa: It matches the **intensive subsistence** type: small plots, heavy labour.
**IRRI** (Los Baños, Philippines, **1960**) released **IR8** "miracle rice".

80.s:
Consider the following statements:

2. Hydroponics is a soil-free method of growing crops.
3. Aquaponics combines hydroponics with fish rearing and is classed as an agroecological practice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: vertical farming permits year-round cropping in non-tropical regions (APPSC-GS 2021 key), and hydroponics is soil-free. Statement 3 is wrong: aquaponics does combine hydroponics with fish, but neither it nor hydroponics is agroecological (UPSC trap). So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' leaves out statement 2, and the options with statement 3 include a wrong statement.
80.tq: Hydroponics and aquaponics are NOT agroecological.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **vertical farming** allows **year-round crops in non-tropical regions** (APPSC-GS 2021 key).
Statement 2 is correct: **hydroponics** is **soil-free**.
Statement 3 is wrong: aquaponics = hydroponics + fish, but ⚠ **neither** is **agroecological** (UPSC) — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Permaculture** = self-sustaining ecological food systems.
**Organic farming** bans synthetic inputs + **GMOs**.

80.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?

Organic farming — synthetic inputs and genetically modified organisms are avoided

xs: **Natural farming — compulsory dependence on synthetic fertilisers and chemical pesticides** is wrong — so option **(3)** is the answer.

xa: Organic farming relies on **crop rotation + manures**.
**Subhash Palekar** pioneered **ZBNF**.

80.s: Who pioneered Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF)?
80.x: Subhash Palekar pioneered Zero Budget Natural Farming. It is distinct from the broader organic-farming framework and from the Green Revolution breeding programme.

xs: **Subhash Palekar** pioneered **Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF)** — so option **(3)** is correct.

xa: **APCNF**: **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha** — world's largest agro-ecological programme.

80.s: Which programme is described as the world's largest agro-ecological programme, covering about 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh hectares?
80.x: APCNF (Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming) is the world's largest agro-ecological programme, with 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha. The National Mission on Natural Farming is the national mission (8.80 lakh ha), and IPM is a pest-control approach, not a programme of that size.
80.tq: APCNF = world's largest agro-ecological programme.
xs: **APCNF** is the **world's largest agro-ecological programme**: **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha** (Jul 2026) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **National Mission on Natural Farming** is the national scheme: **8.80 lakh ha**, **18.19 lakh** farmers by Mar 2026.
**IPM** is a pest-control method (bio-pesticides, pheromone traps, predators), not a programme.
xa: **ZBNF** was pioneered by **Subhash Palekar**.
⚠ **Hydroponics** and **aquaponics** are not agroecological.

80.s: Who is associated with the crop-combination method of agricultural regionalisation introduced in 1954?

xs: **J.C. Weaver (1954)** devised the **crop combination** method — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Bhatia** = diversification and concentration; **Kendall** = efficiency; **Sengupta** = macro regions of India.

80.x: China leads in crude steel, Chile in copper, Australia in iron ore and Brazil in coffee, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
80.tq: Recall the top producer of each commodity.
n: China is the world’s largest producer of crude steel. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
China is the world’s largest producer of coal. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
Australia is the world’s largest producer of iron ore. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
Australia is the world’s largest producer of bauxite. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
xs: The correct match is **a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(2)**.
**Crude steel** → **China** (a-ii); **Copper** → **Chile** (b-iii).
**Iron ore** → **Australia** (c-i); **Coffee** → **Brazil** (d-iv).
xa: **Australia** also leads in **bauxite**.
Diamonds: **Russia** by volume; **Botswana** by value.
World's largest fishing ground: **Northwest Pacific**; busiest container port: **Shanghai**.

80.s:

n: Russia is the world’s largest producer of diamonds by volume. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
Botswana is the world’s largest producer of diamonds by value. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.

xa: **Chile** leads in **copper**; **Australia** in **iron ore** and **bauxite**.
**China** leads in **gold**, coal and crude steel.
**Thailand** leads in **natural rubber**.

80.s: Which of the following statements about plantation agriculture is incorrect?

Cocoa is associated with South Asia.

Tea plantation agriculture is practised in Sri Lanka. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]

xs: The incorrect statement is "**Cocoa is associated with South Asia**" — option **(4)**.

**Coffee** in **Brazil**, **tea** in **India and Sri Lanka**, and **tropical regions** are correct.
xa: **Rubber** plantations are associated with **Malaysia**.

World cocoa: **Côte d'Ivoire 1st, Ghana 2nd**.

n: Plantation agriculture is a product of colonialism. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Plantation agriculture is export-oriented monoculture. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Plantation agriculture generally involves a single cash crop. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Plantation agriculture is export-oriented. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xs: **Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.

xa: It is **capital-intensive**.
Regions: **Latin America**, **South-East Asia**, **South Asia**, **Sub-Saharan Africa**.

80.s:

n: Dairy farming requires refrigeration. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Dairy farming requires transport. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture specialises in olives. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture specialises in grapes. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture specialises in citrus fruits. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture specialises in fruits. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]

xs: **Both Statement A and Statement B are true** — option **(1)**.
A: **dairy farming** specialises in **milk** and **requires refrigeration and transport**.

xa: Dairy regions: **Denmark**, the **Netherlands**, **New Zealand**, the US **Midwest**, **south-eastern Australia**.
Mediterranean regions: **California**, **Central Chile**, the **Cape Province**, **south-western Australia**.
**Whittlesey (1936)** mapped **13** agricultural regions.

80.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Nomadic herding involves seasonal migration with animals for fodder and water.
II. Intensive subsistence farming uses high labour input on small plots.
III. Livestock ranching is small-scale subsistence rearing of animals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
80.x: I and II are correct: nomads migrate seasonally with herds, and intensive subsistence farming puts heavy labour into small plots. III is false because ranching is large-scale and commercial.
80.tq: Discriminate subsistence from commercial farming.
n: Nomadic herding involves seasonal migration with animals. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is undertaken in search of fodder and water. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Intensive subsistence farming involves high labour input on small plots. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Livestock ranching involves large-scale commercial rearing of animals. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xs: Statements **I and II only** are correct — option **(4)**.
I is correct: **nomadic herding** = **seasonal migration with animals** in search of **fodder and water**.
II is correct: **intensive subsistence farming** = **high labour input on small plots**.
III is wrong: **livestock ranching** is **large-scale commercial** rearing on **ranches**.
xa: Ranching regions: **western US**, **Pampas**, **Australia**, **New Zealand**, **South Africa**.
Nomadic herding regions: **Sahara**, **Central Asia**, **Arabian Desert**, parts of **Rajasthan** and **J&K**.
Intensive subsistence farming gives a **high yield per hectare** in **Monsoon Asia**.

80.s:
How many of the following are regions associated with commercial grain farming?
1. Prairies
2. Pampas
3. Steppes
4. Mediterranean Basin
80.x: Three are grain regions: the Prairies, Pampas and Steppes. The Mediterranean Basin has Mediterranean farming.
80.tq: Recall the farming type of each region.
n: Commercial grain farming is practised in the Prairies of the United States and Canada. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Commercial grain farming is practised in the Pampas of Argentina. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Commercial grain farming is practised in the Steppes of Russia and Ukraine. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture is practised in the Mediterranean Basin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xs: **Only three** are commercial grain regions — option **(3)**.
The **Prairies** (US, Canada), **Pampas** (Argentina) and **Steppes** (Russia, Ukraine) are grain regions.
The **Mediterranean Basin** has **Mediterranean agriculture** (fruits, olives, grapes).
xa: The **Downs** of **Australia** are also a commercial grain region.
Commercial grain farming: **large, highly mechanised** farms; **wheat dominates**; **temperate grasslands**.
It is **extensive**, with a **high commodity rate**.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about shifting cultivation:
1. It is found in thickly forested areas of high rainfall such as the Amazon Basin, Tropical Africa, South-East Asia and North-East India.
2. It is a primitive subsistence, slash-and-burn agriculture in which forests are cleared by burning and cultivated temporarily with low technology.
3. It is a capital-intensive, export-oriented form of commercial agriculture.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
80.x: Statement 2 is correct: shifting cultivation is primitive slash-and-burn subsistence farming with temporary cultivation and low technology. Statement 1 is correct: it occurs in thick, high-rainfall forests of the Amazon, Tropical Africa, South-East Asia and North-East India. Statement 3 is wrong: capital-intensive export monoculture describes plantation agriculture. So only statement 3 is NOT correct; the other options wrongly name statement 1 or 2.
80.tq: Shifting = subsistence, forests, rain; plantation = capital, export.
xs: Only statement **3** is NOT correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: shifting cultivation is in **thickly forested, high-rainfall** areas — **Amazon Basin, Tropical Africa, South-East Asia, North-East India**.
Statement 2 is correct: it is **primitive subsistence, slash-and-burn** farming — **temporary cultivation**, **low technology**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **capital-intensive, export-oriented** farming describes **plantation agriculture**.
xa: AP's version is **podu**, in the agency tracts.
Plantation agriculture is a **product of colonialism**.
**Intensive subsistence** farming uses **family labour** on small plots.

80.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Nomadic herding is practised in the Sahara and Central Asia.
Nomadic herding is practised in parts of Jammu and Kashmir and the Sahara.
Nomadic herding is practised in the Amazon rainforest and the Congo Basin.
Nomadic herding is practised in the Arabian Desert and parts of Rajasthan.
80.x: Option C is incorrect: the Amazon and Congo rainforests support shifting cultivation, not nomadic herding. Herding is practised in dry or cold lands such as the Sahara, Central Asia, Arabia, Rajasthan and Jammu and Kashmir.
80.tq: Match pastoral nomadism to dry or cold grazing lands, not dense rainforest.
n: Nomadic herding is practised in the Sahara. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is practised in Central Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is practised in the Arabian Desert. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is practised in parts of Rajasthan. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is practised in parts of Jammu and Kashmir. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xs: The incorrect statement is "**Nomadic herding is practised in the Amazon rainforest and the Congo Basin**" — option **(3)**.
The **Amazon Basin** is a region of **shifting cultivation**, in thickly forested, **high-rainfall** areas.
Nomadic herding is in the **Sahara**, **Central Asia**, the **Arabian Desert**, parts of **Rajasthan** and **J&K**.
xa: Herders migrate seasonally in search of **fodder and water**.
**Livestock ranching** is the commercial, large-scale form of animal rearing.
Shifting cultivation regions: **Amazon Basin**, **Tropical Africa**, **South-East Asia**, **North-East India**.

80.s:
Assertion (A): Intensive subsistence farming uses family labour.
Reason (R): Intensive subsistence farming produces a high yield per hectare.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
80.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: high yields do not explain why families supply the labour; small holdings and poverty do.
80.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Intensive subsistence farming uses family labour. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Intensive subsistence farming produces a high yield per hectare. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A: intensive subsistence farming uses **family labour** and **high labour input on small plots**.
R: it gives a **high yield per hectare** — an outcome, not the reason families supply the labour.
xa: **Rice dominates** in **wet areas**.
Region: **Monsoon Asia** — East, South and South-East Asia.
Whittlesey's **Oriental intensive** type: **high output per hectare, low output per worker**.

80.s: Which crop dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas?
80.x: Rice dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas; wheat takes over in drier parts.
80.tq: Recall the main crop of each farming type.
n: Rice dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xs: **Rice** dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas — option **(4)**.
Intensive subsistence farming in **Monsoon Asia** relies on **wet paddy**.
**Wheat** dominates **commercial grain farming**; **tea** and **coffee** are **plantation** crops.
xa: It uses **high labour input** on **small plots** with **family labour**.
It gives a **high yield per hectare**.
**China** is the largest rice producer; **India** the **second-largest** and **number-one exporter**.

80.s:
Assertion (A): Commercial grain farming has a high commodity rate.
Reason (R): Wheat dominates commercial grain farming.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
80.x: Both are true but R does not explain A: wheat dominance does not explain the high marketed share; large mechanised farms and low local demand do.
80.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: Commercial grain farming has a high commodity rate. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Wheat dominates commercial grain farming. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
A: commercial grain farming has a **high commodity rate**.
R: **wheat dominates** it — but the crop type does not explain the high marketed share.
Large, **highly mechanised** farms are the notes' distinguishing feature.
xa: Regions: **Prairies**, **Pampas**, **Steppes**, **Downs**.
It is associated with **temperate grasslands**.
It is an **extensive** form of farming.

80.s:
Consider the following statements:

III. Mixed farming is practised in Western Europe, the eastern United States and Argentina.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
80.x: All four are correct: mixed farming combines crops and livestock with heavy machinery in western Europe, the eastern USA, Argentina, south-east Australia, New Zealand and South Africa.
