List-I (Industrial corridor)
a. VCIC
b. CBIC
c. HBIC

List-II (Associated feature)
i. Orvakal node
ii. Krishnapatnam node
iii. Part of ECEC and ADB-funded

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
86.x: VCIC is part of the ECEC and is ADB-funded; CBIC has the Krishnapatnam node; HBIC has the Orvakal node.
86.tq: Start from the sure corridor-node pairs and eliminate inconsistent combinations.
xs: Correct code **a-iii, b-ii, c-i** — option **(1)**.
**VCIC** is the first phase of the **ECEC** and is **ADB**-funded.
**CBIC** has the **Krishnapatnam** node; **HBIC** has the **Orvakal** node.
xa: VCIC AP nodes: **Vizag, Chittoor, Kopparthy**.
CBIC partner: **Japan (JICA)**; length **560 km**.
**APIIC** manages **571 industrial parks** and is the nodal agency in AP.

86.s: The Andhra Pradesh nodes of the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) are:
86.x: VCIC's AP nodes are Visakhapatnam, Chittoor and Kopparthy (about 33,000 acres). Krishnapatnam is the CBIC node and Orvakal the HBIC node (B, D wrong); Durgapur is the Budget 2026-27 East Coast Industrial Corridor node (C wrong).
86.tq: VCIC = Vizag-Chittoor-Kopparthy; CBIC = Krishnapatnam; HBIC = Orvakal.
xs: VCIC's AP nodes are **Vizag, Chittoor and Kopparthy** — option **(1)**.
**Krishnapatnam** is the **CBIC** node and **Orvakal** the **HBIC** node.
**Durgapur** is the Budget 2026-27 **East Coast Industrial Corridor** node; **Sri City** is an automobile hub.
xa: VCIC AP nodes cover **33,000 acres** at **₹5,000 crore**.
ADB loan for VCIC: **₹3,300 crore** (2024-25).
⚠ Some notes (Jan 2026) list **7** nodes with **JICA** as partner; others give **ADB** and three nodes.

86.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to Defence Industrial Corridors?
o: Tamil Nadu — Chennai, Coimbatore and Hosur
Tamil Nadu — Madurai, Salem and Tiruchirappalli
Uttar Pradesh — Chitrakoot, Kanpur and Lucknow
Uttar Pradesh — Aligarh, Agra and Jhansi
86.x: The Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor has Chennai, Coimbatore, Hosur, Salem and Tiruchirappalli; Madurai is not listed among its five nodes.
86.tq: Find the swapped or substituted node in the corridor list.
xs: **Tamil Nadu — Madurai, Salem and Tiruchirappalli** is wrongly matched — option **(2)**: **Madurai** is not a TN DIC node.
TN's **5** nodes: **Chennai, Coimbatore, Hosur, Salem, Tiruchirappalli**.
UP's **6** nodes: **Aligarh, Agra, Jhansi, Chitrakoot, Kanpur, Lucknow** — so options (3) and (4) are correct pairs.
xa: There are **two** Defence Industrial Corridors.
Together they have **₹74,756 crore** of commitments.
The first DIC was announced **between Chennai and Bengaluru** (APPSC-GS 2019).

86.s: India’s first Defence Industrial Corridor was announced along which stretch?
86.x: India’s first Defence Industrial Corridor was announced along the Chennai-Bengaluru stretch.
86.tq: Avoid confusing the first Defence Industrial Corridor with the names of major economic corridors.
xs: The first Defence Industrial Corridor was announced along the **Chennai-Bengaluru** stretch — option **(1)** (APPSC-GS 2019 answer key).
**Amritsar-Kolkata**, **Visakhapatnam-Chennai** and **Delhi-Mumbai** are **industrial** corridors (AKIC, VCIC, DMIC), not DICs.
xa: India has **two** DICs — **Uttar Pradesh** (**6** nodes) and **Tamil Nadu** (**5** nodes).
Investment commitments: **₹74,756 crore**.
⚠ Don't confuse with **CBIC**, the Chennai-Bengaluru **industrial** corridor (**560 km**, Japan/JICA).

86.s: Which of the following pairs of SEZ examples and states is correctly matched?
86.x: Vallarpadam is an example from Kerala and Nanguneri is an example from Tamil Nadu. SEZs are intended to attract investment and exports, including in lagging regions.
86.tq: Start with the state-location pair to test the distribution of SEZ examples.
xs: **Vallarpadam — Kerala**; **Nanguneri — Tamil Nadu** — option **(1)**.
Both are SEZ examples aimed at attracting **investment and exports in lagging regions**.
xa: **SEZ Act 2005**, in force **10 Feb 2006**, with **single-window clearance**.
Status (**31 Mar 2025**): **368 notified, 276 operational** SEZs.
**MP** has **5 SEZs**: 3 IT/ITeS at **Indore and Gwalior**; mineral- and agro-based at **Jabalpur**.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in India:
1. The SEZ Act, 2005 came into force on 10 February 2006.
2. The SEZ framework provides single-window clearance.
3. Budget 2026-27 allows SEZ manufacturing units to sell their entire output in the Domestic Tariff Area without any duty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Budget 2026-27 gave a one-time permission to sell to the Domestic Tariff Area at concessional duty, capped as a share of exports, not duty-free unlimited sales. So B is right; A omits statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
86.tq: DTA sales: one-time, concessional duty, capped - not duty-free.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: the **SEZ Act 2005** came into force on **10 Feb 2006** — correct.
Statement 2: it provides **single-window clearance** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: Budget 2026-27 gave a **one-time** permission to sell to the **Domestic Tariff Area** at **concessional duty**, **capped** as a share of exports.
xa: Status (**31 Mar 2025**): **368 notified, 276 operational** SEZs; **6,695** units.
SEZ examples: **Vallarpadam (Kerala)**, **Nanguneri (TN)**.
NIMZs are **bigger than SEZs** and distinct from them.

86.s: As on 31 March 2025, the number of notified and operational SEZs in India was respectively
86.x: As on 31 March 2025, India had 368 notified SEZs, of which 276 were operational.
86.tq: Keep the order of the two categories intact while using paired numerical data.
xs: As on **31 Mar 2025**: **368 notified** and **276 operational** SEZs — option **(3)**.
**6,695** is the number of **units** in SEZs, not of SEZs.
xa: SEZs employed **31.8 lakh** people.
**SEZ Act 2005**, in force **10 Feb 2006**.
**India Industrial Land Bank** maps **4,100+** parks/estates/SEZs on **6.56 lakh ha**.

86.s: National Investment and Manufacturing Zones are associated with which policy and targets?
o: Budget 2026–27; manufacturing at 50% of GDP and 100 million jobs
National Manufacturing Policy 2011; manufacturing at 25% of GDP and 100 million jobs
SEZ Act 2005; manufacturing at 16–17% of GDP and 10 million jobs
National Manufacturing Policy 2005; manufacturing at 10% of GDP and 25 million jobs
86.x: NIMZs are under the National Manufacturing Policy 2011, which targeted manufacturing at 25% of GDP and 100 million jobs.
86.tq: Match the policy, year and two numerical targets as one linked fact set.
xs: **NIMZs** come from the **National Manufacturing Policy 2011**, targeting manufacturing at **25% of GDP** and **100 million jobs** — option **(2)**.
The **SEZ Act** is of **2005**; **16-17%** is manufacturing's **current** share of GDP, not a target.
xa: NIMZs are **large integrated townships**, **bigger than SEZs**.
They differ from SEZs in **governance, exit and fiscal rules**.
The **25%** target is set for **2047**.

86.s: Which statement best distinguishes NIMZs from SEZs?
o: NIMZs are exclusively agricultural zones without manufacturing activity.
NIMZs are large integrated townships and are bigger than SEZs, with differences in governance, exit and fiscal rules.
NIMZs are small export enclaves with exactly the same governance and fiscal rules as SEZs.
86.x: NIMZs are conceived as large integrated townships, bigger than SEZs, and differ from them in governance, exit and fiscal rules.
86.tq: Compare the scale and regulatory features rather than relying on the common industrial purpose.
xs: NIMZs are **large integrated townships**, **bigger than SEZs**, differing in **governance, exit and fiscal rules** — option **(2)**.
So they are neither small export enclaves nor identical in rules to SEZs, and they are built around township development.
xa: NIMZs come from the **National Manufacturing Policy 2011**.
Targets: manufacturing **25% of GDP**, **100 million jobs**.
SEZs: **SEZ Act 2005**, in force **10 Feb 2006**, single-window clearance.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about BHAVYA:
1. It provides for 100 plug-and-play industrial parks.
2. Its allocation is ₹33,660 crore.
3. It covers FY 2026–27 to 2031–32.
4. The parks are selected through challenge mode and run by NICDC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: All four statements correctly describe BHAVYA: 100 parks, ₹33,660 crore, the period FY 2026–27 to 2031–32, challenge-mode selection and operation by NICDC.
86.tq: Use a complete coded combination when all listed programme attributes are correct.
xs: All four statements are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**BHAVYA**: **100 plug-and-play industrial parks**, **₹33,660 crore**.
Period **FY 2026-27 to 2031-32**; parks chosen by **challenge mode**, run by **NICDC**.
xa: BHAVYA = **Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana**.
**NICDC** is the ex-**DMICDC**, set up **Jan 2008**.
India has **4,500+** mapped industrial parks.

86.s: Which one of the following correctly lists the industrial corridors associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: East Coast, Delhi–Mumbai and Golden Quadrilateral only
VCIC, CBIC and Hyderabad–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor
86.x: The Andhra Pradesh corridors listed are VCIC, CBIC and the Hyderabad–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
86.tq: Identify the exact corridor set and reject options mixing corridors with projects or industrial centres.
xs: AP's corridors are **VCIC, CBIC and the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (HBIC)** — option **(4)**.
**Durgapur** is an East Coast Industrial Corridor node; **Sivakasi** and **Pithampur** are industrial centres, not corridors.
xa: AP nodes: **Vizag, Chittoor, Kopparthy** (VCIC); **Krishnapatnam North** (CBIC); **Orvakal** (HBIC).
ADB support of **US$ 840 million** for AP corridors (AP Survey 2025-26).
**APIIC** manages **571 industrial parks**.

86.s: India has more than 4,500 mapped industrial parks, while manufacturing currently accounts for approximately what share of GDP, with a target for 2047?
86.x: India has more than 4,500 mapped industrial parks; manufacturing contributes about 16–17% of GDP, with a target of 25% by 2047.
86.tq: Match the present share with the future target while retaining the direction of change.
xs: Manufacturing is **16-17% of GDP**, with a target of **25%** by **2047** — option **(2)**.
India has **4,500+** mapped industrial parks.
xa: The **National Manufacturing Policy 2011** also set the **25% of GDP** target, with **100 million jobs**.
**India Industrial Land Bank** (**27 Aug 2020**): **4,100+** parks on **6.56 lakh ha**.
Industrial growth is concentrated in **southern and western** states.

86.s: The nodal agency managing about 571 industrial parks in Andhra Pradesh is:
86.x: The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) is the nodal agency and manages 571 industrial parks. NICDC (A) and NICDIT (D) are national corridor bodies; APFDC (C) is the AP Forest Development Corporation.
86.tq: AP parks = APIIC (571).
xs: **APIIC** is AP's nodal agency and manages **571 industrial parks** — option **(2)**.
**NICDC** and **NICDIT** are the **national** corridor implementing bodies, not AP agencies.
xa: AP corridors: **VCIC, CBIC, HBIC**; ADB support **US$ 840 million**.
**NICDC** (ex-DMICDC, **Jan 2008**) runs **BHAVYA** parks.

87.s:
Consider the following statements about the steel sector:
1. India is the world's largest crude steel producer.
2. China accounts for over 50% of world steel production.
3. The National Steel Policy 2017 targets 300 MT of steel capacity by 2030-31.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
87.x: Statement 1 is wrong: India is the 2nd largest crude steel producer, after China. Statement 2 is correct: China produces over 50% of world steel. Statement 3 is correct: NSP 2017 targets 300 MT capacity (and 255 MT production) by 2030-31. So C is right; A and D include the false statement 1, B omits statement 3.
87.tq: India = 2nd after China; NSP 2017 = 300 MT capacity, 255 MT output.
xs: **Statements 2 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 is wrong: India is the **2nd largest** crude steel producer, **after China**.
Statement 2: **China** produces **over 50%** of world steel — correct.
Statement 3: **National Steel Policy 2017** targets **300 MT capacity** by **2030-31** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **300 MT** = capacity target; **255 MT** = production target.
NSP 2017 inputs needed: **437 MT iron ore** and **161 MT coking coal**.

87.s: India’s crude steel production in 2025–26 was recorded as
87.x: Crude steel production in 2025–26 was 168.4 MT, representing a 10.7 percent increase and approximately 9 percent CAGR since 2021–22.
87.tq: Distinguish annual production from installed capacity.
xs: India's crude steel output in **2025-26** was **168.4 MT** — option **(4)**.
It grew **10.7%**, with a CAGR of about **9%** since **2021-22**.
xa: India is the **2nd largest** crude steel producer after **China**.
NSP 2017 target: **255 MT** production by **2030-31**.

87.s:
Which one of the following correctly represents the process mix in India’s steel industry?

Blast furnace–basic oxygen furnace : Electric arc furnace : Induction furnace
87.x: The process mix is 43% BF–BOF, 22% EAF and 35% induction furnace.
87.tq: Preserve the order of the three processes while comparing their shares.
xs: The process mix is **43% BF-BOF : 22% EAF : 35% induction furnace** — option **(3)** (India Steel Association, **8 Sep 2026**).
**56%** is the BF-BOF share **projected for 2030**, not the current share.
xa: Mini/secondary units use the **electric arc** and **induction furnaces** — the **22%** and **35%** shares.
Induction furnaces work in **small batches** and are **energy-efficient**.
India is the **leading producer** of **sponge iron (DRI)**.

87.s: India is the leading producer of which of the following?
o: Sponge iron or direct reduced iron
87.x: India is the leading producer of sponge iron, also known as direct reduced iron (DRI).
87.tq: Use the exact product synonym to avoid confusing sponge iron with crude steel.
xs: India is the **leading producer** of **sponge iron (DRI)** — option **(2)**.
In aluminium India is **2nd largest** primary producer, not the leader; in copper India is a **net importer** of concentrate.
xa: Mini/secondary units melt **scrap or sponge iron** in electric arc and induction furnaces.
India is the **2nd largest** crude steel producer after China.
Copper world leader: **Chile**.

87.s: Why does India continue to import substantial quantities of coking coal despite domestic production?
o: Domestic coking coal is high in ash
Domestic iron ore is unsuitable for steelmaking
Coking coal is not used in blast furnaces
87.x: Domestic coking coal is high in ash, which makes imports necessary despite domestic production.
87.tq: Identify the quality-based cause rather than a false absolute statement.
xs: India imports coking coal because **domestic coal is high-ash** — option **(1)**.
In **2024-25** coking coal output was **66.49 MT** but imports were **57.07 MT**.
Iron ore is adequate: output **289.398 MT**, imports only **6.4 MT**.
xa: NSP 2017 needs **161 MT coking coal** and **437 MT iron ore** by 2030-31.
NSP targets: **300 MT capacity**, **255 MT** production.
Indian steel emits **2.54 tCO2/t** vs **1.9** world average.

87.s: Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, the Ministry of Steel has an allocation for green-hydrogen pilot projects in steel of:
87.x: The Ministry of Steel has Rs 455 crore for green-hydrogen pilots in steel till 2029-30. Rs 25,938 crore is the PLI-Auto outlay (B); Rs 33,660 crore is BHAVYA (C); Rs 3,000 crore is NICDIT in BE 2026-27 (D).
87.tq: Green H2 in steel: Rs 455 crore to 2029-30.
xs: The Ministry of Steel has **₹455 crore** for green-hydrogen pilots in steel **till 2029-30** — option **(1)**.
This falls under the **National Green Hydrogen Mission**.
xa: The **PLI for Specialty Steel** was approved in **2021**.
Indian steel emits **2.54 tCO2/t** vs **1.9** world average — **10-12%** of national CO2.
**EU CBAM** exposure is a key criticism of Indian steel.

87.s: The power-oriented location of aluminium smelters is primarily explained by the fact that they are generally established near:
o: hydroelectric or captive thermal power sources
87.x: Because aluminium smelting consumes 14,000–15,000 kWh per tonne, smelters are located near hydel or captive thermal power sources rather than being governed solely by proximity to mines.
87.tq: Apply the raw-material-versus-power distinction to an industrial-location scenario.
xs: Aluminium smelters are placed near **hydel or captive thermal power** — option **(4)**.
Smelting needs **14,000-15,000 kWh** per tonne, so **power**, not the mine, decides location.
xa: Example: **NALCO**'s smelter and **captive power** plant are at **Angul**, Odisha.
Aluminium is the **2nd most important** metallurgical industry after steel.
India is the **2nd largest** primary aluminium producer; **Odisha** is the top bauxite state.

87.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
87.x: NALCO has its alumina refinery at Damanjodi in Koraput district. Its smelter and captive power facilities are at Angul.
87.tq: Separate the refinery location from the smelter and captive-power location within the same company.
xs: **NALCO refinery — Damanjodi** (Koraput) is correct — option **(2)**.
NALCO's **smelter and captive power** are at **Angul**, not Damanjodi; **Korba** is **BALCO**.
xa: NALCO uses **Panchpatmali** bauxite and was built with **French** help.
It is the **largest complex**.
⚠ **Vedanta**'s **Jharsuguda** plant is the largest aluminium **smelter**.

87.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
87.x: Vedanta's largest aluminium smelter is located at Jharsuguda in Odisha. BALCO is at Korba, HINDALCO is at Renukoot and Hirakud, and MALCO is at Mettur.
87.tq: Start from the sure company–location pair and eliminate the swapped plant locations.
xs: **Vedanta — Jharsuguda** (Odisha) is correct — option **(1)**; it is the **largest aluminium smelter**.
**BALCO** is at **Korba**, **HINDALCO** at **Renukoot** and **Hirakud**, and **MALCO** at **Mettur**.
xa: BALCO uses **Amarkantak** bauxite.
HINDALCO's bauxite: **Lohardaga** (Jharkhand).
NALCO's **Damanjodi-Angul** complex is the **largest complex**.

87.s:
Arrange the following aluminium companies in descending order of sales as indicated:
A. INDAL
B. HINDALCO
C. MALCO
D. NALCO
87.x: The sales order is HINDALCO, NALCO, INDAL and MALCO.
87.tq: Convert the stated ranking into a descending-order sequence.
xs: Sales order: **HINDALCO > NALCO > INDAL > MALCO** = **B, D, A, C** — option **(1)**.
**HINDALCO** is the **top seller**; **MALCO** comes last.
xa: HINDALCO plants: **Renukoot** and **Hirakud**.
INDAL plants: **Muri** (Jharkhand), **Belagavi** (Karnataka), **Alupuram** (Kerala).
MALCO: **Mettur** (TN).

87.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
87.x: Muri is in Jharkhand, not Chhattisgarh. Belagavi and Alupuram are also INDAL locations.
87.tq: Find the geographically shifted state in an otherwise familiar company–plant list.
xs: **INDAL — Muri, Chhattisgarh** is wrong — option **(4)**: **Muri is in Jharkhand**.
INDAL's plants are **Muri** (Jharkhand), **Belagavi** (Karnataka) and **Alupuram** (Kerala).
xa: Exam angle: "**Muri - Chhattisgarh**" is the classic wrong pair.
The Chhattisgarh aluminium plant is **BALCO** at **Korba**.
INDAL is third in sales: **HINDALCO > NALCO > INDAL > MALCO**.

87.s: Which one of the following statements regarding aluminium production in India is correct?
o: India is the second-largest aluminium producer and Odisha is the largest bauxite-producing state.
Aluminium is a coal-oriented industry requiring negligible electricity.
Uttar Pradesh is the largest bauxite-producing state and India is the third-largest aluminium producer.
The largest aluminium smelter is located at Muri in Jharkhand.
87.x: Aluminium is power-oriented, requiring about 14,000–15,000 kWh per tonne. India is the second-largest aluminium producer and Odisha is the largest bauxite state.
87.tq: Use the power requirement and production-rank clues together.
xs: India is the **2nd largest** primary aluminium producer and **Odisha** is the top bauxite state — option **(1)**.
Aluminium is **power-oriented** (**14,000-15,000 kWh** per tonne), not low-electricity.
The largest smelter is **Vedanta**'s at **Jharsuguda**, not Muri.
xa: India is **7th** in bauxite reserves.
Aluminium is the **2nd most important** metallurgical industry after steel.
Smelters sit near **hydel or captive thermal power** rather than mines.

87.s: Which organisation operates the copper facilities at Khetri and Ghatsila–Mosabani?
87.x: Khetri in Rajasthan and Ghatsila–Mosabani in Jharkhand are copper centres operated by Hindustan Copper Limited.
87.tq: Identify the public-sector operator rather than the metal-producing location alone.
xs: **Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL)** runs **Khetri** (Rajasthan) and **Ghatsila/Mosabani** (Jharkhand) — option **(2)**.
**HINDALCO** runs the **Dahej** copper plant; **Hindustan Zinc** runs **Zawar**; **Sterlite** was at **Thoothukudi**.
xa: **Malanjkhand** (MP) is India's **largest open-pit copper mine** (HCL).
India holds **under 2%** of global copper reserves.
World leader in copper: **Chile**.

87.s: Malanjkhand, located in Madhya Pradesh, is noted for being:
o: the largest aluminium smelter in India
the first public integrated steel plant
87.x: Malanjkhand is India's largest open-pit copper mine and is associated with Hindustan Copper Limited.
87.tq: Distinguish a mine from a smelter and from plants belonging to other metallurgical industries.
xs: **Malanjkhand** (MP) is India's **largest open-pit copper mine** — option **(1)**.
The largest aluminium smelter is **Jharsuguda**; the first public integrated steel plant is **Rourkela**; lead-zinc mines are at **Zawar**.
xa: Other HCL copper centres: **Khetri** (Rajasthan), **Ghatsila/Mosabani** (Jharkhand).
India is a **net importer** of copper concentrate.
**Thoothukudi**'s Sterlite copper plant was **shut** after environmental litigation.

87.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Dahej — HINDALCO copper plant using imported concentrate
87.x: Dahej in Gujarat has a HINDALCO copper facility that uses imported concentrate. Zawar is associated with Hindustan Zinc, Visakhapatnam with a zinc smelter, and Thoothukudi with Sterlite copper.
87.tq: Use operator and input material together to reject swapped metallurgy pairs.
xs: **Dahej — HINDALCO copper plant using imported concentrate** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Zawar** = **lead-zinc** mines of Hindustan Zinc; **Visakhapatnam** = **zinc smelter**; **Thoothukudi** = **Sterlite copper** plant.
xa: Sterlite at Thoothukudi was **shut** after environmental litigation.
HCL copper: **Khetri, Ghatsila/Mosabani, Malanjkhand**.
India holds **under 2%** of global copper reserves.

87.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India holds less than 2 per cent of global copper reserves.
2. India is a net importer of copper concentrate.
3. Chile leads in global copper reserves.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: All three statements are correct: India's global reserve share is under 2 per cent, it imports copper concentrate on a net basis, and Chile is the leading country mentioned for copper reserves.
87.tq: Combine a percentage, trade position and world-leader fact in one statement set.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
India holds **under 2%** of global copper reserves and is a **net importer** of copper concentrate.
**Chile** is the world leader.
xa: **Dahej** (HINDALCO) uses **imported concentrate**.
Indian copper: **Khetri**, **Ghatsila/Mosabani**, **Malanjkhand** (HCL).
**Thoothukudi** Sterlite plant was **shut**.

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding emissions from India's steel industry:
1. Indian steel emits about 2.54 tonnes of CO2 per tonne of steel.
2. The corresponding world average is about 1.9 tonnes of CO2 per tonne.
3. The steel sector contributes approximately 10–12 per cent of India's national CO2 emissions.
4. Indian steel faces exposure to the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: All four statements are correct. The stated Indian intensity exceeds the world average, the sector contributes 10–12 per cent of national CO2 emissions, and EU CBAM creates exposure for Indian steel.
87.tq: Compare the national and global emission figures before assessing the policy implication.
xs: All four statements are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
Indian steel emits **2.54 tCO2/t** vs a **1.9** world average.
The sector is **10-12%** of national CO2 and faces **EU CBAM** exposure.
xa: The draft **CCTS** notification binds **255 plants** from FY 2026-27.
Ministry of Steel: **₹455 crore** for green-hydrogen pilots till **2029-30**.
BF-BOF share projected at **56% by 2030**.

87.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the alternatives considered before Visakhapatnam was selected for the steel plant?
87.x: The alternatives mentioned were Bailadila, Goa, Neyveli, Salem and Hospet. Durgapur was not included in that list.
87.tq: Find the location outside a specified shortlist rather than selecting a familiar steel centre.
xs: **Durgapur** was not among the alternatives — option **(2)**.
**NSR's committee** chose Vizag over **Bailadila, Goa, Neyveli, Salem and Hospet**.
xa: The **1965-66** agitation slogan: "**Visakha Steel - Andhra's Right**".
Foundation stone: **20 Jan 1971**; first blast furnace "**Godavari**" (foundation **1982**).
Vizag was India's **first shore-based** steel plant.

87.s:
Consider the following statements about the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant:
1. Its foundation stone was laid on 20 January 1971.
2. Its first blast furnace was named 'Godavari'.
3. It was India's first public-sector integrated steel plant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
87.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Rourkela was the first public integrated plant; Vizag was the first shore-based plant. So B is right; A omits statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
87.tq: Rourkela = first public integrated; Vizag = first shore-based.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: foundation stone on **20 Jan 1971** — correct.
Statement 2: first blast furnace named "**Godavari**" — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Rourkela** was the first public integrated plant; **Vizag** was the **first shore-based** plant.
xa: Godavari blast furnace foundation: **1982**.
An explosion at the Vizag Steel Plant killed **8** on **8 Jun 2026**; a **3-member** probe panel followed.
Vizag was chosen by **NSR's committee** over Bailadila, Goa, Neyveli, Salem and Hospet.

87.s: The 1965–66 agitation associated with the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant used the slogan:
87.x: The agitation slogan was “Visakha Steel – Andhra's Right.”
87.tq: Recall the exact slogan rather than a paraphrase of the demand.
xs: The **1965-66** agitation slogan was "**Visakha Steel - Andhra's Right**" — option **(4)**.
"**Godavari**" was the name of the plant's first blast furnace, not of a movement.
xa: Foundation stone: **20 Jan 1971**.
**NSR's committee** chose Vizag over **Bailadila, Goa, Neyveli, Salem and Hospet**.
Vizag was the **first shore-based** steel plant.

88.s:
Consider the following statements about the cotton textile industry:
1. The first mill at Fort Gloster was established in 1818 and failed.
2. The first successful cotton mill was established in Mumbai in 1854 by C. N. Davar.
3. Cotton textile centres later spread to Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
88.x: All three statements are correct. Fort Gloster was the unsuccessful 1818 mill, while C. N. Davar established the first successful mill at Mumbai in 1854; the industry later dispersed to other regions.
88.tq: Combine the first-establishment facts with the subsequent spatial-diffusion statement.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
Statement 1: the **1818 Fort Gloster** mill near Kolkata **failed** — correct.
Statement 2: the first successful mill was at **Mumbai, 1854**, by **C.N. Davar** — correct.
Statement 3: the industry dispersed to **Tamil Nadu and MP**, since cotton is **not weight-losing** — correct.
xa: It began near the **black-soil** cotton tracts of **Maharashtra and Gujarat**.
First jute mill: **Rishra, 1855**; first woollen mill: **Kanpur, 1876**.
⚠ Cotton = not weight-losing (dispersed); steel = **weight-losing** (near raw material).

88.s: The concentration of cotton spinning in Coimbatore is particularly associated with:
o: Jute, softwood and riverine retting water
Petroleum, imported wool and sea-borne coal
Hydel power, cheap labour and local cotton
88.x: Coimbatore's spinning concentration is supported by hydel power, cheap labour and local cotton.
88.tq: Match the industrial centre with its specific locational advantages.
xs: Coimbatore's spinning rests on **hydel power, cheap labour and local cotton** — option **(4)**.
Jute, softwood and retting water belong to **jute/paper**; iron ore and limestone to **steel/cement**.
xa: Coimbatore is the "**Manchester of South India**".
⚠ Manchester of India = **Ahmedabad**; Cottonopolis = **Mumbai**.
Cotton centres: **Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Surat, Sholapur, Nagpur, Coimbatore, Madurai, Kanpur, Ludhiana**.

88.s: Approximately what proportion of India's jute mill capacity is concentrated in the belt along the Hooghly River?
88.x: About 90% of jute mill capacity is concentrated along the Hooghly basin.
88.tq: Identify the approximate percentage rather than confusing capacity concentration with output share.
xs: **Nearly 90 percent** of jute capacity is in the **Hooghly** belt — option **(3)**.
The belt is **100 km long and 3 km wide** along the Hooghly (PYQ: "most jute mills in the Hugli basin").
xa: West Bengal has **71** of **97** mills and **over 80%** of output.
First jute mill: **Rishra, 1855**.
AP jute mills: **Chittivalasa, Nellimarla** (since the **1920s**).

88.s: Which one of the following is NOT a major locational factor responsible for the concentration of jute mills in the Hooghly basin?
o: Kolkata port and the Hooghly waterway
Availability of cheap labour from eastern and northern India
Availability of extensive iron-ore deposits in the immediate basin
88.x: Iron-ore deposits are not identified as a major reason for the Hooghly concentration. Deltaic raw jute, water transport, port facilities and cheap labour are important factors.
88.tq: Find the option belonging to a neighbouring industry rather than the jute industry's actual locational factors.
xs: **Iron-ore deposits** are not a reason for the Hooghly jute belt — option **(4)**.
The listed reasons: **Ganga-Brahmaputra delta** raw jute, **soft water for retting**, the **Hooghly waterway** and **Kolkata port**.
Also **cheap labour** from WB, Bihar, UP, and a big **gunny-bag** market.
xa: About **90%** of capacity in a **100 km x 3 km** belt.
Kolkata port served both **export** and **machinery** imports.
**Bangladesh** is the largest jute exporter (~**75%**).

88.s:
Consider the following statements about the jute industry:
1. Of India's 97 jute mills (2026), West Bengal has 71 and Andhra Pradesh 12.
2. Bangladesh is the largest exporter of jute, with about 75% of exports.
3. West Bengal accounts for less than half of India's jute output.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
88.x: Statement 1 is correct: 97 mills, WB 71, AP 12. Statement 2 is correct: Bangladesh exports about 75%. Statement 3 is wrong: West Bengal accounts for over 80% of output. So only two statements are correct.
88.tq: Jute: WB 71 mills, AP 12 (2nd); Bangladesh top exporter.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** only two.
Statement 1 is correct: India has **97 jute mills (2026)** — **West Bengal 71**, **Andhra Pradesh 12**.
Statement 2 is correct: **Bangladesh** is the **largest exporter**, with about **75%**.
Statement 3 is wrong: West Bengal gives **over 80%** of India's jute output.
xa: About **90%** of jute capacity lies in a **100 km x 3 km** belt along the **Hooghly**.
AP jute mills: **Chittivalasa** and **Nellimarla**; AP's **12** mills are the **2nd highest** number.
**Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987:** **100%** of foodgrains and **20%** of sugar in jute bags.
First jute mill: **Rishra**, near Kolkata, **1855**.

88.s: The Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987 provides for compulsory packing in jute bags of:
88.x: The Act provides for 100% of foodgrains and 20% of sugar to be packed in jute bags.
88.tq: Discriminate between the two percentages and their respective commodities.
xs: The **Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987** mandates jute bags for **100% of foodgrains and 20% of sugar** — option **(3)**.
These mandates mean about **90%** of jute output is used at home.
xa: **National Jute Policy**: announced **2005**.
Raw jute MSP: **₹5,650/quintal** (Jute Corporation of India).
**JUTE-ICARE**: certified seed and microbial retting "**SONA**".

88.s: The jute scheme that promotes certified seed and microbial retting using 'SONA' is:
88.x: JUTE-ICARE promotes certified seed and microbial retting with SONA. The National Jute Development Programme (A) and Jute Diversification Scheme (B) are separate schemes; the Jute Packaging Materials Act 1987 (D) mandates jute bags for foodgrains and sugar.
88.tq: SONA retting = JUTE-ICARE.
xs: **JUTE-ICARE** promotes **certified seed** and microbial retting "**SONA**" — option **(3)**.
The **Jute Packaging Materials Act** (**1987**) mandates jute bags; it is not a seed or retting scheme.
xa: Other schemes: **National Jute Development Programme (NJB)**, **Jute Diversification Scheme**, jute geotextiles.
**National Jute Policy**: **2005**.
Jute needs **soft water for retting** — a Hooghly location factor.

88.s: India's sugar industry occupies which position among agro-based industries in the country?
o: The second-largest agro-based industry after cotton textiles
The third-largest agro-based industry after jute
The fourth-largest agro-based industry after cement
88.x: The sugar industry is India's second-largest agro-based industry, next only to cotton textiles.
88.tq: Use direct rank recall and distinguish the industry from the leading agro-based sector.
xs: Sugar is the **second-largest agro-based industry after cotton textiles** — option **(1)**.
So it is not the largest agro-based industry; **cotton textiles** come first.
xa: India is the **world's largest sugar consumer** and **2nd largest producer after Brazil** (~**19%**).
**534** operational factories (2024-25); ~**400 lakh MT** capacity.
Capacity is roughly **equal** between **private and cooperative** units.

88.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's position in the world sugar industry:
1. India is the world's largest sugar consumer.
2. India is the second-largest sugar producer after Brazil.
3. India accounts for approximately 19 per cent of world sugar output.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
88.x: India is the largest consumer, the second-largest producer after Brazil, and contributes about 19 per cent of world sugar output.
88.tq: Check each numerical and comparative statement independently before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
India is the **world's largest sugar consumer** and the **2nd largest producer after Brazil**.
India's share is about **19%** of world output.
xa: ⚠ Older notes call India the **largest producer**.
State shares: **UP 35%**, Maharashtra **22%**, Karnataka **10%**, TN **8%**.
Duty-free import of up to **10 lakh tonnes** raw sugar allowed (**27 Aug 2026**).

88.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the state-wise share of India's sugar production.

List-I (State)
A. Uttar Pradesh
B. Maharashtra
C. Karnataka
D. Tamil Nadu

List-II (Approximate share)
1. 35 per cent
2. 22 per cent
3. 10 per cent
4. 8 per cent

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
88.x: Uttar Pradesh accounts for about 35 per cent, Maharashtra 22 per cent, Karnataka 10 per cent and Tamil Nadu 8 per cent.
88.tq: Start with the sure pair of Uttar Pradesh and its highest stated share, then complete the matching.
xs: Correct code **A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4** — option **(1)**.
**UP 35%**, **Maharashtra 22%**, **Karnataka 10%**, **Tamil Nadu 8%**.
xa: UP's share comes from the **Ganga-Yamuna doab** and **Tarai**.
⚠ **Maharashtra** (~**9.9 MT**) led the latest season's output, ahead of UP (~**8.9 MT**).
UP + Bihar once had ~**70%** of capacity.

88.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the north–south characteristics of the sugar industry?
o: North India — generally higher sucrose content and yield
88.x: Tropical cane in South India generally has higher sucrose content and yield. North India has subtropical cane with comparatively lower sucrose content.
88.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the paired north–south characteristics.
xs: **North India — higher sucrose and yield** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**.
The **South** has **tropical cane** with **higher sucrose** and yield; the **North** has **subtropical** cane with lower sucrose.
The South also has the **longer crushing season**, so options (2), (3) and (4) are correct pairs.
xa: Yields: **TN ~105 t/ha** vs **UP ~81**.
Crushing season: **200-250 days** (South) vs **150-180** (North).
The North has **older private mills** → shift south.

88.s:
Consider the following statements about the north-south contrast in India's sugar industry:
1. The crushing season in the North (UP, Bihar) is generally November to February.
2. The crushing season in the South generally runs from October to May/June.
3. Cooperative mills dominate the North, especially Bihar, while the South has mostly private mills.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
88.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the North has many private mills (Bihar mostly non-cooperative), while cooperative mills are strong in the South, especially Maharashtra. So B is right; A omits statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
88.tq: Cooperatives = Maharashtra/South; longer season = South.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: North crushing season **Nov-Feb** — correct.
Statement 2: South crushing season **Oct-May/June** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: the North has many **private** mills (**Bihar mostly non-cooperative**); **cooperatives** are strong in the South, esp. **Maharashtra**.
xa: South's season lasts **200-250 days** vs **150-180** in the North.
**Well-run cooperative mills** are a reason the South gained.
Southern tropical cane has **higher sucrose**.

88.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of important cooperative sugar-mill centres in Maharashtra?
o: Chittoor, Visakhapatnam, Nalgonda, Katni and Satna
Nasik, Pune, Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur and Sholapur
Meerut, Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Gorakhpur and Deoria
Bodhan, Kadapa, Nandyal, Yerraguntla and Jaggayyapeta
88.x: Nasik, Pune, Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur and Sholapur are identified with Maharashtra's cooperative sugar mills.
88.tq: Recognise the complete regional list and eliminate lists combining unrelated sugar and cement centres.
xs: **Nasik, Pune, Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur and Sholapur** are Maharashtra's cooperative sugar belt — option **(2)**.
**Meerut-Saharanpur-Muzaffarnagar** and **Gorakhpur-Deoria** are UP belts; **Satna, Katni, Nalgonda, Yerraguntla, Jaggayyapeta, Nandyal** are cement clusters.
xa: **Maharashtra** (~**9.9 MT**) led the latest season's sugar output.
**Bodhan** (Nizamabad) is **Shakkarnagar**, grown around the **Nizam Sugar Factory**.
Maharashtra's capacity share: **22%**.

88.s: The principal reason sugar mills are generally located within about 20 km of sugarcane-growing areas is that sugarcane:
o: Requires saline soil and cannot grow near cities
Can be transported only by water
Produces more sugar when stored for a long period
Is perishable and yields only about 9–12 per cent sugar
88.x: Sugarcane is perishable and gives only about 9–12 per cent sugar, making transport over long distances uneconomic.
88.tq: Apply the raw-material perishability and bulk-loss principle to industrial location.
xs: Cane is **perishable** and yields only about **9-12%** sugar — option **(4)** — so mills sit within ~**20 km** of cane.
That makes sugar a **raw-material-oriented** industry.
xa: **Bagasse** fuels the mill boilers, making mills energy self-sufficient.
**Molasses** → alcohol/**ethanol** (**20%** blending target).
**Press mud** → manure.

88.s: Which of the following pairs of sugar-producing areas and states is correctly matched?
88.x: Meerut, Saharanpur and Muzaffarnagar form the western Uttar Pradesh sugar belt. Gorakhpur, Deoria and Basti are in eastern Uttar Pradesh, while the Godavari and Chittoor belts are in Andhra Pradesh.
88.tq: Check the state before the individual district association to avoid location swapping.
xs: **Meerut-Saharanpur-Muzaffarnagar — western UP** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Gorakhpur-Deoria-Basti** is **eastern UP**; **Nasik-Pune-Satara** is **Maharashtra**; the **Godavari-Chittoor** belts are in **AP**.
xa: UP + Bihar once held ~**70%** of capacity.
**Stand-alone refineries** are on the **Gujarat and West Bengal** coasts.
AP sugar belts: **West and East Godavari, Visakhapatnam, Chittoor**.

88.s: Which of the following districts or regions is NOT included among the Andhra Pradesh sugar belts identified for the sugar industry?
88.x: The Andhra Pradesh sugar belts include West Godavari, East Godavari, Visakhapatnam and Chittoor. Nandyal is identified as a cement cluster.
88.tq: Separate sugar-belt locations from nearby Andhra Pradesh cement centres.
xs: **Nandyal** is not an AP sugar belt — option **(2)**; it is an AP **cement** cluster.
AP sugar belts: **West Godavari, East Godavari, Visakhapatnam, Chittoor**.
xa: AP cement clusters: **Yerraguntla (Kadapa)**, **Jaggayyapeta (NTR)**, **Nandyal**.
The **Kadapa-Kurnool** limestone rock systems make Rayalaseema a cement hub.
**Shakkarnagar** grew around the **Nizam Sugar Factory**.

88.s:
Match the following sugar-industry by-products with their principal uses.

List-I (By-product)
A. Bagasse
B. Molasses
C. Press mud

List-II (Use)
1. Manure
2. Alcohol and ethanol
3. Boiler fuel and paper pulp

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
88.x: Bagasse is used as boiler fuel and for paper pulp, molasses for alcohol and ethanol, and press mud as manure.
88.tq: Start from the distinctive bagasse–boiler fuel pair and complete the remaining matches.
xs: Correct code **A-3, B-2, C-1** — option **(1)**.
**Bagasse** = boiler fuel and **paper pulp**; **Molasses** = **alcohol/ethanol**; **Press mud** = **manure**.
xa: Bagasse makes mills **energy self-sufficient**.
Ethanol blending target: **20%**.
Sugar diverted to ethanol fell from **12% (2022-23)** to **9% (2025-26)**.

88.s: Which one of the following statements regarding ethanol production is correct?
o: Bagasse provides approximately three-fourths of ethanol production
Grain currently provides approximately three-fourths of ethanol production
Sugarcane provides the entire ethanol supply
Molasses has no role in ethanol production
88.x: Grain now provides approximately three-fourths of ethanol production, although molasses remains an important sugar-industry feedstock.
88.tq: Distinguish the current feedstock share from the role of sugar-industry by-products.
xs: **Grain** now provides about **three-fourths** of ethanol — option **(2)**.
Sugar diverted to ethanol fell from **12% (2022-23)** to **9% (2025-26)**.
**Molasses** is still an ethanol feedstock, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Ethanol blending target: **20%**.
**Bagasse** is boiler fuel and paper pulp, not the ethanol source.
**Press mud** is used as manure.

88.s: The Rangarajan Committee on the sugar sector recommended, among other measures:
o: A 70:30 revenue-sharing formula and removal of the minimum-distance rule
Complete abolition of cooperative sugar mills
A 30:70 revenue-sharing formula and compulsory nationalisation of mills
Location of all sugar mills on the coast
88.x: The committee recommended a 70:30 revenue-sharing formula and removal of the minimum-distance rule.
88.tq: Use the exact committee recommendation and reject reversed numerical ratios.
xs: The **Rangarajan Committee** recommended **70:30 revenue sharing** and removal of the **minimum-distance rule** — option **(1)**.
It did not propose abolishing cooperatives or nationalising mills.
xa: Cane pricing: Centre's **FRP** vs higher State **SAP**.
Capacity is roughly **equal** between private and cooperative units.
**534** operational factories (2024-25).

88.s: In the latest sugar season (2026), which State led India's sugar output?
88.x: Maharashtra (~9.9 MT) led sugar output, ahead of Uttar Pradesh (~8.9 MT) and Karnataka (~4.7 MT). UP (A) has the largest share in the long-run pattern (35%) but came second this season; Karnataka (B) was third; Tamil Nadu (D) is smaller.
88.tq: Latest season: Maharashtra > UP > Karnataka.
xs: **Maharashtra** (~**9.9 MT**) led the latest season's sugar output — option **(3)**.
**UP** (~**8.9 MT**) came second and **Karnataka** (~**4.7 MT**) third.
xa: ⚠ **UP** holds the largest capacity share (**35%**), but Maharashtra led the latest output.
Maharashtra's capacity share: **22%**; Karnataka **10%**; TN **8%**.
Southern advantage: **tropical cane**, longer season, **cooperative** mills.

88.s: With reference to sugarcane pricing in India, consider: 1. FRP is fixed by the Centre. 2. SAP is fixed by States and is usually higher than FRP. Which is/are correct?
88.x: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) is set by the Centre, and several States announce a higher State Advised Price (SAP). Both statements are correct, so A and B are incomplete and D is wrong.
88.tq: FRP = Centre; SAP = State (higher).
xs: **Both statements** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: **FRP** is the **Centre's** cane price — correct.
Statement 2: **SAP** is the **higher State** cane price — correct.
xa: **Rangarajan Committee**: **70:30** revenue sharing; remove the minimum-distance rule.
Duty-free import of up to **10 lakh tonnes** raw sugar (**27 Aug 2026**).
Capacity: ~**400 lakh MT** in **534** factories.

88.s: India is the world's second-largest cement producer and contributes more than approximately what share of world cement output?
88.x: India is the second-largest cement producer and contributes more than 8 per cent of world output.
88.tq: Separate the cement share from the sugar industry's approximately 19 per cent world share.
xs: India is the **2nd largest cement producer**, with **over 8 per cent** of world output — option **(3)**.
**19%** is India's share of world **sugar**, not cement.
xa: Capacity: **~700 MTPA**.
Per capita use: **~290 kg** vs world **540 kg**.
Largest producing state: **Rajasthan** (2026).

88.s:
Consider the following statements about the cement industry in India:
1. Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh are major cement-producing states.
2. South India holds over 30% of national cement capacity.
3. As per 2026 data, Andhra Pradesh is the largest cement-producing state, followed by Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
88.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2026 order is Rajasthan first, then AP, Telangana, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and TN (only older sources rank AP first by capacity). So B is right; A omits statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
88.tq: Largest cement producer (2026) = Rajasthan; AP second.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **AP, Rajasthan, Karnataka, MP** are major cement states — correct.
Statement 2: **South India** holds **over 30%** of capacity — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: in 2026 **Rajasthan** is largest, then **AP**, Telangana, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, TN.
xa: ⚠ Older notes rank **AP first by capacity**.
Capacity: **~700 MTPA**; India is **2nd largest** producer.
Clusters: **Satna and Katni** (MP), **Chittoor** (AP), **Nalgonda** (Telangana).

88.s:
Which of the following pairs of cement clusters and states is correctly matched?
1. Satna and Katni — Madhya Pradesh
2. Chittoor — Andhra Pradesh
3. Nalgonda — Telangana
4. Khilari and Chaibasa — Jharkhand
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
88.x: Satna and Katni are in Madhya Pradesh, Chittoor in Andhra Pradesh, Nalgonda in Telangana, and Khilari and Chaibasa in Jharkhand.
88.tq: Verify each location–state pair and watch for neighbouring-state substitutions.
xs: All four pairs are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**Satna and Katni** = MP; **Chittoor** = AP; **Nalgonda** = Telangana.
**Khilari** (Palamu) and **ACC (Chaibasa)** = Jharkhand.
xa: AP clusters: **Yerraguntla (Kadapa)**, **Jaggayyapeta (NTR)**, **Nandyal**.
**Dalmia Bharat** and **Zuari** plants are in the **Kadapa-Kurnool** belt.
South India holds **over 30%** of capacity.

88.s:
Consider the following statements about the cement industry of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The limestone of the Kadapa-Kurnool rock systems makes Rayalaseema a cement hub.
2. Yerraguntla is a cement cluster in Kadapa district.
3. Jaggayyapeta is a cement cluster in Kurnool district.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
88.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kadapa-Kurnool limestone makes Rayalaseema a cement hub. Statement 2 is correct: Yerraguntla is in Kadapa. Statement 3 is wrong: Jaggayyapeta is in NTR district. So only two statements are correct.
88.tq: AP cement: Yerraguntla (Kadapa), Jaggayyapeta (NTR), Nandyal.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** only two.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Kadapa-Kurnool rock systems (limestone)** make **Rayalaseema** a cement hub.
Statement 2 is correct: **Yerraguntla** is in **Kadapa**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Jaggayyapeta** is in **NTR** district, not Kurnool.
xa: Another AP cluster: **Nandyal**; **Dalmia Bharat** and **Zuari** plants are in the Kadapa-Kurnool belt.
**Rajasthan** is the largest cement-producing state; AP **2nd**.
Other clusters: **Satna and Katni** (MP), **Chittoor** (AP), **Nalgonda** (Telangana).
India is the **2nd largest cement producer** (**over 8%** of world output).

88.s: Green cement in the form of Portland Pozzolana Cement uses which combination of industrial by-products?
o: Fly ash from thermal plants and slag from steel plants
88.x: Portland Pozzolana Cement uses fly ash from thermal power plants and slag from steel plants.
88.tq: Use the source-industry association: thermal plants supply fly ash and steel plants supply slag.
xs: **PPC** (green cement) uses **fly ash** from thermal plants and **slag** from steel plants — option **(1)**.
**Bagasse, molasses and press mud** are **sugar** by-products.
xa: Main cement inputs: **limestone, silica, alumina, gypsum**.
Cement is among the sectors moving from **PAT** to the **CCTS** (**24 Jun 2026**).
India's per capita cement use: **~290 kg**.

88.s: Which statement correctly describes cement consumption in India in comparison with the world average?
o: India's per capita use is about 540 kg, compared with a world average of about 290 kg
India's per capita use is about 290 kg, compared with a world average of about 540 kg
Both India and the world average are about 290 kg
Both India and the world average are about 700 kg
88.x: India's per capita cement consumption is approximately 290 kg, while the world average is about 540 kg.
88.tq: Check the direction of the comparison before selecting the paired numerical values.
xs: India's per capita cement use is **~290 kg** vs a world average of **540 kg** — option **(2)**.
**~700** is India's capacity in **MTPA**, not per capita use.
xa: India is the **2nd largest** producer, **over 8%** of world output.
Largest producing state: **Rajasthan**.
South India: **over 30%** of capacity.

88.s: Which of the following combinations represents the principal inputs of the cement industry?
o: Raw jute, cotton, wool and local cane
Naphtha, natural gas, sulphur and rock phosphate
88.x: The principal cement inputs listed are limestone, silica, alumina and gypsum; fly ash and slag are also used.
88.tq: Separate the core mineral inputs of cement from the chemical and fibre inputs of other industries.
xs: Cement inputs: **limestone, silica, alumina and gypsum** — option **(3)**.
**Bamboo, poplar, softwood, rags** are **paper** inputs; **naphtha, gas, sulphur, rock phosphate** are **fertiliser** inputs.
xa: Cement also uses **coal**.
Green cement (**PPC**) adds **fly ash** and **slag**.
Plants sit near **limestone** deposits.

88.s: India's first cement plant, set up in 1904 using sea shells as lime, was located at:
88.x: The first cement plant came up at Madras (Chennai) in 1904 and failed. Porbandar (A) had the first successful plant (Indian Cement Co., 1912-14); Katni (C) is a later MP cluster; Ranipet (D) had the first super-phosphate factory (1906).
88.tq: Cement first = Madras 1904; first successful = Porbandar.
xs: The first cement plant was at **Madras (Chennai)** in **1904**, using **sea shells** — option **(2)**; it **failed**.
**Porbandar** had the first **successful** plant (Indian Cement Co., **1912-13**; UPSC notes: **1914**).
**Ranipet** had the first **super-phosphate** factory (**1906**); **Katni** is an MP cement cluster.
xa: Exam angle: "first cement plant **1904**?" — **Chennai** (APPSC G2 **2024**, **2025**).

xs: India's modern car industry began with **Premier Automobiles** at **Kurla (Mumbai)** in **1947** — option **(2)**.

"Detroit of India" = **Chennai**.

89.s: The automobile sector was described as a 'Sunrise Sector' because its share in GDP rose from 2.77% in 1992-93 to approximately:
89.x: The automobile sector's share in GDP rose from 2.77% in 1992-93 to approximately 7.1%, leading to its description as a Sunrise Sector.
89.tq: Compare the starting percentage with the approximate later share.
xs: The auto sector's GDP share rose from **2.77%** (1992-93) to about **7.1%** — option **(3)** — hence "**Sunrise Sector**".
Its share thus more than doubled since **1992-93** — the basis of the **Sunrise** label.
xa: **PLI-Auto** (**2021**): **₹25,938 crore**, minimum **50%** domestic value addition.
**FAME India** from **2015**; FAME-II from **2019**.
By **22 Aug 2025**, **8 OEMs** had DVA certificates for **84 EV variants**.

89.s: FAME India was introduced in 2015, while FAME-II was introduced in:
89.x: FAME India began in 2015 and FAME-II was introduced in 2019.
89.tq: Discriminate between the original scheme and its second phase by their respective years.
xs: **FAME India** began in **2015** and **FAME-II** in **2019** — option **(4)**.
Both aim at **EV adoption**.
xa: EV passenger-car scheme notified **15 Mar 2024**.
**PLI-Auto** approved **2021**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the PLI-Auto scheme:

2. Its outlay is ₹25,938 crore.
3. It is intended for advanced automotive technology.

xs: All four statements are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**PLI-Auto**: approved **2021**, outlay **₹25,938 crore**.
It is for **advanced automotive technology**, with a minimum **50% domestic value addition**.

The umbrella **PLI** (2020) covers **14 sectors**, **₹1.97 lakh crore**.

89.s:
With reference to the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, consider the following statements:

2. The total outlay under the scheme is ₹1.97 lakh crore.

xs: All three statements are correct — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
**PLI** (**2020**) covers **14 sectors** with outlay **₹1.97 lakh crore**.
The **Electronics PLI** grew out of the **National Policy on Electronics 2019**.

**PLI for Bulk Drugs** supports pharma.

89.s: The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in:

xs: **Semiconductor fab — Dholera** is correct — option **(1)**.
**Micron's ATMP** is at **Sanand**, not Jagiroad or Dholera; **Tata's** plant is at **Jagiroad, Assam**, not Sanand.

**ISM** launched **2021**; **Semicon 2.0** cleared **16 Jul 2026**.
**Sanand** is also an automobile hub (**Tata Motors, MG Motor**).

89.s: Which one of the following best explains why the IT industry is described as 'footloose'?
o: It is independent of raw materials and is attracted by engineering talent and a technology ecosystem.
It can operate only near coalfields and ports.
It depends exclusively on bulky local raw materials.
It requires heavy mineral inputs at the production site.
89.x: The IT industry is footloose because it is largely independent of raw materials and is located mainly according to engineering talent and the technology ecosystem.
89.tq: Apply the meaning of a geographical term rather than matching it to a physical resource.
xs: IT is **footloose**: **raw-material independent**, located by **engineering talent** and a **tech ecosystem** — option **(1)**.
It needs only **light inputs**, not bulky raw materials, coalfields or ports.
xa: Clusters: **Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Noida/NCR**.
IT + electronics = footloose vs **steel + shipbuilding** = raw-material or port-bound.
Bengaluru = "**Silicon Valley of India**".

89.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
89.x: Bengaluru is known as the Silicon Valley of India, while Hyderabad is known as Cyberabad.
89.tq: Discriminate between the two prominent IT-city nicknames.
xs: **Bengaluru — Silicon Valley of India** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Hyderabad** is "**Cyberabad**", not Silicon Valley; **Pune** and **Chennai** are not Cyberabad.
xa: IT clusters: **Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Noida/NCR**.
The **Bengaluru-Tamil Nadu** region is also called the Silicon Valley of India.

89.s: The Department of Electronics, which foresaw India's export potential in software as early as the mid-1970s, was set up in the:
89.x: The Department of Electronics was set up in the Prime Minister's Office and recognised India's software export potential as early as the mid-1970s.
89.tq: Use the institutional-location clue to identify the correct administrative authority.
xs: The **Department of Electronics** was set up in the **Prime Minister's Office** — option **(3)**.
It foresaw **software** export potential as early as the **mid-1970s**.
xa: **STPI** set up in **1991**.
**National Policy on Electronics 2019** led to the electronics PLI.
IT is a **footloose** industry.

89.s: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) were set up in:
89.x: Software Technology Parks of India were set up in 1991. STPs along with EMC 2.0 support the IT and software sector.
89.tq: Distinguish the policy-history date from other technology and industrial milestones.
xs: **STPI** was set up in **1991** — option **(3)**.
Today **STPs + EMC 2.0** support the sector.
xa: The **Department of Electronics** (PMO) saw software exports coming by the **mid-1970s**.
IT clusters: **Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Noida/NCR**.
**EMC**: greenfield **50%**, brownfield **75%**.

89.s: India is described as the “Pharmacy of the World” and ranks respectively in the following positions by production volume and export value:
89.x: India is known as the “Pharmacy of the World”; it ranks third by pharmaceutical production volume and eleventh by export value.
89.tq: Keep production volume and export value as separate ranking measures; do not reverse them.
xs: India — "**Pharmacy of the World**" — is **3rd by production volume** and **11th by export value** — **Third and eleventh**, option **(3)**.
⚠ The order matters: **3rd** is volume, **11th** is export value — option (2) reverses them.
xa: API import dependence on **China** fell to ~**65%** (from **70-80%**).
Support: **PLI for Bulk Drugs**, **Bulk Drug Parks**, **26 critical raw materials** commercialised.
Hubs: **Hyderabad**, **Ahmedabad-Vadodara**, **Visakhapatnam - Parawada Pharma City**.

89.s:

2. Gujarat
3. Himachal Pradesh

89.tq: Test list completeness by checking each state individually before selecting the code.
xs: **Bulk Drug Parks** are in **AP, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh** — **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.

xa: **26 critical raw materials** have been commercialised.
API dependence on China down to ~**65%**.

India is the "**Pharmacy of the World**".

89.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

89.s: In the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC), the southern and northern portions are associated respectively with:
89.x: The southern part of VCIC is associated with automobiles, whereas the northern part is associated with pharmaceuticals.
89.tq: Watch for the reversed-comparison trap in paired regional descriptions.
xs: In the VCIC, the **south** is **automobiles** and the **north** is **pharmaceuticals** — option **(1)**.
South: **Sri City** (Isuzu), **Kia** (Sri Sathya Sai); north: **Parawada Pharma City** (Vizag).
xa: Parawada is a **Vizag VCIC node** bulk-drug cluster.

**Sri City** also hosts **Foxconn**.

90.s: Which one of the following is an agro-based industry?
90.x: Cotton textiles are agro-based because cotton is an agricultural raw material. Cement, aluminium and iron and steel are mineral-based industries.
90.tq: Use the raw-material classification to distinguish agro-based from mineral-based industries.
xs: **Cotton textile industry** is **agro-based** — option **(4)**: cotton is an agricultural raw material.
**Iron and steel, cement and aluminium** are **mineral-based** industries.
xa: Other agro-based: **sugar, jute, food processing, dairy** (Amul, Anand).

Agro-based units locate **near raw material** due to **weight loss or perishability**.

2. Mineral-based industry — Steel at Visakhapatnam

xs: All four pairs are correct — **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
**Agro-based**: **Mega Food Park, Mallavalli** (Krishna); **Mineral-based**: **steel at Vizag**.

List-I (Industry type)
(a) Forest-based
(b) Marine-based
(c) Animal-based
(d) Agro-based

(i) Coastal aquaculture processing
(ii) Dairy
(iii) Pulp and paper
(iv) Sugar

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.

xs: Correct code **a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
**Forest-based** = **pulp and paper**; **Marine-based** = **coastal aquaculture processing**.
**Animal-based** = **dairy**; **Agro-based** = **sugar**.
xa: ⚠ Largest forest-based industry = **pulp and paper**.
Marine-based seafood processing: **Kerala, Gujarat, AP** coasts.
Animal-based also includes **leather** and **wool**.

90.s: Why do agro-based industrial units generally locate near the source of raw materials?
o: Agricultural raw materials are usually heavier after processing
The raw materials may lose weight or perish during transport
Agricultural raw materials are always imported
Agro-based industries require no transport facilities
90.x: Agro-based units locate near raw materials because the materials may be perishable or may undergo weight loss during processing.
90.tq: Apply the location principle of weight loss and perishability.
xs: Agro-based units locate near raw material because the materials **lose weight or perish** — option **(2)**.
Their raw materials are agricultural, not imported, and the units still need transport.
xa: Agro-based examples: **cotton textiles, sugar, jute, food processing, dairy**.
AP example: **Mega Food Park, Mallavalli**.
⚠ **Footloose** industries are the opposite: they need skilled labour + internet, **not raw material**.

90.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Indian paper industry is correct?

1. India accounts for approximately 5% of world paper production.
2. Recycled fibre contributes about 71–75% of the raw material.
3. Wood pulp contributes about 21% of the raw material.
4. India’s per capita paper consumption is about 57 kg per year.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
90.x: India accounts for about 5% of world paper, recycled fibre contributes 71–75%, and wood pulp contributes about 21%. Indian per capita consumption is about 16 kg, not 57 kg; 57 kg is the world figure.
90.tq: Separate the Indian figure from the comparative world figure before selecting the statements.
xs: **Statements 1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
India makes about **5%** of world paper; **recycled fibre** is **71-75%** and **wood pulp** ~**21%** of raw material.
Statement 4 is wrong: India uses only **16 kg/person/year**; **57 kg** is the **world** figure.
xa: Wood pulp comes from **eucalyptus, poplar, subabul**; agro-residue is **5-8%**.
Paper needs **100-150 t of water** per tonne.
**Pulp and paper** is the largest forest-based industry.

90.s: The term “gold collar” is associated with which sector?
o: Quaternary sector involving research and development
90.x: The quinary sector is described as the “gold collar” sector and involves top-level decision-making.
90.tq: Distinguish quinary decision-making from quaternary knowledge and R&D activities.
xs: "**Gold collar**" refers to the **Quinary sector** — **top decision-making** — option **(3)**.
**Quaternary** is **knowledge/R&D/IT**; **Secondary** is manufacturing; **Primary** is extraction.
xa: **Tertiary** = services.
Ladder: primary → secondary → tertiary → quaternary → quinary.
**Sunrise** areas: **AI, green hydrogen, EVs, semiconductors**.

90.s:
With reference to the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, consider the following statements:

1. Schedule A industries were reserved for the public sector.
2. Arms, atomic energy, and iron and steel were included in Schedule A.
3. Schedule B industries were open only to private enterprises.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Schedule A industries, including arms, atomic energy, and iron and steel, were reserved for the public sector. Schedule B industries were open to both public and private sectors, making statement 3 false.

xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: **Schedule A** was **reserved for the public sector** — correct.
Statement 2: Schedule A included **arms, atomic energy, iron and steel** — correct.

90.s: The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises was formed in 2007 by merging which two ministries?
o: Ministry of Rural Development and Ministry of Agriculture
Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industries
Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Small Scale Industries and Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries

o: Classification exclusively by number of workers
A composite criterion of investment and turnover, without distinguishing manufacturing from services

xa: **Ministry of MSME**: formed **2007** by merging two ministries.

90.s: Which one of the following is classified as a basic or primary good?

90.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes heavy industries from light industries?
o: Heavy industries are always labour-intensive, whereas light industries are always capital-intensive

Heavy industries are confined to services, whereas light industries are confined to mining

Heavy industries are **capital-intensive**, not labour-intensive.

90.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

92.s: In the present system of National Highway numbering, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Odd-numbered highways generally run east-west and increase from north to south.
Even-numbered highways generally run north-south and increase from west to east.
National Highways are numbered exclusively according to their length.
Odd-numbered highways generally run north-south and increase from west to east.
92.x: Odd-numbered National Highways generally run north-south and their numbers increase from west to east. Even-numbered highways generally run east-west and increase from north to south.

xs: **Odd-numbered NHs run north-south and rise from west to east** — option **(4)** is correct.

Numbering follows **direction**, not length.
xa: Longest NH: **NH-44** (Srinagar-Kanyakumari, **4,112 km**); shortest: **NH-966B** (**8 km**).
**NH-27** (Porbandar-Silchar) is an east-west road; **NH-16** runs Kolkata-Chennai along the east coast.
NHs = **1.46 lakh km**, ~**2%** of road length but ~**40%** of traffic.

92.s:

xs: **Daocheng Yading** — Sichuan, China; **Laerdal** — **24.5 km**; **Atal Tunnel** — about **9.0 km**; **Hubballi** — **1,507 metres** — so option **(1)** a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
**Daocheng Yading** is the **highest civilian airport** (**4,411 metres** above sea level).
The **Atal Tunnel** (Rohtang, HP) is India's longest tunnel above **10,000 feet**.
xa: Atal Tunnel connects **Manali - Lahaul-Spiti**; **9.02 km** (PYQ 2025).
**Zojila Tunnel**: **13.15 km**.
**Janasu tunnel** (**14.58 km**): India's longest transport tunnel.

92.s:
Assertion (A): The Silk Route is not a single modern highway.
Reason (R): It was a historic trade route involving both land and sea routes.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
92.x: Both are true and R explains A: the Silk Route was a web of land and sea trade routes, so it is not a single modern highway.
92.tq: Check whether R is the cause of A.
n: The Silk Road or Silk Route was a historic trade route involving land and sea routes. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
The Silk Road or Silk Route is not a single modern highway. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xs: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A — so option **(1)**.
The **Silk Road** ran from **China** through **Central Asia** to **Europe** — a **historic trade route** of **land and sea routes**, ⚠ **not** a single modern highway.
xa: **Asian Highway Network**: an international road network promoted by **UNESCAP**.
**Trans-African Highways**: e.g. the **Tripoli–Cape Town** route.
**Golden Quadrilateral** connects **Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata**.

92.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Railway)
a. Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
b. Nilgiri Mountain Railway
c. Kalka–Shimla Railway

List-II (Location)
i. Himachal Pradesh

n: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway is located in West Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 128-130]
The Nilgiri Mountain Railway is located in Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 128-130]
The Kalka–Shimla Railway is located in Himachal Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 128-130]
xs: **Darjeeling Himalayan** — West Bengal, **Nilgiri Mountain** — Tamil Nadu, **Kalka–Shimla** — Himachal Pradesh — so option **(3)** a-iii, b-ii, c-i.

**Chenab Bridge** (J&K) is on the **USBRL**.
